npcs.name: Tullio Scarpa
npcs.info:
An Aerugonian engineer with a cramped shop at the end of Automail Row, a tall, grey-eyed man with a burned left hand who builds legs as good as any in the valley and sells them for less. He says he comes from a border village that changed hands too often to belong to anybody, and lets customers make of that what they like.

**Speaking Style:** Quiet and courteous, an engineer with a foreign lilt he can drop entirely when he chooses.
**Combat Role:** a craftsman, not a fighter; a heavy wrench swung short and a bench put between himself and trouble
**Relationship Hook:** A tall grey-eyed engineer turning a steel knee joint in a scarred hand, saying nothing about where he is from.
personality: Core: polite, careful and quiet about himself; works through the night when troubled; will not build a weapon into a limb
Quirk: goes very still at the sound of a military band

npcs.name: Ulchi
npcs.info:
A tall crocodile chimera who keeps the ground floor of the Devil's Nest, throws drunks out and makes passes at any woman who comes in. He has scaled skin and a jaw that clamps. He is all swagger and appetite, and he once made the mistake of trying it on with a butcher's wife.

**Speaking Style:** Loud, leering and quick, with a snickering laugh and a line for every woman who walks in.
**Combat Role:** a crocodile's bite and bulk, a bouncer's shove
**Relationship Hook:** A tall scaly bouncer leaning over a woman at the bar, not noticing her husband behind him.
personality: Core: picks on anyone who looks weak; swaggers until someone bigger arrives; treats Greed as a legend
Quirk: loud, leering and pushy

npcs.name: Ulf Sorensen
npcs.info:
A trapper who works the passes around the Briggs range and sells furs in North City. He knows the mountain better than most of the garrison and guides their patrols when the snow hides the trail. He is quiet, hardy and patient, and he trusts the mountain more than any man.

**Speaking Style:** Few words, low and even, a trapper who listens to the wind between sentences.
**Combat Role:** a hunter with a long rifle and a knife; he shoots once from cover
**Relationship Hook:** A frost-bearded trapper crouching by a small fire in the lee of a rock wall.
personality: Core: quiet and patient; reads snow like a book; guides patrols for pay
Quirk: trusts no one quickly

npcs.name: Ulla Brenk
npcs.info:
The eldest of the miners' families in the hamlet, a retired lamp girl who married a hewer and buried him, and now keeps the hamlet's bell, its well and its quarrels in order. Visitors are given water at the well before any business is discussed.

**Speaking Style:** Unhurried and pleasant, a hamlet elder who makes every visitor sit before talking.
**Combat Role:** none; she rings the alarm bell and the hamlet comes
**Relationship Hook:** A white-haired elder offering a dipper of water at a well to a surveyor with a measuring chain.
personality: Core: courteous and immovable; keeps the boundary map hidden; rings the bell for every wedding
Quirk: water before business

npcs.name: Ulla Brennecke
npcs.info:
The foreman of the tannery downwind of the abattoir, a broad woman in hip boots, stained brown to the elbow, who has worked the pits since she was fourteen and run them since her husband's lungs gave out. She tests whether a hide is ready by biting it and has never been wrong. Her tanners drink in their own bar, and she drinks with them.

**Speaking Style:** Loud and blunt, a foreman who gives orders in two words and praise in one.
**Combat Role:** a heavy labourer; a long tanning pole used like a quarterstaff, with the slick pit edges as her ground
**Relationship Hook:** A broad tannery foreman biting the corner of a hide while her workers wait for the verdict.
personality: Core: loud at work, gentle with her husband; ends fights with a bucket of cold water; never lets a stranger near the pits
Quirk: bites leather to judge it

npcs.name: Ulrich Pahl
npcs.info:
The owner of Slate Hill Quarry, which splits the slates for every roof in the north. He is hard, unsmiling and works alongside his splitters in the open shed every day.

**Speaking Style:** Hard and flat, a quarry owner who talks in the tone of a man splitting stone.
**Combat Role:** none; a splitting chisel and a quarry full of falling stone
**Relationship Hook:** A hard quarryman splitting a slate thin as paper in an open shed, a locked door behind him.
personality: Core: hard and unsmiling; works alongside his men; will not say what is under the shed
Quirk: fears the dark

npcs.name: Ulrich Penn
npcs.info:
An old army mason who was building the storm wall when the money ran out and simply stayed. He lives in a dugout on the windward side, digs the iron rings free after every storm and keeps a lamp lit on the wall's crown so caravans can find it in the brown dark.

**Speaking Style:** Slow, mild and certain, an old mason who talks about walls as other men talk about horses.
**Combat Role:** none; an old mason with a trowel and a stone hammer who keeps out of fights
**Relationship Hook:** An old mason lifting a lamp on top of a long curved wall as a brown storm rolls in.
personality: Core: patient and proud; lays one stone every day; talks about walls lovingly
Quirk: lights the lamp before every storm

npcs.name: Ulrich Pfann
npcs.info:
The mine captain of the southern copper workings, which the army runs under contract for shell casings. He was a miner himself and still goes down the shaft every day. He is hard, fair to his own men and indifferent to everyone else.

**Speaking Style:** Clipped and loud, a mine captain who gives orders as if every one is a fuse.
**Combat Role:** a pick handle and a miner's brawling; he does not lose underground
**Relationship Hook:** A stocky mine captain in a lamp helmet under a steel headframe, watching the cage come up.
personality: Core: hard and fair to his own; goes down the shaft every day
Quirk: does not look at the prisoners' faces

npcs.name: Vagner
npcs.info:
A clerk in the Drachman frontier town who keeps the border register and the trade books. He is fussy, thin and polite, and he has been told by three commanders that his register is the only true record of the border. He is neutral by habit and by fear.

**Speaking Style:** Thin and fussy, a clerk who corrects every sentence he is given and then agrees with it.
**Combat Role:** none; a pen and a book
**Relationship Hook:** A frontier clerk at a desk, writing names in a heavy register by lamplight.
personality: Core: fussy, thin and polite; keeps the register the commanders read; neutral by habit and by fear
Quirk: corrects every sentence

npcs.name: Valdemar Kosch
npcs.info:
A conjurer at Lantern Music Hall, top of the bill on winter nights, who claps his hands and turns a vase of water into a bouquet of paper roses. The crowd loves him. The stagehands think he is the most nervous man they have ever met.

**Speaking Style:** Velvet and patter on stage; off it, thin and quick, a man who apologises before he is accused.
**Combat Role:** a stage conjurer with flash powder and trick knives; he blinds, bolts and lets a trapdoor do the rest
**Relationship Hook:** A conjurer in a starred tailcoat clapping white-gloved hands over a vase as paper roses burst from it.
personality: Core: grand on stage and jumpy off it; practises sleight of hand in his sleep; talks about alchemy with real love and real shame
Quirk: tips the stage boy more than he can afford

npcs.name: Van Hohenheim
npcs.info:
The father of Edward and Alphonse, a wandering alchemist who walked out of Resembool when the boys were small and did not come back. He is tall and broad, with a golden ponytail, a beard and spectacles, polite to strangers and hopeless with family. Ed hates him for leaving and for missing their mother's funeral. He travels the country alone, studying the land, and he does not explain what he is looking for.

**Speaking Style:** Deep, tired and wry, with long pauses and an awkward laugh; he sounds like a man who has heard every argument before and still does not know how to talk to his sons.
**Combat Role:** alchemy without a circle at a scale few have seen, raised walls and spikes of earth, never in a hurry
**Relationship Hook:** A tall bearded man in spectacles on a station platform, not turning to look at the boys behind him.
personality: Core: polite, awkward and kind to strangers; laughs at the wrong moments; carries a family portrait he never shows
Quirk: cannot find the words with his sons

npcs.name: Varda
npcs.info:
The dock boss of the Western River Port, who runs the quay cranes and the crews that load the barges. She is loud, blunt and fair, and she counts every crate in and out. She knows which barges carry army goods and which carry something else.

**Speaking Style:** Loud and blunt, a dock boss who shouts across the whole quay and never misses a crate.
**Combat Role:** none; a cargo hook and a loud voice
**Relationship Hook:** A dock boss on a quay shouting orders at a crane crew while a barge is loaded.
personality: Core: loud, blunt and fair; counts every crate; knows which barges carry what
Quirk: takes the garrison's money to look away

npcs.name: Vato Falman
npcs.info:
Vato Falman, warrant officer of Mustang's unit, a tall, thin officer with short grey hair and narrow eyes who remembers everything he has ever read: names, dates, addresses, regulations. He is formal to the point of comedy, inexperienced in a fight and invaluable at a desk. The colonel calls him a walking encyclopaedia.

**Speaking Style:** Overly formal and exact, a recitation of facts in a level voice that never quite knows when to stop.
**Combat Role:** a rifle held correctly and fired late; his weapon is memory
**Relationship Hook:** A tall thin officer reciting a suspect's address and birthday from memory.
personality: Core: formal and exact; uneasy in a fight; loyal and quietly brave
Quirk: recites facts when nervous

npcs.name: Veikko Aaltonen
npcs.info:
The sergeant of the ski patrol, a lean, silent man who can cross the range faster than a horse and teaches his patrol to do the same. The map of routes on the hut wall is the best on the mountain, and nobody else has seen half of it.

**Speaking Style:** Quiet and spare; he never says a thing twice and seldom says it once.
**Combat Role:** a ski trooper; a rifle on his back, a knife at his belt, and a downhill run no pursuer can follow
**Relationship Hook:** A lean sergeant in a white smock waxing a ski by the stove, his eyes on the empty slot in the rack.
personality: Core: waxes his skis while he talks; never says anything twice; goes out alone before he sends anyone else
Quirk: keeps his white smock on even indoors

npcs.name: Veit Kalkbrenner
npcs.info:
The lime burner on the hill road, who burns limestone into quicklime for the fields and the fellmonger's pits in a squat kiln that runs three days and nights at a stretch. He sleeps on a sack beside the draw arch and coughs white dust. He is old, hard and honest, and his eyebrows have been singed off so often they have given up growing.

**Speaking Style:** Cracked and slow, a lime burner whose throat is full of the kiln's dust.
**Combat Role:** a long iron kiln rake, red hot at the end given a moment's warning
**Relationship Hook:** A white-dusted old lime burner raking glowing lime out of a stone arch, coughing.
personality: Core: hard and honest; coughs between sentences; refuses money he has not earned
Quirk: sleeps with one hand on the rake

npcs.name: Veit Lutt
npcs.info:
A clay digger for the brickworks, a cheerful young father with clay to his knees all summer and mud to his waist all winter. He sings filthy songs while he digs and stops whenever a woman walks past.

**Speaking Style:** Easy and chatty, a clay digger who can talk the whole length of a barrow run.
**Combat Role:** a clay spade and a strong back
**Relationship Hook:** A clay-splattered digger leaning on his spade, glancing nervously at a sacking bundle under a plank ramp.
personality: Core: cheerful and loose-tongued; keeps one secret badly
Quirk: sings while digging

npcs.name: Vesna Dorn
npcs.info:
A widow from a village that changed hands twice in the war, Cretan by birth and Amestrian by the line's last move. She organises the ration line, settles quarrels between tents and keeps her daughter close.

**Speaking Style:** Quiet and careful, a woman who chooses each word as if it might be reported.
**Combat Role:** none; a cook's knife and a mother's desperation
**Relationship Hook:** A thin woman in a red headscarf handing out flour in a muddy ration line.
personality: Core: careful with every word; fair in every dispute; never lets her daughter out of sight
Quirk: speaks both languages and admits to one

npcs.name: Vidar Engel
npcs.info:
The captain commanding the Ishval garrison, a lean, grey-eyed officer who drills his men at dawn on the sand square and rides patrol himself twice a week. He keeps his uniform immaculate and his opinions to himself.

**Speaking Style:** Short, flat and final; an officer who gives an order once and walks away from it.
**Combat Role:** a veteran officer with sabre and revolver; cool, quick and willing to wait for the right shot
**Relationship Hook:** A lean captain watching his men drill on a sand square, hands clasped behind his back.
personality: Core: disciplined and private; drills the men at dawn without fail; never mentions the canyon
Quirk: rides the patrols himself

npcs.name: Viktor Lamm
npcs.info:
The surgeon of the forward dressing station, a major of fifty with blood to the elbows and a cigarette behind each ear. He was a city surgeon in Central once. He works in a dugout lit by lanterns, where a man either lives long enough to reach the railhead or does not.

**Speaking Style:** Hoarse and fast, a surgeon who talks while he cuts and never stops.
**Combat Role:** none; a scalpel and a dugout full of orderlies
**Relationship Hook:** A blood-spattered surgeon working by lantern light in a timbered dugout.
personality: Core: fast and foul-mouthed; smokes two at once; never sleeps
Quirk: treats any wounded man, whatever coat

npcs.name: Viktor Strebe
npcs.info:
The chute man at the screens, who opens and closes the wooden gates that pour the sorted coal into the wagons. He keeps an eye on the picker boys because nobody else does, and he has taught every one of them where not to put their hands.

**Speaking Style:** Calm and practical, a chute man who explains everything twice so the boys hear.
**Combat Role:** none; a gate lever and a pair of quick hands
**Relationship Hook:** A chute man on a timber walkway looking down at the picker boys with worry in his face.
personality: Core: explains things twice; afraid for his own job
Quirk: protective of the boys

npcs.name: Vinzenz Ruhl
npcs.info:
A sergeant in the reserve trenches who runs a card game in the rest dugouts every night. He is fat for a front-line soldier, generous with tobacco and always smiling. Half the company owes him something, and most of them like him anyway.

**Speaking Style:** Friendly and greasy, a sergeant who calls everyone 'friend' and means 'debtor'.
**Combat Role:** a trench knife and a soldier's dirty tricks; he fights only when he is sure to win
**Relationship Hook:** A fat sergeant grinning as he deals cards on an upturned crate in a candlelit dugout.
personality: Core: friendly and greedy; calls everyone 'friend'; keeps the books in his head
Quirk: never takes his own patrol

npcs.name: Volker Grabe
npcs.info:
The lieutenant's chief collector, a sergeant built like a coal wagon who walks the rounds with two privates and a notebook. He drinks in the tavern and never pays, eats at the bakehouse and never pays, and the town calls him the levy on legs.

**Speaking Style:** A parade-ground bark used on civilians, flat and heavy as a rifle butt.
**Combat Role:** rifle butt and boots, close and brutal, a front-line soldier's way
**Relationship Hook:** A huge sergeant ticking names in a notebook in a dusty square while miners glare from doorways.
personality: Core: bullies by habit; never pays for food; hates his officer and obeys him; drinks to stop remembering the war
Quirk: respects anyone who stands up to him

npcs.name: Volker Strand
npcs.info:
The builder who put the station quarter back up in brick after 1907 and now owns half the terrace he built. He is a big, cheerful man in a good suit with plaster under his nails, and he tells anyone who will listen that Resembool wants more brick and less stone. He rents the shops below and the flats above, and collects in person.

**Speaking Style:** Easy and salesmanlike, a builder who makes every question sound like a business opening.
**Combat Role:** a builder's fists and a bricklayer's trowel, more brawl than skill
**Relationship Hook:** A big builder in a tight suit rapping his knuckles on a new brick wall, grinning.
personality: Core: cheerful and pushy; calls brick the future; collects the rent himself and stays for tea
Quirk: knocks on walls to prove them sound

npcs.name: Volkmar Dauber
npcs.info:
The district's wheelwright, a broad, loud man who with his two sons builds every cart wheel that rolls between Resembool and the coach road. He heats the iron tyres in a ring of fire and shrinks them on with buckets of river water in clouds of steam, roaring orders the whole time. He believes in oak, iron and horses, and in nothing that runs on petrol.

**Speaking Style:** Booming and practical, a wheelwright who gives orders to wood and sons alike.
**Combat Role:** a wheelwright's sledge and a spoke used as a club; big and blunt
**Relationship Hook:** A red-faced wheelwright roaring through steam as a hot tyre hisses onto a wheel.
personality: Core: loud and practical; distrusts engines; judges a man by his cart wheels
Quirk: roars at his sons and boasts of them to others

npcs.name: Walburga Kuhn
npcs.info:
The brewer of Fir Hill Brewery, a widow who runs her husband's brewery better than he ever did and brews the dark beer every tavern in the north pours. She is generous, shrewd and never seen without a tasting cup.

**Speaking Style:** Rich and laughing, a brewer whose voice carries the smell of malt.
**Combat Role:** none; a mallet for barrel hoops and a cellar door that locks
**Relationship Hook:** A plump brewer raising a tasting cup beside a gleaming copper kettle.
personality: Core: generous and shrewd; always has a tasting cup; remembers her husband fondly and his debts less so
Quirk: pays her men on time

npcs.name: Waldemar Saalfeld
npcs.info:
The captain who heads the fort's research and development shop, a precise grey man with a slide rule in his breast pocket and drawings rolled under each arm. Six winters have gone into turning steel plate, a field gun and a tractor engine into the machine on the assembly floor, and he talks about it the way other men talk about their children.

**Speaking Style:** Measured and exact, every number given to the decimal; he warms only when the talk turns to steel.
**Combat Role:** an engineer officer who fights with what the shop holds; a pistol, a pry bar, and a hoist chain dropped at the right moment
**Relationship Hook:** A grey captain in spectacles bent over a drawing table, slide rule in hand, while a turret hangs from a hoist beyond the glass.
personality: Core: measures twice and argues once; trusts figures before rank; turns almost gentle when a welder asks a good question; never lets a visitor past the middle of the hall
Quirk: corrects a drawing while talking about something else

npcs.name: Walpurga Brenneisen
npcs.info:
A charcoal burner who has tended the smoking mounds in Ashgrove Wood since her husband died in one, a tall, black-handed woman of fifty with an axe on her hip and a dog that never barks. She sells her charcoal to the gunsmiths and the forges in the city and does not like the officers who come out to shoot the boar, or their beaters.

**Speaking Style:** Flat and smoky; she says the least that will do and lets you guess the rest.
**Combat Role:** a tall woman with a felling axe and a lifetime of swinging it; one blow, well placed
**Relationship Hook:** A tall soot-smudged woman with an axe watching a column of smoke rise from a charcoal mound in a clearing.
personality: Core: dry, hard and unexpectedly kind; never lets a fire go untended; says nothing to anyone in a uniform
Quirk: watches the smoke before she watches people

npcs.name: Walther Imhof
npcs.info:
The caretaker of the army's cemetery, a heavy old private with a limp who hauls water from the railhead in a hand cart to keep a strip of grass alive between the markers. He keeps the book on a shelf in the lodge and dusts it daily.

**Speaking Style:** Slow and deep, a caretaker's patient voice; he reads names as if introducing them.
**Combat Role:** an old soldier with a rifle and a bad leg; he holds a doorway and no more
**Relationship Hook:** An old caretaker hauling a water cart between ranks of white markers under a half-mast flag.
personality: Core: patient and honest; waters the grass at the same hour every day; salutes the half-mast flag at dawn with nobody watching
Quirk: cannot lie to a widow

npcs.name: Wei Shunde
npcs.info:
A Xingese tea merchant kept waiting at the barrier with a string of tea-laden camels outside. He sits on a bench in the records room with his hands folded and asks politely, every hour, whether there is news.

**Speaking Style:** Formal and patient, an old trader whose courtesy gets thinner each day.
**Combat Role:** none; an old merchant who sits still and outlasts
**Relationship Hook:** An old Xingese merchant sitting very straight on a bench with his papers on his knees.
personality: Core: courteous and immovable; asks for news every hour; refuses to pay a bribe
Quirk: keeps his papers in silk

npcs.name: Wen Qiaoyun
npcs.info:
A healer of the warm-spring valley, who lays the sick on mats by the pools and works the earth's flow through them with her hands in the water. She came to the valley to train for a season and has stayed nine years.

**Speaking Style:** Soothing and unhurried, a voice made for patients lying in warm water.
**Combat Role:** a healer; she fights only to reach a patient, with a staff and a calm that unsettles attackers
**Relationship Hook:** A healer kneeling at a steaming pool with her hands in the water and a patient lying on a mat beside her.
personality: Core: keeps her hands in water when she talks; stays calm in every crisis but money; argues with the farmers politely and loses
Quirk: names each pool as if it were a patient

npcs.name: Wen Shaoqi
npcs.info:
A Xingese silk and tea merchant who came north the long way with an Amestrian pass and two trunks, and has waited two days at the customs counter for a stamp. She spends the time drinking the hall's dreadful tea and making the clerks laugh.

**Speaking Style:** Light, amused and unhurried, each compliment carrying a small hook.
**Combat Role:** a merchant who travels alone; a weighted fan, a hairpin blade and a fast way out
**Relationship Hook:** A Xingese merchant fanning herself beside two lacquered trunks, smiling at a clerk who has not stamped her pass.
personality: Core: laughs easily and watches everything; offers tea from her own stock to anyone kind; never sits with her back to her trunks
Quirk: bargains even when she has no need to

npcs.name: Wendel Asch
npcs.info:
The name over the tannery's army contract, a soft-handed man in a good coat who visits the lime pits once a week and holds a scented handkerchief to his nose. He is charming to inspectors and sends cakes to the depot clerks at the year's end.

**Speaking Style:** Oily and apologetic, a man who agrees with you before you finish and means none of it.
**Combat Role:** none; he runs, and if cornered he offers money
**Relationship Hook:** A soft-faced man in a good coat holding a handkerchief to his nose beside steaming lime pits.
personality: Core: agrees with everyone; holds a handkerchief to his face at the pits; panics quietly and then smiles
Quirk: would sell his brother-in-law in a moment if it came to it

npcs.name: Wendel Fosse
npcs.info:
The railhead clerk, a stooped old private past his service years who was kept on because nobody else could read his filing. He checks the weekly supply train off the ramp with a pencil behind his ear and a box of forms on a stool.

**Speaking Style:** Fussy and mild, an old clerk's precise little voice that apologises for the facts.
**Combat Role:** none; an old clerk who drops flat and waits
**Relationship Hook:** An old clerk on a loading ramp, a clipboard in his hand and a battered box at his feet.
personality: Core: fussy and decent; files everything twice; talks to the empty ramp between trains
Quirk: keeps the second box under his own stool

npcs.name: Wendel Harrow
npcs.info:
The deputy of the shift at Mine Number Eight, the man who goes down first with the safety lamp and comes up last with the tally. He is broad, bald under his cap and fast with his fists, and the young men on his crew would follow him into a fire.

**Speaking Style:** Short words, loud in the dark, a deputy who gives orders as if each one costs him.
**Combat Role:** a pick handle and a brawler's head-down rush, learned in pit-yard fights
**Relationship Hook:** A shift deputy holding up a brass lamp in a low gallery while the timbers creak overhead.
personality: Core: blunt and fast to decide; counts his men under his breath; trusts timber more than paper; loses his temper and apologises after
Quirk: will not leave a man below

npcs.name: Wendel Pruett
npcs.info:
The head porter at Rush Valley Station, a broad, red-faced man in a railway cap two sizes too small, who has carried bags off the southern trains since the town was three workshops and a well. He can tell which arriving passenger has a steel leg by the sound of the step before he turns round, and he greets every one of them like a cousin.

**Speaking Style:** Hearty and familiar, a porter who calls strangers cousin and keeps one ear on the next whistle.
**Combat Role:** a heavy porter; a loaded trolley rammed into a crowd and a grip that lifts a man by his belt
**Relationship Hook:** A red-faced porter heaving a trunk off a train and calling a stranger with a steel leg his cousin.
personality: Core: calls every stranger cousin; listens to footsteps before he looks at faces; takes a tip with a wink and a bribe with a straight face
Quirk: loses his temper only with the booking clerk

npcs.name: Wendel Strauch
npcs.info:
A chainman from the military survey who walked away from his post with a canteen and a bag of brass pegs and now lives in the shade of the dry canal. He has walked its length twice. He still wears his uniform and salutes passing camels by habit.

**Speaking Style:** Plain and anxious, a farm boy's voice that keeps asking if you see it too.
**Combat Role:** a private with a rifle and a bayonet, steady only when cornered
**Relationship Hook:** A gangly soldier in a dirty uniform hammering a brass peg into the floor of a wide dry trench.
personality: Core: nervous and honest; sets out pegs in neat rows; talks to himself about angles
Quirk: salutes by habit

npcs.name: Wendelin Asch
npcs.info:
The owner of the Northern Foundry, which casts stove plates, rail chairs and, under contract, shell casings for the army. He is grey and weary and keeps to the pattern loft, where the wooden patterns for every casting hang like ghosts.

**Speaking Style:** Weary and correct, an owner who speaks in a soft voice and never meets your eye.
**Combat Role:** none; a foundry full of molten iron and men who would follow him into it
**Relationship Hook:** A grey owner in a loft of hanging wooden patterns, holding one up to the furnace glow below.
personality: Core: weary and correct; keeps to the pattern loft; never meets anyone's eye
Quirk: pays his men's doctors' bills

npcs.name: Wendelin Rau
npcs.info:
The hermit of the tarn is a gaunt, silent fisherman who has lived in a turf hut on the black shore for years. He nets trout in the snowmelt, trades fish with the goatherds and turns away anyone who asks him where he came from.

**Speaking Style:** Slow and hoarse from disuse, a hermit who speaks as if remembering how.
**Combat Role:** an old infantry soldier; he still handles a rifle like a drill sergeant and still hates to
**Relationship Hook:** A gaunt bearded hermit in a faded army greatcoat standing by a black mountain lake, nets over his shoulder.
personality: Core: silent unless pressed; never lights a fire by day; trades fish and never takes coin
Quirk: wakes shouting and goes back to sleep

npcs.name: Wenzel Hader
npcs.info:
An old farmer who has come back to his house in the ceded strip after two years away, and refuses to leave. His farm is a shell, his fields are full of craters and the boundary stone he grew up beside is gone. He is mule-stubborn, half deaf and quite unafraid.

**Speaking Style:** Cracked and stubborn, an old farmer who argues with the army as if it were a bad neighbour.
**Combat Role:** an old shotgun he has no cartridges for
**Relationship Hook:** An old farmer sitting on the step of his ruined farmhouse, a folded deed in his lap and a patrol in front of him.
personality: Core: half deaf when it suits him; unafraid of either army
Quirk: mule-stubborn

npcs.name: Wenzel Stahl
npcs.info:
The night foreman at the tram depot, a long-boned man in a peaked cap who signs the cars in when the last ones come home and signs them out again before dawn. He has worked the trams since they ran behind horses, and he can name every car in the shed by the squeal of its brakes. Drivers say he is fair, slow to anger and impossible to hurry.

**Speaking Style:** Unhurried and low, a night man's voice that never rises above the hum of the shed.
**Combat Role:** none worth the name; a big quiet man with a switch iron and the dark of the shed on his side
**Relationship Hook:** A tall old foreman in a peaked cap, rubbing out a line in his night book as a dark tramcar rolls past the window.
personality: Core: patient and dry; knows every car by its sound; keeps his book in pencil so he can rub it out
Quirk: feels responsible for anyone in his shed

npcs.name: Wiebke Brahm
npcs.info:
A lance corporal who leads the wiring party in the fields before Fotset, a small, hard, silent woman who goes out every night with cutters and coils to mend the belt the shells tore up by day. She has been out more nights than anyone alive on that stretch of line.

**Speaking Style:** Flat and whispered, the voice of someone who has spent two years talking only in no man's land.
**Combat Role:** wire cutters, a revolver and a knife; she fights flat in the mud and close
**Relationship Hook:** A small mud-caked soldier crouching among coils of barbed wire at night with cutters in her hand.
personality: Core: silent and hard; counts nights, not days
Quirk: trusts the enemy's wiring party more than her own officers

npcs.name: Wiebke Kohler
npcs.info:
The matriarch of the charcoal-burning family in the pinewood clearing, black to the elbows, with a pipe in her teeth and a mound that has not gone out in nine years. Her sons cut the wood, her daughters stack it, and she decides everything.

**Speaking Style:** Rough and sing-song, an old burner who mutters charms over her mound and curses in the same breath.
**Combat Role:** a charcoal rake and a family that comes running
**Relationship Hook:** An old charcoal burner with a clay pipe watching a soldier come up the track through the smoke.
personality: Core: shrewd and superstitious; trusts coin more than kin; fierce for her family
Quirk: smokes a pipe constantly

npcs.name: Wigand Hartwig
npcs.info:
The proprietor of the alchemists' shop off the library road, a small, neat old man in a velvet skullcap who weighs everything twice on brass scales. He has sold chalk to three generations of State Alchemists and talks about them as if they were his pupils. He is fussy, kind to students and frightened of nothing but damp.

**Speaking Style:** Dry and precise, an old shopkeeper who pronounces every element in full.
**Combat Role:** none; an old man whose shop is full of things that burn, and who knows which ones
**Relationship Hook:** A neat old shopkeeper weighing white powder on brass scales, peering over his spectacles at a small customer.
personality: Core: fussy, kind and precise; knows every State Alchemist's handwriting; frightened of officers but polite to them
Quirk: gives students the broken chalk for nothing

npcs.name: Wigand Hoss
npcs.info:
The jailer of the stockade, an old sergeant who has kept the keys of the iron corridor longer than most of his prisoners have been alive. He warms his hands at the brazier, reads the same three books in turn and knows each prisoner's breakfast.

**Speaking Style:** Slow and grandfatherly, the voice of a man who has said goodnight to every kind of prisoner.
**Combat Role:** an old jailer's economy; a ring of keys swung like a flail, a shoulder into a door, and a truncheon kept for wrists
**Relationship Hook:** An old jailer warming his hands over a brazier, a ring of keys the size of a dinner plate at his hip.
personality: Core: speaks to prisoners as lodgers rather than criminals; keeps a draughts board on the brazier chair; rereads the same three books in turn
Quirk: never hurries a key in a lock

npcs.name: Wigbert Hale
npcs.info:
An old shepherd who has run a flock on the downs for fifty years and still walks the skyline every day with a crook taller than himself. He knows every dew pond, every hawk's nest and every wind that brings rain, and speaks in weather sayings he mostly contradicts. Half the town's children have been sent up to him for a summer to learn the work.

**Speaking Style:** Wandering and wry, an old shepherd who talks in sayings and then contradicts them.
**Combat Role:** an old shepherd's crook and a sling he has used on foxes for fifty years
**Relationship Hook:** An old shepherd leaning on a tall crook beside a dew pond, squinting at the weather.
personality: Core: wry and wandering; never hurries a flock or a story; teaches any child who climbs the hill
Quirk: speaks in weather sayings

npcs.name: Willem Pfeil
npcs.info:
A corporal who leads the parties that go into the crater field under truce flags to fetch the dead. He has done it more often than any man on the front, and both sides know his face and his white flag.

**Speaking Style:** Quick and bright, a corporal who talks fast to keep himself from thinking.
**Combat Role:** a rifleman who would rather not; quick, scrappy and good at getting out of a crater fast
**Relationship Hook:** A wiry ginger corporal waving a white truce flag over a cratered field of wire.
personality: Core: talks constantly on the way out and never on the way back; keeps his truce flag cleaner than his rifle; respects the Cretans more than he lets on
Quirk: superstitious about the number thirteen

npcs.name: Wilm Graf
npcs.info:
The keeper of the capital's old arsenal, a quartermaster sergeant who signs for every crate that comes in or goes out. He knows the count of every rifle and shell in the building to the last round. He is suspicious, honest and rude to officers who try to skip his forms.

**Speaking Style:** Clipped and suspicious, a quartermaster who reads each request twice before he answers.
**Combat Role:** an old soldier with a pistol and a locked door between him and a thief
**Relationship Hook:** A quartermaster sergeant checking a book against a stack of crates.
personality: Core: suspicious and honest; lives by his forms; rude to impatient officers
Quirk: counts everything twice

npcs.name: Wilm Treacher
npcs.info:
The lamp keeper, a lame old collier who lost a foot in a fall and was given the lamp room instead of a pension. He polishes every glass, trims every wick and counts the brass tokens on their hooks at the end of every shift. Nobody comes up the shaft without passing him.

**Speaking Style:** Soft and deliberate, an old man who says each miner's name as if it were a prayer.
**Combat Role:** none; a crutch and an old man's stubbornness
**Relationship Hook:** An old lamp keeper staring at three brass tokens still hanging on a board at dusk.
personality: Core: gentle and exact; knows every token by its dents
Quirk: carries a guilt he cannot set down

npcs.name: Wilma Strass
npcs.info:
The drill sergeant of the southern depot, a lean, scarred woman who has turned ten years of farm boys into soldiers. She served two tours at Fotset before a shell splinter took two fingers from her left hand. She drills the recruits hard because she has buried the ones other sergeants drilled softly.

**Speaking Style:** A parade-ground voice like a rifle crack, never louder than it needs to be to reach the back rank.
**Combat Role:** bayonet drill turned into a weapon; she fights close, fast and without wasted motion
**Relationship Hook:** A scarred drill sergeant in a peaked cap watching a line of recruits on a dusty parade ground.
personality: Core: hard on the square and gentle behind the stores; speaks of Fotset only as 'down there'; keeps the names of every recruit she lost
Quirk: notices a loose bootlace at forty paces

npcs.name: Wilma Stroh
npcs.info:
A girl of fifteen from a beet farm on the plain, who taught herself alchemy from a book bought off a pedlar and drew her first working circle on a flour sack. She has come to the registry to ask whether what she does is legal, with the sack folded under her arm.

**Speaking Style:** Quick and bright, a farm girl rushing her words, delighted and frightened by her own questions.
**Combat Role:** no training; she can raise a wall of packed earth out of the ground and hide behind it
**Relationship Hook:** A freckled farm girl clutching a flour sack marked with a circle, standing alone on a slate floor.
personality: Core: talks fast when nervous, which is always; draws circles in anything: flour, dust, frost; proud and terrified in equal measure
Quirk: keeps secrets from her father and feels bad about every one

npcs.name: Wilmar Penrose
npcs.info:
The last clerk of the mining company, a stooped, ink-stained man who never left Baschool when the mine closed and keeps the store's back office as if the owners might come back. He sleeps on the counter and reads the books by candlelight.

**Speaking Style:** Thin and apologetic, a clerk's careful voice gone hoarse from talking to nobody.
**Combat Role:** an old clerk who hides; a locked safe, a back door and a candle snuffed
**Relationship Hook:** A stooped old clerk reading a dusty book by candlelight in an empty, boarded company store.
personality: Core: dusts the shelves of an empty shop; calls every visitor a customer; keeps the till locked though it holds only scrip
Quirk: cannot look a miner's child in the eye

npcs.name: Wim Doberstein
npcs.info:
A gangly lad of fourteen who runs errands for the alchemists' supply shop and earns extra coin cutting the grass at the Tucker place. He comes twice a week with a pair of shears too big for him, and Nina will not let him start until he has thrown the ball for the dog a dozen times. He thinks Shou Tucker the cleverest man in the east because nobody has ever told him otherwise.

**Speaking Style:** Eager and breathless, a boy who says 'sir' twice in every sentence and forgets to finish half of them.
**Combat Role:** none; quick feet and a pair of garden shears he would drop before he swung them
**Relationship Hook:** A freckled boy with shears too big for him being knocked flat on a lawn by a huge white dog while a little girl laughs.
personality: Core: chatters when nervous and is nervous most of the time; loves the white dog more than his own family's; lies badly and blushes when he does
Quirk: will not walk past the side of the house where the cellar grating is

npcs.name: Winry Rockbell
npcs.info:
An automail engineer of fifteen who learned her craft in her grandmother's workshop in Resembool, and whose best work walks around on a childhood friend's arm and leg. She is bossy, warm and practical, tells the brothers off for every broken joint, and falls in love with any well-made machine she sees. She grew up with Ed and Al as family and waits for them to come home. A wrench is never far from her hand, and she will throw it at Ed's head.

**Speaking Style:** Bright, bossy and warm; she scolds the brothers like a sister, laughs at her own temper and goes breathless with delight over a new machine.
**Combat Role:** none worth the name; a thrown wrench and a mechanic's toolkit
**Relationship Hook:** A girl with a wrench at a workshop door, arms crossed, waiting for a boy who broke his arm again.
personality: Core: bossy, fierce and practical; she lectures before she hugs; cries in private, and for other people; goes starry-eyed over good machinery
Quirk: carries a wrench and throws it

npcs.name: Xie Ruhua
npcs.info:
Head servant of the House of Foreign Guests, a calm woman of fifty who runs its kitchen, its linen and its silences. Guests find her endlessly helpful, and she finds guests endlessly interesting.

**Speaking Style:** Smooth, quiet and attentive, a head servant's voice that only ever seems to agree.
**Combat Role:** none; she knows the house's every passage and which door locks from the outside
**Relationship Hook:** A head servant standing very still in a narrow passage, one ear turned towards a thin wall.
personality: Core: agrees with everyone and promises nothing; knows every board in the corridor that creaks; edits her reports with a kind heart
Quirk: prefers foreign guests to court ones

npcs.name: Xun Baizhi
npcs.info:
A master of the Hall of Purification Arts, tall and austere, who teaches the third-year students to read the earth's flow through a sick body. She sets her own five knives at the points of the star without looking and has never been seen to miss a point.

**Speaking Style:** Low and deliberate, a teacher who lets silence do half the correcting.
**Combat Role:** a master alkahestrist; five kunai thrown into a star around her opponent, and the ground of that star turned against him
**Relationship Hook:** A tall master raising one eyebrow at a kneeling student whose brass star has gone dark.
personality: Core: corrects with silence and a raised eyebrow; sets her knives without looking; treats every patient the same, prince or porter
Quirk: keeps a list of students the clans have asked for, and burns it monthly

npcs.name: Yakov Belling
npcs.info:
The trader at the pelt post, a dark-eyed man of mixed Amestrian and Drachman blood who grades each pelt with his thumb and a look, and whose grades are final. He sells traps, powder, coffee and advice, and only the advice comes cheap.

**Speaking Style:** Smooth and dark, with a faint Drachman lilt he lets grow stronger when he is bargaining.
**Combat Role:** a trader with a shotgun under the counter and a skinning knife in his boot
**Relationship Hook:** A dark-eyed trader running his thumb through a pelt on the counter, already naming its grade.
personality: Core: grades a pelt with his thumb before his eyes; talks to his coffee pot in Drachman; never haggles twice
Quirk: likes a good liar better than a bad honest man

npcs.name: Yakovlev
npcs.info:
An officer of the internal affairs office at Central Command, a bespectacled, silent man who carries orders from the top and watches the officers who receive them.

**Speaking Style:** Quiet, flat and bureaucratic, an internal affairs man who reads orders aloud without inflection.
**Combat Role:** a sidearm and the authority of internal affairs
**Relationship Hook:** A bespectacled internal affairs officer standing silent behind the Führer's secretary.
personality: Core: quiet and flat; carries orders from the top; gives nothing away
Quirk: watches everyone

npcs.name: Yan Shoude
npcs.info:
Chief physician to the Emperor, an old alkahestrist who has kept the imperial pulse for thirty years. Small, white-bearded and unfailingly courteous, he has the steadiest hands in the palace.

**Speaking Style:** Dry and patient, an old physician's voice that never hurries a diagnosis or a lie.
**Combat Role:** an old alkahestrist; five kunai from his sleeve and the earth's flow turned through an attacker's legs, buying time rather than winning
**Relationship Hook:** An old physician holding a jar up to the light and counting the shelves again with his lips moving.
personality: Core: calls the Emperor only the patient; washes his hands before and after every conversation; tells the truth to the brazier and a softer one to the court
Quirk: trusts no colleague and is polite to every one of them

npcs.name: Yanka
npcs.info:
A mill worker in North City's grain mill quarter, who runs the mill's yard and keeps the stores of bread for the town. She is tired, warm and practical, and she feeds the mill's men and the garrison's extra crew. She knows every sack in the warehouse.

**Speaking Style:** Tired and warm, a worker who talks about bread and mills as if they were the only things that matter.
**Combat Role:** none; a sack hook and a strong back
**Relationship Hook:** A woman in a mill yard carrying a flour sack beside a stack of grain.
personality: Core: tired, warm and practical; feeds the mill's men; knows every sack
Quirk: writes spoiled sacks that are not spoiled

npcs.name: Yao Clan Steward
npcs.info:
The steward of the Yao clan's estate in the Xing capital, who keeps the gatehouse, the clan's accounts and its visitors. He is courteous, careful and exact, and he decides who may see the clan's head. He is loyal to the clan and suspicious of outsiders.

**Speaking Style:** Measured and courteous, a steward who speaks for the clan and never for himself.
**Combat Role:** none; a book and a gate key
**Relationship Hook:** A clan steward at a gatehouse, checking a visitor's name against a list.
personality: Core: courteous, careful and exact; decides who sees the clan head; loyal and suspicious of outsiders
Quirk: keeps a price for every favour

npcs.name: Yaqub Sennar
npcs.info:
An old priest with a chisel, a mallet and a tremor in one hand, who recarves the scripture the war chipped from the temple walls, one line a week, from memory. He works on a ladder in the ring of light and stops when the light moves on.

**Speaking Style:** Deep and unhurried; he recites rather than speaks, and every pause has weight.
**Combat Role:** an old warrior priest's guard; he turns blows aside and waits for his opponent to tire
**Relationship Hook:** An old priest on a ladder cutting a line of scripture into a curved wall in a shaft of sunlight.
personality: Core: devout and doubtful; carves only in daylight; recites each line aloud before he cuts it
Quirk: forgives slights before they are finished

npcs.name: Yara
npcs.info:
An Ishvalan woman who sells cloth in Reole's market hall, one of the few of her people allowed to trade in the Amestrian town. She keeps her prices low and her counter tidy, and she knows every weave of the desert. She is patient, wary and watchful of the church's men.

**Speaking Style:** Quiet and careful, a trader who speaks low because the wrong ears listen in the market.
**Combat Role:** none; she trades and keeps her head down
**Relationship Hook:** A cloth trader at her stall, counting coins while the church's men walk past.
personality: Core: patient and wary; gives fair prices and expects the same; watches the church's men without looking at them
Quirk: remembers every debt

npcs.name: Yevgeni Skorin
npcs.info:
A Drachman ski scout who crosses the snow below the wall by night in a white smock and stops each time a rifle shot short of the wire. He is young, fast and proud of it, and he leaves his tracks in plain sight because he wants the fort to know he was there.

**Speaking Style:** Bright and boastful under a heavy northern accent, laughing between breaths.
**Combat Role:** a ski scout; a carbine on his back, a knife in his boot, and the speed to be gone before the first flare lands
**Relationship Hook:** A young scout in a white smock crouched on skis in the dark snow, grinning up at the wall.
personality: Core: boasts in two languages; leaves tracks in plain sight on purpose; counts paces under his breath
Quirk: hums village songs on the long climb home

npcs.name: Yin Xiaoyu
npcs.info:
A fisher girl of twelve with three cormorants of her own, which she raised from eggs and which follow her about the bank like dogs. She works the river at night with her uncle and knows every boat that moves without lights.

**Speaking Style:** Light and quick, a fisher girl who chatters to birds and goes shy with people.
**Combat Role:** none; three cormorants that go for a stranger's eyes when she whistles
**Relationship Hook:** A small fisher girl on the riverbank with a cormorant on her arm, one hand tucked into her sleeve.
personality: Core: chatters to her birds, shy with people; names every bird after a star; brave on the water and timid on land
Quirk: keeps secrets badly

npcs.name: Yoki
npcs.info:
A first lieutenant with a pencil moustache who owns the coal mine at Youswell and squeezes the miners for every coin, cutting wages and raising taxes while he lives in a walled estate with bodyguards. He bribes his way up and bullies his way down, and he believes any man with a State Alchemist's watch can be bought.

**Speaking Style:** Oily, pompous and whiny, a petty officer who bullies down and grovels up, then squeals when it goes wrong.
**Combat Role:** none worth the name; bodyguards, bribes and, much later, a stolen car
**Relationship Hook:** A smug officer with a pencil moustache announcing another wage cut to a room of coal miners.
personality: Core: pompous, greedy and petty; grovels to anyone above him; bullies anyone below him
Quirk: always thinks he is the hero of the story

npcs.name: Yue Hongxiu
npcs.info:
The leading lady of the capital's opera, famous for the faithful consort in the season's piece. Off the stage she is sharp-tongued, quick and fiercely protective of her troupe.

**Speaking Style:** Clear and carrying, an opera singer's voice that cannot quite speak quietly.
**Combat Role:** an opera fighter; acrobatic stage swordplay with a real edge on it, tumbling out of reach
**Relationship Hook:** An opera actress in half her paint turning from the mirror with a teapot lid in her hand.
personality: Core: sharp-tongued off the stage and gentle on it; checks every costume lining herself; protective of the troupe's youngest
Quirk: superstitious about whistling in the dressing room

npcs.name: Yuriy Rockbell
npcs.info:
A surgeon from Resembool, Pinako Rockbell's son and Winry Rockbell's father, who works beside his wife Sarah in a field clinic in the Ishval war. He is gentle and practical, and he will not turn away a patient from either side. The Ishvalans and the Amestrians alike owe their lives to the pair.

**Speaking Style:** Soft-spoken and patient, a doctor with a tired laugh who never stops working while he talks.
**Combat Role:** none; a surgeon who puts himself between a patient and danger
**Relationship Hook:** A doctor in round glasses bandaging a wounded man in a ruined square.
personality: Core: gentle, tired and practical; keeps his wife's spirits up with bad jokes; talks about Resembool to calm patients
Quirk: never refuses a patient

npcs.name: Yusuf Daramy
npcs.info:
The man who runs the coffee stall by the weighing post, where deals are sealed with a cup and a handshake. He has a brass pot that never cools and a memory for every herder's name, price and grudge.

**Speaking Style:** Easy, quick and teasing; he pours coffee and gossip in the same breath.
**Combat Role:** none; a fast talker who throws hot coffee and runs
**Relationship Hook:** A coffee seller pouring from a long brass pot over a deal being shaken on.
personality: Core: gregarious and discreet; remembers every deal ever sealed at his stall; never closes the stall
Quirk: teases the soldiers until they laugh

npcs.name: Yuwen Tie
npcs.info:
The hermit at the top of the cloud stair, an old warrior who served in the Emperor's own guard and left in disgrace. He lives in a bare stone room with one mat and one bowl, and young warriors climb thousands of steps to sit on his stair and ask him to teach them.

**Speaking Style:** Slow, deep and rare, a voice that speaks once in a day and means it.
**Combat Role:** a royal guard master; unarmed, he moves on a narrow stair like water, and anyone who comes up it comes down faster
**Relationship Hook:** An old hermit standing barefoot in a bare stone room, looking down into the mist at a figure on the stair.
personality: Core: speaks once a day and means it; eats from one bowl and sleeps on one mat; tests students by ignoring them
Quirk: has not forgotten one face from the palace

npcs.name: Zahra Imsel
npcs.info:
The Ishvalan woman who runs the soup kitchen's great pot, tall, quick and red-eyed, serving the queue twice a day and remembering every child's name. She married the town's station master, which half the slum forgives and half does not.

**Speaking Style:** Warm and brisk, scolding and laughing in the same breath over the steam of the pot.
**Combat Role:** a cook who knows the slum's alleys; a ladle, a pot of boiling soup, and a cry that brings the whole lane
**Relationship Hook:** A tall Ishvalan woman ladling soup into an endless line of bowls, smiling at a child.
personality: Core: remembers every child's name; ladles with one hand and scolds with the other; guards the curtain to the elders' corner
Quirk: murmurs the old prayers at the stove

npcs.name: Zainab Hourani
npcs.info:
An old Ishvalan woman who walks out from the refugee camp once a year and knots white cloths onto the bare wooden frame where the Rockbell doctors had their awning. She stays a day, sweeps the ground under the frame and walks back.

**Speaking Style:** Slow and plain; an old woman who says a thing once and expects it remembered.
**Combat Role:** none; an old woman with a walking stick who simply will not leave
**Relationship Hook:** An old woman tying a white cloth to the bare frame of a ruined field clinic.
personality: Core: grateful and stern; ties a cloth for every life the doctors saved; will not hear the doctors spoken ill of
Quirk: sweeps the ground where the cots stood

npcs.name: Zampano
npcs.info:
A solid man in his late thirties, an army operative with a straight face and a good line in lies, who turns when he needs to into a boar-like beast with quills on his back that he can fire. He is brave, sensible and ashamed of what he has become. He has a son he will not go home to.

**Speaking Style:** Level-headed and measured, a man who can lie with a straight face and enjoys doing it.
**Combat Role:** a boar-like chimera form with quills he shoots from his back
**Relationship Hook:** A heavy-set man in an army coat lying smoothly to a sentry.
personality: Core: level-headed and brave; ashamed of his body; fights for what he thinks is right
Quirk: a good actor who enjoys a lie

npcs.name: Zhai Yanbo
npcs.info:
Boss of a drilling crew in the brine field, a hard-handed woman who took over her husband's crew when the gas well burned him last winter. She works the treadwheels harder than any of her men and expects them to keep up.

**Speaking Style:** Flat and blunt, a crew boss who says the dangerous thing in the same tone as the dull one.
**Combat Role:** a driller with an iron bit-bar and a crew at her back; she swings once, hard
**Relationship Hook:** A hard-handed crew boss standing under a timber derrick with an iron bar on her shoulder.
personality: Core: says the dangerous thing in a flat voice; works harder than anyone on her crew; never says her husband's name
Quirk: distrusts owners as a matter of faith

npcs.name: Zhuo Heng
npcs.info:
Foreman of the flashpowder works outside the wall, a careful man missing two fingers of his left hand and very proud of the eight that remain. He mixes the Yao clan's smoke, flash and pepper charges himself and lets nobody else touch the strongest batches.

**Speaking Style:** Low and even, never above a murmur in the sheds, where a raised voice is a careless voice.
**Combat Role:** a powder man; a pouch of pepper charges and the nerve to throw them close, then a long knife for whoever is still standing
**Relationship Hook:** A foreman with two fingers missing stirring a basin of powder with a wooden spoon, his mask pulled down to speak.
personality: Core: counts his fingers when he is nervous; speaks in the sheds as if in a temple; trusts powder more than people
Quirk: loyal to the Yao clan without loving it

npcs.name: Ziyad Karun
npcs.info:
A lanky, silent Ishvalan who carries the camp's only rifle, an old single-shot with a cracked stock, and hunts the gazelles that come to the stepwell. He follows Faris Nadeem out of friendship more than conviction and is the better shot of the two by far.

**Speaking Style:** Says almost nothing, and what he says is short; a pause before every answer.
**Combat Role:** a patient rifleman; one careful shot from cover and then he moves
**Relationship Hook:** A lanky young man crouched on a fallen column with an old rifle across his knees.
personality: Core: silent and steady; follows his friend against his own judgement; never wastes a shot
Quirk: brings meat to the old ones first

npcs.name: Zora Halek
npcs.info:
The mule-train boss of the gully road is a Cretan woman of thirty-five who has run goods through the thornbush for fifteen years. She knows every patrol on both sides by name and has never lost a mule, though she has lost several partners.

**Speaking Style:** Smooth and amused, a smuggler who speaks both languages and flirts in each.
**Combat Role:** a knife fighter and pistol shot who fights in the thornbush where only she knows the paths
**Relationship Hook:** A lean dark-braided smuggler leading a mule down a thorny gully under a darkening sky.
personality: Core: charming and dangerous; keeps promises and keeps receipts; never runs from a storm, only from soldiers
Quirk: treats her mules better than her partners

npcs.name: Zou Bingwen
npcs.info:
An apothecary of the elixir street, a fussy little man with spectacles and a wall of a thousand drawers he can open blindfold. He mixes tonics to his grandfather's recipes and is very sure of them, until this week.

**Speaking Style:** Fussy and precise, an old apothecary's voice weighing each word on a brass scale.
**Combat Role:** none; a drawer of powders that blind and a back door into the alley
**Relationship Hook:** A small apothecary peering over his spectacles at a sealed bottle behind a curtained counter.
personality: Core: opens any drawer blindfold; weighs everything, even words; proud of his grandfather's recipes
Quirk: guilty, and showing it in the way he dusts

npcs.name: Zuhair Aman
npcs.info:
The eldest of the Asbec elders, a frail, white-bearded man with a cane who sits on cushions behind the soup kitchen's curtain and settles the slum's quarrels over glasses of tea. He taught in Ishval before the war and still corrects everyone's grammar.

**Speaking Style:** Thin and dry, a teacher's voice that corrects grammar in the middle of a quarrel.
**Combat Role:** an old man who does not fight; he stands between the quarrel and the knife and dares it
**Relationship Hook:** A frail Ishvalan elder with a white beard pouring tea behind a curtain while two angry men wait.
personality: Core: corrects grammar in the middle of quarrels; pours tea before every judgement; forbids talk of revenge
Quirk: laughs only at his own age

locations.name: Abandoned Mine West
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

A mine in the western hills that closed when its seam ran out, its adit boarded and its heaps grown with grass. The miners' huts are used now by whoever is on the move.

areas.name: Adit Mouth
areas.text: The boarded entrance to the mine, its planks pried loose.

areas.name: Miners' Huts
areas.text: The row of huts where the old miners lived, roofless now.

locations.name: Aerugo
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The principality south of Amestris, a much smaller trading country of rich farmland whose soldiers wear red overcoats. It has been at war with Amestris longer than Creta has and is mostly losing ground; most of its army is tied down holding the line and its towns are tired of fighting.

areas.name: Border Hills
areas.text: The hills of red earth behind the enemy line.

areas.name: Hill Town Gate
areas.text: The gate of the first hill town on the Aerugo side.

locations.name: Aerugo Front Line
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The line where the armies of Amestris and Aerugo face each other across scrub and ruin. Trenches run for miles, and the patrols go out at night and come back in silence.

areas.name: Front Trench
areas.text: The main trench with its duckboards and its sandbag walls.

areas.name: No Man's Scrub
areas.text: The strip of scrub and wire between the two lines.

locations.name: Aerugonian Customs Post
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 13-17 · Danger: Moderate]

The Aerugonian customs post on the road below the pass, once busy with trade and now a guard post with a striped barrier. Its officers still stamp the papers of the few who cross under a flag of truce.

areas.name: Customs Hut
areas.text: A tiled hut of stamps, books and a coffee pot.

areas.name: Striped Barrier
areas.text: The barrier across the road and the sentry beside it.

locations.name: Aerugonian Farmlands
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The rich farmland of Aerugo that begins below the border hills, the country's wealth and its pride. Wheat, olives and fruit run to the horizon, and the farmers watch the north for smoke.

areas.name: Cypress Lane
areas.text: A straight lane between tall cypresses and wheat.

areas.name: Farm Courtyard
areas.text: A walled yard of barns, oxen and dogs.

locations.name: Aerugonian Prisoner Compound
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 11-15 · Danger: Moderate]

A stockade of wire and huts east of the supply road where Aerugonian soldiers taken at the front are held. They wear what is left of their red overcoats and trade buttons for cigarettes through the wire.

areas.name: Compound Wire Gate
areas.text: The guarded gate with its sentry box and its prisoner roll.

areas.name: Prisoner Huts
areas.text: Rows of plank huts with straw mattresses and hand-carved dice.

locations.name: Alchemists' Railhead
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

When the Führer ordered State Alchemists to the front in 1908, they came in by train to this railhead: a spur of track run out into the desert, a ramp and a water tower. It still takes the garrison's supplies once a week.

areas.name: Alchemists' Railhead Ramp
areas.text: A loading ramp of sleepers where wagons are unloaded.

areas.name: Alchemists' Railhead Water Tower
areas.text: A tall tank on legs, its sides pocked with bullet holes.

locations.name: Armstrong Mansion
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The town seat of the Armstrong family, one of the oldest military lines in Amestris: a pillared mansion with a ballroom, a portrait gallery of very large ancestors and five children raised to carry the name. Alex Louis Armstrong was raised here, and Cathrine, the youngest, is the soft-voiced pride of the house.

areas.name: Armstrong Music Room
areas.text: A white room with a grand piano and a harp nobody plays.

areas.name: Armstrong Portrait Gallery
areas.text: A long gallery of gilt frames, every ancestor larger and more moustached than the last.

areas.name: Armstrong Rose Garden
areas.text: Formal beds of roses around a sundial, with a gravel walk wide enough for a duel.

locations.name: Army Rifle Range
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High]

Recruits from the capital's barracks march out here on the heath to learn the rifle, lying in a line on sandbags while a sergeant shouts at them. When the red flag goes up, the shepherds take their flocks to the far side of the ridge and wait.

areas.name: Army Rifle Range Earth Butts
areas.text: High earth banks behind the targets, the markers' trench at their foot.

areas.name: Army Rifle Range Firing Line
areas.text: A row of firing points behind sandbags, with numbers painted on boards.

areas.name: Army Rifle Range Test Shed
areas.text: A windowless shed with a door that locks from outside.

locations.name: Asbec
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

A town near the Briggs range with a slum of Ishvalan refugees on its edge. The slum's shacks are patched with tin, and the town's people go there for cheap labour and avoid it at night.

areas.name: Refugee Slum
areas.text: The shacks and alleys of the slum at the town's edge.

areas.name: Town Square
areas.text: The square of the town, with its well and its market stalls.

locations.name: Asbec Back-Street Hideout
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-16 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A shuttered house on a back street of the slum, lent by an Ishvalan family to people the army is looking for. From the outside it looks like every other house on the lane.

areas.name: Hideout Alley Door
areas.text: The back door onto an alley too narrow for a cart, where a lookout sits on a crate.

areas.name: Hideout Shuttered Room
areas.text: The front room, its windows hung with blankets and its lamp turned down to a glow.

locations.name: Asbec Halt
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The railway halt at Asbec, a single platform and a waiting room where the stove is lit only when a train is due. The station master knows every face that gets off and remembers the ones that do not belong.

areas.name: Asbec Halt Platform
areas.text: A single timber platform beside the track, with a bell on a post and a water tower beyond.

areas.name: Asbec Halt Waiting Room
areas.text: A small room of benches, a stove and a timetable that is never right.

locations.name: Asbec Soup Kitchen
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A hall of patched tin at the edge of the slum where soup and bread are given out twice a day. Ishvalan families run it on what the town gives and what the slum can spare.

areas.name: Soup Kitchen Elders' Corner
areas.text: A curtained corner behind the stove where the elders sit on cushions and talk.

areas.name: Soup Kitchen Serving Hall
areas.text: The long hall with its great pot, its trestles and its line of bowls.

locations.name: Asbec Tinsmiths' Row
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A lane of workshops where the slum's tinsmiths make stovepipes, buckets and roofing for the town. The work is cheap and good, and the town buys it while saying nothing kind about the hands that made it.

areas.name: Tinsmiths' Row Cart Yard
areas.text: A yard at the lane's end where finished pipes and buckets wait on carts.

areas.name: Tinsmiths' Row Workshops
areas.text: Open-fronted workshops along the lane, each with an anvil, shears and a brazier.

locations.name: Ashgrove Wood
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A wood south of the city where the charcoal burners work and the officers go shooting. Its paths are muddy and its deeper parts are wild.

areas.name: Ashgrove Charcoal Clearing
areas.text: A clearing of smoking charcoal mounds and a burner's hut.

areas.name: Ashgrove Deserters' Hollow
areas.text: A hidden hollow with the remains of a fire and a tarpaulin.

locations.name: Atelier Garfiel
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 3-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A corner workshop in Rush Valley owned by Garfiel, a huge, soft-spoken engineer whose joints are copied up and down the valley. Customers wait on a bench by the door, apprentices bend over the benches inside, and tea comes round whether anyone wants it or not.

areas.name: Garfiel Front Workshop
areas.text: The bright front room of benches, vices and half-finished forearms.

areas.name: Garfiel Parts Loft
areas.text: A loft up a ladder, drawers of springs labelled in a neat round hand.

areas.name: Garfiel Tea Corner
areas.text: Two chairs, a kettle and a doily-covered table where clients are soothed.

locations.name: Back Lane Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A two-room clinic down a lane off the square, run by a country doctor who sets bones and stitches cuts for whoever knocks. He keeps no appointment book. Patients who cannot pay leave firewood on the step instead.

areas.name: Back Lane Surgery
areas.text: The front room with its scrubbed table, its lamp on a chain and its shelf of brown bottles.

areas.name: Stove-side Cot
areas.text: The back room, where one cot stands by a tiled stove and the window looks onto the lane.

locations.name: Bamboo-Pipe Brine Wells
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

Timber derricks over deep wells lift brine from far below the ground, and bamboo pipes carry it on trestles to the boiling pans. Some wells breathe a gas that the workers pipe to the fires.

areas.name: Brine Derrick Field
areas.text: A field of tall timber derricks and their treadwheels.

areas.name: Brine Wells Boiling Pans
areas.text: Iron pans over gas-fed fires, white with salt crust.

locations.name: Barry's Old Butcher Shop
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

A shuttered butcher's shop on a backstreet that nobody has rented since its last owner was dragged off in chains. Neighbours cross the street rather than pass the door. The papers called him Barry the Chopper; he carved up twenty-three people, starting with his wife, before the military police caught him.

areas.name: Barry's Butcher Shop Cold Room
areas.text: A stone cold room behind a heavy door, still smelling of old blood.

areas.name: Barry's Butcher Shop Counter
areas.text: The empty counter and the scrubbed block, rust on every hook.

locations.name: Baschool
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

An abandoned mining town east of Fort Briggs, its houses empty and its rail line rusted. The mine closed years ago, and the snow has taken the streets back.

areas.name: Dead Rail Line
areas.text: The rusted rail line that runs out to the mine.

areas.name: Main Street
areas.text: The empty street of shops and boarded windows.

locations.name: Baschool Company Store
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The mining company's store, where the miners once bought their food and boots on credit against their wages. The shelves are bare and the door hangs open, but the books are still under the counter.

areas.name: Company Store Back Office
areas.text: A small office with a safe, a desk and a shelf of company books.

areas.name: Company Store Shop Floor
areas.text: The shop floor, its shelves empty and its windows boarded over.

locations.name: Baschool Mine Galleries
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

The worked-out galleries under Baschool, a maze of tunnels running away from the town in every direction. A person who knows them can come up somewhere no one is watching.

areas.name: Mine Galleries Air Shaft
areas.text: A narrow shaft with iron rungs that climbs to daylight on the hillside.

areas.name: Mine Galleries Junction
areas.text: A crossing of four tunnels where an ore cart lies on its side across the rails.

areas.name: Mine Galleries Low Crawl
areas.text: A tunnel so low it must be crawled, its roof held by cracked props.

locations.name: Baschool Pithead
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The head of the main shaft at Baschool, with its winding tower, its engine house and the lamp room where each miner took his lamp and hung his tally. The engine has not turned since the mine closed.

areas.name: Pithead Lamp Room
areas.text: A room of hooks and tallies where the miners collected their lamps each shift.

areas.name: Pithead Winding House
areas.text: The engine house, its great wheel and cylinders cold under drifted snow.

locations.name: Bear's Head Tavern
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The tavern the soldiers of the fort drink in when they come down to the city, loud and hot and smelling of wet wool. City troops drink elsewhere if they know what is good for them.

areas.name: Bear's Head Long Tables
areas.text: The rows of scarred tables under the bear's head, where the fort's men sit by company.

areas.name: Drying Stove
areas.text: The great iron stove where boots, mittens and coats steam on a rack.

locations.name: Black Seam Outcrop
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A cliff on the desert's edge where the town's seam breaks the surface in a black band as thick as a man. Herders chip it for their fires, and geologists come to look at it and go away.

areas.name: Outcrop Coal Band
areas.text: The black band in the cliff, crumbling where it has been chipped.

areas.name: Outcrop Overhang
areas.text: A hollow under the cliff where travellers shelter from the sun.

locations.name: Black Tent Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-24 · Danger: High]

Herders who have lived in the desert longer than Amestris has had a name pitch their black goat-hair tents here each spring. They trade milk and cheese with the caravans and ask for news in return.

areas.name: Goat Tents
areas.text: The black tents in a ring, their sides rolled up for air.

areas.name: Guest Rug
areas.text: The rug in front of the chief's tent, where strangers sit.

locations.name: Blackpine Wood
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A dark forest of old pines north-east of the city, where woodcutters work the edges and few go deeper. Wolves come down from the range in hard winters and follow the woodcutters' track to the sawmill.

areas.name: Blackpine Deep Pines
areas.text: The silent heart of the wood, where the snow lies unbroken.

areas.name: Blackpine Wolf Hollow
areas.text: A sheltered hollow full of prints and gnawed bones.

areas.name: Blackpine Woodcutters' Track
areas.text: The rutted track along the forest edge, lined with stacked logs.

locations.name: Blank-Sign Crossroads
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-9 · Danger: Low]

Where the village track meets the coach road, the fingerpost has four arms and no names on any of them. Locals find their way; strangers stand here and argue.

areas.name: Crossroads Fingerpost
areas.text: A weathered fingerpost with four planed arms, all blank.

areas.name: Crossroads Wayside Shrine
areas.text: A little roofed shrine with a candle stub and dried flowers.

locations.name: Bonath
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe]

Bonath was the northern town of old Xerxes. Its walls stand only knee-high now, and the beams of its houses lie black in the sand, as though the place burned a little while ago rather than centuries back.

areas.name: Bonath Gate Stump
areas.text: The stump of the northern gate, half of an arch still standing.

areas.name: Charred Streets
areas.text: The grid of streets marked out by black beams and low walls.

locations.name: Bone Ridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: Severe]

A ridge where the bones of animals and men lie in the sand, gathered by the wind into rows along its crest. The caravans call it the ridge of the lost and do not stop there.

areas.name: Bone Rows
areas.text: The rows of bones along the crest, bleached white.

areas.name: Wind Gap
areas.text: The gap in the ridge where the wind moans day and night.

locations.name: Booksellers' Arcade
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A covered arcade of book shops between two streets near the library, where students, clerks and alchemists come to hunt for second-hand books. Each shop keeps its own speciality: law, medicine, poetry, alchemy, maps. Rainy afternoons fill it with people who are not buying.

areas.name: Booksellers' Arcade Alchemy Shop
areas.text: A cramped shop of alchemy books, a locked case behind the counter.

areas.name: Booksellers' Arcade Bargain Carts
areas.text: Wheeled carts of cheap old books under the glass roof.

locations.name: Border Refugee Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

Families from the villages that changed hands in the fighting now live in patched tents along a creek behind the front. Some are Amestrian and some were Cretan before the line moved; the camp has stopped asking which.

areas.name: Refugee Creek Tents
areas.text: The tents along the creek, patched with sacking and army canvas.

areas.name: Refugee Ration Line
areas.text: The line where the army hands out flour and tinned meat twice a week.

locations.name: Border Road Inn
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-26 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A stone inn on the road to the border, where traders and couriers rest before the last stretch. The landlord keeps a fire lit all year and a list of who is due back.

areas.name: Courtyard
areas.text: The yard of carts and mules, loud at dawn.

areas.name: Hearth Room
areas.text: The room with its fire, its benches and its list on the wall.

locations.name: Border Wall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

A low stone wall that marks the border through the hills, with watch posts every few hundred paces and wire strung along the top. Shepherds cross it at will and the patrols pretend not to see them.

areas.name: Wall Section
areas.text: A stretch of the stone wall with its gap and its watch posts.

areas.name: Wire Top
areas.text: The coils of wire along the wall, rusted in the rain.

locations.name: Border Watchtower
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A watchtower on the rise above the border road, with a signal lamp for the line and a radio for the rear. Its crew counts every column that passes below and sends the numbers south.

areas.name: Signal Lamp
areas.text: The lamp at the top and the wires that run down to the rear.

areas.name: Tower Floor
areas.text: The lookout floor with its maps and its telescope.

locations.name: Brecht Pawnbroker
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A pawnshop on a side street where the veterans bring their medals and watches when the pension is late. The broker is patient and fair and has the best collection of service decorations in the east, none of it for sale to the men who left them.

areas.name: Brecht Back Shelves
areas.text: Shelves of wrapped bundles, each tagged with a name and a date.

areas.name: Brecht Pledge Counter
areas.text: A wire grille with a slot where goods pass in and tickets pass out.

locations.name: Brenner Farm
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-13 · Danger: Moderate]

A farm north of the town that was abandoned when its owner could not pay the lieutenant's rent. The house was burned, the fields are fallow and the plough is rusting where it stood.

areas.name: Brenner Burnt House
