areas.text: The black shell of the farmhouse, open to the sky.

areas.name: Brenner Root Cellar
areas.text: A cellar under the yard, its door hidden by weeds.

locations.name: Brenner's Department Store
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Five floors of everything a household in the capital could want, from hatpins to a gramophone, and the first shop in the city with an electric lift. Crowds gather on the pavement every season when the windows are changed, and girls from the provinces queue for jobs behind its counters.

areas.name: Brenner's Glove Counter
areas.text: A long glass counter of gloves in every colour, a stool for trying them on.

areas.name: Brenner's Loading Bay
areas.text: A loading bay off the back lane, crates stacked by a stair going down.

areas.name: Brenner's Rooftop Tea Room
areas.text: A tea room under a glass roof at the top of the lift, cakes on stands.

locations.name: Bridge of Clan Truces
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

By old law the stone bridge over the canal south of the market is neutral ground, and clans at feud meet on its crown to talk instead of fight. Each side comes up its own steps with the same number of men.

areas.name: Truce Bridge Crown
areas.text: The top of the arch, where the two parties stand a step apart.

areas.name: Truce Bridge Witness Steps
areas.text: The steps on either bank where each side's men wait.

locations.name: Briggs
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

The mountain range at the far north of Amestris, a natural wall against Drachma: snow the year round, winters far below zero and blizzards with no warning. Evergreens grow on the lower slopes, and eagles, deer, wolves and the infamous Briggs grizzlies, three metres tall on their hind legs, live among them.

areas.name: Ice Ridge
areas.text: The narrow ridge of ice on the range's crest.

areas.name: Snow Slope
areas.text: The long slope of snow above the fort, dangerous when the wind is up.

locations.name: Briggs Barrack Tiers
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Floor upon floor of soldiers' quarters inside the wall, the bunks four high and the boots drying on the heating pipes. The garrison eats together in a mess hall that smells of cabbage and gun oil.

areas.name: Barrack Tiers Bunk Rooms
areas.text: Long rooms of iron bunks four high, each with a footlocker and a hook for a rifle.

areas.name: Barrack Tiers Mess Hall
areas.text: A hall of long tables and benches, with a serving hatch and a samovar of tea.

locations.name: Briggs Boiler Deck
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The lowest working level of the fort, where the furnaces and the great heating pipes keep the wall alive through the winter. The engineers here know every knock and hiss in the lines by heart, and they are proud of it.

areas.name: Boiler Deck Furnace Row
areas.text: Three coal furnaces in a line, their doors glowing, with stokers working in shirtsleeves.

areas.name: Boiler Deck Listening Post
areas.text: The far corner of the deck, where a stool and a lamp sit by the deepest valve.

areas.name: Boiler Deck Pipe Gallery
areas.text: A low gallery of trunk pipes as thick as a man, ticking and knocking in the heat.

locations.name: Briggs Charcoal Clearing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A clearing on the lower slope where charcoal burners tend smouldering mounds of earth and logs for days at a time. Their charcoal goes to the smiths of North City and to the fort's forge.

areas.name: Charcoal Burners' Turf Hut
areas.text: A low hut of turf and logs where the burners sleep in shifts.

areas.name: Charcoal Mound Ring
areas.text: A ring of earth mounds, each leaking thin blue smoke from its vents.

locations.name: Briggs Customs Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Because no one crosses between the two countries except through the fort, this hall inside the gate is where the crossing is done: papers read, trunks opened, names written into a book as thick as a doorstep.

areas.name: Customs Hall Counter
areas.text: A long dark counter with brass rails, stamps on chains and a clerk behind each window.

areas.name: Customs Hall Search Room
areas.text: A side room with a bare table, where trunks are emptied and coats are turned out.

locations.name: Briggs Engineering Bay
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The fort's research and development shop, where steel plate is tested, engines are stripped and the garrison's new fighting vehicle is put together piece by piece. Visitors from Central are shown one end of the hall and not the other.

areas.name: Engineering Bay Assembly Floor
areas.text: The main floor, where a turret hangs from a hoist above an open hull.

areas.name: Engineering Bay Drawing Office
areas.text: A glassed room above the floor, its tables covered in drawings and slide rules.

locations.name: Briggs Garrison Graveyard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A field of wooden markers on a ledge below the wall, where the garrison buries its dead in the short summer and keeps them in the ice house until then. Every board carries a name, a rank and nothing else.

areas.name: Garrison Graveyard Ice House
areas.text: A stone hut cut into the slope where the winter dead wait for the thaw.

areas.name: Garrison Graveyard Rows
areas.text: The rows of markers, their names burned in with a hot iron.

locations.name: Briggs Gun Gallery
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The long gallery of gun positions on the Drachma face of the wall, its ports looking down a valley that the gunners have ranged to the yard. Nothing crosses that valley in daylight without the gallery knowing.

areas.name: Gun Gallery Ammunition Hoist
areas.text: The hoist shaft that brings shells up from the magazines in iron cradles.

areas.name: Gun Gallery Ports
areas.text: A row of deep ports in the wall, each with its field gun, its shell rack and its range card.

locations.name: Briggs Lookout Hut
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-22 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A hut on a crag above the pass with a bell on a chain for warning the fort of an avalanche. The hut is stocked for a week and its door is never locked.

areas.name: Bell Rope
areas.text: The rope and bell that warn the fort of slides.

areas.name: Stores Room
areas.text: The room of tinned food, blankets and a stove.

locations.name: Briggs Main Tunnel
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The great passage that runs the whole length of the wall, wide enough for two lorries abreast. Every stair, lift and side gallery of the fort opens off it, and a runner can cross from one end to the other faster than the wind can cross the parapet above.

areas.name: Main Tunnel Bulkhead
areas.text: A steel door the height of three men, rolled on a track, that closes the tunnel off by sections.

areas.name: Main Tunnel Lorry Lane
areas.text: The paved centre of the passage, rutted by tyres and lit by a line of caged lamps.

locations.name: Briggs North Rampart
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High]

The walk along the top of the wall on its northern side, where sentries stand roped to the rail when the wind is up. On a clear day the watch can see a long way into Drachma, and on a bad day it cannot see its own boots.

areas.name: North Rampart Sally Hatch
areas.text: An iron hatch in the parapet that opens on a line of rungs down the outer face.

areas.name: North Rampart Walk
areas.text: The top of the wall, scraped of snow each morning, with a rope rail along its edge.

locations.name: Briggs Pass
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

The gorge that cuts through the Briggs range near the fort, the only road a cart can take in winter. The garrison keeps a post at each end and a rope across the worst of the ice.

areas.name: Gorge Road
areas.text: The road cut into the gorge wall, icy and narrow.

areas.name: Rope Crossing
areas.text: The frozen stream crossed by a rope and a plank bridge.

locations.name: Briggs Pass Telegraph Relay
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-16 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small hut on stilts beside the pass where the telegraph wire to the fort is boosted and tested. A lineman lives here through the winter with a dog, a stove and a stack of spare wire.

areas.name: Relay Hut Instrument Room
areas.text: The one room of the hut, with the relay set, a stove and a bunk.

areas.name: Relay Hut Pole Line
areas.text: The line of poles running up the pass, each one crusted with ice.

locations.name: Briggs Pinewood
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A belt of dark pines on the middle slopes of the range, the only real cover between the fort and the lower valleys. Woodcutters, hunters and deserters all know it, for different reasons.

areas.name: Pinewood Deer Track
areas.text: A narrow track under the pines, trodden by deer and by men pretending to be deer.

areas.name: Pinewood Fallen Giant
areas.text: A huge fallen pine, its roots torn up, with snow banked against it.

locations.name: Briggs Rail Snowshed
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A long timber shed built over the railway where the slope above it sheds snow, so that slides pass over the line instead of burying it. Trains rattle through it in the dark.

areas.name: Snowshed Gallery
areas.text: The dark inside of the shed, a tunnel of beams with rails down its middle.

areas.name: Snowshed Roof
areas.text: The sloped roof of the shed, buried under the snow it was built to carry.

locations.name: Briggs Remount Stables
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

Stalls for the garrison's horses, shaggy hardy beasts bred for snow, kept warm against the inner face of the wall. Patrols that cannot take a lorry take a horse, and the grooms know which animal will face a blizzard.

areas.name: Remount Stables Stalls
areas.text: Two rows of stalls under a low roof, each horse in a heavy blanket.

areas.name: Remount Stables Tack Loft
areas.text: A loft of saddles, snowshoes for horses and harness hung on pegs.

locations.name: Briggs Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The road from North City up to Fort Briggs, a route of packed snow, milestones and supply wagons. It is kept open by the garrison's own men and closed when the snow is too deep.

areas.name: Lower Road
areas.text: The road from the city out past the farms, rutted and busy.

areas.name: Upper Road
areas.text: The road climbing toward the range, with its milestones and its snow posts.

locations.name: Briggs Ski Patrol Hut
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-18 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A hut west of the fort where the garrison's ski troops base their patrols, with racks of skis, white smocks and a bench for waxing. A man who joins the patrol learns to cross the range faster than a horse.

areas.name: Ski Patrol Rack Room
areas.text: A room of skis in racks, poles in barrels and white smocks hanging to dry.

areas.name: Ski Patrol Waxing Bench
areas.text: A bench by the stove with irons, blocks of wax and a tin of pine tar.

locations.name: Briggs Sled Kennels
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The fort's kennels on the lower slope, where sled dogs are bred and trained to haul mail, medicine and ammunition when the lorries cannot move. The kennelman knows each dog by name and some soldiers by number.

areas.name: Kennels Dog Run
areas.text: A fenced run of trodden snow where the teams are harnessed and exercised.

areas.name: Kennels Harness Shed
areas.text: A shed of harness, sledges and a barrel of frozen fish for the dogs.

locations.name: Briggs Stockade
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The prison cut into the inner face of the wall: a corridor of cells with doors of riveted iron. Smugglers taken on the pass, deserters and the odd Drachman scout wait here for a decision from the general.

areas.name: Stockade Cell Corridor
areas.text: A narrow corridor of iron doors, each with a hatch and a number in white paint.

areas.name: Stockade Guard Brazier
areas.text: The guard post at the corridor's mouth, with a brazier, a chair and a ring of keys.

locations.name: Briggs Stores Tunnels
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The supply tunnels behind and below the wall, where the fort keeps enough coal, flour, tinned meat and ammunition to hold out a winter without a single train. The quartermaster counts it all twice a week.

areas.name: Stores Tunnels Coal Cellar
areas.text: A black vault of coal heaped to the ceiling, with shovels and barrows at the door.

areas.name: Stores Tunnels Tally Room
areas.text: A cramped office with a tally board, a book and a telephone to the quartermaster.

locations.name: Briggs Supply Railhead
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The end of the line from North City, where the trains stop and the fort's supplies go onto lorries and sledges for the climb. A plough engine waits in steam all winter to clear the track.

areas.name: Railhead Loading Dock
areas.text: A long timber dock beside the track, with a steam crane and a line of lorries.

areas.name: Railhead Plough Shed
areas.text: A shed of black planks where the plough engine sits in steam, ready to move.

locations.name: Briggs Tank Proving Ground
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A bowl of open snow behind the wall where the engineers test what they build: gun carriages, sledges, and now a heavy armoured machine with a turret. The ground is torn up in long double furrows.

areas.name: Proving Ground Observation Trench
areas.text: A trench with a sandbagged lip where engineers watch the trials with notebooks.

areas.name: Proving Ground Test Bowl
areas.text: The open snow of the bowl, crossed and recrossed by track furrows.

locations.name: Briggs Telegraph Room
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The fort's wire room, where the telegraph line from North City and the switchboard for the fort's own telephones are kept running day and night. When the lines ice up, linemen go out on the range to clear them by hand.

areas.name: Telegraph Room Key Bench
areas.text: A bench of telegraph keys and sounders, with message pads and a pot of cold tea.

areas.name: Telegraph Room Switchboard
areas.text: A wall of brass jacks and cords where the fort's telephone calls are put through.

locations.name: Briggs Wall Infirmary
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The hospital of the fort: a ward of iron beds, a theatre and a workbench where the fort's doctor fits and repairs automail. Frostbite is the common complaint, and the doctor has strong opinions on which metals a northern limb should carry.

areas.name: Wall Infirmary Limb Bench
areas.text: The doctor's workbench, strewn with springs, nerve leads and half-built hands.

areas.name: Wall Infirmary Ward
areas.text: A long warm room of iron beds under blankets, with a stove at each end.

locations.name: Briggs Wallfoot Snowfield
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

The open snow at the foot of the wall on its northern side, the ground an attacker must cross to reach the gate. There is no cover on it worth the name, which is the whole point.

areas.name: Wallfoot Open Snow
areas.text: The flat white field below the wall, crossed only by the wind.

areas.name: Wallfoot Wire Line
areas.text: A line of barbed wire on posts, half buried, that marks the gunners' nearest range.

locations.name: Brunner's Military Tailors
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The tailoring house that makes uniforms for the capital's officers. The master tailor and his three sons measure, cut and sew to order; new promotions come in for fresh epaulettes, and a general's coat can take a month.

areas.name: Brunner Cutting Room
areas.text: A big table under bright lamps where the blue wool is cut.

areas.name: Brunner Fitting Mirrors
areas.text: Three tall mirrors and a step for the customer to stand on.

locations.name: Camel Post Station
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Where the telegraph does not reach, the mail goes by camel. This station keeps fresh beasts and a rider ready to carry the post bags between the fort, the crossing and the ruins.

areas.name: Post Hook
areas.text: The shed where the bags hang and are signed for.

areas.name: Rider Corral
areas.text: The corral of post camels, fed and watered for the next run.

locations.name: Canal Ward
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The old quarter by the canals, with its footbridges, laundry boats and houses that lean over the water. Its people are workers and their families, and most have a relative in the army.

areas.name: Footbridge Row
areas.text: The small bridges and the steps that climb to the houses above.

areas.name: Main Canal
areas.text: The wide canal with its boats and its stone quay.

locations.name: Capital Gazette Press
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The offices and press hall of the capital's leading daily newspaper. Reporters type up the day's speeches from the Parliament House, crimes, army notices and train times; the presses roll at midnight and the bundles go out to the news stands before dawn.

areas.name: Capital Gazette Newsroom
areas.text: A noisy room of desks and typewriters, reporters shouting for copy boys.

areas.name: Capital Gazette Press Hall
areas.text: The pressroom where the big rotary presses shake the floor at night.

locations.name: Capital Grammar School
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A school of red brick where the children of clerks and soldiers learn their letters, sums and the history of Amestris. The headmistress is strict, the yard is loud, and every child knows the names of the State Alchemists by heart.

areas.name: Capital Grammar Classroom
areas.text: A room of wooden desks, inkwells and a large map of Amestris on the wall.

areas.name: Capital Grammar Schoolyard
areas.text: A walled yard of skipping ropes, marbles and shouting.

locations.name: Capital Military Police Precinct
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The station house of the military police for the inner districts. They handle soldiers' brawls, thefts from the barracks and, since the capital has no other police, a great deal of ordinary crime. The desk sergeant writes everything down.

areas.name: Capital Precinct Charge Desk
areas.text: The front desk with the charge book and a bell.

areas.name: Capital Precinct Holding Cells
areas.text: A row of barred cells along a cold corridor.

locations.name: Capital Opera House
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Society goes to the opera to be seen as much as to listen, and the capital's opera house is built for both: four tiers of boxes curving round the stage, so everyone can watch everyone else. The Führer keeps a box by the stage that is seldom used, and the box next to it is seldom empty.

areas.name: Capital Opera Backstage Wings
areas.text: The dark wings of ropes, flats and the dressing rooms behind them.

areas.name: Capital Opera Horseshoe Auditorium
areas.text: The gilded hall of red seats and stacked boxes under the chandelier.

locations.name: Capital Stockyards
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

Cattle, sheep and pigs come in by rail to these yards and pens at the edge of the city, where they are sold, slaughtered and sent to the butchers. The smell carries a long way on a hot day.

areas.name: Capital Stockyards Killing Floor
areas.text: The slaughterhouse floor, tiled and drained.

areas.name: Capital Stockyards Sale Ring
areas.text: A sawdust ring with tiered benches for the buyers.

locations.name: Capital Tramway Depot
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The yard where the capital's electric trams sleep at night, a long shed of green cars on parallel tracks with a repair pit at one end. Drivers and conductors clock on at dawn and the first cars rattle out before the bakers open.

areas.name: Capital Tramway Clocking Office
areas.text: A small office with a punch clock and the drivers' rota.

areas.name: Capital Tramway Repair Pit
areas.text: A pit under the rails where fitters work on wheels and motors.

areas.name: Capital Tramway Running Shed
areas.text: The long shed of parked tramcars, sparks spitting where the wires meet.

locations.name: Caravan Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 16-20 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A canvas clinic stands in the lee of the crossing walls: four cots, a crate of bandages and a doctor who treats heat sickness, snakebite and broken legs for whoever comes. Payment is whatever a patient has.

areas.name: Cot Row
areas.text: The four canvas cots under a flapping roof.

areas.name: Dressing Crate
areas.text: The crate that serves as table, desk and pharmacy.

locations.name: Carved Stone of Xerxes
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-30 · Danger: Severe]

Far to the east of the ruins a single slab of rock lies tilted out of the sand, its face cut deep with lines, circles and figures. Desert people walk around it and not across its shadow. Nobody alive can read it.

areas.name: Shadow Ring
areas.text: The ring of trodden sand where pilgrims walk around the slab.

areas.name: Slab Face
areas.text: The carved face of the stone, best read in low sun.

locations.name: Cavalry Remount Depot
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-13 · Danger: Moderate]

Paddocks and stables west of the city where horses are broken for the army's carts and patrols. Trucks have taken over much of the work, but the hills south of the line still need horses.

areas.name: Breaking Paddock
areas.text: A ring of rails where young horses learn to carry men.

areas.name: Farrier's Forge
areas.text: A forge of hammers, horseshoes and a hissing trough.

locations.name: Celadon Kiln Hill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

A long kiln climbs the hill in steps, fired for days at a time with pine wood, and the potters' village sits at its foot. The pale green ware it makes goes to the court and the clan houses.

areas.name: Celadon Shard Heaps
areas.text: Mounds of broken seconds behind the village, green under the dust.

areas.name: Celadon Stepped Kiln
areas.text: The long brick kiln with stoke holes up its side.

locations.name: Cemetery of the North
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The city's cemetery, with iron railings, yews and rows of stones. Soldiers of the fort are buried here when the snow allows the digging, and the stones bear the names of the first garrison.

areas.name: Northern Stone Rows
areas.text: The rows of graves and their stones, frosted over.

areas.name: Yew Walk
areas.text: The path under the old yews, dark even at noon.

locations.name: Central City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The capital of Amestris and the seat of its government: the legislature, the military's top command, the national libraries and laboratories and the great rail terminal all sit within its walls. Soldiers in state blue walk the avenues, and every stranger's papers are looked at twice. A traveller arrives by train and is expected to leave the same way.

areas.name: Central Station
areas.text:
The rail terminal's glass hall, the platforms and the ticket office where the yard clerk sells the trains out.

The rail and coach service serves this yard: coaches run to East City (about 14 Cens), North City (about 16 Cens), Dublith (about 14 Cens), West City (about 16 Cens); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Military Quarter
areas.text: The barracks streets and the State Military's offices, guarded and grey.

areas.name: Parliament Avenue
areas.text: The broad boulevard of ministries and the Parliament House, flags hung between the lamps.

locations.name: Central Command
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-30 · Danger: Severe]

The top of the military government of Amestris: the head of state and his generals keep their offices in a moated compound on a pyramid-like structure at the heart of the capital. Only officers with the right rank cross the bridge, and the courtyards are watched from every floor.

areas.name: Command Moat
areas.text: The water and the bridge that is the only way in, with its gate and its sentries.

areas.name: Command Pyramid
areas.text: The stepped building of offices, the generals' floors and the head of state's stair.

locations.name: Central Gardens
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High]

The public gardens at the middle of the capital, clipped hedges and plane trees around a bandstand. Clerks eat their lunch here and nannies push prams along the paths.

areas.name: Bandstand
areas.text: The round bandstand in the middle of the lawns.

areas.name: Plane Walk
areas.text: The shaded walk under the plane trees, where the benches are.

locations.name: Central Hospital
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The state hospital of the capital, where soldiers and civilians injured in the fighting are taken. Its beds are full after every street battle, and its doctors ask no questions beyond the injury.

areas.name: Receiving Ward
areas.text: The entrance hall, the stretchers and the triage desk.

areas.name: Surgical Wing
areas.text: The white operating rooms and the wards above them.

locations.name: Central Locomotive Works
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High]

The railway's great workshop, where locomotives are built and repaired. Hundreds of fitters, boilermakers and foundrymen work in long sheds, and the shift whistle sets the clocks of the whole quarter.

areas.name: Central Locomotive Boiler Shop
areas.text: A deafening shop where boilers are riveted.

areas.name: Central Locomotive Drawing Office
areas.text: A quiet upstairs room of drafting tables.

areas.name: Central Locomotive Erecting Shop
areas.text: A long hall of locomotives on jacks, a crane overhead.

locations.name: Central Military Cemetery
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-20 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The capital's burying ground for soldiers, laid out in straight rows on a gentle rise outside the inner walls. Officers who fall are carried here with a flag, a volley and a speech, and their families come on rest days with flowers. The groundsmen keep the grass short and the gates locked at dusk.

areas.name: Central Cemetery Honour Ground
areas.text: A flagstone square with a flagpole where the volleys are fired over the coffins.

areas.name: Central Cemetery Officers' Rows
areas.text: The long rows of matching white stones, each with a rank cut above the name.

locations.name: Central Prison
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High]

The capital's great prison, run by the State Military: hundreds of felons and court-martialed soldiers behind its walls, and Central Command leaning on its warders whenever it wants a man held or forgotten. The condemned wait here for the formal sentence, and the town says some of them never reach the gallows.

areas.name: Death Row Block
areas.text: The cells of the condemned, quiet and lit by a single lamp each.

areas.name: Prison Yard
areas.text: The exercise yard between the walls, where the guards count heads twice a day.

areas.name: Records Office
areas.text: The dusty room where inmates are entered, struck and signed out.

locations.name: Central Rail Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High]

The freight yard behind Central Station: sidings full of wagons, the engine sheds and the cargo cranes that move supplies to the fronts. Guards watch the wagons, and no one rides them without a pass.

areas.name: Engine Sheds
areas.text: The sheds of steam engines, hot and loud, with their black smoke.

areas.name: Sidings
areas.text: The rails and the parked wagons, with the switchmen's hut at the end.

locations.name: Central Road Crossing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The crossing where the northern line meets the road south to the capital. The gate is lowered for every train and the signal box keeps the timetable on a chalk board.

areas.name: Gate Arm
areas.text: The barrier arm and the bell that rings before it falls.

areas.name: Signal Box
areas.text: The box of levers and the chalk timetable.

locations.name: Central Telephone Exchange
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The building where every telephone call in the capital is connected by hand. Rows of young women in headsets plug cords into switchboards from morning till night, and a supervisor watches them from a raised chair. The military has its own board in a locked room upstairs.

areas.name: Central Exchange Military Board
areas.text: A locked upstairs room with one switchboard and a soldier on the door.

areas.name: Central Exchange Switchboard Floor
areas.text: The long hall of switchboards and the chatter of operators.

locations.name: Chang Clan Compound
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The Chang clan keeps its house in the meanest corner of the clan quarter: one courtyard, a gate whose red paint has weathered to brick, and a hall too small for the family's pride. Of the fifty clans the Chang are among the weakest, and nobody at court lets them forget it.

areas.name: Chang Brick-Red Gate
areas.text: The faded street gate, its carved crest missing half its gilt.

areas.name: Chang Kitchen Yard
areas.text: The back yard where the household cooks, washes and keeps its few hens.

areas.name: Chang Tablet Room
areas.text: A narrow room of ancestor tablets honoured with cheap incense and very good manners.

locations.name: Charburners' Clearing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A clearing in the woods west of the city where a family of charcoal burners keeps its mounds smouldering for weeks at a time. They sell to the foundry and the blacksmiths, and they rarely come into town.

areas.name: Charburners' Mounds
areas.text: The smoking earth mounds of the charcoal burn, tended day and night.

areas.name: Charburners' Turf Hut
areas.text: The family's hut of turf and logs, with charcoal sacks stacked outside.

locations.name: Charcoal Burners' Clearing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-13 · Danger: Moderate]

A clearing in the pinewood where a family of burners turns the waste wood into charcoal under mounds of turf. The smoke never stops and the family are as black as the miners.

areas.name: Burners' Branch Hut
areas.text: A hut of branches and sacking where the family sleeps.

areas.name: Burners' Mound
areas.text: A smouldering mound of turf and wood, tended night and day.

locations.name: Cinder Alley
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High]

A narrow alley between warehouse walls in the old quarter, still scorched black along both sides. Everyone in the capital has heard what happened here: the woman officer accused of murdering Maes Hughes broke out of prison, and the Flame Alchemist cornered her here and burned her where she stood.

areas.name: Cinder Alley Lamp Corner
areas.text: The bend in the alley under the one gas lamp, where the fire stopped.

areas.name: Cinder Alley Scorched Wall
areas.text: A stretch of brick blackened to head height, the mortar cracked by heat.

locations.name: Clan Flashpowder Works
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

Outside the city wall, where a spark does least harm, a yard of low sheds makes the grenades Xing's warriors carry: smoke, blinding flash, and a pepper bomb that leaves a grown man weeping on his knees. Nothing in Amestris works quite like them.

areas.name: Flashpowder Mixing Sheds
areas.text: Damp sheds where powder is mixed with wooden spoons and no one speaks loudly.

areas.name: Flashpowder Test Pit
areas.text: A blackened pit beyond the sheds where each batch is tried.

areas.name: Pepper-Bomb Drying Shed
areas.text: A shed of racks where pepper charges dry in paper shells, eye-wateringly.

locations.name: Clan Halls
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The halls of the great clans, each a walled compound of wooden buildings and painted doors. The clan heads hold court in their own halls, and the lesser families come to them for favours.

areas.name: Ancestral Hall
areas.text: The hall of the clan's ancestors, with their tablets and their incense.

areas.name: Clan Courtyard
areas.text: The pine-shaded courtyard where petitioners wait for the clan head.

locations.name: Cleric's Hermitage Caves
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

When the war began, the Grand Cleric withdrew into these caves with a few priests to keep the faith out of the army's reach. He came down only in the last year, to offer himself to the Führer in exchange for his people.

areas.name: Cleric's Hermitage Ladder Cliff
areas.text: The red cliff face with rope ladders between the caves.

areas.name: Cleric's Hermitage Spring
areas.text: A thin stream of water down a mossy rock.

areas.name: Grand Cleric's Cell
areas.text: A small cave with a mat, a lamp and a carved prayer stone.

locations.name: Clock Tower
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A stone tower above the old square, with a clock that has kept the city's time for longer than anyone remembers. From its top the whole city and the road to the east can be seen.

areas.name: Clock Room
areas.text: The room of the gears and the great bell, with the wind of the city through the louvres.

areas.name: Clock Tower Stair
areas.text: The stone stair with its arrow slits and worn steps.

locations.name: Cloud Step Hermitage
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 20-26 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A stair of stone climbs into the cloud on the way up the high peaks, and at its top an old guard who left the court lives alone. Young warriors climb to ask him to teach them.

areas.name: Cloud Step Stairway
areas.text: Thousands of steps cut into the mountainside, slick with mist.

areas.name: Hermit's Cold Room
areas.text: A bare stone room with one mat and one bowl.

locations.name: Coach Road Roadmender's Cottage
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-7 · Danger: Low]

The district pays one man to keep the coach road mended between the village and the town, and he lives in this cottage beside his heap of broken stone. He knows every rut and every traveller.

areas.name: Roadmender's Night Gate
areas.text: A field gate across the road that the roadmender locks at dusk.

areas.name: Roadmender's Stone Heap
areas.text: A heap of broken stone and the bench where it is hammered to size.

locations.name: Coal Flats
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The flats below the town where the coal dust settles and the runoff gathers in pools that never clear. Nothing grows here but a hard grass, and the wind never stops.

areas.name: Dust Flats
areas.text: The black plain of dust with its paths of trodden stone.

areas.name: Pool Edge
areas.text: The shore of the pools, where nothing grows.

locations.name: Coal Screens of Youswell
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-13 · Danger: Moderate]

A tall shed on timber legs where the coal from the pits is shaken through iron screens and sorted by size. Boys too young for the pit stand at the belts and pick out the slate with bleeding fingers.

areas.name: Screen Shed Chutes
areas.text: Wooden chutes that pour the sorted coal into the wagons beneath.

areas.name: Screen Shed Picking Belt
areas.text: A moving belt of coal and the row of boys bent over it.

locations.name: Coal Spur Junction
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 7-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The junction where the coal spur leaves the main line, a signal box and a set of points watched by one man and his dog. Every coal train out of Youswell passes under his window.

areas.name: Junction Points
areas.text: The switch rails where the spur parts from the main line.

areas.name: Junction Signal Box
areas.text: A room of levers, a bell and a stove, high above the tracks.

locations.name: Cold Seam Colliery
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

Unlike the dead mine to the east, this colliery still works its seam, sending coal by rail to the gasworks and the engine sheds. Its winding wheel turns from dawn to dusk and its miners live in a row of soot-black cottages.

areas.name: Coal Face Gallery
areas.text: The working gallery deep below, lit by safety lamps.

areas.name: Cold Seam Winding House
areas.text: The house of the winding engine, its great wheel overhead.

areas.name: Collier Cottages
areas.text: A row of soot-black cottages where the miners' wives keep the steps scrubbed.

locations.name: Copper Diggings
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

A few miners dig for copper in the green-stained rocks on the western side of the desert. They work shallow pits by hand and wash the ore in a sluice that only runs after rain.

areas.name: Dry Sluice
areas.text: The wooden sluice and its empty channel.

areas.name: Green Pits
areas.text: The shallow pits in the stained rock.

locations.name: Cormorant Fishers' Village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A village of fishers who work the river at night with tame cormorants and lanterns hung over the rafts. The birds dive for fish and a ring at the throat keeps them from swallowing the big ones.

areas.name: Cormorant Roosting Poles
areas.text: Tall poles on the bank where the birds dry their wings.

areas.name: Fishers' Net Lofts
areas.text: Stilted lofts where nets are mended and fish are salted.

locations.name: Cornello's Manor
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

The manor of the man who ruled Reole, a big house with guards at the gate and a garden of roses that is still tended by his old gardener. The house is not as grand as its owner wanted.

areas.name: Manor Gate
areas.text: The gate with its guards and its iron name-plate, now blank.

areas.name: Rose Garden
areas.text: The walled garden of roses, overgrown at the edges.

locations.name: Court of Fifty Concubines
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Behind the palace's eastern wall lies the court of the consorts. Each clan chief sends a daughter to be the Emperor's concubine and bear him one heir, and each daughter keeps a wing here under her clan's colour. Visitors sign the wardens' book on the way in and again on the way out.

areas.name: Chang Consort's Wing
areas.text: The smallest wing, kept spotless by two maids who have nothing else to do.

areas.name: Consorts' Colonnade
areas.text: A covered walk of fifty lacquered doors, each under a banner of its clan's colour.

areas.name: Wardens' Records Room
areas.text: The wardens' office by the gate, where every visit is written down twice.

locations.name: Creta
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The country west of Amestris, which has fought it over the border for as long as anyone remembers. Creta is a federation of old tribes joined under one union; its central government keeps its own guarded borders between the tribes, which have little love for one another.

areas.name: Border Pass
areas.text: The pass across the border, guarded by both sides in turn.

areas.name: Mountain Village
areas.text: The village of stone houses on the slope, its well at the centre.

locations.name: Creta Border Post
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The post on the Amestris side of the border with Creta, a fence of wire and sandbags with a gate that opens for patrols and traders alike. The post's men are on edge and quick to draw.

areas.name: Sandbag Line
areas.text: The line of sandbags and the firing slits behind them.

areas.name: Wire Gate
areas.text: The gate of wire and its guard hut.

locations.name: Cretan Hill Fort
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High]

On the Cretan side of the border a stone fort on a knoll watches the Amestrian posts across the valley. Its garrison wears grey-green with coloured sashes and its single mountain gun is pointed at Pendleton.

areas.name: Cretan Fort Well Court
areas.text: The courtyard of the fort, a well and stacked firewood.

areas.name: Cretan Gun Rampart
areas.text: The stone rampart with its mountain gun and its sentries.

locations.name: Cretan Tribal Line
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-24 · Danger: High]

Within its own borders Creta keeps guarded federal lines between the territories of the old tribes, who have no love for one another. This valley is one such line: a fence down the middle, a federal toll gate, and herders on each side who will not speak to the herders on the other.

areas.name: Divided Pasture
areas.text: The pasture split by a fence of posts and rope, sheep cropping either side.

areas.name: Federal Toll Gate
areas.text: A gatehouse of the federal government, its guards in a uniform neither tribe wears.

locations.name: Crossing Camel Market
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Outside the walls of the crossing, dealers sell and hire camels, mules and the odd tired horse. A camel is looked at in the mouth, the feet and the eyes, in that order, and an Amestrian who skips the feet is known for a fool.

areas.name: Brand Fire
areas.text: The dealers' fire where the irons heat and the deals are spat on.

areas.name: Kneeling Rows
areas.text: The lines of kneeling camels, each tied to a stake.

locations.name: Curtis House
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The home of the Sig Curtis household in Dublith, a plain house with a herb garden and a kitchen where the bread is baked each morning. The family takes in guests and expects them to help with the chores.

areas.name: Herb Garden
areas.text: The beds of herbs and the old bench beside the wall.

areas.name: Kitchen
areas.text: The warm kitchen with its stove and its bread board.

locations.name: Curtis Meats
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A narrow butcher's shop in Dublith run by Izumi and Sig Curtis, with Mason their one hand behind the counter. A plain sign over the door says only meat, the day's specials are chalked on a board outside, and the shop runs a long way back to the house behind it.

areas.name: Cold Store
areas.text: The cold room at the back, hung with carcasses.

areas.name: Shop Counter
areas.text: The counter and the scales, with the price board above.

locations.name: Daliha
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

Daliha was the great district of Ishval, its plaza wide enough for the whole faith to kneel at once. The colonnade around it is broken and the lamp posts are stumps, but the flagstones still lie true, and the priests still sweep them.

areas.name: Daliha Colonnade
areas.text: The broken row of columns around the plaza's edge.

areas.name: Daliha Lamp Row
areas.text: The road into the plaza lined with stumps of lamp posts.

areas.name: Daliha Plaza
areas.text: The wide red plaza, swept clean every morning.

locations.name: Daliha Qanat
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

From the hills to Daliha, a row of shaft mouths dots the ground like the holes of a flute. Each drops to a tunnel where water from the hills runs downhill in the dark. Ishvalan diggers built it long before Amestris drew its borders, and it still flows.

areas.name: Daliha Qanat Fallen Shaft
areas.text: A collapsed shaft mouth choked with earth and stone.

areas.name: Daliha Qanat Outflow Pool
areas.text: The pool at Daliha's edge where the channel surfaces.

areas.name: Daliha Qanat Tunnel
areas.text: A low tunnel with a channel of running water down its middle.

locations.name: Daliha Temple
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-18 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

At the head of the Daliha plaza stands the temple of Ishvala, a dome open at its crown so that a ring of sunlight crosses the floor through the day. The faithful say Ishvala made all things as they are meant to be, and that it is arrogance for human hands to remake them; the walls carry that teaching carved line after line.

areas.name: Daliha Temple Ablution Court
areas.text: A small court with a stone basin where the faithful wash before prayer.

areas.name: Daliha Temple Scripture Walls
areas.text: Curved walls covered top to bottom in carved scripture.

areas.name: Daliha Temple Sun Floor
areas.text: The floor beneath the dome where the ring of light moves.

locations.name: Desert Approach Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The track that comes in off the sand and joins the town's lanes behind the mine, the last stretch anyone crossing from the east must walk. It is the road the pit boys take with their fathers' dinner pails at noon.

areas.name: Approach Road Verge
areas.text: The sandy shoulder where the exhausted fall and the boys find them.

areas.name: Thorn Tree Bend
areas.text: A bend in the track where a dead thorn tree gives the only shade for miles.

locations.name: Desert Crossing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: Severe]

The last walled stop before the great desert: a caravan yard of mud-brick walls, wells and pens, where traders gather to cross east toward Xing or to come back west. The rates are high and the water is measured out by the bucket.

areas.name: Caravan Yard
areas.text:
The walled yard of camels, carts and tents, the headman's hut at its heart.

The rail and coach service serves this yard: coaches run to Youswell (about 9 Cens), Ishval (about 8 Cens), Xing Capital (about 30 Cens); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Water Store
areas.text: The cisterns and the measuring buckets, guarded day and night.

locations.name: Desert Edge Well
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A well on the last of the grass before the desert, with a stone curb and a bucket on a rope. Caravans water here on the way out and the herders water their goats here on the way back.

areas.name: Scrub Camp
areas.text: The camp of tents and cook fires where the caravans rest.

areas.name: Well Curb
areas.text: The stone ring of the well and the bucket on its rope.

locations.name: Desert Patrol Cemetery
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 16-22 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

Soldiers lost to heat, storms and bandits in the desert are buried here in rows, under white wooden markers that need repainting every year. A sergeant from the fort tends it on his own time.

areas.name: Bugle Gate
areas.text: The gate and its vane, which hums in the wind.

areas.name: Patrol Graves
areas.text: The rows of white markers behind the wire.

locations.name: Desert Road Fort
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A small Amestris fort on the desert road, built to keep the caravans safe and the smugglers out. Its garrison is small and bored, and its officers are glad of any visitor.

areas.name: Desert Fort Gate
areas.text: The stone gate and its guardroom.

areas.name: Watch Tower
areas.text: The tower over the road, with its telescope and its lamp.

locations.name: Desert Telegraph Relay
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The telegraph line from East City ends here, in a brick hut with a battery shed and a tall mast. An operator taps out the convoy reports and the weather and reads cheap novels between messages.

areas.name: Battery Shed
areas.text: The shed of acid jars that powers the line.

areas.name: Key Room
areas.text: The hut with its sounder, its key and its stack of message forms.

locations.name: Desert Water Depot
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The army keeps its desert water here: steel tanks on stilts, filled by a pump engine from a deep bore. Every patrol draws its ration and signs for it, and the guard does not let anyone forget.

areas.name: Bore Engine House
areas.text: The engine house of the bore pump, hot and loud.

areas.name: Tank Stilts
areas.text: The row of tall tanks and the ladders up them.

locations.name: Desert Well Basin
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: Severe]

A basin in the desert where a little water collects after rain and reeds grow around its edges. It is the only green place for a day's ride and the caravans camp on it when they can.

areas.name: Basin Water
areas.text: The shallow pool, cloudy and warm.

areas.name: Reed Edge
areas.text: The ring of reeds around the water, thick with flies.

locations.name: Devil's Nest
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A large pub on the bad side of Dublith, dark wood and card tables, run by a crew of hard-looking outcasts who seem to hear everything that moves in the country's underworld. Doors in its cellars open onto passages nobody maps.

areas.name: Card Room
areas.text: The back room of card tables, smoke and quiet voices.

areas.name: Front Bar
areas.text: The bar room with its red lamps and its long counter.

locations.name: Diggers' Camp
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A camp of bell tents beside the market ruins, where a team sent from the capital digs, sieves and labels what the sand gives up. The leader keeps a tidy table of finds and a less tidy temper.

areas.name: Finds Tent
areas.text: The big tent with the folding table and the labelled trays.

areas.name: Sieve Lines
areas.text: The rows of sieves and barrows where the sand is sifted.

locations.name: Dockside Free Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-16 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A doctor who would not work for the army keeps a free clinic by the docks for bargemen, laundresses and anyone else the military hospital will not see. She pays for it from donations and her own pocket.

areas.name: Clinic Doorstep
areas.text: The doorstep where the queue starts before dawn.

areas.name: Whitewashed Ward
areas.text: A room of six cots, whitewashed walls and the smell of carbolic.

locations.name: Dr. Knox's House
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-24 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The untidy house of a military coroner who drinks too much, sleeps too little and has seen every way a body can end. He left his wife and son years ago, after the war followed him into his sleep. Dr. Knox does not like visitors, and visitors who come anyway find him cutting someone open on the kitchen table.

areas.name: Knox House Back Bedroom
areas.text: A dusty back room with a cot, used for patients who must not be seen.

areas.name: Knox House Kitchen Surgery
areas.text: A kitchen table scrubbed for surgery, a lamp on a chain and a bucket beneath.

locations.name: Drachma
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High]

The large country to the north, behind the Briggs range: a belligerent state that has fought Amestris on and off for generations. A pact of non-aggression signed early in the century holds, shakily, and every border incident threatens it. Its soldiers are hardened by the same winter the garrison knows.

areas.name: Border Road
areas.text: The fortified road south to the frontier, lined with sentry posts.

areas.name: Frontier Town
areas.text: The first town across the border, with its barracks and its shuttered inns.

locations.name: Drachman Border Blockhouse
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

A blockhouse of thick logs on the Drachman side of the border, its loopholes facing the fort. Its garrison of a dozen men changes every fortnight and sometimes waves to the Briggs patrols, and sometimes does not.

areas.name: Blockhouse Loophole Room
areas.text: The log-walled room behind the rifle loopholes, with a stove and a rack of rifles.

areas.name: Blockhouse Striped Barrier
areas.text: A striped pole across the track, with a sentry box beside it.

locations.name: Drachman Siege Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

A Drachman army camp in the hollows across the border, out of the fort's range, with tents for thousands and guns hidden under white sheets. Its commander keeps it ready to move on a day's notice.

areas.name: Siege Camp Command Tent
areas.text: A large tent with maps on a trestle table and a banner at its door.

areas.name: Siege Camp Tent Lines
areas.text: Rows of grey canvas tents dug into the snow, with stoves and steaming chimneys.

locations.name: Dragon's Pulse Peaks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High]

The highest mountains of Xing stand north of the capital, still snow-capped when the plains are hot. The Xingese hold that the life of the earth runs down from peaks like these as blood runs through veins, and they call that flow the Dragon's Pulse.

areas.name: Pulse Peaks Snowline Camp
areas.text: Stone windbreaks and a fire pit at the last level ground below the snow.

areas.name: Warriors' Listening Ledge
areas.text: A bare ledge over the drop where trainees sit blindfolded for hours.

locations.name: Dry Canal of Xerxes
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-30 · Danger: Severe]

A channel wide enough for three carts runs through the desert east of the ruins, banked with spoil on both sides. The desert peoples say the last king had it dug against drought. It carries no water and the curve of it goes on past sight.

areas.name: Spoil Banks
areas.text: The long heaped banks on either side, high enough to hide a camel.

areas.name: Trench Floor
areas.text: The flat floor of the channel, cool in the morning shade of its walls.

locations.name: Dry Lake Bed
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-30 · Danger: Severe]

Herders swear their grandfathers fished here. The lake is long gone: its bed is white clay split into tiles the size of a hand, and at noon a false lake shimmers over it so convincingly that animals pull toward it. Halfway across lie the ribs of a wooden boat, bleached grey.

areas.name: Boat Bones
areas.text: The ribs of a wooden boat in the middle of the lake bed.

areas.name: Cracked Clay
areas.text: The flat tiles of white clay.

locations.name: Dry Riverbed
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A riverbed south of South City that runs dry for most of the year, a channel of stones between banks of scrub. Patrols use it for cover and the herders use it for water in the wet season.

areas.name: Scrub Bank
areas.text: The bank of scrub where the patrols take cover.

areas.name: Stone Bed
areas.text: The channel of white stones, hot and open.

locations.name: Dry Well Waystation
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: Severe]

A shelter of stone at a dry well on the desert road. The well has not given water for a season, and the keeper sells what he has in bottles at a price that makes travellers swear.

areas.name: Dry Well Pit
areas.text: The well with its empty bucket and its broken windlass.

areas.name: Stone Shelter
areas.text: The shelter with its benches and its shuttered window.

locations.name: Dublith
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A warm town in the middle of the southern area on the shore of Kauroy Lake, its chief sight for visitors. Fishermen, shopkeepers and butchers live side by side on the good side of town; the bad side has its own bars and its own rules.

areas.name: Dublith Market
areas.text: The square market of fish, meat and iron, busy in the mornings.

areas.name: Lakeside Pier
areas.text:
The wooden pier where the fishing boats tie up and the island ferry leaves.

The rail and coach service serves this yard: coaches run to Central City (about 14 Cens), South City (about 12 Cens); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Station Road
areas.text: The road up from the pier to the small rail halt.

locations.name: Dublith Abattoir
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low]

The slaughterhouse on the east edge of Dublith that supplies the town's butchers, Curtis Meats among them. It is scrubbed down twice a day, and the men there know Sig Curtis as the butcher who carries a side of beef on each shoulder.

areas.name: Dublith Carcass Room
areas.text: A cool room of carcasses hung on rails, waiting for the butchers' carts.

areas.name: Dublith Killing Floor
areas.text: A sloping tiled floor running to drains, sluiced every hour.

locations.name: Dublith Brick Kilns
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low]

Clay pits and kilns north-west of the town where Dublith's red bricks and roof tiles are fired. Half the houses in town are built of them, and the other half wish they were.

areas.name: Dublith Clay Pit
areas.text: A raw red pit with planks and barrows at the bottom.

areas.name: Dublith Kiln Firing Yard
areas.text: Bottle kilns smoking among stacks of finished brick.

locations.name: Dublith Cattle Pens
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low]

Wooden pens beside the rail sidings where cattle from the southern farms are unloaded and sold before they walk up to the abattoir. On sale days drovers and buyers shout at each other across the rails.

areas.name: Dublith Cattle Ramp
areas.text: A plank ramp from the wagons down to the pens.

areas.name: Dublith Cattle Sale Ring
areas.text: A ring of rails where cattle are walked round and bid on.

locations.name: Dublith Chapel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small chapel on the hill above Dublith with a bell tower and a wall of votive plaques from the fishermen who came home. The priest is an old man who remembers every boat by name.

areas.name: Bell Tower
areas.text: The tower and its bell, rung for each lost boat.

areas.name: Dublith Chapel Hall
areas.text: The whitewashed hall with its pews and the wall of plaques.

locations.name: Dublith Fig Orchards
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low]

Walled orchards of figs and lemons on the warm slopes west of Dublith, picked by families from town in late summer. The fruit goes north on the trains packed in straw.

areas.name: Dublith Fig Rows
areas.text: Rows of broad-leaved figs between dry-stone walls.

areas.name: Dublith Fruit Packing Shed
areas.text: A shed of crates, straw and women packing fruit.

locations.name: Dublith Low Wharf
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-8 · Danger: Low]

The bad side's stretch of waterfront, rotten jetties and shuttered drinking dens below the respectable piers. Boats tie up here that never come in to the fish hall.

areas.name: Low Wharf Nameless Jetties
areas.text: Jetties with missing boards, boats tied up without names.

areas.name: Low Wharf One-Lamp Den
areas.text: A low room with one lamp, one bottle and many eyes.

locations.name: Dublith Military Police Post
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-7 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A two-room post of the military police with a lock-up at the back, the only uniform in Dublith most days. The sergeant reads the newspaper on the step and lets the bad side keep its own order.

areas.name: Dublith Police Cells
areas.text: Two barred cells smelling of lake water and old drink.

areas.name: Dublith Police Front Room
areas.text: A desk, a telephone and a map of the town pinned to the wall.

locations.name: Dublith Post and Telegraph Office
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The office where Dublith posts its letters and sends its telegrams, one clerk at the key and another at the counter. In the season half the post is picture cards of Kauroy Lake going north.

areas.name: Dublith Sorting Room
areas.text: A back room of sacks and pigeonholes, sorted by lamplight.

areas.name: Dublith Telegraph Counter
areas.text: A brass-grilled counter and the clicking key behind it.

locations.name: Dublith Rail Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

The freight sidings at the south end of Dublith, with cargo sheds and a few wagons waiting for the next run north. The yardmen drink in the shed at lunch and nobody minds.

areas.name: Cargo Shed
areas.text: The shed of crates and sacks, dark and dusty.

areas.name: Siding Track
areas.text: The sidings where the wagons wait, with tar-black sleepers.

locations.name: Dublith Schoolhouse
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A one-storey school on the slope above the market, where fishermen's and shopkeepers' children learn their letters and sums. The schoolmistress keeps a jar of frogs on the windowsill for nature lessons.

areas.name: Dublith School Yard
areas.text: A dusty yard with a bell post and a fig tree for shade.

areas.name: Dublith Schoolroom
areas.text: Rows of desks, a blackboard and a stove for the cold months.

locations.name: Dublith Sewers
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-10 · Danger: Low]

The old brick sewers under the bad side of Dublith, a maze of drains, culverts and dead ends running down to the lake. Townsfolk keep away from the grates, but the men from the bar on the corner seem to know every turning.

areas.name: Dublith Chalked Passage
areas.text: A dry passage marked with arrows and signs only the crew can read.

areas.name: Dublith Culvert Junction
areas.text: A round chamber where four drains meet under a grating.

areas.name: Dublith Sewer Outfall
areas.text: The mouth where the tunnels spill into the lake behind a rusted grille.

locations.name: Dublith Tannery
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low]

The tannery downwind of the abattoir, where hides from the town's butchers soak for weeks in pits of bark and lime. Nobody lives near it by choice, and the tanners drink in a bar of their own.

areas.name: Dublith Hide Lofts
areas.text: Slatted lofts where hides hang in the wind off the lake.

areas.name: Dublith Tan Pits
areas.text: An open yard of sunken pits, brown liquor and long poles.

locations.name: Dublith Town Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-5 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The town doctor's house and surgery, three rooms behind a brass plate near the market. Fish hooks, butchers' cuts and summer fevers make up most of his work.

areas.name: Dublith Clinic Surgery
areas.text: A scrubbed room with a couch, a basin and a cabinet of instruments.

areas.name: Dublith Clinic Waiting Bench
areas.text: A bench in the hall under a calendar from a seed merchant.

locations.name: Dune Sea
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: Severe]

The sea of dunes that fills the middle of the desert, shifting with every wind. Caravans navigate by the stars and by bones left in the sand, and the dunes swallow tracks within a day.

areas.name: Crest Road
areas.text: The ridge of the largest dune, where the caravans are most exposed.

areas.name: Hollow Floor
areas.text: The sheltered hollow between dunes, where the wind is quieter.

locations.name: Dust Lane Market
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-9 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A lane of stalls behind the square where the wives sell eggs, mended shirts and whatever the goats gave this week. It is the one place in town where the lieutenant's store does not set the price.

areas.name: Dust Lane Egg Stalls
areas.text: Trestles of eggs, cheese and mended clothing under grey awnings.

areas.name: Dust Lane Pump Corner
areas.text: The corner where the lane meets the pump and the women trade news.

locations.name: Eagle Crag Lookout
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-24 · Danger: High]

From this crag a man with field glasses can see most of the border hills and a slice of Creta beyond. The army keeps two men up here in a stone hut with a heliograph, and changes them every week.

areas.name: Eagle Crag Summit
areas.text: The bare top of the crag with its view of the hills.

areas.name: Heliograph Hut
areas.text: The stone hut where the mirror and its stand are kept.

locations.name: Eaglehead Crag
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

A crag shaped like a hooked beak east of the fort, where eagles nest and a spotting post looks down on both sides of the border. Climbers from the garrison practise on its face in summer.

areas.name: Eaglehead Nest Ledge
areas.text: A narrow ledge below the top where eagles build their great nests.

areas.name: Eaglehead Spotting Post
areas.text: An iron frame with a telescope and a flag box, bolted to the crag's top.

locations.name: East City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The military command base of the eastern area, on the Marl River. Many call it a backwater with no future, yet its army is the strongest offensive force in Amestris: the east bore the heaviest load of the Ishval war and its ranks are full of veterans. Colonel Mustang's unit is posted here, and the Fullmetal Alchemist files his reports at its headquarters.

areas.name: Drill Ground
areas.text: The open parade ground in front of the barracks, scraped bare and dusty.

areas.name: East Station
areas.text:
The rail halt at the city's edge, with its tram stop and its noisy yard.

The rail and coach service serves this yard: coaches run to Central City (about 14 Cens), Resembool (about 6 Cens), Youswell (about 12 Cens), Ishval (about 10 Cens); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Veterans' Row
areas.text: The street of narrow houses where the veterans of the Ishval war drink and argue.

locations.name: East City Engine Roundhouse
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A great round shed where the locomotives of the eastern lines are cleaned, repaired and turned around. The fitters are proud men and the army's demands on their engines make them angry.

areas.name: Roundhouse Ash Heaps
areas.text: A dusty yard where the fireboxes are emptied and the ash piles up.

areas.name: Roundhouse Engine Bays
areas.text: Stalls around the turntable where engines rest over inspection pits.

locations.name: East City Gasworks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The gasworks that light the city's streets and the officers' houses, fed with coal from the wharf by a little railway. The gasholders rise and fall each day, and children say you can tell the time by them.

areas.name: Marl Gasworks Holder Yard
areas.text: A yard of great round gasholders inside iron frames.

areas.name: Marl Gasworks Retort Bench
areas.text: A long hall of furnaces where coal is baked into gas and coke.

locations.name: East City Ishvalan Slum
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate]

Where the city's drains empty into the Marl River, a few hundred Ishvalans who fled the war live in shacks built from crates and roofing tin. The garrison pretends the place is not there, and the people in it keep it that way by never giving the soldiers a reason to look.

areas.name: Slum Elder's Lean-To
areas.text: An open-sided shelter where the elder hears quarrels and keeps the slum's one lamp.

areas.name: Slum Outfall Shingle
areas.text: A strip of pebbles under the great brick sewer mouth, where the children fish for scrap.

areas.name: Slum Patched Shacks
areas.text: Crooked rows of crate-wood huts, every one mended with something different.

locations.name: East City Stockyards
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

Pens and slaughterhouses by the railway where cattle from the eastern farms are bought for the army's kitchens. The noise begins before dawn and the smell goes on all day.

areas.name: Stockyard Holding Pens
areas.text: Rows of wooden pens with cattle waiting for the buyers.

areas.name: Stockyard Killing Floor
areas.text: A tiled hall with hooks and drains, washed down with hoses at the end of the day.

locations.name: East City Telephone Exchange
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Every telephone line in the city runs through this narrow building, where rows of operators push plugs into boards from dawn to midnight. The army owns two of the boards outright and keeps a soldier standing behind them.

areas.name: Marl Exchange Cable Vault
areas.text: A cellar where the city's wires come in through the wall in thick black bundles.

areas.name: Marl Exchange Switchboard Room
areas.text: Tall boards of jacks and lamps with a row of stools in front of them.

locations.name: East City Town Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The civilian government of the city keeps its offices behind a grand front, though every decree it posts has passed a general's desk first. Births, deaths, rents and permits are written up here, and the mayor is courteous to every uniform.

areas.name: Town Hall Council Chamber
areas.text: A panelled room of curved benches where the council meets and decides little.

areas.name: Town Hall Registry Office
areas.text: Books of births and deaths and a long counter where people queue for certificates.

locations.name: East City Worsted Mill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A wool mill where the fleece of the Resembool sheep is spun and woven into cloth for the army's coats. Its looms run in shifts, its girls come from every village between here and the hills, and its bell rules the streets around it.

areas.name: Worsted Mill Spinning Floor
areas.text: A long floor of spinning frames and girls walking between them.

areas.name: Worsted Mill Wool Store
areas.text: A loft of bales stacked to the rafters, smelling of sheep and lanolin.

locations.name: East Road Coaching Inn
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 3-8 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

Halfway on the coach road from East City, this inn changes the horses and feeds the passengers who could not get a seat on the train. Its stables are bigger than its dining room.

areas.name: Coaching Inn Dining Room
areas.text: A long table under the beams where passengers eat in their coats.

areas.name: Coaching Inn Stable Yard
areas.text: A cobbled yard with a pump, a stable block and a coach waiting on its shafts.

locations.name: Eastbound Cistern
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

The last sure water before the long empty stretch toward Xing is held in a domed cistern with a stone lid. Every caravan scratches its tally on the wall when it fills up, and the wall is covered.

areas.name: Cistern Lid
areas.text: The heavy stone lid and its chains, worked by two people.

areas.name: Tally Wall
areas.text: The wall of scratched marks, one for every caravan that drank.

locations.name: Eastern Barracks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The barracks of the East City garrison, long blocks of bunks, mess halls and stores. The men are hard and proud, and newcomers are given the worst beds until they earn better.

areas.name: Bunk Hall
areas.text: The long room of iron bunks and footlockers.

areas.name: Mess Hall
areas.text: The long tables and the cook's hatch, loud at meal times.

locations.name: Eastern Border Post
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The border post on the far eastern side of the empire, where the road leaves for the lands beyond Xing and the officers check every cart and rider. Their papers are in order and their patience is short.

areas.name: Ford Crossing
areas.text: The shallow river ford beside the post, with its stones.

areas.name: Post Gate
areas.text: The stone gate with its flags and its book.

locations.name: Eastern Command Headquarters
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The headquarters of the eastern military command, a squat block of offices with a guarded gate and a parade ground in front. Its generals run the district's patrols and its files on the Ishvalan refugees.

areas.name: Headquarters Gate
areas.text: The gate with its sentry box and its visitors' book.

areas.name: Records Room
areas.text: The records of the east, locked in steel cabinets.

locations.name: Eastern Command Motor Pool
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A tin-roofed shed where the garrison keeps its handful of motor lorries and two staff cars. The machines are newer than the men who drive them, and half of every week is spent getting one of them to start.

areas.name: Motor Pool Lorry Shed
areas.text: Lorries nose to tail under the tin roof, with tools hanging on every post.

areas.name: Motor Pool Petrol Store
areas.text: A brick hut of red drums with a sand bucket by the door and no smoking allowed.

locations.name: Eastern Command Rifle Range
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A long strip of rough ground behind the drill ground with firing points at one end and an earth bank at the other. The garrison qualifies here every season, and Hawkeye's scores are pinned up in the hut as a dare.

areas.name: Rifle Range Firing Points
areas.text: Sandbagged mats at measured distances, each with a chalked number.

areas.name: Rifle Range Target Butts
areas.text: A trench under the bank where markers raise and patch the paper targets.

locations.name: Eastern Command Stockade
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The military prison of the eastern command, a squat walled block where deserters, drunks and captured rebels wait on a court-martial. Its cells are cold and its sergeants are bored, which is worse for the prisoners than cruelty.

areas.name: Stockade Iron Cells
areas.text: A corridor of iron doors with slots at eye level and a drain down the middle.

areas.name: Stockade Walking Yard
areas.text: A bare square of beaten earth where prisoners walk in a circle for an hour a day.

locations.name: Eastern Command Troop Sidings
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A fan of sidings beside the main line where the garrison loads men and horses for the eastern frontier. Whole companies can be put on the rails here within an hour, which the eastern officers say with some pride and the capital notes with less.

areas.name: Troop Sidings Loading Ramps
areas.text: Timber ramps up to the wagon doors, scarred by hooves and hobnails.

areas.name: Troop Sidings Yard Office
areas.text: A hut of telegraph keys, chalked boards and a stove that never goes out.

locations.name: Eastern Courier Press
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The city's daily paper is set, printed and folded in this building on the square, and its newsboys are out before the trams. It prints what the garrison permits and hides the rest in the advertisements, where only regular readers look.

areas.name: Courier Composing Room
areas.text: Cases of metal type and a stone table where pages are locked into frames.

areas.name: Courier Editor's Den
areas.text: A glass-walled office over the press floor, papers on every surface and a blue pencil.

locations.name: Eastern Customs House
locations.info:
