[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Every load bound east or west is weighed and written down at this whitewashed office. The barrier pole across the road is painted in stripes, and the clerks inside work in shirtsleeves under a slow ceiling fan.

areas.name: Barrier Pole
areas.text: The striped pole across the road and the sentry who lifts it.

areas.name: Weighing Room
areas.text: The office where every load is weighed and entered.

locations.name: Eastern Farm Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

The farm road that runs from Resembool up toward the East City highway, lined with gates, barns and small fields. Carts use it to take the wool and the hay to the station.

areas.name: Farm Gate
areas.text: The first gate of the road, with a sign and a lantern.

areas.name: Hay Barn
areas.text: The big barn at the bend, full of hay in summer.

locations.name: Eastern Gate Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The road that leaves East City for the east and the north, with a gatehouse where papers are checked and every cart is searched. Traffic is heavy in the mornings and thin after dark.

areas.name: Checkpoint Barrier
areas.text: The barrier of pole and chain across the road.

areas.name: Eastern Gatehouse
areas.text: The stone gate with its guardroom and its lamp.

locations.name: Eastern Harbour Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The road from the capital to the river port, lined with inns and porters' huts. Barges carry tea and iron down the river from the mountains, and the porters carry the goods to the carts.

areas.name: Inn Row
areas.text: The row of inns that serve the road's travellers.

areas.name: Porters' Quay
areas.text: The stone quay where the barges unload and the porters wait.

locations.name: Eastern Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The city's great market, a covered hall of fish, vegetables and cheap tools, with stalls spilling into the square outside. Soldiers buy their supper here and the traders know them all.

areas.name: Market Hall
areas.text: The covered hall with its iron roof and its rows of stalls.

areas.name: Outer Square
areas.text: The square outside, where the carts unload at dawn.

locations.name: Eastern Military Cemetery
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A walled field outside the old city where the eastern command buries its own. The rows from the Ishval years run on and on, and some of the stones carry no name at all, only a rank and a year.

areas.name: East Cemetery Gate Lodge
areas.text: A gatekeeper's cottage with the burial book on a lectern by the door.

areas.name: East Cemetery Ishval Rows
areas.text: The long rows of plain white stones from the war years, all the same height.

locations.name: Eastern Military Hospital
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The military hospital of East City, where the garrison's wounded and sick are treated. Its wards are full with men from the front and the drill ground alike.

areas.name: Dispensary
areas.text: The small room of bottles and bandages behind a grille.

areas.name: Ward Three
areas.text: The long ward of cots and screens, quiet in the afternoons.

locations.name: Eastern Remount Depot
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

Paddocks on the city's western edge where the army buys, breaks and keeps its horses for the eastern patrols. Horse dealers from the farm country come in every month and argue with the depot captain over the height of every animal.

areas.name: Remount Depot Farriery
areas.text: A smoky forge where cavalry shoes are fitted by the dozen.

areas.name: Remount Depot Paddocks
areas.text: Wide grass enclosures where green horses run off the morning before training.

locations.name: Eastern Tenements
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High]

The poor streets of the capital's east, a crush of brick tenements where the families of clerks and labourers live and where soldiers are rarely seen after dark.

areas.name: Back Alleys
areas.text: The alleys that run behind the blocks, unlit and busy at night.

areas.name: Tenement Yard
areas.text: The courtyard between the blocks with its well and its washing.

locations.name: Eastern Tram Depot
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The depot where the city's trams are kept, cars in rows and a repair shed that smells of oil. The drivers know every line and will take a passenger for a fee.

areas.name: Car Shed
areas.text: The long shed of tram cars and their wheels.

areas.name: Repair Pit
areas.text: The pit under the cars where the mechanics work by lamplight.

locations.name: Eastern War Orphans' Home
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A charity house for the children of soldiers who did not come back from the eastern war, kept going by the officers' wives and a grant that shrinks a little every year. The children know the drill-ground bugle calls better than lullabies.

areas.name: Orphans' Home Kitchen Garden
areas.text: Beds of beans and potatoes the older children tend with borrowed tools.

areas.name: Orphans' Home Long Dormitory
areas.text: A long attic room of iron cots, each with a folded blanket and a box underneath.

locations.name: Eastgate Brewery
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A brewery at the city gate whose pale beer is drunk in every barracks and bar in the east. The brewer is a veteran and gives the veterans' hall its beer at cost.

areas.name: Eastgate Barrel Cellar
areas.text: A cool vaulted cellar full of barrels and one locked door at the end.

areas.name: Eastgate Brew House
areas.text: A tall room of copper vats and steam, with a ladder up to the mash tun.

locations.name: Elder Shan's Camp
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 16-22 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small band of Ishvalan refugees lives among the columns of the ruins, under canvas strung from stone to stone. Their elder, Shan, is a priestess with a cane and a patch over one eye. Strangers are watched hard here, and Amestrians harder.

areas.name: Canvas Lines
areas.text: Rows of shelters made from canvas and fallen stone.

areas.name: Elder's Seat
areas.text: A flat block of stone under an awning, where Shan hears her people.

locations.name: Elixir Apothecaries' Street
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Every shop on this street is a wall of small drawers holding roots, dried seahorses and powdered shell. The apothecaries mix tonics to old recipes and label a few as elixirs of long life, though the whole city knows how the old emperors ended.

areas.name: Apothecaries' Drawer Walls
areas.text: Shopfronts lined floor to ceiling with labelled drawers.

areas.name: Elixir Street Back Counters
areas.text: The low counters at the back of the shops where the stronger tonics are kept.

locations.name: Elric House
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The Elric family's house on the edge of Resembool, where Trisha Elric raised her two sons after their father left. In October 1911 the brothers burned it to the ground themselves, so there would be no home to turn back to; after that only the blackened shell, the porch steps and the overgrown garden remain.

areas.name: Kitchen Garden
areas.text: Trisha's old vegetable and herb beds behind the house, gone to weeds inside the hedges.

areas.name: Porch
areas.text: The stone steps of the old front porch, all that stands clear of the ash.

locations.name: Envoy's Rest
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe]

A ring of stones on a rise where Xingese envoys used to camp on the way west. A broken litter lies in the middle, and passers-by add stones to a cairn for the travellers who never arrived.

areas.name: Offering Cairn
areas.text: The heap of stones left by passing travellers.

areas.name: Stone Ring
areas.text: The ring of stones that marks the camp.

locations.name: Ever-Full Granaries
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The Emperor's granaries stand by the canal, long storehouses raised on stone piers against damp and rats. They hold the grain that feeds the capital in a bad year, and the clerks count the sacks by the thousand.

areas.name: Ever-Full Storehouse Rows
areas.text: Rows of raised storehouses with sliding doors and ladders.

areas.name: Granary Clerks' Counting House
areas.text: The office where sacks are tallied on long boards.

locations.name: Exiles' Track
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

The track the Ishvalan refugees took from their burned country to the ruins of Xerxes runs north through the sand. Cairns mark it every mile, and each has a name scratched on it.

areas.name: Broken Sandal Rest
areas.text: The rest place where the walkers sit.

areas.name: Cairn Mile
areas.text: A stretch of the track with its name-scratched cairn.

locations.name: Far Bank Inn
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

On the eastern side of the desert, where the sand starts to give way to stone, stands a low wooden inn kept by Xingese. It is the first bed many travellers from Amestris have seen in weeks, and the cook's noodles are famous on both sides of the sand.

areas.name: Noodle Hearth
areas.text: The kitchen hearth and its long bench, always steaming.

areas.name: Sleeping Mats
areas.text: The back room of mats and folded quilts.

locations.name: Fir Hill Brewery
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A brewery on a fir-covered slope west of the city, brewing the dark beer every tavern in the north serves. Its cellars are cut into the hill and stay cold all year.

areas.name: Fir Hill Cellars
areas.text: The cold cellars cut into the hill, where the barrels rest in rows.

areas.name: Fir Hill Copper House
areas.text: The brewhouse of copper vats and steam, smelling of malt.

locations.name: First Branch Ruins
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High]

The blackened shell of the National Central Library's First Branch, which went up in flames one night and took every volume inside with it. The library has roped off the gate and posted a notice; the cause of the fire is officially unknown.

areas.name: First Branch Burnt Hall
areas.text: The roofless reading hall, ash underfoot and iron shelf frames standing bare.

areas.name: First Branch Cellar Stair
areas.text: A stair down to the flooded cellar where a few books survived.

locations.name: Flat-Top Mesa
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe]

Alone over the dunes stands a tall rock with a top as flat as a parade ground. Only a goat path goes up, switching back and forth across the north face. Whoever sits on top sees the crossing, the fort's tower and, on a clear morning, the broken dome of Xerxes far to the south-east.

areas.name: Goat Path
areas.text: The narrow path that climbs the rock in tight turns.

areas.name: Mesa Top
areas.text: The flat summit, bare rock and wind, with the whole desert below.

areas.name: Watcher's Cache
areas.text: A cleft near the edge, stoppered with a flat stone.

locations.name: Flooded Number Three Pit
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 11-16 · Danger: Moderate]

An old shaft abandoned when it struck water, its headframe rusting and its gate nailed shut. The water in the shaft lies a long way down and smells of iron.

areas.name: Number Three Gate
areas.text: The nailed gate and the warning boards, half rotted away.

areas.name: Number Three Shaft Lip
areas.text: The edge of the shaft and the black water far below.

locations.name: Fort Briggs
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Amestris' first garrison against Drachma: a single immense wall stretched across the narrow valley where the mountains leave a gap, holding labs, a prison, gun positions, quarters, supply tunnels and one great tunnel down its length. Anyone passing between the two countries must go through it. To the people of Amestris the name means strength, and soldiers shiver at a posting here.

areas.name: Commander's Keep
areas.text: The command rooms high in the wall, their windows looking north at Drachma, lit all night.

areas.name: Fort Gate
areas.text:
The great gate on the Amestrian face of the wall, with its sentries and the supply road from North City.

The rail and coach service serves this yard: coaches run to North City (about 9 Cens); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Parade Yard
areas.text: The yard of packed snow inside the wall where the garrison drills before the wind rises.

locations.name: Fort Escort Yard
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The walled yard behind headquarters where travellers bound for Fort Briggs wait for the fort's own escort to come down and fetch them. The fort keeps its own schedule, and the waiting room has seen men sit there three days.

areas.name: Escort Sledge Bay
areas.text: The covered bay where the escort's sledges and dogs rest between trips.

areas.name: Escort Waiting Room
areas.text: A plain room with a bench, a stove and a window onto the yard gate.

locations.name: Forward Dressing Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A dugout behind the line where the wounded are patched before the long ride back to South City. A surgeon and two orderlies work here by lamplight when the shelling is heavy.

areas.name: Dressing Dugout
areas.text: A low dugout of sandbags, lamps and a bloody table.

areas.name: Stretcher Yard
areas.text: The trampled ground where stretchers wait for the carts.

locations.name: Fotset
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The town whose taking started the war with Aerugo. It is now a line of ruins and ash held by whichever army is winning that month, with a few families still living in the cellars.

areas.name: Cellars
areas.text: The cellars where the families hide from the shells.

areas.name: Market Ruins
areas.text: The square of broken stalls and blackened walls.

locations.name: Fotset Chapel Ruin
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The shell of Fotset's old chapel at the edge of the ruined town, its roof gone and its bell lying cracked in the nave. Soldiers of both sides have scratched their names into its walls.

areas.name: Roofless Nave
areas.text: Open sky over broken pews and a fallen bell.

areas.name: Scratched Wall
areas.text: A wall covered with names, dates and messages in two languages.

locations.name: Fotset Rail Bridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 13-17 · Danger: Moderate]

The iron bridge that once carried the line from Fotset south into Aerugo, blown when the Amestrian push was driven back to the town. Its girders hang into the ravine and both armies watch it in case the other tries to mend it.

areas.name: Bridge Ravine
areas.text: The dry ravine beneath, littered with fallen iron.

areas.name: Broken Span
areas.text: The girders reaching out over nothing.

locations.name: Fotset Refugee Tents
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A camp of patched tents along the road east of the front, where the people driven out of Fotset have lived for three years. A charity from South City runs a soup kitchen and the army runs a register.

areas.name: Refugee Tent Rows
areas.text: Lanes of tents patched with sacking and army blankets.

areas.name: Soup Kitchen
areas.text: A canvas awning, a great pot and a long queue.

locations.name: Fountain Promenade
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-11 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A tiled walk of fountains and potted palms laid out in the years of peace, when the south still drew holidaymakers from the capital. Couples stroll it in the evening while a band from the barracks plays on the bandstand.

areas.name: Lion Fountain
areas.text: The largest fountain, a stone lion spouting into a wide basin.

areas.name: Promenade Bandstand
areas.text: A green iron bandstand where the regimental band plays.

locations.name: Frontier Customs House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

Where the old trade road crosses the border, a customs house of stone checks what little legal traffic still passes between Amestris and Creta. Merchants wait for days for the officer's stamp.

areas.name: Frontier Barrier Pole
areas.text: The striped pole across the road and the merchants waiting behind it.

areas.name: Frontier Stamp Counter
areas.text: The counter where papers are read and stamped, or not.

locations.name: Frontier Pinewood
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-15 · Danger: Moderate]

A pinewood west of the town that supplies the mine's props and the town's firewood. It is quieter than anywhere else in the district and the miners walk here on their day off.

areas.name: Pinewood Deep Stand
areas.text: A stand of old pines where the light barely reaches.

areas.name: Pinewood Logging Track
areas.text: A rutted track between stumps where the log carts run.

locations.name: Frostline Outpost
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

A small outpost high on the range, a hut and a flag pole that watch the road to Drachma. Its two men are changed every month and do not look forward to the change.

areas.name: Signal Pole
areas.text: The flag pole above the hut, with its wind-torn flag.

areas.name: Watch Hut
areas.text: The timber hut with its stove and its telescope.

locations.name: Frostworks Automail
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

An automail workshop that specialises in limbs for the cold: lighter alloys that do not freeze to the skin, sealed joints that keep out snowmelt. Soldiers from the fort come down to have their ports checked before winter.

areas.name: Cold Test Shed
areas.text: A shed left unheated on purpose, where new limbs are tested in the frost.

areas.name: Frostworks Fitting Bench
areas.text: The bench by the window where ports are checked and limbs attached.

locations.name: Frozen Lake
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A lake north of the city, frozen solid from autumn to spring, with fishing huts dotted across its ice. Men drive sleds across it in winter, and a careless one goes through.

areas.name: Ice Sheet
areas.text: The white plain of the lake with its huts and its sled tracks.

areas.name: Pine Shore
areas.text: The shore of dark pines where the huts are built.

locations.name: Führer's Residence
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-26 · Danger: High]

The official home of King Bradley, set in walled gardens near the command compound. His wife lives here with their adopted son Selim, a polite boy who wants to be like his father; Mrs. Bradley takes tea on the lawn and receives callers with real warmth. The guard at the gate is changed every four hours.

areas.name: Führer's Residence Drawing Room
areas.text: A sunny drawing room of family portraits, a sword rack above the hearth.

areas.name: Führer's Residence Front Lawn
areas.text: The lawn and gravel drive, with a wicker table set for tea.

areas.name: Führer's Residence Gatehouse
areas.text: The sentry box and iron gate on the avenue.

locations.name: Garrison Park
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A public park laid out for the garrison band, with a bandstand, a boating pond and benches under chestnut trees. On rest days it is full of families; the rest of the week, of old soldiers feeding the ducks.

areas.name: Garrison Park Bandstand
areas.text: A green iron bandstand with a pointed roof and folding chairs set out in front.

areas.name: Garrison Park Boating Pond
areas.text: A round pond with hired rowing boats and a stone edge where children sail toy ships.

locations.name: Garrison Steam Baths
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A public bathhouse near the barracks where soldiers sweat out their leave and veterans soak their bad legs. Rank is left in the changing room, and things are said in the steam that would never be said on the drill ground.

areas.name: Steam Baths Hot Room
areas.text: A tiled room of benches lost in steam, too hot to stay in for long.

areas.name: Steam Baths Plunge Pool
areas.text: A cold stone pool under a skylight where men gasp and swear.

locations.name: Gate Road Trading Post
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A hundred yards past the border gate, a trader with a wide hat and a mule cart has built himself a shack and sells whatever the road needs: water by the cup, flatbread, tobacco, bootlaces, lamp oil. The soldiers at the gate are his best customers and pretend not to see who else buys from him.

areas.name: Gate Road Mule Yard
areas.text: A pen behind the shack where his mule and cart stand.

areas.name: Gate Road Tin Awning Counter
areas.text: The shaded counter of the shack and the blanket of goods before it.

locations.name: Gate Ward Guardhouse
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The guardhouse by the northern gate, where the military police check papers on the road out and lock up drunks and pickpockets overnight. The sergeant in charge has seen everything at least once.

areas.name: Gate Ward Cell
areas.text: The cell at the back with its straw mat and its bucket.

areas.name: Gate Ward Papers Desk
areas.text: The front desk where travellers show their papers under a hanging lamp.

locations.name: Ginseng Slopes
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

The cool north faces above the capital grow wild ginseng, and the diggers who find it use bone picks so as not to bruise the root. An old root is a fortune and is guarded like one.

areas.name: Ginseng Shade Hollows
areas.text: Damp hollows under the trees where the roots grow.

areas.name: Root Diggers' Camp
areas.text: A camp of lean-tos where diggers dry and wrap their finds.

locations.name: Glass Flats
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: Severe]

Flats of fused glassy sand where the heat makes mirages and the light blinds the unprepared. Caravans cross them at night and rest in the shade of the rocks.

areas.name: Glass Field
areas.text: The flat plain of glassy sand that shines like a lake.

areas.name: Shade Rocks
areas.text: The outcrop of rock where the caravans wait out the day.

locations.name: Glasswater Tarn
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A mountain lake west of the fort that freezes a metre thick, where ice cutters saw blocks in midwinter and haul them down to North City's ice houses. The ice is so clear that a man can see fish under his boots.

areas.name: Tarn Block Stacks
areas.text: Rows of ice blocks at the shore, packed in sawdust and waiting for the sleds.

areas.name: Tarn Cutting Field
areas.text: The open ice where blocks are sawn out in a grid of black channels.

locations.name: Glotz Pawn Shop
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A pawn shop in the West Alley of Rush Valley, crowded with costly things beside old tools, where the owner knows stolen goods when he sees them and buys them anyway. Its bell rings for every customer.

areas.name: Back Store
areas.text: The store of forgotten things in boxes and crates.

areas.name: Pawn Counter
areas.text: The counter of watches, rings and tools under a dim lamp.

locations.name: Goatherds' Steading
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 7-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A farm of stone sheds and pens where a family raises goats on the poor grazing north of the town. They sell milk and cheese in the market and refuse to pay the lieutenant's rent.

areas.name: Steading Cheese Shed
areas.text: A cool shed of shelves where cheeses ripen in cloth.

areas.name: Steading Goat Pens
areas.text: Stone pens loud with goats and kids.

locations.name: Grain Canal Locks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

A short canal joins the river to the capital, climbing through two wooden locks. Grain barges queue at the lower gate, and the keepers decide who goes up first.

areas.name: Grain Canal Upper Lock
areas.text: The upper gates and their winding gear, worked by four men at once.

areas.name: Lock-Keepers' Hut
areas.text: A hut on the bank with a pennant board and a brazier.

locations.name: Grain Mill Quarter
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The quarter of mills and warehouses on the city's south side, where the farms' grain is milled and stored. Its streets are crowded in harvest and quiet in the depth of winter.

areas.name: Mill Yard
areas.text: The yard of carts and sacks outside the mill.

areas.name: Warehouse Row
areas.text: The row of stone warehouses with their iron doors.

locations.name: Grand Marl Hotel
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The best hotel in the east, built for visiting officials from the capital and kept half empty the rest of the year. Its porters can find anything, its dining room serves river trout, and its walls are thinner than the prices suggest.

areas.name: Grand Marl Lobby
areas.text: Marble floor, palms, a reception desk and leather chairs facing the door.

areas.name: Grand Marl Upper Rooms
areas.text: Corridors of numbered doors with a lamp at each landing and a creaking lift.

locations.name: Grand Meridian Hotel
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Where foreign envoys, wealthy families and generals' wives stay when they come to the capital. A string trio plays in the palm court every afternoon while tea is poured from silver, and the porters can find anything for a guest, from a doctor to a train seat on a full train.

areas.name: Meridian Listening Room
areas.text: A narrow room above the ballroom with a chair, a notebook and a grille in the floor.

areas.name: Meridian Marble Lobby
areas.text: A cool hall of marble and brass, with the lift cage and the porters' bench.

areas.name: Meridian Palm Court
areas.text: A glass-roofed court of potted palms, white tablecloths and a string trio.

locations.name: Grauwald
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-26 · Danger: High]

West of the capital the farmland ends at a long forest of pine, once the hunting ground of the old military families and still fenced along its northern edge. Townsfolk walk its outer paths on holidays; very few go deep, where the light goes green and the paths stop agreeing with the maps.

areas.name: Grauwald Boundary Path
areas.text: A path that follows the old boundary stones between the pines.

areas.name: Grauwald Charcoal Clearing
areas.text: A clearing with a turf hut and a cold, grassed-over charcoal mound.

areas.name: Grauwald Hunting Lodge
areas.text: A shuttered timber lodge with antlers over the door and a lock that has been oiled.

locations.name: Grauwasser Reservoir
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High]

The capital's water comes from this reservoir in the hills north-west of the city: a long lake held back by a stone dam, with a pumping house that sends the water down in iron pipes. Fishing is forbidden, and the keeper fines anyone he catches.

areas.name: Grauwasser Dam Walk
areas.text: The walkway along the top of the stone dam, with the lake on one side and a long drop on the other.

areas.name: Grauwasser Pumping House
areas.text: A brick house of steam pumps and pipes.

areas.name: Grauwasser Reed Shore
areas.text: The far shore of reeds and mud where the herons stand.

locations.name: Grey Wolf Hills
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A run of bare hills east of the city, scoured by the wind, where only a few hardy shepherds graze their flocks in summer. In winter the hills belong to the wolves and the blizzards.

areas.name: Grey Wolf Scoured Slopes
areas.text: The wind-scoured slopes of the hills, where the snow lies in hard ridges.

areas.name: Grey Wolf Shepherd's Hut
areas.text: The low stone hut where the shepherds shelter in summer.

locations.name: Greyface Quarry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

The grey stone of West City's newer buildings came from this quarry cut into a hillside. The quarry still works, slowly, and most of what it sends down now is rubble for the border roads.

areas.name: Back Gallery
areas.text: A dark gallery at the rear of the pit, its mouth half hidden by spoil.

areas.name: Greyface Cliff
areas.text: The grey cliff of cut stone, hung with ropes and ladders.

locations.name: Greywall Quarry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The quarry east of the fort where the stone for the wall was cut, still worked in summer to repair it. A derrick stands over the face, and the blocks lie in rows waiting for the sledges.

areas.name: Greywall Quarry Face
areas.text: The cut face of grey stone, stepped and scarred with drill holes.

areas.name: Greywall Quarry Powder Store
areas.text: A stone hut with an iron door where the blasting powder is kept.

locations.name: Grizzly Gully
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

A gully of tall pines and broken rock on the range where the great Briggs bears den. The bark is scored higher than a man can reach, and hunters who know the range go around it.

areas.name: Grizzly Gully Clawed Pines
areas.text: A stand of pines with bark torn in long strips, far above head height.

areas.name: Grizzly Gully Den Mouth
areas.text: A low cave under a rock shelf, its floor scattered with fur and bones.

locations.name: Grumman's Office
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The commanding general's rooms at the top of Eastern Command, comfortable and a little untidy. Lieutenant General Grumman likes a game of chess more than a report, and the colonels he trusts are sent for to play rather than to explain.

areas.name: Grumman's Chess Table
areas.text: A low table by the window with a worn board and two chairs pulled close.

areas.name: Grumman's Outer Office
areas.text: A clerk's desk, a coat stand and a bench where officers wait to be called in.

locations.name: Gun Line Ridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 13-17 · Danger: Moderate]

A low ridge east of Fotset where the southern command's field guns are dug in. When they fire the ground shakes as far back as the railhead, and the gunners are half deaf by the end of a tour.

areas.name: Gun Pits
areas.text: Sandbagged pits under nets, each with its field gun and crew.

areas.name: Observation Post
areas.text: A slit trench on the crest with a periscope toward Aerugo.

locations.name: Gunja
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High]

Gunja climbed a hillside in steps, each house roofed by the courtyard of the one above. The army burned it from the top down. The terraces are still there, and the stone hand mills still sit in the doorways where the women ground meal.

areas.name: Gunja Mill Doorways
areas.text: A lane of doorways with millstones left on the sills.

areas.name: Gunja Stepped Courts
areas.text: Courtyards that are also roofs, falling away down the slope.

locations.name: Haldane Automail Fitters
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A narrow workshop near the hospital where a mechanic and his surgeon sister fit and repair automail for the city's maimed veterans. They trained in Rush Valley and say so on the sign, and they charge the army more than the men.

areas.name: Haldane Fitting Room
areas.text: A padded chair with straps, a tray of tools and a nerve-connection clamp on a swing arm.

areas.name: Haldane Machine Bench
areas.text: A cluttered bench of springs, plates and half-built fingers.

locations.name: Halden Coal Wharf
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

A wharf on the river west of the capital where coal barges unload for the gasworks, the rail yard and the city's stoves. Steam cranes swing baskets ashore all day, and the bargemen drink in the hut at the end of the quay.

areas.name: Halden Bargemen's Hut
areas.text: A smoky hut with a stove, a kettle and a deck of cards.

areas.name: Halden Crane Quay
areas.text: The quay where the steam crane swings baskets from the barges.

locations.name: Halden Junction
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Halden is a junction town in the south-west where the line to the border meets the line running south toward the other areas. It has a water tower, a hotel, a goods shed and a station master who knows every train by its whistle.

areas.name: Halden Goods Shed
areas.text: A shed of sacks and crates waiting for the next train.

areas.name: Halden Platform
areas.text: The platform under the water tower, its benches full of travellers waiting to change.

areas.name: Station Master's House
areas.text: The house by the line where the timetable hangs on a nail.

locations.name: Haldorf Dairy
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Milk for the capital's breakfast tables leaves this farm in churns on a cart before the sun is up, rattling down the north road behind a patient grey mare. The family is large and loud and up at four, and the farmer's wife sells butter and cheese at the gate to anyone who walks out from the city.

areas.name: Haldorf Creamery
areas.text: A stone room kept cold with slate shelves of butter, cheese and skimming pans.

areas.name: Haldorf Milking Shed
areas.text: A long shed of stalls, three-legged stools and steam rising off warm pails.

locations.name: Hall of Nine Cups Teahouse
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The busiest teahouse in the capital, named for the nine painted cups hung over its door. A storyteller sits on a raised dais every evening and tells the court's scandals as old legends, so nobody can be arrested for them.

areas.name: Nine Cups Storyteller's Dais
areas.text: A raised platform with a stool, a fan and a wooden clapper.

areas.name: Nine Cups Upper Gallery
areas.text: A balcony of private tables over the main room, best for listening.

locations.name: Hall of Purification Arts
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Students of alkahestry learn in this long hall, where a ring with a five-pointed star is inlaid in brass at every practice place. The masters teach medicine before anything else: first how to read the flow of the earth, then how to guide it through a sick body.

areas.name: Purification Infirmary Room
areas.text: A side room where real patients come to be treated by the senior students.

areas.name: Purification Masters' Library
areas.text: A room of medical scrolls and charts of the body's channels.

areas.name: Purification Practice Floor
areas.text: The long floor of brass stars where students kneel with their knives laid out.

locations.name: Hall of Scholars
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe]

Under a colonnade at the east of the ruins, shelves are cut straight into the rock walls: this was a school for philosophers and alchemists, where a slave who learned well could rise into the court. The shelves are empty, the scrolls long gone to dust or to thieves.

areas.name: Colonnade Walk
areas.text: The shaded walk of columns at the front of the hall.

areas.name: Lecture Pit
areas.text: A round sunken floor with stone benches stepped around it.

areas.name: Rock Shelves
areas.text: The long room of shelves cut into the living rock.

locations.name: Hallerhof Dairy
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A dairy farm on the edge of the city that sends its milk in churns on the first tram every morning. The farmer's wife makes a hard cheese that the officers' wives fight over.

areas.name: Hallerhof Cheese Room
areas.text: A cool room of wheels of cheese on wooden shelves.

areas.name: Hallerhof Milking Parlour
areas.text: A long barn of cows in stalls and the hiss of milk into pails.

locations.name: Halling's Tavern
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 6-11 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The tavern Mr. Halling keeps with his wife and his boy Kyle, where the shifts come to drink off the dust. It is loud, warm and cheap for anyone with coal under his nails; a stranger in a good coat is charged as though the roof were made of silver.

areas.name: Halling's Back Kitchen
areas.text: A hot room of stewpots where his wife cooks and Kyle washes up.

areas.name: Halling's Taproom
areas.text: Long tables scarred by boots and tankards, and a counter where Halling pours.

areas.name: Halling's Upstairs Rooms
areas.text: Four narrow rooms under the eaves let to whoever the family trusts.

locations.name: Han Smugglers' House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

A plain merchant's house near the western gate, with a sign for dried goods and not much on its shelves. People who need to cross the desert without the Emperor's officers hearing of it come here and ask for the master.

areas.name: Han Dried-Goods Counter
areas.text: The shopfront, stocked just enough to pass for a shop.

areas.name: Han Guides' Back Room
areas.text: A windowless room where guides sleep between crossings and draw routes on the floor in chalk.

locations.name: Hartwig's Alchemical Supply
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A narrow shop that sells everything an alchemist uses: chalk, reagents, brass compasses for drawing circles, textbooks and slates. The old proprietor weighs everything twice and knows the name of every State Alchemist who has ever come in.

areas.name: Hartwig Drafting Counter
areas.text: A counter of chalk, compasses and rulers for drawing circles.

areas.name: Hartwig Reagent Shelves
areas.text: Shelves of glass jars with handwritten labels, some locked behind glass.

locations.name: Heirs' Pavilions
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Twenty-four princes and nineteen princesses stand to inherit the throne, and each keeps a pavilion in this walled garden near the palace. The pavilions sit at careful distances. Raked gravel shows every footprint by morning.

areas.name: Food Tasters' Kitchen
areas.text: A shared kitchen where each pavilion's taster eats first and watches the others.

areas.name: Garden of Separate Paths
areas.text: Raked walks laid out so that no two heirs' guards need ever pass close.

areas.name: Twelfth Prince's Pavilion
areas.text: Ling Yao's shuttered pavilion, its doors sealed with a strip of Yao paper.

locations.name: Hermit's Bivouac
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

A shelter under an overhang high on the range, with a fire ring and the bones of a lean-to. Patrols use it in a storm, and few of them wonder who built it.

areas.name: Bivouac Lean-to
areas.text: The frame of branches against the rock, roofed with old pine boughs.

areas.name: Bivouac Overhang
areas.text: The dry ground under the rock, with a fire ring and a flat stone for a seat.

locations.name: Heron Islet
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-8 · Danger: Low]

A low islet of reeds and willow in the west of Kauroy Lake, too small and too wet for anyone to live on. Herons nest there in hundreds, and on still evenings their clamour carries to the shore.

areas.name: Heron Islet Mud Flats
areas.text: Grey mud and a black rib of boat showing at low water.

areas.name: Heron Islet Rookery
areas.text: Willows bent under nests of sticks and white droppings.

locations.name: Highcrag Goat Steading
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A hill farm on the western foothills where a family keeps goats, makes a hard cheese and sells milk to the fort's kitchen. They have farmed the slope for four generations.

areas.name: Goat Steading Cheese Cellar
areas.text: A cellar dug into the slope, lined with wheels of hard cheese on boards.

areas.name: Goat Steading Farmhouse
areas.text: The stone farmhouse with its great stove, its table and its lamp in the window.

locations.name: Hill Barley Brewery
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-16 · Danger: Moderate]

Barley from the western farms is malted and brewed here into the brown beer the garrison drinks. The brewer's drays roll out at dawn with barrels for every tavern in the city.

areas.name: Copper Vat House
areas.text: A hall of copper vats, warm and smelling of wet grain.

areas.name: Dray Yard
areas.text: The yard of drays and heavy horses.

locations.name: Hill Powder Magazine
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-24 · Danger: High]

The western army's powder and shells are kept here, in a magazine dug into a hillside and banked with earth so that an explosion would go up instead of out. Guards are searched for matches at the gate.

areas.name: Magazine Mouth
areas.text: The heavy door into the hill, copper hinges so they will not spark.

areas.name: Search Gate
areas.text: The gate where every man turns out his pockets.

locations.name: Hill Shepherd Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A camp of herders on the hill above the front, with canvas huts, a few sheep and a dog that barks at every patrol. The herders trade milk and cheese with both armies and tell each one what the other has said.

areas.name: Canvas Huts
areas.text: The huts of canvas and wood with their cooking pots.

areas.name: Hill Pasture
areas.text: The pasture of sheep above the camp, where the dog keeps watch.

locations.name: Hillside Convalescent Home
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A villa on the eastern hills, once a rich family's summer house, now a home where wounded officers recover in the sun. The terrace looks out over the city and the nurses keep the war off the radio.

areas.name: Matron's Office
areas.text: A tidy office of files, keys and a sharp-eyed matron.

areas.name: Sun Terrace
areas.text: A wide terrace of wheelchairs and wicker, with a view of South City.

locations.name: Hilltop Lookout
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A bench on the hill above Resembool where the town's young go to look at the road to the east. On a clear day the smoke of East City can be seen on the sky.

areas.name: Lookout Bench
areas.text: The bench on the rise with its view down the valley.

areas.name: Stone Cairn
areas.text: The small cairn beside the bench, with its carved stone.

locations.name: Hollin Peat Moor
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A flat moor south-west of the city where the poorer families cut peat to burn instead of buying coal. In winter it lies under snow, and the black pools between the stacks freeze over badly.

areas.name: Hollin Black Pools
areas.text: The dark pools between the banks, glazed with thin ice.

areas.name: Hollin Peat Banks
areas.text: The cut banks where the peat is dug and stacked to dry.

locations.name: Holm Oak Wood
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-13 · Danger: Moderate]

A dark wood of evergreen oaks west of the line, where charcoal burners work and wild boar root in the leaf litter. Patrols cut through it to stay out of sight of the Aerugonian guns.

areas.name: Boar Run
areas.text: A narrow trail through the undergrowth, churned by hooves.

areas.name: Charcoal Clearing
areas.text: A clearing of smoking mounds and blackened ground.

locations.name: House of Foreign Guests
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The court lodges the rare foreigner here, in a courtyard house a short walk from the palace. It is comfortable, the food is good and the servants are attentive, chiefly to what the guests say.

areas.name: Foreign Guests' Courtyard
areas.text: The enclosed garden at the house's centre, with a pond and a single bench.

areas.name: Foreign Guests' Listening Corridor
areas.text: A servants' passage running behind the guest rooms.

locations.name: Hughes Family Home
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-16 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A comfortable apartment on a quiet residential street where Maes Hughes lives with his wife Gracia and their little daughter Elicia. Gracia keeps an open table; the Elric brothers have eaten here, slept on the sofa and been made to admire more photographs of Elicia than any two travellers should. Neighbours know the family as kind, loud and generous with pie.

areas.name: Hughes Bureau Corner
areas.text: A writing bureau in the hall with a locked lower drawer.

areas.name: Hughes Family Kitchen
areas.text: A warm kitchen where Gracia bakes, with a long table and a quiche cooling on the sill.

areas.name: Hughes Family Parlour
areas.text: A bright parlour of framed photographs, a sofa with a crocheted throw and a toy box in the corner.

locations.name: Ice House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The ice house of North City, a round stone store where blocks of lake ice are kept under straw through the summer. The keeper sells the ice by the bucket to the butchers and the bars.

areas.name: Ice Store
areas.text: The round room of ice blocks under their straw.

areas.name: Keeper's Door
areas.text: The heavy door and the scale beside it.

locations.name: Ice Road Crossing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

A crossing of the frozen river below the fort, marked by poles that are replaced every spring. Sleds take the ice road in winter and a wrong turn leads straight into the current.

areas.name: Ice Surface
areas.text: The white crust of the river, ridged by the wind.

areas.name: Marker Poles
areas.text: The line of poles that show the safe crossing.

locations.name: Imperial Archive
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The archive of the emperor's house, a long building of shelves and scrolls where the court's records and histories are kept. Scholars come with a letter of introduction and leave with ink on their hands.

areas.name: Reading Desk
areas.text: The desks where scholars read under paper lanterns.

areas.name: Scroll Room
areas.text: The shelves of scrolls, each in its wooden case.

locations.name: Imperial Horse Relay
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

The first relay on the western road, where imperial couriers change horses and the dispatch bags change hands. A bell rings when a rider is sighted and fresh horses are saddled before he reaches the gate.

areas.name: Relay Dispatch Room
areas.text: A small room of pigeonholes and sealed bags.

areas.name: Relay Horse Lines
areas.text: Long rails where saddled horses wait in a row.

locations.name: Imperial Hunting Park
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-24 · Danger: High]

A long wall encloses the Emperor's hunting park: forest, meadows and a lake stocked with deer. The court once hunted here every autumn.

areas.name: Hunting Park Deer Meadow
areas.text: An open meadow where the deer graze in the evening.

areas.name: Hunting Park Gamekeepers' Lodge
areas.text: A lodge with bows, nets and a kennel.

locations.name: Imperial Palace
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The Emperor's palace in the heart of the capital, with gilded roofs, terraces of stone and gates guarded by men in lacquered armour. Only those with a seal may enter the inner halls.

areas.name: Inner Hall
areas.text: The hall of the seal, behind a screen and a row of guards.

areas.name: Outer Court
areas.text: The first court of the palace, with its audience hall and its waiting benches.

locations.name: Imperial Physicians' Pavilion
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The court physicians work beside the Emperor's private rooms, from a pavilion with a herb store, a brazier kept lit day and night, and a guard who empties every basket on a cloth before it goes in. The Emperor is old and his health is said to be failing.

areas.name: Physicians' Brazier Room
areas.text: The warm room where decoctions simmer under a physician's eye.

areas.name: Physicians' Herb Store
areas.text: Shelves of labelled jars behind a lattice door, smelling of root and bark.

locations.name: Inkstone Lane
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A lane of brush makers, ink grinders and paper sellers, where letter-writers sit at folding tables and write for those who cannot. A good hand here earns more than a poor clerk at court.

areas.name: Inkstone Letter-Writers' Tables
areas.text: Folding tables along the wall where scribes take dictation.

areas.name: Inkstone Paper-Drying Court
areas.text: A courtyard of wooden frames where wet sheets dry in the sun.

locations.name: Iron Bridge West
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The main line east to Central crosses the river on this iron girder bridge, and it is guarded at both ends by men with rifles who check every cart on the road deck beneath the rails.

areas.name: Iron Bridge Girder Walk
areas.text: A narrow catwalk among the girders, used by the painters and nobody else.

areas.name: Iron Bridge Road Deck
areas.text: The lower deck where carts cross under the rails, the trains booming overhead.

locations.name: Ishval
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

The south-eastern region of the Ishvalans, who follow Ishvala, a hard country of rock and sand on the edge of the great desert. It was razed in the civil war that began in 1901; its survivors were scattered across Amestris and the army holds the empty land. Amestrian soldiers are not welcome where any Ishvalan still stands.

areas.name: Holy Ground
areas.text: The shrine of Ishvala, open to the sky, where the faithful kneel.

areas.name: Ishvalan Bazaar
areas.text: The old bazaar square of baked-clay stalls, empty since the war; in the rebuilt years it fills again with spice and caravans.

areas.name: Trade Road Gate
areas.text:
The road gate where the army checks everyone who comes in; in the rebuilt years the caravans from Xing pass here.

The rail and coach service serves this yard: coaches run to East City (about 10 Cens), Desert Crossing (about 8 Cens); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

locations.name: Ishval Army Encampment
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

The army's main camp in Ishval spread across a flat of hard ground behind the lines: rows of tents, a field kitchen, a latrine trench and an officers' mess where State Alchemists sat over bottles after the day's work. A smaller version of it still houses the garrison.

areas.name: Ishval Encampment Kitchen Fire
areas.text: The field kitchen's fire pit and its blackened kettles.

areas.name: Ishval Encampment Tent Rows
areas.text: Lines of grey tents with ropes and pegs in the dust.

areas.name: Ishval Officers' Mess Tent
areas.text: A long tent with a trestle table and a stove, used for drinking more than eating.

locations.name: Ishval Border Gate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

The checkpoint where the road from East City enters the Ishval country. Amestrian soldiers check papers here, and any Ishvalan waits in a line that moves slowly.

areas.name: Checkpoint Hut
areas.text: The hut of papers and stamps beside the barrier.

areas.name: Queue Lane
areas.text: The line of waiting travellers under the sun.

locations.name: Ishval Dry Wash
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A dry riverbed winds through the ruins and out to the salt country. Most of the year it is a road of round stones. After a storm in the hills it fills in minutes, chest-deep and brown, and the line of dead brush on its banks shows how high it rose last time.

areas.name: Ishval Wash Brush Line Bank
areas.text: The high bank with its tide line of tangled dead brush.

areas.name: Ishval Wash Round-Stone Bed
areas.text: The stony bed of the wash, smooth underfoot and loud when walked.

locations.name: Ishval Military Cemetery
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-16 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The army buried its own dead in a fenced square near the old encampment, and the markers stand in ranks as if on parade, each with a name, a rank and a unit. A single caretaker hauls water from the railhead to keep a strip of grass alive between the rows, because a general once said there should be grass.

areas.name: Ishval Cemetery Caretaker's Lodge
areas.text: A tin-roofed hut with the book on a shelf and a cot behind a curtain.

areas.name: Ishval Cemetery Marker Ranks
areas.text: Rows of white markers with a ribbon of watered grass between them.

locations.name: Ishval Occupation Barracks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The garrison that holds the empty land lives in brick blocks the army put up after the war, on the site of an Ishvalan school whose foundations still show at the corners. The men drill at dawn, ride patrol through the ruins by day and play cards for cigarettes at night.

areas.name: Ishval Barracks Card Room
areas.text: A smoky room at the end of a block with a felt table and a stove.

areas.name: Ishval Barracks Sand Square
areas.text: The packed-sand square where the garrison drills under the flag.

areas.name: Ishval Sergeant Major's Garden
areas.text: A patch of tomatoes and onions behind a reed fence.

locations.name: Ishval Quartermaster Depot
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate]

Every sack and cartridge the garrison uses comes off the train at the railhead and ends up here, in a long warehouse with sandbagged walls and a clerk who counts everything twice. The quartermaster sergeant is the most obliging man in Ishval, if a request comes on the right form.

areas.name: Ishval Depot Long Room
areas.text: The warehouse floor of crates, sacks and chalked tallies.

areas.name: Ishval Depot Ration Scale
areas.text: The weighing scale at the door where every issue is booked.

locations.name: Ishval Rail Survey Line
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

East of the ruins a line of white-painted stakes runs dead straight toward the desert, a stake every hundred paces, as far as the eye can follow. Two army surveyors walk it in the cool hours with a theodolite and a mule cart, and sleep under the cart at noon.

areas.name: Ishval Survey Stake Run
areas.text: The straight run of stakes heading east into the haze.

areas.name: Ishval Surveyors' Noon Camp
areas.text: A mule cart with a tarp rigged off its side and rolled maps under the seat.

locations.name: Ishval Scrub Pastures
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

South of the ruins the rock breaks into thorn scrub, poor grazing that feeds goats only if they range all day. A few Ishvalan herders who never left the land move through it with their flocks and keep well clear of the patrols.

areas.name: Ishval Marked Waterhole
areas.text: A seep in the rock with a scratched stone beside it.

areas.name: Ishval Thorn Track Maze
areas.text: Narrow paths through the scrub, worn by hooves.

locations.name: Ishval War Ruins
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

The ruined towns of the old Ishval, left as the war made them. Walls stand without roofs, the wells are dry and the dead were never all buried. The Ishvalans come here to pray for the ones they lost.

areas.name: Blackened Lane
areas.text: The lane of burned houses with their doorways open to the sky.

areas.name: Dry Well Square
areas.text: The old square with its dry well and the broken shrine beside it.

locations.name: Ishval Wheat Terraces
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

Ishval never had much farmland, so its people made some: walls of dry stone stacked along the slopes, each holding a shelf of earth carried up in baskets. Six years of neglect since the war and the dust has filled the shelves level with their walls, and goats graze where there was barley.

areas.name: Ishval High Wheat Row
areas.text: A single row of green wheat on the top terrace, with a water jar half buried beside it.

areas.name: Ishval Terrace Threshing Floor
areas.text: A round floor of beaten earth at the slope's foot, where the harvest was trodden out.

areas.name: Ishval Terrace Wall Stair
areas.text: The steps built into the walls, worn hollow by bare feet.

locations.name: Ishvalan Graves
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-22 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A graveyard of red stones at the edge of the ruined land, with rows of graves for those who died in the war and were buried later by their families. Each stone carries a name and the rites are said at dusk.

areas.name: Dusk Wall
areas.text: The low wall where the rites are said at sunset.

areas.name: Stone Rows
areas.text: The rows of red stones, each with its name and its ribbon.

locations.name: Ishvalan Red Canyon
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

A canyon cuts deep into the hills east of the ruins, its walls so steep the floor sees the sun only at noon. Ledges along the walls lead to caves, and the caves are where the Ishvalans who will not stop fighting keep their stores.

areas.name: Red Canyon Ledge Path
areas.text: A ledge along the wall, with a sheer drop on one side.

areas.name: Red Canyon Noon Floor
areas.text: The dry, boulder-strewn floor, in shadow most of the day.

areas.name: Red Canyon Store Cave
areas.text: A cave with sacks of meal and jars of water stacked against its walls.

locations.name: Ishvalan Refugee Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

A camp of tents and shacks on the edge of the ruined land, where Ishvalans who lost their homes scrape a living and wait for news of kin. The camp is crowded and poor, and the soldiers who watch it are often tired.

areas.name: Tent Rows
areas.text: The rows of canvas tents with their cook fires and their washing.

areas.name: Water Cart Stop
areas.text: The water cart's halt, where the queues form each morning.

locations.name: Ishvalan Shrine Hill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

A low hill of red rock above the ruined town, with a shrine at its top and prayer cloths tied along the path. The view from the top covers the ruins to the south and the road to the east.

areas.name: Pilgrim Path
areas.text: The path up the hill, lined with prayer cloths.

areas.name: Summit Shrine
areas.text: The small shrine at the top, open to the wind.

locations.name: Island Cove
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A sheltered cove on Yock Island's south side, where the test-takers are landed and the boats are hauled up on the pebbles. A boathouse on stilts keeps the oars dry.

areas.name: Boathouse
areas.text: The boathouse on its stilts, with its racks of oars.

areas.name: Pebble Beach
areas.text: The beach of smooth pebbles and drying weed.

locations.name: Jade Temple
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-26 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A temple of the capital's old faith, with carved gates, bronze bells and a hall where monks chant before dawn. Its courtyard is open to all, and its incense is sold at the gate.

areas.name: Bell Court
areas.text: The courtyard of bronze bells and the stone path to the hall.

areas.name: Chant Hall
areas.text: The hall of monks and incense, dim and quiet.

locations.name: Kanda
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High]

Kanda was one of the named districts of Ishval, a quarter of clay houses and narrow lanes that the army fought through street by street in the last year of the war. It is empty now except for the army's numbered stakes and the people who come back in secret to look.

areas.name: Kanda Domed Square
areas.text: A square of broken domes where the district gathered to pray.

areas.name: Kanda Narrow Lanes
areas.text: Lanes too tight for a cart, walls pocked with bullets.

areas.name: Kanda Stake Field
areas.text: Open ground beyond the houses studded with numbered army stakes.

locations.name: Kanda Field Command
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-20 · Danger: High]

Brigadier General Fessler ran the Kanda front from a gutted merchant's house with a tent roof and a map table, and rated his campaign by how fast the district was cleared rather than what it cost his men. The house is a ruin of its own now, its canvas long rotted.

areas.name: Fessler's Map Table Room
areas.text: The roofless room where the map table still stands, its legs sunk in sand.

areas.name: Kanda Field Command Courtyard
areas.text: The courtyard where the staff stood, its walls scarred.

locations.name: Kanda Sniper Ridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A spine of rock looks down over the whole of Kanda, every lane and doorway laid open to it. In the last year of the war the army's marksmen lay along it for days at a time; the cracks between the rocks are still full of brass.

areas.name: Kanda Brass Cairn Summit
areas.text: The highest rock, with a waist-high cairn of cartridge cases.

areas.name: Kanda Marksmen's Line
areas.text: A row of shallow scrapes behind the rocks where the shooters lay.

locations.name: Kanda Stockade
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-20 · Danger: High]

A stockade of posts and wire on the edge of Kanda, where the army held Ishvalans who were caught or who had served in its own ranks. It stands empty, its gate chained, and the garrison uses the yard to store wire.

areas.name: Kanda Stockade Lookout
areas.text: A raised platform with a view over the whole enclosure.

areas.name: Kanda Stockade Wire Yard
areas.text: The open yard inside the fence, piled with rolls of wire.

locations.name: Kauroy Bathing Beach
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-5 · Danger: Low]

A strip of sand east of the town where visitors and townsfolk bathe in summer, with striped huts for changing and a lifeguard who cannot swim. On hot afternoons half of Dublith is in the water.

areas.name: Kauroy Bathing Huts
areas.text: A row of striped huts on wheels at the top of the sand.

areas.name: Kauroy Sand Shelf
areas.text: Shallow water over sand that ends in a sudden dark edge.

locations.name: Kauroy Beacon
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low]

A squat stone tower on a spit south of the town, lit each evening so the night boats can find Dublith across Kauroy Lake. The keeper trims the lamp at dusk and sleeps in a hut at its foot.

areas.name: Kauroy Beacon Hut
areas.text: A hut of one room with a cot, a kettle and a dog.

areas.name: Kauroy Beacon Lamp Room
areas.text: A glass-walled room at the top, the lamp and its trimmings.

locations.name: Kauroy Boatyard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low]

A boatyard on the lake shore where the fishing boats of Dublith are built and patched, each plank bent over a steam box from oak brought down out of the hills. The builders say they can tell a boat's owner by its leak.

areas.name: Kauroy Slipway
areas.text: Greased timbers running into the lake, a hull on its cradle.

areas.name: Kauroy Steam Shed
areas.text: A steaming shed where planks soften for bending.

locations.name: Kauroy Dairy Farm
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low]

A dairy farm at the lake's western edge, where the cows wade into the shallows to cool off in the afternoon heat. Its cheese is sold at Curtis Meats and on the trains north.

areas.name: Kauroy Cheese Room
areas.text: A cool stone room of wheels of cheese on wooden shelves.

areas.name: Kauroy Milking Shed
areas.text: A shed of stalls, stools and pails, warm with cows.

locations.name: Kauroy Ferry Pier
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

The jetty from which the small ferry runs out to the island and back, with its boat, its ropes and its ticket board. The ferryman does not carry anyone who has no reason to be on the water.

areas.name: Jetty
areas.text: The wooden jetty and the moored ferry boat.

areas.name: Rope Store
areas.text: The shed of coiled ropes and oars.

locations.name: Kauroy Fish Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-5 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A long open hall on the Dublith waterfront where the night's catch is sold at dawn, perch, pike and eel laid out on ice. By the middle of the morning the slabs are hosed down and only the gulls stay.

areas.name: Kauroy Auction Slabs
areas.text: Ice-covered slabs where buyers bid by raising a finger.

areas.name: Kauroy Gutting Benches
areas.text: Wet benches at the back, knives flashing and buckets of guts.

locations.name: Kauroy Ice Works
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low]

A plant by the rail line that freezes lake water into blocks with an ammonia machine, the newest thing in Dublith. The butchers and the fish hall buy their ice here, and in the heat children wait at the chute for chips.

areas.name: Kauroy Ammonia Room
areas.text: A hissing room of pipes, gauges and a flywheel.

areas.name: Kauroy Ice Chute
areas.text: A wooden chute where blocks slide down to the carts.

locations.name: Kauroy Lake
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A wide lake beside Dublith, grey and calm in most weather, with reeds on its shores and fishing boats far out on its water. The lake is the town's livelihood and its boundary; the far shore is an hour's sail.

areas.name: Open Water
areas.text: The open lake with its boats and its cold wind.

areas.name: Reed Shore
areas.text: The shore of reeds where the boats are pulled up.

locations.name: Kauroy Lake Hotel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-5 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A white hotel with balconies over Kauroy Lake, built for visitors who come south for the warm weather and the view of the island. Its terrace serves cold drinks until midnight in summer.

areas.name: Kauroy Hotel Balcony Rooms
areas.text: Upper rooms with shutters and narrow iron balconies.

areas.name: Kauroy Hotel Terrace
areas.text: A tiled terrace of wicker chairs above the water.

locations.name: Kauroy Net Lofts
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-5 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Long sheds on the west shore where nets are tarred, hung and mended by fishermen too old to go out. The talk in the lofts is the town's slowest news and its most thorough.

areas.name: Kauroy Net Rafters
areas.text: Rafters draped with brown nets drying in the draught.

areas.name: Kauroy Net Tar Pot
areas.text: A fire under an iron pot of tar, where nets are dipped.

locations.name: Kauroy Outflow Mill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-7 · Danger: Low]

A stone mill at the head of the river that drains Kauroy Lake to the east, grinding grain for Dublith and the farms round about. The weir beside it holds the lake at its summer level.

areas.name: Kauroy Outflow Weir
areas.text: A timber weir with boards that lift on chains.

areas.name: Kauroy Outflow Wheelhouse
areas.text: The thundering wheel and the stones it turns.

locations.name: Kauroy Reed Marsh
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-9 · Danger: Low]

A marsh at the west end of Kauroy Lake where the reeds grow higher than a man's head and the channels shift with every flood. Thatchers cut there in winter; in summer only the eel-catchers and the mosquitoes go in.

areas.name: Kauroy Deserter's Hummock
areas.text: A dry island in the marsh with a lean-to of reeds and a fire pit.

areas.name: Kauroy Reed Channels
areas.text: Narrow channels of black water where a punt is the only way through.

locations.name: Kauroy South Shore Hamlet
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A hamlet of a dozen cottages on the far shore of Kauroy Lake, an hour's sail from Dublith and a day's walk round. Its people fish, keep goats and go into the town only on market days.

areas.name: South Shore Hamlet Goat Fold
areas.text: A stone fold behind the cottages, the goats bleating.

areas.name: South Shore Hamlet Shingle
areas.text: A shingle beach of boats, nets and goats.

locations.name: Kellerhof Brewery
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A family brewery at the edge of the north road, supplying half the beer halls and officers' messes in the capital. Its dray carts leave at dawn behind heavy horses, and the brewer's daughter keeps the books with a sharper pencil than her father ever did.

areas.name: Kellerhof Barrel Cellar
areas.text: A cool cellar of stacked barrels under brick arches.

areas.name: Kellerhof Brewhouse
areas.text: A tall brewhouse of copper vats and steam.

areas.name: Kellerhof Dray Yard
areas.text: A cobbled yard where the heavy horses are harnessed to the carts.

locations.name: Kessel Ford
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A village at a ford on the river south-west of the city, where a rope ferry takes carts across when the water is too high to wade and a sledge track crosses the ice when it is frozen. Its people fish, farm and trade with the city's market.

areas.name: Ford Green
areas.text: The village green of log houses around a well and a notice board.

areas.name: Kessel Ferry Landing
areas.text: The plank landing, the rope across the river and the ferryman's hut.

locations.name: Kessel Hamlet
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 7-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A hamlet of a dozen cottages north of the town, built by miners who wanted to live away from the dust. They walk an hour each way to the pit and say it is worth it.

areas.name: Kessel Bell Frame
areas.text: A timber frame with a bell, used for weddings and alarms.

areas.name: Kessel Well Green
areas.text: A patch of green around the well, the only grass in miles.

locations.name: Kettle and Stove Café
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A warm café off the market where clerks, junior officers and the occasional off-duty stationmaster sit for hours over a single coffee. The owner lets them, because a full room keeps the heat in.

areas.name: Café Corner Table
areas.text: A table in the back corner, half hidden by the coat stand.

areas.name: Café Window Tables
areas.text: The tables along the steamed front window, each with a newspaper on its stick.

locations.name: Kiosk Corner
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High]

An ordinary street corner near Central Command, with a news stand, a bench and a public telephone kiosk with a glass door. Clerks queue here at lunchtime to ring their mothers. The kiosk's glass is newer than the rest of it.

areas.name: Kiosk Corner News Stand
areas.text: A wooden stand of papers and tobacco, with a stool for the seller.

areas.name: Kiosk Corner Telephone Box
areas.text: The glass-doored kiosk with its new pane and a receiver on a short cord.

locations.name: Kunai Forge Lane
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A lane of smithies off the market where the hammering never stops. The smiths make the plain throwing knives every warrior carries and finer ones balanced for alkahestrists, who set five in the ground at the points of a star to work their art.

areas.name: Kunai Balance Bench
areas.text: A bench where the master tests each finished knife on one finger.

areas.name: Kunai Quenching Troughs
areas.text: Stone troughs along the gutter where hot blades hiss into oily water.

locations.name: Laboratory 5
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-28 · Danger: Severe]

A state laboratory on the outskirts of the capital, beside Central Prison, said to have closed years ago. Yet a soldier still stands at its gate day and night, razor wire runs along its high wall, and a few lamps are kept burning in its corridors.

areas.name: Laboratory Corridors
areas.text: The long corridors of offices and locked doors, the scientists' desks left as they were.

areas.name: Sealed Chambers
areas.text: The chambers where the experiments were kept, and the drains under them.

locations.name: Lakeside Halt
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

The small rail halt of Dublith, a timber platform and a ticket cage on the line north to Central City. The trains are few and the timetable is kept on a board in the cage.

areas.name: Halt Platform
areas.text: The timber platform with its bench and its lamp.

areas.name: Ticket Cage
areas.text: The cage of tickets and the timetable board.

locations.name: Lantern Music Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A music hall with a stage, a small brass band and a programme of comic singers, jugglers and the odd conjurer. The curtain shows a summer meadow, which gets the loudest cheer of the night.

areas.name: Meadow Curtain Wings
areas.text: The narrow space behind the meadow curtain, cluttered with props and ropes.

areas.name: Music Hall Stalls
areas.text: The packed benches and the gas footlights in front of the stage.

locations.name: Lantern Opera House
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The capital's opera plays every night to a hall packed with clan servants and merchants. The actors wear painted faces that tell the audience at a glance who is loyal and who is false.

areas.name: Opera Gong Stage
areas.text: The lantern-hung stage with the musicians' bench at one side.

areas.name: Opera Painted-Face Room
areas.text: The crowded dressing room, all mirrors, paint pots and costume chests.

locations.name: Larch Hollow
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

Larch Hollow is a hill village of timber houses with a stone well and a schoolroom over the smithy. Its people have lived beside the war so long they can tell an Amestrian rifle from a Cretan one by the sound.

areas.name: Hollow Well
areas.text: The stone well where the village meets to talk and draw water.

areas.name: Smithy Schoolroom
areas.text: A schoolroom up a ladder over the smith's forge, warm in winter.

locations.name: Larch Ridge Halt
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-20 · Danger: High]

The last stop on the branch line toward the border is a single platform and a hut with a stove. Troops get down here and walk the rest of the way, and the wounded are loaded here for the ride back.

areas.name: Larch Ridge Platform
areas.text: The single platform with a lamp post and a stack of stretchers.

areas.name: Stove Hut
areas.text: The keeper's hut with its pot-bellied stove and its telegraph key.

locations.name: LeCoulte Automail
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

The automail shop of Ridel and Dominic LeCoulte, set in the mountains near Rush Valley, where the materials are plentiful and the shop has regular customers from Rush Valley. Its showroom holds arms and legs on stands.

areas.name: Fitting Bench
areas.text: The bench and its clamps, where the fittings are made to measure.

areas.name: Showroom
areas.text: The room of limbs on stands, polished and labelled.

locations.name: LeCoulte Cliff Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-10 · Danger: Low]

The road up from Rush Valley into the mountains, a ledge cut into the rock with a long fall on one side and a plank bridge over a ravine near the top. Customers of the LeCoulte shop climb it with their limbs wrapped in oilcloth.

areas.name: LeCoulte Cliff Ledge
areas.text: A shelf of road barely a cart wide, the drop on the left.

areas.name: LeCoulte Plank Bridge
areas.text: Planks lashed over a ravine, a rope for a rail.

locations.name: Leto Mission House
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 16-22 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A preacher of Leto keeps a small chapel and water barrel by the road, offering a cup of water and a sermon to every traveller. Since the scandal in Reole, few stop for the sermon.

areas.name: Sun Disc Chapel
areas.text: The chapel with its sun disc and its rows of benches.

areas.name: Water Barrel
