areas.text: The barrel by the road, with a tin cup on a chain.

locations.name: Lieutenant's Tax Office
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 7-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The office from which Yoki's clerk rules the town on paper: the rent of every cottage, the duty on every cart of coal and the fines nobody understands. A queue of miners forms there at the end of every month.

areas.name: Tax Office Counting Room
areas.text: Desks, books and the bolted strongbox under a window with bars.

areas.name: Tax Office Queue Porch
areas.text: A covered porch where the miners wait their turn, caps in hand.

locations.name: Limb Works of the South
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 9-13 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

An automail workshop near the hospital that fits arms and legs to soldiers who lost theirs at the front. The mechanics learned the trade in Rush Valley and charge the army by the limb.

areas.name: Limb Fitting Room
areas.text: A room of padded chairs where nerves are connected and men try not to scream.

areas.name: Limb Forge
areas.text: The back workshop of lathes, springs and half-built arms.

locations.name: Limestone Quarry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-13 · Danger: Moderate]

A quarry north-west of the city that has cut the pale stone of South City's finest buildings. Now its blocks go to the front for bunkers, and its powder is counted twice.

areas.name: Quarry Face
areas.text: A pale cliff stepped with ledges and scarred by blasting.

areas.name: Stone Yard
areas.text: Rows of cut blocks waiting for carts and trains.

locations.name: Linden Court Hotel
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A respectable hotel of four floors near the station, used by the military to put up visiting officers and State Alchemists who come to the capital on business. The rooms are plain and clean and the porter asks no questions about rank or what is in the luggage.

areas.name: Linden Court Front Desk
areas.text: A brass-railed desk with the bell, the key board and the register.

areas.name: Linden Court Guarded Room
areas.text: A twin room on the third floor with a chair outside the door for the guard.

locations.name: Linden Street Church
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-16 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small, plain church that serves the old families of the quarter. Few in the capital go to church any more, and the young pastor knows most of his congregation by their first names. On weekday mornings he keeps a soup kitchen in the hall.

areas.name: Linden Street Bell Tower
areas.text: A narrow tower with a ladder to the bell and a small room below it.

areas.name: Linden Street Nave
areas.text: The plain nave with its worn pews and candles in jam jars.

areas.name: Linden Street Soup Hall
areas.text: The parish hall where soup is served at long tables on weekday mornings.

locations.name: Lindenhof Coffee House
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A coffee house under the linden trees where junior officers spend their afternoons over cards and the papers. The owner's daughter remembers everyone's order and nobody's debts.

areas.name: Lindenhof Card Room
areas.text: A smoky back room with a green-baize table and a curtain instead of a door.

areas.name: Lindenhof Window Tables
areas.text: Small marble tables in the window where the regulars sit to watch the street.

locations.name: Lindqvist Alchemy Supply
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A shop of alchemical supplies: chalk, mineral samples, reference books, glass and the reagents a working alchemist needs. The owner asks for a State Alchemist's certificate or a teacher's letter before she sells anything stronger than chalk; no law asks it of her.

areas.name: Lindqvist Licence Counter
areas.text: The counter with its balance, its book and its sign about papers.

areas.name: Lindqvist Mineral Shelves
areas.text: The shelves of labelled jars, ores and crystals that line the shop.

locations.name: Little Panda Bamboo Grove
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

A cold forest of bamboo climbs the slopes east of the capital, so dense that the light comes through green. Pandas live here, slow and solitary, and by old custom the woodcutters leave them be.

areas.name: Green-Light Bamboo Thicket
areas.text: The deep grove where stems crowd so close a man walks sideways.

areas.name: Woodcutters' Bamboo Track
areas.text: A cart track at the grove's edge where cut stems are bundled.

locations.name: Lower Marl Reed Marsh
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A marsh of reeds and channels where the Marl River spreads out below the city. Wildfowlers and eel-catchers know its paths; everyone else gets lost.

areas.name: Reed Marsh Eel Channels
areas.text: Narrow channels of black water where eel traps are set.

areas.name: Reed Marsh Wildfowler's Hide
areas.text: A hide of woven reeds on stilts where the wildfowlers wait for ducks.

locations.name: Lower Marl Tannery
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A tannery downstream of the city where cattle hides from the stockyards are turned into leather for the army's boots and belts. Nobody lives near it by choice, and the river runs a different colour for a mile below.

areas.name: Marl Tannery Drying Lofts
areas.text: Lofts with slatted walls where leather hangs to dry in the wind.

areas.name: Marl Tannery Soaking Pits
areas.text: Rows of pits of lime and bark where hides soak for weeks.

locations.name: Lower Town School
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The school of the lower town, where children of the millers, the tanners and the railwaymen learn their letters and their sums. The schoolmaster reads them the State Military's notices as lessons in civics.

areas.name: Lower Town Schoolroom
areas.text: The single room of desks around the stove, with a map of Amestris on the wall.

areas.name: Schoolmaster's Cupboard
areas.text: The locked cupboard of books and chalk the schoolmaster keeps the key to.

locations.name: Madame Christmas's Bar
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A hostess bar on a side street off the officers' quarter, run by a broad, gravel-voiced woman everyone calls Madame Christmas. Officers come for the drink and the girls' company and stay for the talk, which is better than anything printed in the capital. Her nephew is Roy Mustang, and she has never once let him forget it.

areas.name: Christmas Bar Back Telephone
areas.text: A cramped back passage with a wall telephone, a crate stool and a pad of pencilled names.

areas.name: Christmas Bar Velvet Booths
areas.text: Curtained booths along the wall where the officers sit with the hostesses.

locations.name: Magistrate's Court of the Capital
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Anyone may beat the drum at the gate of the capital's court to demand a hearing, and the magistrate is bound to come out. Behind the hall a courtyard leads to the cells.

areas.name: Magistrate's Gaol Cells
areas.text: A row of wooden cages along a courtyard wall.

areas.name: Magistrate's Petition Drum
areas.text: The great drum under its roof at the gate, its skin dark with hands.

locations.name: Maren Hamlet
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-11 · Danger: Moderate]

A farming hamlet south-west of the city whose fields run almost to the wire. Its families have learned to tell the guns apart by their sound and to take in the washing when the shelling starts.

areas.name: Hamlet Chapel
areas.text: A small whitewashed chapel with a broken bell.

areas.name: Hamlet Well
areas.text: The well and its trough, where everyone hears the news first.

locations.name: Market Row
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High]

The market street that runs from the rail terminal toward the old quarter, with stalls for food, cloth, papers and pawned tools. Soldiers come here to buy what they cannot get in the barracks.

areas.name: Pawn Corner
areas.text: The corner of old tools, watches and forged papers.

areas.name: Stall Lane
areas.text: The lane of awnings, the noise and the cheap food.

locations.name: Marl Bank School
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A city school by the river for the children of soldiers and workmen, run by a headmistress who has buried a husband from the war. The older boys drill in the yard with sticks and the younger ones copy circles into their slates.

areas.name: Marl Bank Classroom
areas.text: Desks in rows facing a blackboard, a stove in the corner and the drone of times tables.

areas.name: Marl Bank Playground
areas.text: An asphalt yard with a high fence, a water pump and chalk marks for games.

locations.name: Marl Flats Market Gardens
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate]

Flat fields on the river plain west of the city where market gardeners grow the vegetables for the city's market. The glasshouses shine in the sun and the carts set out for the city before light.

areas.name: Marl Flats Cabbage Rows
areas.text: Open fields of cabbages and leeks with a windmill pumping water.

areas.name: Marl Flats Glasshouses
areas.text: Long glasshouses of tomatoes and cucumbers, warm and damp inside.

locations.name: Marl Iron Bridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A riveted iron bridge that carries the road east across the Marl River. It was put up by army engineers during the war to move guns, and soldiers still stand guard at each end as if the war had not ended.

areas.name: Iron Bridge Sentry Posts
areas.text: Two sentry boxes, one at each end, with a lamp and a telephone.

areas.name: Iron Bridge Underside Ledge
areas.text: A narrow ledge under the girders, reached by climbing down from the bank.

locations.name: Marl Junction Signal Box
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A signal box where the line to Resembool leaves the main eastern line. The signalman sees every train in the east go past his window and writes them all in a book.

areas.name: Marl Junction Lever Frame
areas.text: A row of tall iron levers with brass plates showing which points they work.

areas.name: Marl Junction Points
areas.text: The points where the lines split, with a lamp and a hut for the lineman.

locations.name: Marl River Coal Wharf
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The city's main wharf on the Marl River, where barges bring coal down from Youswell and take back flour and tools. The cranes run all day and the dust settles on every window within a mile.

areas.name: Coal Wharf Bargemen's Shelter
areas.text: A shed with a brazier where the bargemen wait for their turn to unload.

areas.name: Coal Wharf Crane Berth
areas.text: A stone quay where steam cranes swing grabs of coal from the barges into carts.

locations.name: Marl Weir Pump House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A weir across the Marl River with a steam pumping station that keeps the city's drains from backing up in the floods. The engineers who work it know the tunnels under the city better than anyone above ground.

areas.name: Pump House Engine Hall
areas.text: A great beam engine that rocks back and forth, polished brass and hissing steam.

areas.name: Weir Sluice Gates
areas.text: Iron sluice gates across the river with wheels to raise and lower them.

locations.name: Mauro's Surgery
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 4-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The village doctor's cottage, where a quiet, stooped physician called Mauro treats every ailment for whatever the patient can spare. The villagers swear he has never lost a case he took.

areas.name: Surgery Herb Garden
areas.text: A walled patch of medicinal herbs behind the cottage, carefully labelled.

areas.name: Surgery Treatment Room
areas.text: A scrubbed room with a cot, a basin and a locked drawer he never opens in company.

locations.name: Military Investigations Office
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The office of the State Military's investigators, a floor of desks, interview rooms and filing cupboards a short walk from Central Command. Murders touching the army, deserters, frauds in the supply lines and the paper of every court martial pass through here. Maes Hughes runs it with a grin and a photograph of his daughter on every desk he can reach.

areas.name: Investigations Court-Martial Archive
areas.text: Shelves of bound trial records, kept in order by a clerk with a rubber stamp.

areas.name: Military Investigations Case Room
areas.text: A long room of desks and corkboards where the officers pin up their cases.

areas.name: Military Investigations Interview Room
areas.text: A bare room with one table, two chairs and a window painted shut.

locations.name: Military Survey Camp
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A survey party of the State Military camps between the ruins and the oasis, mapping the desert with theodolites and chains. Their State Alchemist spends most of his time freeing his motor car from the sand.

areas.name: Map Tent
areas.text: The tent of maps, tables and pinned charts.

areas.name: Stuck Car
areas.text: The motor car buried to its axles at the camp edge.

areas.name: Theodolite Line
areas.text: The row of survey stations along the ridge.

locations.name: Mine Number Eight
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-15 · Danger: Moderate]

One of the numbered shafts that riddle the hills behind the town, newer than the main pit and worked hard. Its galleries run long and low, and the props that hold them up were cut too thin to save on timber.

areas.name: Number Eight Cage
areas.text: The iron cage that drops the shift down the shaft on a singing cable.

areas.name: Number Eight Long Gallery
areas.text: A tunnel too low to stand in, propped every few feet with fresh pine.

areas.name: Number Eight Pithead Yard
areas.text: The yard at the top where the tubs are tipped and the crews are counted.

locations.name: Miners' Allotments
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Plots of beans and potatoes on the hill above the town, dug by miners who want something green after a shift in the dark. Every plot has its own fence and its own feud.

areas.name: Allotment Bean Rows
areas.text: Rows of beans on poles and potatoes in ridges.

areas.name: Allotment Water Barrels
areas.text: Barrels filled from the town's water tower by bucket.

locations.name: Miners' Hall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The hall where the miners meet to talk pay and safety, with plain benches and a banner that has been mended many times. Outsiders are welcome if they sit at the back.

areas.name: Meeting Room
areas.text: The room of benches and a table for the chairman.

locations.name: Miners' Widows' Laundry
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A yard of coppers and lines where the women whose husbands died below take in washing for the whole town. The work is endless, because nothing in Youswell stays white for a day.

areas.name: Laundry Copper Yard
areas.text: Steaming coppers on brick hearths and tubs of grey water.

areas.name: Laundry Drying Lines
areas.text: Lines of shirts flapping in the wind and going grey again as they dry.

locations.name: Mountain Hideout
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High]

The caves and gorges in the red hills east of Ishval, where the survivors of the war who refuse the army's rule keep their camps. The paths are known to few and the caves are hard to search.

areas.name: Cave Mouth
areas.text: The first cave and its fire pit, sheltered from the wind.

areas.name: Gorge Path
areas.text: The narrow path between the cliffs, where a waterfall falls in the dry season.

locations.name: Mountain Pass West
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

A high pass through the western mountains that is the main route for traders on foot. It is closed by snow for half the year and watched by both sides when it is open.

areas.name: Pass Track
areas.text: The track of loose stone that climbs to the top.

areas.name: Summit Hut
areas.text: The hut at the top of the pass, shut against the snow.

locations.name: Mountain Shrine
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-26 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A shrine on a crag above the capital's northern valley, reached by a stair cut into the rock. Ribbons hang from its pines and the wind carries the prayers away.

areas.name: Crag Shrine
areas.text: The shrine on the summit, with its ribbons and its bell.

areas.name: Rock Stair
areas.text: The stair cut into the crag, steep and worn.

locations.name: Mulberry Silk Sheds
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate]

On the low hills by the river, long sheds house silkworms on racks of mulberry leaves. Women reel the thread off boiled cocoons and wind it for the dyers of the capital.

areas.name: Cocoon Reeling Room
areas.text: A steamy room of basins and wheels where thread is drawn off the cocoons.

areas.name: Mulberry Leaf Racks
areas.text: Tiered trays of leaves and worms, rustling like rain.

locations.name: Mustang Unit Office
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A long room on the second floor of Eastern Command where the colonel's officers share desks, cigarettes and an endless pile of administration handed down from above. Hawkeye keeps the schedule, Havoc keeps the window open, and the colonel keeps finding reasons not to sign anything.

areas.name: Mustang Unit Paperwork Desk
areas.text: The colonel's desk, buried under forms with a pen lying idle on top.

areas.name: Mustang Unit Wireless Corner
areas.text: A bench of valves, wires and headphones where Fuery takes things apart.

locations.name: Nameless Village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-10 · Danger: Low]

A small village between East City and Resembool whose station placards are left blank, so the maps call it a town with no name. Most travellers pass it by on the road.

areas.name: Mill Wheel
areas.text: The wheel on the stream and the miller's house beside it.

areas.name: Village Track
areas.text: The dirt track that runs through the houses and out to the road.

locations.name: Nameless Village Halt
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-10 · Danger: Low]

The train between East City and Resembool stops here only when someone waves it down, at a platform whose name board was never painted. The village likes it that way.

areas.name: Halt Blank Name Board
areas.text: A long white board on posts with nothing written on it but bird droppings.

areas.name: Halt Shelter Bench
areas.text: A three-sided shelter with a bench and a lamp nobody lights.

locations.name: Nameless Village Smallholdings
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-10 · Danger: Low]

The village's fields run out in long strips on either side of the track, each worked by a family with a goat, a cow if they are lucky, and a patch of rye. Before the doctor came, half of them had someone too sick to work.

areas.name: Smallholdings Goat Tethers
areas.text: A common patch where the goats are tethered by day on long chains.

areas.name: Smallholdings Rye Strips
areas.text: Long strips of rye divided by grassy balks, with a scarecrow on each.

locations.name: National Central Library
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The largest library in Amestris, split into branches that hold books and records gathered from the whole nation. Most of it is open to the public; some branches, the First Branch's government records among them, admit only State Alchemists and officers of rank, and the staff check every bag at the door.

areas.name: Reading Halls
areas.text: The long halls of tables and brass lamps, where scholars work by the windows.

areas.name: Restricted Stacks
areas.text: The shelves behind a grille, where the forbidden alchemy texts are kept.

locations.name: New Optain Line Platform
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The arrival platform for the line from New Optain, where the passenger trains come in under a smoky iron roof. Since a hijacked train pulled in here with a general aboard and two boys holding its captors, the guard on it has been doubled.

areas.name: Optain Platform Buffer Stops
areas.text: The end of the line, two iron buffers and a lamp post scarred by a stray bullet.

areas.name: Optain Platform Waiting Room
areas.text: Benches, a stove, a timetable on the wall and a ticket window that is usually shut.

locations.name: No Man's Strip
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-26 · Danger: High]

Between the Amestrian posts and the Cretan ones lies a strip of burned farmland nobody has worked for years. A ruined farmhouse stands in the middle of it, and both sides send men to it at night.

areas.name: Burned Furrows
areas.text: Old furrows black with burning, cut by shell holes.

areas.name: Ruined Farmhouse
areas.text: A roofless farmhouse with a cellar that is not as empty as it looks.

locations.name: North Area Barracks
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The barracks of the North Area's own troops, the men who answer to the city's headquarters rather than to the fort. They patrol the streets, guard the trains and are sent out whenever headquarters receives a tip worth acting on.

areas.name: Barracks Armoury Hatch
areas.text: A barred window where rifles and ammunition are signed out against a book.

areas.name: Barracks Ready Room
areas.text: The room by the gate where a squad sits in its coats, waiting to be called out.

areas.name: North Barrack Square
areas.text: The swept parade square between the blocks, with its flagpole and its frozen water trough.

locations.name: North Area Military Hospital
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The military hospital of the north, which takes the frostbite cases and the injured from the fort as well as the city's sick. Its surgeons are good at amputation and its automail ward is never empty.

areas.name: Fitting Ward
areas.text: The ward where amputees wait for their automail and learn to use it.

areas.name: Frostbite Ward
areas.text: The long ward of beds under warm blankets, smelling of liniment.

locations.name: North City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The State Military's command centre for the north, a picturesque town south of the Briggs range, under snow most of the year and tied to the capital by rail. Fort Briggs is hard to reach by ordinary transport, so soldiers bound for it report at the northern headquarters first and then walk the main road or wait for an escort down from the fort.

areas.name: Fort Road Gate
areas.text: The gate where the road to Fort Briggs leaves the city.

areas.name: North Station
areas.text:
The rail halt where the northern trains arrive, with its ticket hall and its waiting room.

The rail and coach service serves this yard: coaches run to Central City (about 16 Cens), Fort Briggs (about 9 Cens); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Square Fountain
areas.text: The city square with its frozen fountain and its clock.

locations.name: North City Bathhouse
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A public bathhouse heated by a great coal boiler, with hot pools, cold plunges and wooden benches. In the depth of winter it is the warmest room in the city, and half the town's business is done in its steam.

areas.name: Bathhouse Boiler Cellar
areas.text: The roaring cellar room of the coal boiler and its gauges.

areas.name: Bathhouse Hot Pool
areas.text: The tiled pool under the steam, ringed by benches.

locations.name: North City Coal Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The coal yard by the line, where the trains drop the coal that keeps every stove in the city burning. Coalmen weigh it out by the sack and carry it house to house on their backs.

areas.name: Coal Yard Heaps
areas.text: The black heaps by the siding, shovelled into sacks under arc lamps.

areas.name: Coal Yard Weighbridge
areas.text: The iron weighbridge and its hut, where every cart is weighed in and out.

locations.name: North City Gas Works
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The gas works that light the city's streets and the headquarters, roasting coal in its retorts and storing the gas in a great iron holder that rises and sinks with the day. The tar it leaves is sold to the roofers.

areas.name: Gas Works Retort House
areas.text: The hot brick house of ovens where the coal is roasted for its gas.

areas.name: Gasholder Ring
areas.text: The ground around the great iron holder, fenced off and smelling of tar.

locations.name: North City Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The civil office of the city, where permits, deeds and burial papers are stamped. The mayor holds office with the northern command's approval, and everyone in the building knows whose approval matters more.

areas.name: City Hall Permit Counter
areas.text: A long counter of stamps and inkpads, with a clerk behind each grille.

areas.name: Mayor's Parlour
areas.text: The panelled room upstairs with its portrait of the Führer and its good carpet.

locations.name: North City Horse Fair
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A fairground at the eastern edge of the city where horses and ponies are traded once a month. The army buys the strongest for its supply trains, and the farmers buy what is left.

areas.name: Horse Fair Pens
areas.text: The rough pens where the dealers keep their stock, with hay and buckets.

areas.name: Horse Fair Sale Ring
areas.text: The trampled ring where the horses are walked and the bids are shouted.

locations.name: North City Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The market of North City, with stalls of furs, smoked meat and warm cloth. The traders are used to selling to soldiers and carry the news of the road with their wares.

areas.name: Fur Row
areas.text: The stalls of furs and coats, hung from poles.

areas.name: Meat Hall
areas.text: The hall of smoked meat and sausage, dark and smoky.

locations.name: North City Officers' Billet
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A boarding house the northern command rents whole for officers newly posted to the city. Most stay a week before orders send them up the road to the fort; a few stay months, waiting on a posting that never comes.

areas.name: Billet End Room
areas.text: The cold room at the end of the top corridor, kept for whoever arrived last.

areas.name: Billet Letter Hall
areas.text: The narrow entrance hall, with a letter rack for every room and a bell for the landlady.

locations.name: North City Stockade
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The military stockade on the western edge of the city, where soldiers serving punishment and civilian prisoners waiting for transfer to the capital sleep in long huts. They clear the city's snow by day.

areas.name: Stockade Huts
areas.text: The long timber huts with their bunks and their single stove each.

areas.name: Stockade Watch Platform
areas.text: The raised platform over the gate, with a lamp and a rifle rack.

locations.name: North City Telephone Exchange
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The city's telephone exchange, where a dozen operators connect the headquarters, the hospital, the mills and a handful of rich houses. The line to the capital runs from here, and so does the line up to the fort.

areas.name: Exchange Lineman's Store
areas.text: A back store of wire drums, climbing irons and lanterns.

areas.name: Exchange Switchboard
areas.text: The long room of operators on high stools, plugging and unplugging their cords.

locations.name: North Command Headquarters
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The headquarters of the northern command, a grey block of offices and records. Its generals handle the supply to the fort and the reports to the capital, and its sentries are the most careful in the city.

areas.name: Front Office
areas.text: The reception hall and the duty desk.

areas.name: North Records
areas.text: The records of the north, in long steel cabinets.

locations.name: North Herald Press
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The office of the north's daily paper, which prints the weather, the train times, the army's notices and as much gossip as the censor will let through. Its front window carries the day's pages pasted up for those who will not buy one.

areas.name: Editor's Cubby
areas.text: A cramped office of proofs, a spike of rejected copy and a kettle.

areas.name: Herald Press Floor
areas.text: The thumping room where the flatbed press runs at night and the type is set by hand.

locations.name: North Line Trestle
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The iron trestle that carries the northern line across a ravine south of the city. Every train to the capital crosses it, so the army keeps a sentry at each end, stamping his feet.

areas.name: Trestle Rail Deck
areas.text: The narrow deck of rails and sleepers over the ravine.

areas.name: Trestle Ravine Floor
areas.text: The frozen stream at the bottom of the ravine, under the girders.

locations.name: North Watchtower
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A stone watchtower on the northern edge of the city, where a sentry keeps the road to the range in view. Its lamp is lit every night and seen from the fort.

areas.name: Lamp Room
areas.text: The room at the top with its lamp and its telescope.

areas.name: Watchtower Stair
areas.text: The stone stair up the tower, icy in the morning.

locations.name: Northbank Sawmill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A sawmill on the north bank of the river, where the logs from the pine forests are cut into planks. In summer the wheel drives the saws; in winter a steam engine takes over and the wheel stands frozen.

areas.name: Northbank Log Boom
areas.text: The river bank where the floated logs are chained, frozen in now.

areas.name: Northbank Saw Floor
areas.text: The long shed where the steam saw screams through the logs.

locations.name: Northern Drill Field
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

An open field west of the city where the North Area's troops drill, shoot and dig practice trenches in the frozen ground. Recruits learn to fire in mittens here before anyone sends them to the fort.

areas.name: Drill Field Firing Line
areas.text: The trampled line of firing positions, littered with brass.

areas.name: Drill Field Trenches
areas.text: A zigzag of trenches cut into the frozen ground, half full of snow.

locations.name: Northern Farms
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The farms that feed North City in summer and sell their grain at the market in winter. The farmers are quiet and hardy, and they know the road to the fort better than the officers do.

areas.name: Barn Yard
areas.text: The yard of timber barns with a frozen well.

areas.name: Field Track
areas.text: The track between the fields where the carts pass in winter.

locations.name: Northern Foundry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A foundry that casts stove plates, rail chairs and, under contract, shell casings for the army. Its cupola can be seen glowing from the square on a dark afternoon.

areas.name: Foundry Casting Floor
areas.text: The sand floor where the moulds are laid and the iron is poured.

areas.name: Foundry Pattern Loft
areas.text: The loft of wooden patterns for every casting the foundry has ever made.

locations.name: Northern Inn
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-16 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A plain inn in North City for the carters and soldiers on leave, with a warm taproom and rooms upstairs. The stew is good and the beds are colder than the room.

areas.name: Back Room
areas.text: The room behind the bar with its table and its locked door.

areas.name: North Inn Taproom
areas.text: The warm room with its stove, its stools and its ceiling beams.

locations.name: Northern Jade Diggings
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

Jade is cut from the cliffs of a northern valley in terraces, and the stones go down in baskets to the sorting sheds. Most of the diggers come from the poorest clans and owe their wages before they earn them.

areas.name: Jade Diggings Cliff Terraces
areas.text: Narrow terraces cut along the cliff face, with ropes and ladders.

areas.name: Jade Sorting Sheds
areas.text: Sheds where the stones are washed and graded under lamps.

locations.name: Northern Quartermaster's Depot
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The depot where everything bound for the fort is counted, stacked and loaded: flour, coal, ammunition, boots and spare parts for the fort's machines. Its siding takes the freight trains from the capital.

areas.name: Depot Loading Siding
areas.text: The rail siding where freight wagons are unloaded by hand and crane.

areas.name: Depot Tally Shed
areas.text: The shed where the counts are kept, with books stacked to the roof.

areas.name: Tarpaulin Stacks
areas.text: The yard of crates under snow-laden tarpaulins, row after row.

locations.name: Northern Rail Halt
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A small halt on the northern line, a timber platform and a stove for the waiting passengers. The trains here are late in winter and the porters stamp their feet while they wait.

areas.name: Platform Two
areas.text: The timber platform and its lamp, with the snow piled at its edge.

areas.name: Waiting Room
areas.text: The little room with its stove and its bench.

locations.name: Northern Savings Bank
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A small stone bank on the square where soldiers send their pay home and farmers borrow against the next harvest. Its manager knows every debt in the city by heart.

areas.name: Green Vault
areas.text: The strongroom behind its green steel door, opened twice a day.

areas.name: Savings Banking Hall
areas.text: The cold marble hall with its counter, its brass rail and its ticking clock.

locations.name: Northern Steppe Horse Runs
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

North of the capital the hills open into grassland where herders raise the horses the imperial guard rides. The herds are counted every spring.

areas.name: Steppe Herders' Felt Tents
areas.text: Round felt tents with smoke holes in their roofs.

areas.name: Steppe Horse Corrals
areas.text: Rail corrals where the herds are gathered for the count.

locations.name: Northroad Coaching Inn
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-18 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

On the road north out of West City a coaching inn changes horses for the mail coach and puts up travellers who would rather not take the train. It has a painted sign of a galloping horse and a cellar full of good cider.

areas.name: Cider Cellar
areas.text: A cool cellar of casks under the inn.

areas.name: Northroad Horse Yard
areas.text: The yard where the horses are changed in a clatter of hooves.

locations.name: Oasis Palms
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: Severe]

A small oasis of date palms and a green pool, with clay huts for the families who keep the palms and sell the fruit to the caravans. It is the only shade for a long way.

areas.name: Green Pool
areas.text: The pool of water, shaded by the palms.

areas.name: Palm Grove
areas.text: The grove of date palms with their baskets of fruit.

locations.name: Old Arsenal
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The old arsenal of the capital, a brick store of shells, rifles and shot kept behind iron gates and a double guard. Its keepers sign for every crate that leaves and every one that comes in.

areas.name: Keepers' Office
areas.text: The office where the crates are signed out in a book.

areas.name: Shell Store
areas.text: The vaulted store of shells in their crates, dry and cold.

locations.name: Old Border War Memorial
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-11 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A bronze column in a small square, raised for the war with Aerugo that South City fought in 1835. The city's guides bring visitors here to tell them the south has always held, and wreaths for the present war pile up around its base.

areas.name: Memorial Square
areas.text: A small square around the column, shaded by plane trees.

locations.name: Old Caravan Track
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: Severe]

A track worn into the desert by centuries of caravans, marked by cairns and bleached bones. Those who know it can ride it by night; those who do not follow it to its end.

areas.name: Cairn Line
areas.text: The line of stone markers along the track.

areas.name: Lost Bend
areas.text: The bend where the track vanishes in sand and must be found again.

locations.name: Old Customs House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The customs house where trade from Aerugo was once weighed and taxed, from the years when the two countries dealt with each other in peace. It has been shut since the war began, and a single watchman sleeps in its hall.

areas.name: Records Loft
areas.text: A loft of boxes and books going back decades.

areas.name: Weighing Hall
areas.text: An empty hall of great scales and dust.

locations.name: Old Frontier Mill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A mill on the southern stream, burned in the first months of the war and never rebuilt. Its wheel still stands and its stones are used by the families in the valley to grind their corn.

areas.name: Frontier Mill Wheel
areas.text: The broken wheel above the stream, creaking in the wind.

areas.name: Mill Cellar
areas.text: The cellar under the mill, damp and full of barrels.

locations.name: Old Garrison Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate]

An old yard behind the barracks where the garrison keeps its spare crates, rusted guns and the wreck of a motor lorry. No one has used it for years but the rats.

areas.name: Crate Stacks
areas.text: The stacks of crates, the old guns and the lorry's shell.

locations.name: Old Lake Fort
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A fort on the lake's south shore, built long ago and left to ruin when the town grew past it. Its walls still stand against the wind and the fishermen use its courtyard to dry their nets.

areas.name: Fort Cellar
areas.text: The cellar under the walls, dark and damp.

areas.name: Fort Courtyard
areas.text: The courtyard of drying nets between the broken walls.

locations.name: Old Lumber Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

A lumber camp on the lower slopes of the range, its trees felled and its sawmill half built. The camp was abandoned when the timber contract ended, and the sledges are still stacked where the men left them.

areas.name: Sledge Row
areas.text: The row of sledges stacked under a lean-to.

areas.name: Stump Field
areas.text: The field of cut stumps and bare slopes.

locations.name: Old Market of Xerxes
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

The marketplace was a long street of stone stalls with a sundial column where the merchants set their hours. Every stall still has its counter, and children from the refugee camp play at selling sand to one another across them.

areas.name: Stall Street
areas.text: The long market street with its rows of empty counters.

areas.name: Sundial Square
areas.text: The open square at the market's end, where the tall column throws its shadow.

areas.name: Weighhouse
areas.text: A roofless hall where goods were weighed and taxed.

locations.name: Old Olive Grove
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-11 · Danger: Moderate]

An ancient grove of olive trees west of the city, gnarled and hollow, with dry grass and cicadas between them. The families who own it have harvested the same trees for longer than Amestris has had a Führer.

areas.name: Hollow Trees
areas.text: The oldest trees, split and hollow enough to stand inside.

areas.name: Olive Press Yard
areas.text: A yard of stone presses and jars under a fig tree.

locations.name: Old Quarry Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The old road that runs out of East City past a disused quarry, now a route for the garrison's wagons and the workmen going to the eastern depots.

areas.name: Quarry Cut
areas.text: The deep cut in the rock where the old quarry was worked.

areas.name: Sentry Hut
areas.text: The hut at the road's edge with its barrier and its book.

locations.name: Ostermann Uniform Outfitters
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Every new officer posted east is sent here for a proper uniform cut, because the stores issue fits nobody. The old tailor knows the measure of half the colonels in the army and gossips about none of them.

areas.name: Ostermann Cutting Table
areas.text: A broad table of chalked cloth, shears and paper patterns in labelled rolls.

areas.name: Ostermann Fitting Mirrors
areas.text: Three tall mirrors at angles, so a man can see his back for the first time in years.

locations.name: Ostfeld Brickworks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A brickworks on the clay fields west of the city that made the barracks, the hospital and most of the new streets. Its kiln burns day and night, and the pit beside it grows deeper every year.

areas.name: Ostfeld Clay Pit
areas.text: A deep red pit with a narrow track down its side and puddles at the bottom.

areas.name: Ostfeld Kiln Ring
areas.text: A circular kiln of many chambers where bricks are fired in turn.

locations.name: Oven Street
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The bakers' street, the one street in North City where the snow never settles, because the ovens behind every front warm the cobbles. People walk the long way round in winter just to pass through it.

areas.name: Flour Cellar
areas.text: The vaulted cellar under the oldest bakery, stacked with sacks.

areas.name: Oven Street Fronts
areas.text: The row of bakery windows with their loaves, their pretzels and their steam.

locations.name: Parliament House
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The Parliament building of Amestris, a columned hall of benches and committees where the nation's laws are argued and passed. Visitors wait for hours in its halls, and the guards are polite and very thorough.

areas.name: Chamber Floor
areas.text: The benches and the speaker's dais under the glass dome.

areas.name: Committee Corridor
areas.text: The offices and rooms where the real work of the house is done.

locations.name: Pavilion Music Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A music hall of comic songs, jugglers and dancing girls where the garrison spends its pay on the nights after payday. The gallery is for privates and throws things; the boxes are for officers and pretend not to laugh.

areas.name: Pavilion Gallery Bar
areas.text: A crowded bar at the top of the house where privates drink beer between acts.

areas.name: Pavilion Stage
areas.text: A sloped stage with footlights and a painted backcloth of a seaside that nobody here has seen.

locations.name: Pawnbroker of Front Street
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-11 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A narrow pawnshop near the market where soldiers pawn watches before going south and widows pawn medals after. The broker is honest by the standards of the trade and remembers every face.

areas.name: Front Street Pawn Counter
areas.text: A counter behind a grille, with a book and a loupe.

areas.name: Medal Case
areas.text: A glass case of medals, rings and watches with tickets on them.

locations.name: Pendleton
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High]

Pendleton was the first town Amestris took from Creta in the border war, and the western command has made a banner of it ever since. Its streets are half barracks and half rubble, its few remaining families sell soup to the troops, and the fighting has never moved far from its last houses.

areas.name: Pendleton Billets
areas.text: Whole streets of houses turned into billets, chalk numbers on every door.

areas.name: Soup Kitchen Lane
areas.text: The one lane where townsfolk still trade, ladling soup to queues of soldiers.

areas.name: Victory Column Square
areas.text: The square around the column raised for the town's capture, its plinth chipped by rifle fire.

locations.name: Pendleton Field Hospital
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-24 · Danger: High]

Behind the front a field hospital of tents takes the wounded from the trenches before they are sent on by train. Its surgeons work by lamplight and its orderlies sleep standing up.

areas.name: Field Surgery Tent
areas.text: A tent of white canvas stained brown, with an operating table under a lamp.

areas.name: Field Triage Tent
areas.text: The first tent, where the wounded are sorted by who can wait.

areas.name: Pendleton Ambulance Track
areas.text: The rutted track down which the carts take the wounded to the halt.

locations.name: Pendleton Front
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-26 · Danger: High]

West of Pendleton the hills are cut into trenches that the two armies have traded back and forth for years. Nothing grows there but wire. Patrols go out at dusk in fours and fives, the way the western army has learned to fight, and not all of them return by dawn.

areas.name: Clay Trench Line
areas.text: The forward trench, its sides propped with doors from Pendleton's houses.

areas.name: Crater Field
areas.text: The cratered ground between the lines, where the dead lie until a truce lets them be fetched.

areas.name: Dugout Command
areas.text: A dugout roofed with rail sleepers where a lieutenant keeps the field telephone.

locations.name: Pendleton War Cemetery
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-24 · Danger: High]

A field of wooden markers runs down the hill below Pendleton, and every week the rows grow longer. The markers are painted with names when the names are known, and with a unit number when they are not.

areas.name: Gravedigger's Shed
areas.text: A shed of spades and a book kept in pencil.

areas.name: Pendleton Marker Rows
areas.text: The long rows of wooden markers, paint fading in the rain.

locations.name: Pickaxe Inn
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 6-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The inn meant for visitors, the only one in town with clean sheets and a bath that can be filled. Inspectors, coal buyers and the odd sightseer from the capital stay here; the bill reaches them on the morning they leave.

areas.name: Pickaxe Inn Bathhouse
areas.text: A tin bath behind a curtain and a copper of water heated with the town's own coal.

areas.name: Pickaxe Inn Parlour
areas.text: Plush chairs, a tired fern and a clock that runs ten minutes slow.

locations.name: Pine Smoke Ridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

On a ridge of pine forest, charcoal burners stack wood under earth and let it smoulder for days. Their charcoal feeds the foundry, the forges and every brazier in the capital.

areas.name: Charcoal Mound Clearing
areas.text: A clearing of smoking mounds watched day and night.

areas.name: Pine Smoke Burners' Huts
areas.text: Bark huts where the burners sleep in shifts.

locations.name: Pinewood Orphanage
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A home for orphaned children, many of them the sons and daughters of soldiers who did not come back from the border or from the eastern war. It runs on charity, a small army grant and the work of two tired matrons.

areas.name: Pinewood Dormitory
areas.text: The long room of narrow beds, each with its trunk and a mended blanket.

areas.name: Pinewood Yard
areas.text: The yard behind the house, trampled into a snowfield of games.

locations.name: Pit Pony Stables
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 7-11 · Danger: Moderate]

The stables where the ponies that haul the tubs underground are kept when they come up for their few days of light. The ostler loves them more than he loves most people.

areas.name: Pony Stalls
areas.text: Narrow stalls of tired ponies, their names chalked above.

areas.name: Stable Hay Loft
areas.text: A loft of hay where the ostler sleeps on bad nights.

locations.name: Pit Prop Timber Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 7-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A yard by the spur where pine logs are cut into the props that hold up the roofs below. The logs come down on flatcars from the woods to the west and are sawn to the inch.

areas.name: Timber Yard Log Stacks
areas.text: Pyramids of stripped pine waiting for the saw.

areas.name: Timber Yard Saw Bench
areas.text: The steam saw and its whining blade, deep in sawdust.

locations.name: Platelayers' Hut
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 7-11 · Danger: Moderate]

A tarred hut on the spur where the gang that keeps the rails straight eats its dinner and stores its bars. The gang is old, slow and knows every sleeper on the line.

areas.name: Platelayers' Stove Bench
areas.text: A bench by the stove where the gang drinks its tea.

areas.name: Platelayers' Tool Rack
areas.text: A rack of crowbars, shovels and jacks.

locations.name: Priests' Shrine
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

A shrine of the Warrior priests of Ishvala, cut from red stone and carved with verses of the faith. The priests keep the rites of the dead here and teach the young to fight for the holy land.

areas.name: Priests' Cells
areas.text: The small cells where the priests sleep and meditate.

areas.name: Shrine Hall
areas.text: The hall of carved verses and the altar stone.

locations.name: Pulse Spring Valley
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 16-22 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

Where the streams off the high peaks meet, a green valley holds a dozen warm springs. The sick are carried here on litters, and alkahestrists come to practise, saying the earth's flow runs closest to the surface in this place.

areas.name: Spring Healers' Huts
areas.text: Reed huts where healers lay their patients on mats by the water.

areas.name: Valley Warm Pools
areas.text: A chain of steaming rock pools stepping down the valley floor.

locations.name: Quartermaster's Wool Office
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 3-7 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The army buys the town's wool for its uniforms through this office, where a quartermaster's clerk grades each farm's clip and signs the contracts. The whole town's year turns on what he writes.

areas.name: Wool Office Contract Desk
areas.text: A desk with carbon forms, an army stamp and a locked strongbox.

areas.name: Wool Office Grading Table
areas.text: A long table under a skylight where fleeces are spread and pulled apart.

locations.name: Radio Capital
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High]

The capital's radio station, syndicated across the whole country. It plays mostly political talk, the kind listeners call boring, and its studio takes interviews from anyone the state wants heard.

areas.name: Broadcast Studio
areas.text: The studio with its microphones, red lamps and cushioned chairs.

areas.name: Transmitter Hall
areas.text: The hall of valves and wires, humming all day.

locations.name: Raiders' Hollow
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe]

Behind the salt ridge a hollow hides from the road, with a spring and a cave mouth. Raiders who prey on the caravans camp here and keep their stolen goods under canvas.

areas.name: Cave Store
areas.text: The cave where the loot is kept.

areas.name: Raider Fire
areas.text: The fire and the circle of stolen saddles round it.

locations.name: Rail Spur Halt
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A small rail halt on the spur that carries coal from Youswell to the main line. A timber platform, a water tank for the engines and a bench for the few passengers who come this way.

areas.name: Platform
areas.text: The timber platform and the bench under the lamp.

areas.name: Water Tank
areas.text: The tank and the pipe that fills the engines.

locations.name: Railhead Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 11-15 · Danger: Moderate]

The camp where the troop trains end and the march to the line begins. Soldiers step down from the cars, are formed into columns and given their first look at the smoke over Fotset.

areas.name: Railhead Platform
areas.text: A plank platform at the end of the rails, piled with crates.

areas.name: Tent Lines
areas.text: Rows of canvas tents, cook fires and drying socks.

locations.name: Railway Hotel West
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-16 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The best hotel in the city stands across from the station, all brass rails and potted palms. Visiting staff officers stay here, and so do the wives who come out from Central to see husbands posted to the border.

areas.name: Back Room Nine
areas.text: A small room off the service corridor with two chairs and a curtain.

areas.name: Hotel Palm Lobby
areas.text: The lobby of brass and palms where the porters watch every face.

areas.name: Railway Hotel Dining Room
areas.text: White tablecloths and quiet talk of postings.

locations.name: Rain River
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

The river that runs past Resembool to the south-east, broad and brown in spring and slow in summer. Boats are few and the ford is known to every child in town.

areas.name: Ford
areas.text: The shallow crossing with its flat stones, used by carts in dry weather.

areas.name: Willow Bank
areas.text: The bank under the willows, where the children fish and the washing is laid out.

locations.name: Rain River Alder Wood
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-9 · Danger: Low]

A wet wood along the far bank where alders grow out of the shallows and the light comes through green. Charcoal burners work its dry edge and leave their mounds smoking for days.

areas.name: Alder Wood Charcoal Mounds
areas.text: Turf-covered mounds smouldering in a clearing, tended by a man with a rake.

areas.name: Alder Wood Drowned Grove
areas.text: Trees standing in shallow water where the bank has sunk.

locations.name: Rain River Bridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A wooden bridge over the Rain River on the road to East City, with a toll post at one end and a lamp that lights itself on dark nights. The planks are wet and loose in places.

areas.name: Bridge Deck
areas.text: The planks and rails of the crossing, with the water loud below.

areas.name: Toll Post
areas.text: The small post with its gate, its lamp and its book.

locations.name: Rain River Eel Weir
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-8 · Danger: Low]

A weir of stakes and wicker that funnels the river's eels into traps, worked by one family for longer than Resembool has had a station. They smoke the catch and sell it on market days.

areas.name: Eel Smoking Shed
areas.text: A small shed hung with split eels over an oak-chip fire.

areas.name: Eel Weir Trap Line
areas.text: The line of wicker traps across the channel, checked at dawn from the punt.

locations.name: Rain River Fellmonger's Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-7 · Danger: Low]

Downstream of the town, where the smell can do the least harm, the fellmonger takes the skins of dead sheep, limes them, pulls the wool and sells the pelts on. Nobody visits who does not have to.

areas.name: Fellmonger's Drying Frames
areas.text: Rows of wooden frames with pelts stretched taut in the wind.

areas.name: Fellmonger's Lime Pits
areas.text: Square pits of lime water where the skins soak until the wool slips.

locations.name: Rain River Ferry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-8 · Danger: Low]

Downstream of the bridge, a flat ferry hauled along a chain takes carts and flocks across to the far farms. Ring the bell on the post and the ferryman comes, eventually.

areas.name: Ferry Chain Landing
areas.text: A muddy landing with the chain running into the water and the bell on its post.

areas.name: Ferryman's Hut
areas.text: A one-room hut on stilts with nets, a lamp and a book he does not keep honestly.

locations.name: Rain River Fox Covert
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-9 · Danger: Low]

A tangle of gorse and blackthorn on the high corner of the district, left wild for the foxes that every farmer curses and every hunting officer from East City wants to chase.

areas.name: Covert Gorse Thicket
areas.text: A thicket of gorse higher than a man, with fox runs tunnelling through it.

areas.name: Covert Keeper's Gibbet
areas.text: A rail on two posts where the keeper hangs the vermin he has killed.

locations.name: Rain River Mill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A water mill on the Rain River that grinds the wheat of the district into flour. The miller is a widower who knows every cart on the road.

areas.name: Granary
areas.text: The loft of sacks, dry and dark, reached by a ladder.

areas.name: Grinding Room
areas.text: The great stones and the wheel that turns them, loud and dusty.

locations.name: Rain River Oxbow
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-9 · Danger: Low]

A loop of the Rain River that the current abandoned long ago, now a still crescent of water ringed with willows. Mosquitoes in summer, skating ice in winter and fish all year.

areas.name: Oxbow Lily Water
areas.text: The still middle of the crescent, thick with lily pads and dragonflies.

areas.name: Oxbow Sunken Stern
areas.text: A rotted stern of a rowing boat sticking out of the mud by the inner bank.

locations.name: Rain River Rail Viaduct
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-8 · Danger: Low]

Seven stone arches carry the line from East City over the Rain River before it curves into Resembool. Boys dare each other to walk the parapet when no train is due.

areas.name: Viaduct Parapet Walk
areas.text: The narrow walk beside the rails with a low wall and a long drop.

areas.name: Viaduct Pier Footings
areas.text: The muddy footings of the arches down at the waterline, cold and echoing.

locations.name: Rain River Reed Marsh
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-9 · Danger: Low]

Where the Rain River spreads out east of the town, it loses itself in a marsh of reeds taller than a man. Thatchers cut the reeds in winter and nobody else has much reason to go in.

areas.name: Marsh Black Channels
areas.text: Narrow channels of still dark water between the reeds, easy to get lost in.

areas.name: Marsh Reed Cutting
areas.text: A cleared stretch where the thatchers stack their bundles on a raised bank.

locations.name: Rain River Sheep Wash
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-7 · Danger: Low]

Before shearing the flocks are washed here, pushed one by one through a pool dammed off the Rain River and scrubbed by men standing waist deep. The work is cold, loud and all done in two days.

areas.name: Sheep Wash Dipping Pool
areas.text: The dammed pool, chest deep, with a stone ramp out the far side.

areas.name: Sheep Wash Holding Pens
areas.text: Stone pens where the flocks wait, bleating, to be pushed in.

locations.name: Range Pelt Post
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A trading store west of the range where trappers sell their furs and buy traps, powder and coffee. The trader grades each pelt with a thumb and a look, and his grades are final.

areas.name: Pelt Post Counter
areas.text: A long counter with a fur scale, a book and jars of coffee beans.

areas.name: Pelt Post Drying Racks
areas.text: Racks of stretched skins behind the store, freezing in the open air.

locations.name: Range Weather Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A small army weather station on a rise north-east of the city, where an observer reads the barometer, the wind and the snow depth three times a day and wires them to the fort and to headquarters.

areas.name: Observer's Hut
areas.text: The hut with the telegraph key, the log and a cot.

areas.name: Weather Instrument Box
areas.text: The white louvred box of thermometers and the snow gauge beside it.

locations.name: Rebuilt Station Row
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-7 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The few blocks around the station that Ishvalan bombers blew apart in 1907, put back up in brick because brick was quicker. The street is wider than the rest of the town and a little too tidy, and a bronze plate on the corner lists the dead.

areas.name: Station Row Brick Terrace
areas.text: A terrace of shops and flats in raw red brick, every lintel the same.

areas.name: Station Row Memorial Corner
areas.text: The corner with the bronze plate and a stone trough of geraniums.

locations.name: Red Banner Ravines
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High]

West of the capital the land breaks into dry ravines before the desert, and bandits who fly red rags on the trees rob the caravans going to the sand.

areas.name: Red Banner Dry Gully
areas.text: A narrow gully where the bandits keep their horses.

areas.name: Red Banner Lookout Rock
areas.text: A high rock that watches the western road.

locations.name: Red Coat Encampment
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The main camp of the Aerugonian army facing the front, rows of white tents and drilling men in red overcoats with yellow cords at the shoulder. Most of the country's army is here, and it shows in the faces.

areas.name: Encampment Parade
areas.text: A square of trampled grass where the red coats drill.

areas.name: General's Pavilion
areas.text: A striped pavilion of maps, wine and couriers.

locations.name: Red Gullies
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A maze of eroded gullies of red earth south-west of the line, too broken for wagons and too deep to watch from the towers. Scouts of both armies use it, and both have lost men in it.

areas.name: Gully Floor
areas.text: The narrow sandy bottom of the gullies, hot and airless.

areas.name: Thorn Rim
areas.text: The broken rim where scouts lie in the thorn and watch.

locations.name: Red Mesa Signal Post
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

The telegraph wire stops at the railhead, so the army keeps a heliograph on top of a red mesa to flash messages between the barracks and the patrols. Two signallers live up there in a stone hut, haul their water up by rope, and come down once a fortnight.

areas.name: Red Mesa Heliograph Ledge
areas.text: The ledge at the mesa's edge where the mirror stands on its tripod.

areas.name: Red Mesa Signallers' Hut
areas.text: A hut of piled stone with two bunks and a logbook.

locations.name: Red Sandstone Quarry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

Quarrymen cut red sandstone here and haul it west by wagon to the towns of the east. The faces are stepped and sharp, and the dust stains everything the colour of rust, men included.

areas.name: Cut Faces
areas.text: The stepped red faces where the blocks come out.

areas.name: Timber Crane
areas.text: The great wooden crane that lifts the blocks to the wagons.

locations.name: Red Wadi
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

A dry riverbed cuts a red canyon through the desert south-east of the oasis, its walls striped like a cut cake. Caravans like it for the shade and hate it for the rest: when rain falls on the hills far off, a brown wall of water comes down with no warning, and the flood marks sit well above a rider's head.

areas.name: Canyon Floor
areas.text: The dry gravel bed between the red walls.

areas.name: Flood Lines
areas.text: The high marks on the canyon walls, and the ledges above them.

locations.name: Refugee Weaving Sheds
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate]

Beside the refugee camp the women have built sheds of reed and set up looms rescued from the ruins. They weave prayer cloths, blankets and sashes, and a carter takes them to the market hall in Reole once a month.

areas.name: Refugee Cloth Lines
areas.text: Lines of red and white cloth drying between poles.

areas.name: Refugee Reed Loom Shed
areas.text: The largest shed, with four looms and a bench of spindles.

locations.name: Reole
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

A poor town of the east with a fierce faith in Leto, the sun god. The prophet Cornello made himself its ruler by working miracles, until the Fullmetal Alchemist showed them to be alchemy done with a false stone; Rose Thomas, once his follower, has led the townspeople since. A giant statue of Leto stands over the square.

areas.name: Church Steps
areas.text: The steps of the church and the cathedral's dusty spire above.

areas.name: Reole Market
areas.text: The square market of stalls and carts, always busy.

locations.name: Reole Army Post
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A requisitioned grain merchant's house on the east road, with sandbags in the doorway and the flag over the roof. Eastern Command posted a handful of men here after the town tore itself apart; the townspeople call it the guardhouse and walk on the other side of the street.

areas.name: Reole Army Post Granary Cells
areas.text: Two old grain rooms with bars fitted, used to cool off drunks and rioters.

areas.name: Reole Army Post Porch
areas.text: The front porch with its rifle rack and the sergeant's chair.

locations.name: Reole Brick Yard
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Down by the river the people of Reole make their own bricks: mud from the bank, straw from the farms, a kiln that burns day and night. No builder came from the city to help, so the baker, the schoolmaster and the widows of the fighting all learned to lay a course.

areas.name: Reole Brick Kiln
areas.text: The squat kiln and the woodpile beside it.

areas.name: Reole Brick Mud Pits
areas.text: Trodden pits by the river where the clay is mixed by foot.

areas.name: Reole Brick Racks
areas.text: Long rows of drying bricks under straw mats.

locations.name: Reole Burned Quarter
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A wedge of streets west of the square burned in the fighting between the faithful and those who turned on them. The walls mostly stand; the roofs went first. Families who have nowhere else live in the back rooms that kept a ceiling.

areas.name: Burned Quarter Back Rooms
areas.text: The roofed rooms at the back of the ruins where families camp.

areas.name: Reole Loyalists' Cellar
areas.text: A cellar under a burned house with a sun painted on its wall.

areas.name: Reole Scorched Lane
areas.text: A narrow lane of black-edged doorways.

locations.name: Reole Church
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-22 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The church of Reole, a tall building with a spire and old glass. Its congregation is smaller than it was, and the priests who remain are careful with their words.

areas.name: Crypt Stair
areas.text: The narrow stair down into the cold crypt.

areas.name: Nave
areas.text: The long nave with its pews and the faded mural above the altar.

locations.name: Reole Council House
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

When the church stopped ruling Reole, someone had to. The people meet in the old cloth guild hall, sit on chairs they bring from home and vote with raised hands. Rose Thomas speaks more than she would like and is listened to more than she expects.

areas.name: Reole Council Bell Loft
areas.text: A ladder up to the bell that calls the meetings.

areas.name: Reole Council Floor
areas.text: The open hall where the chairs are set in rough circles.

locations.name: Reole Date Groves
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate]

South of the town the river spreads into a green fan of date palms, the only real wealth Reole has. Families own single trees here, passed down and argued over, and climb them barefoot at harvest with baskets on their backs.

areas.name: Reole Grove Main Ditch
areas.text: The widest irrigation ditch with its sluice boards.

areas.name: Reole Old Palm Stand
areas.text: The oldest trees of the grove, their trunks scarred by generations of ladders.

locations.name: Reole Dispensary
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-13 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A pharmacist's shop with a back room that serves as the town's only surgery. The druggist is not a doctor and says so, but he set more bones in the fighting than any doctor within a day's ride.

areas.name: Reole Dispensary Back Room
areas.text: A scrubbed table, a basin and a cupboard of splints.

areas.name: Reole Dispensary Counter
areas.text: The front counter of jars and scales.

locations.name: Reole Dye Vats
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-13 · Danger: Moderate]

Below the bridge the river runs blue for a few yards where the dyers rinse their cloth. The vats are cut into the bank in a row, each its own colour, and the long poles above them carry wet cloth that sells in the market hall and on the trade road east.

areas.name: Reole Dye Drying Poles
areas.text: Long poles hung with dripping cloth above the bank.

areas.name: Reole Indigo Vat Row
areas.text: The row of cut-stone vats, each a different colour.

locations.name: Reole Goat Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-13 · Danger: Moderate]

On the east edge of town the herders from the dry country bring goats, sheep and the odd camel to sell by the head. The pens are loud and the haggling is louder, and the coffee stall by the weighing post never closes.

areas.name: Reole Goat Pens
areas.text: Rows of wattle pens and the animals in them.

areas.name: Reole Weighing Post Stall
areas.text: The coffee stall beside the post where deals are sealed.

locations.name: Reole Hillside Cemetery
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

Rows of white stones climb the slope behind the town, the older ones cut with the sun of Leto and the newer ones left plain. Rose Thomas walked up here every day for the young man she lost, and believed for a while that the prophet would give him back.

areas.name: Reole Cemetery Upper Rows
areas.text: The newest graves at the top of the slope, plain and close together.

areas.name: Reole Gravedigger's Shed
areas.text: A board shed with spades, a lantern and a register of every burial.

locations.name: Reole Limestone Pits
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A ridge of pale stone east of the town has been dug into shallow pits for lime, which the town needs for mortar and whitewash. The work is hot and blinding, and the pits are worked by whoever needs wages that week.

areas.name: Reole Deep Lime Pit
areas.text: The oldest and deepest of the pits, half filled with rubble.

areas.name: Reole Lime Kiln Row
areas.text: Three stone kilns where the cut stone is burned to lime.

locations.name: Reole Market Hall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

The covered market hall of Reole, with cloth from the east and baskets of spice from the trade road. The hall is loud at the morning and quiet by noon.

areas.name: Cloth Aisle
areas.text: The aisle of bolts and bright colours.

areas.name: Spice Corner
areas.text: The corner of baskets and sacks, sharp in the nose.

locations.name: Reole Pump House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-13 · Danger: Moderate]

The town's water comes up from the river through a small steam pump and a line of iron pipe to a tank above the square. The engine is older than anyone working it, and when it stops the whole of Reole carries buckets.

areas.name: Reole Pump Engine Room
areas.text: A hot room of pistons, gauges and a single stoker.

areas.name: Reole Pump Intake
areas.text: The grated intake on the riverbank, choked with reeds.

locations.name: Reole Schoolhouse
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

One room, one stove, forty children and a teacher who came from East City on a two-year post and stayed through the riots. The map of the nation on the wall has Reole circled in red ink by some pupil long ago.

areas.name: Reole Schoolhouse Yard
areas.text: A dirt yard with a skipping rope tied to a post.

areas.name: Reole Schoolroom
areas.text: Benches, slates and the red-circled map.

locations.name: Reole Station
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-13 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The branch line from the west ends in a single platform of red brick with a water tank for the engines and a ticket window the size of a bread oven. Two trains a day is a good day. Soldiers stand on the platform more often than travellers do since the trouble in the town.

areas.name: Reole Engine Tank
areas.text: The iron water tank where locomotives drink before the long run back.

areas.name: Reole Platform
areas.text: The brick platform with its benches, its bell and its view down the empty line.

areas.name: Reole Telegraph Office
areas.text: A cramped room off the ticket hall with the key, the forms and the stationmaster's stove.

locations.name: Requisition Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

An old assembly hall that the northern command lends to agents sent up from the capital on special business. When it is in use, the hall fills with maps, runners and telephone wire; when it is not, it is cold and locked.

areas.name: Requisition Map Boards
areas.text: The long wall of boards where the north's roads, mines and villages are pinned out in pencil.

areas.name: Requisition Runners' Bench
areas.text: The bench by the door where the messengers wait with their caps in their hands.

locations.name: Resembool
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A quiet rural town in the south-east of Amestris on the banks of the Rain River, known for its sheep and the wool it sends away for army uniforms. Ishvalan fighters bombed the blocks around its station in 1907; the station was rebuilt, the town stayed small, and every spring it holds a great sheep festival. A stranger is noticed at once.

areas.name: Resembool Station
areas.text:
The small station with its platform, its waiting bench and the timetable chalked on a board.

The rail and coach service serves this yard: coaches run to East City (about 6 Cens); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Sheep Lane
areas.text: The lane that runs out past the pens to the hills.

areas.name: Village Green
areas.text: The square at the town's heart, with the well, the cart stand and the wool sheds.

locations.name: Resembool Bakehouse
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-5 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]
