The baker lights her oven at three and the smell of bread reaches the station before the first train does. She bakes apple pie at the end of each week, and children who should be at school find reasons to pass the door.

areas.name: Bakehouse Oven Room
areas.text: The vaulted oven, the peel hanging beside it and a floor dusted white.

areas.name: Bakehouse Shop Window
areas.text: A narrow shop with a glass counter of rolls and pies.

locations.name: Resembool Carding House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low]

A small works on a leat off the river, where the coarser fleeces that the army will not buy are carded and spun into yarn for the town's own knitters. Its engines are older than anyone who works them.

areas.name: Carding Engine Floor
areas.text: Three wire-toothed carding engines in a row, driven by belts from the wheel.

areas.name: Carding House Yarn Loft
areas.text: Skeins of grey and cream yarn hung from poles to dry.

locations.name: Resembool Church
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The small chapel of Resembool with its one bell and its graveyard behind the wall. The priest is kind and a little frightened of strangers.

areas.name: Chapel Nave
areas.text: The pews, the altar and the plain window of colour glass.

areas.name: Churchyard
areas.text: The stones behind the wall, some with no names.

locations.name: Resembool Country Surgery
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-6 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

Since the Rockbell doctors went to the war and did not come back, an old physician retired out of East City has held surgery here three mornings a week. He sends the hard cases to Pinako, who sends the ones she cannot fix to the city.

areas.name: Surgery Consulting Room
areas.text: A desk, an examination couch and a cabinet of instruments gone dull.

areas.name: Surgery Waiting Bench
areas.text: A corridor bench under a framed chart of the bones of the hand.

locations.name: Resembool Downs
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-9 · Danger: Low]

Rolling high ground north and east of the town, cropped short by generations of sheep and open to every wind. A walker can go all day here without meeting anything but a flock and a hawk.

areas.name: Downs Dew Pond
areas.text: A round hollow lined with clay that holds rainwater for the flocks all summer.

areas.name: Downs Skyline Track
areas.text: The ridge path along the top of the downs, with views down the Rain River valley.

locations.name: Resembool Drovers' Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-9 · Danger: Low]

An old grass road wide enough for a flock of a thousand, running from Resembool toward East City alongside the railway. The drovers who walk it take a week to do what the train does in hours, and swear the sheep sell better.

areas.name: Drovers' Milestone Bend
areas.text: A bend marked by a worn stone that gives the miles to East City.

areas.name: Drovers' Watering Hollow
areas.text: A dip in the road with a trough and a hollow where the flocks are rested.

locations.name: Resembool Dry Goods Store
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Flour, nails, lamp oil, cloth by the yard and sweets for a coin: the store sells everything a farm cannot make for itself. The owner orders anything else from East City and takes a week to do it.

areas.name: Dry Goods Back Store
areas.text: Barrels, sacks and crates stacked to the rafters behind a canvas curtain.

areas.name: Dry Goods Shop Floor
areas.text: Shelves to the ceiling, a ladder on a rail and the counter with its till.

locations.name: Resembool Ewe-Milk Dairy
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low]

A farm dairy on the east lane where a family milks its ewes and makes a hard, salty cheese that keeps for a year. The cheese goes to East City by train; the whey goes to the pigs.

areas.name: Dairy Cheese Room
areas.text: A cool dark room of wheels on slatted shelves, each one turned by hand.

areas.name: Dairy Milking Shed
areas.text: A low shed with a stand for the ewes and a row of pails.

locations.name: Resembool Farrier's Forge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-7 · Danger: Low]

The farrier shoes the carthorses and mends the ploughs, and when Rockbell Automail runs short of a fitting he hammers that out too, grumbling that it is clockmaker's work.

areas.name: Farrier's Anvil Corner
areas.text: The anvil, quench tub and bellows, black with years of soot.

areas.name: Farrier's Shoeing Bay
areas.text: A cobbled bay with a ring in the wall and a horse's patience worn into the stones.

locations.name: Resembool Hill Cemetery
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-6 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The town's burying ground on the slope above the lanes, open to the wind and kept by whoever happens to be passing with a scythe. Trisha Elric lies here under a plain stone, and the brothers come up the path to it whenever they are home, however short the visit.

areas.name: Cemetery Lychgate
areas.text: A little roofed gate where the coffins rest on their way in, with a bench under it.

areas.name: Trisha Elric's Gravestone
areas.text: A modest upright stone near the top of the slope, its lettering kept clean.

locations.name: Resembool Hill Oak
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low]

A single oak on the crest north of the town, old enough that nobody remembers it young. The children of the town climb it, carve their names into it and swing from the rope on its lowest bough.

areas.name: Oak Carved Trunk
areas.text: The scarred trunk, rough with names and dates from three generations.

areas.name: Oak Rope Swing
areas.text: The low bough with its frayed rope swing and a worn patch of earth beneath.

locations.name: Resembool Lime Kiln
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-7 · Danger: Low]

Limestone from the hill is burned here into quicklime for the fields and the fellmonger's pits. The kiln burns for three days at a time and the kiln man sleeps beside it.

areas.name: Lime Kiln Charging Top
areas.text: The top of the kiln, reached by a ramp, where stone and coal are tipped in.

areas.name: Lime Kiln Draw Arch
areas.text: The arch at the kiln's foot where the burnt lime is raked out glowing.

locations.name: Resembool Line Signal Box
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-7 · Danger: Low]

A two-storey box beside the junction where the branch from East City meets the Resembool siding. The signalman keeps a kettle on and a register of every train to the minute.

areas.name: Signal Box Lever Frame
areas.text: A row of tall iron levers, polished bright where the hands go.

areas.name: Signal Box Stair
areas.text: The outside stair up to the box, with a lamp hook and a coal bin at its foot.

locations.name: Resembool Line Water Tank
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low]

Every engine on the branch line stops here to drink. The tank stands on iron legs west of the town and is fed from the river by a pump engine that coughs all day.

areas.name: Water Tank Gantry
areas.text: The ladder and walkway up to the tank's lid, with the hose swung out over the line.

areas.name: Water Tank Pump Shed
areas.text: A brick shed of thudding pistons and a cot where the keeper sleeps.

locations.name: Resembool Military Police Post
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 3-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Two military policemen and a sergeant keep order in the town from a two-room post by the road, and most weeks the worst they deal with is a stolen ewe. Since 1907 they have watched the station more closely than the sheep.

areas.name: Police Post Front Desk
areas.text: A desk, a book, a rifle rack and a stove that never quite heats the room.

areas.name: Police Post Lock-Up
areas.text: One barred cell with a cot, used mostly for drunks on festival night.

locations.name: Resembool Post Office
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Letters, parcels and the one public telephone in town all pass across a single counter here. The postmistress connects calls to East City by hand and hears more than she lets on.

areas.name: Post Office Counter
areas.text: A brass-grilled counter with a scale, a stamp drawer and a sorting rack.

areas.name: Post Office Telephone Nook
areas.text: A wall telephone with a stool beneath it and a curtain for privacy.

locations.name: Resembool Schoolhouse
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-5 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

One room, one stove and one teacher for every child in town between six and twelve. Some of the desks still carry the circles two clever boys scratched into them years ago.

areas.name: Schoolhouse Yard
areas.text: A beaten yard with a pump, a bell post and a fence the boys climb.

areas.name: Schoolroom Desks
areas.text: Rows of carved double desks facing a blackboard and a map of Amestris.

locations.name: Resembool Sheep Auction Ring
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-7 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

On market days the flocks are driven through a timber ring here and sold in lots, with the auctioneer's patter too quick for a stranger to follow. Dealers come out from East City on the morning train for it.

areas.name: Auction Sawdust Ring
areas.text: The round ring with its gate in and its gate out, deep in sawdust.

areas.name: Auctioneer's Box
areas.text: A raised box with a gavel, a lot book and a view of every bidder.

locations.name: Resembool Sheep Festival Meadow
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A flat common below the town that sleeps most of the year and wakes each spring for the great sheep festival. Then it fills with pens, stalls, a dance floor laid on barrels and every family from twenty miles around come to see whose ram takes the ribbon.

areas.name: Festival Barrel Floor
areas.text: Boards laid over barrels for the dancing, with lanterns strung above.

areas.name: Festival Judging Pens
areas.text: Rows of hurdle pens with a rope ring in the middle where the rams are walked.

areas.name: Festival Pie Stalls
areas.text: The trestles where the women of the town sell mutton pies and apple cake.

locations.name: Resembool Station Goods Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-8 · Danger: Low]

The sidings behind the passenger platform where the wool wagons are filled and the farm machinery arrives. After 1907 a sentry was posted at the gate, and the post was never taken away.

areas.name: Goods Yard Loading Crane
areas.text: A hand crane on a stone plinth, its chain slung over a waiting wagon.

areas.name: Goods Yard Sentry Gate
areas.text: A gate in the fence with a striped box and a lamp.

locations.name: Resembool Stone Quarry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-8 · Danger: Low]

The town's houses came out of this hill, and the quarry still cuts a few blocks a month for walls and gate posts. The old lower floor flooded years ago and makes a cold, deep pool.

areas.name: Quarry Flooded Pool
areas.text: A cold green pool at the bottom of the old workings, deeper than it looks.

areas.name: Quarry Working Face
areas.text: The pale cut face with its drill holes, wedges and a timber crane.

locations.name: Resembool Wheelwright's Shop
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low]

Every wool cart in the district rolls on wheels made in this shed, where the wheelwright and his two sons heat iron tyres in a ring of fire and shrink them on with buckets of river water.

areas.name: Wheelwright's Back Shed
areas.text: A locked shed with a half-built motor carriage under a sheet.

areas.name: Wheelwright's Tyring Platform
areas.text: A round iron platform where the hot tyre is dropped over the wheel.

locations.name: Resembool Woolpack Inn
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-7 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The town's only lodging, three rooms upstairs over a bar where the shearers drink in season and the drovers out of it. Its landlady judges a stranger by his boots and charges him by the same measure.

areas.name: Woolpack Taproom
areas.text: A low bar room with a peat fire and benches worn smooth by wool-greased trousers.

areas.name: Woolpack Upper Rooms
areas.text: Three bedrooms under the eaves with washstands and sloping ceilings.

locations.name: Reserve Trenches
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A second line of trenches behind the front where companies rest between turns in the forward trench. It is safer, dirtier and more crowded than anywhere else on the line.

areas.name: Communication Trench
areas.text: The zigzag trench that runs forward to the front line.

areas.name: Rest Dugouts
areas.text: Deep dugouts with blanket doors and men sleeping in rows.

locations.name: Ridge Sheep Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

A sheep run on the high ridges where the grass is thin and the wind never stops. The shepherds move their flocks along the slopes with the seasons and have no patience with lines on a map.

areas.name: Ridge Stone Fold
areas.text: A round fold of drystone where the flock is penned at night.

areas.name: Ridge Windward Slope
areas.text: The bare slope above the fold, scoured by the wind.

locations.name: River Port
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The river port of Xing, where barges moored along the wharves carry the empire's tea and iron to the coast. Its harbour office keeps the manifests and charges a toll on each.

areas.name: Harbour Office
areas.text: The office of manifests and tolls, with its long queue.

areas.name: Wharf Row
areas.text: The wharves and their cranes, loud from dawn to dusk.

locations.name: Riverside Sparring Meadow
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low]

A stretch of rough meadow by the water, just out of sight of the town, where Resembool's children wrestle, race and pick fights they will forget by supper. The grass grows back badly in a few round patches.

areas.name: Meadow Bare Circles
areas.text: Round patches of thin grass and baked earth where something once burned the soil.

areas.name: Meadow Fallen Log
areas.text: A fallen willow trunk the onlookers sit on, worn smooth along its top.

locations.name: Rockbell Automail
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The Rockbell family home and its automail atelier, run by Pinako Rockbell and her granddaughter Winry, where limbs are made, fitted and mended. The Elric brothers lodge here whenever they come home, and a visitor with a broken arm or leg is taken straight to the back room.

areas.name: Fitting Room
areas.text: The back room with its bench, the chair and the bandages.

areas.name: Forge Room
areas.text: The forge, the anvil and the racks of tools, warm all day.

locations.name: Rockbell Field Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-16 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

At the height of the war two doctors from Resembool, Yuriy and Sarah Rockbell, set up a clinic under canvas in the Kanda region and treated any wounded who came to them, Ishvalan or Amestrian. The frame of the awning still stands at the edge of the ruins.

areas.name: Rockbell Clinic Awning
areas.text: The bare wooden frame of the awning over the cots' old places.

areas.name: Rockbell Clinic Water Barrel
areas.text: A rusted barrel where the doctors washed between patients.

locations.name: Royal Palace of Xerxes
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-30 · Danger: Severe]

At the heart of the ruined country stands what was once its castle city: terraces climbing to a palace whose great dome has split down the middle. The last king held court here with his alchemists and advisers. The throne is still in its hall, and the sand has piled against it like a cushion.

areas.name: Court Undercroft
areas.text: Vaults below the hall where the court kept its records and its wine.

areas.name: Palace Terraces
areas.text: Stepped terraces of cut stone, once gardens, now dunes held up by walls.

areas.name: Split Dome Hall
areas.text: The throne room under the broken dome, lit by a crack of sky.

locations.name: Ruined Cistern
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

The old water cistern of a ruined Ishvalan town, a vault of stone with its arches broken and its floor dry. The survivors come down to it at night for shelter and the children play at the edges.

areas.name: Broken Arches
areas.text: The arches above, cracked open to the sky.

areas.name: Vault Floor
areas.text: The dry floor of the cistern, scattered with stones.

locations.name: Rush Valley
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

The city just north of Dublith that grew fast as the centre of automail making, nicknamed the boomtown of the broken-down. Engineers crowd the streets, hold contests and press upgrades on anyone with a metal limb, and Atelier Garfiel is among its workshops.

areas.name: Automail Row
areas.text: The row of shops with limbs in their windows, each with its own sign.

areas.name: Forge Street
areas.text: The street of forges and workshops, hot and loud all day.

locations.name: Rush Valley Chapel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-5 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A plain brick chapel above the workshops, quieter than anywhere else in Rush Valley since the priest asked the smiths to stop hammering on rest days and, to the town's surprise, they did. Its yard holds few graves; the town is too new to have many.

areas.name: Rush Valley Chapel Nave
areas.text: A whitewashed nave with a dozen pews and a plain wooden altar.

areas.name: Rush Valley Chapel Yard
areas.text: A walled yard of a few new headstones and a bench.

locations.name: Rush Valley Contest Square
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The open square where Rush Valley holds its automail contests in grip, lift, speed and finish, judged from a wooden stage under strings of bunting. On ordinary days the stage is where the smiths eat lunch and argue about springs.

areas.name: Rush Valley Contest Carts
areas.text: Carts selling skewers and lemonade along the edge of the square.

areas.name: Rush Valley Judging Stage
areas.text: A raised stage of planks with a bell, a table and the judges' chairs.

locations.name: Rush Valley Engineers' Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The hall where Rush Valley's engineers meet to set the contest rules, settle quarrels over stolen designs and pin up apprenticeships on a board by the door. Its meetings are loud and its minutes are short.

areas.name: Rush Valley Apprentice Board
areas.text: A cork board in the porch thick with offers of work and apprenticeships.

areas.name: Rush Valley Guild Meeting Room
areas.text: A long room of benches facing a table with a gavel.

locations.name: Rush Valley Foundry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-9 · Danger: Low]

The foundry on the edge of town that casts the plates and housings most of Rush Valley's shops finish by hand. It runs day and night, and its chimney is the first thing a traveller sees coming up the road.

areas.name: Rush Valley Casting Floor
areas.text: A floor of sand moulds where ladles of white metal are tipped.

areas.name: Rush Valley Cooling Yard
areas.text: An open yard where the castings cool in rows under the sky.

areas.name: Rush Valley Pattern Shop
areas.text: A wooden shop of carved patterns for every plate the town orders.

locations.name: Rush Valley Iron Diggings
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-10 · Danger: Low]

A handful of small iron and nickel workings on the mountainside above Rush Valley, dug by families who sell their ore to the foundry below. The stamp mill thumps all day and the spoil runs grey down the slope.

areas.name: Rush Valley Ore Adits
areas.text: Low tunnel mouths propped with pit timber, carts waiting outside.

areas.name: Rush Valley Stamp Mill
areas.text: A shed of iron stamps crushing ore, loud enough to rattle teeth.

locations.name: Rush Valley Nerve Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-6 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small clinic where patients lie up after the nerves are joined to a new port, the stage of an automail fitting that hurts the most and heals the slowest. Its doctor works with half the shops in town and trusts none of their timetables.

areas.name: Rush Valley Nerve Ward
areas.text: A ward of iron beds under ceiling fans, screens between them.

areas.name: Rush Valley Port Surgery
areas.text: A tiled room with a gas lamp over the table and the port tools laid in rows.

locations.name: Rush Valley Parts Market
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-7 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A covered market selling all an engineer buys by weight or by the dozen: bearings, cable, tempered springs, glass for gauges. The trade comes early and picks the trays clean; tourists come late and pay for what is left.

areas.name: Rush Valley Bearing Stalls
areas.text: Rows of trays where bearings are counted out into paper twists.

areas.name: Rush Valley Cable Row
areas.text: Drums of steel cable unrolled and cut to length with shears.

locations.name: Rush Valley Patients' Lodging
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-6 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A boarding house for people who come to Rush Valley to be fitted and must stay on while they learn to walk or hold a cup again. Every corridor has a rail, the stairs have a ramp beside them, and the landlady was a customer herself.

areas.name: Rush Valley Lodgers' Parlour
areas.text: A parlour of deep chairs where lodgers compare their fittings.

areas.name: Rush Valley Walking Yard
areas.text: A yard with parallel bars and a set of steps going nowhere.

locations.name: Rush Valley Scrap Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-8 · Danger: Low]

A yard of heaps where Rush Valley throws away what it cannot sell: cracked housings, burnt-out joints, the arms of children who outgrew them. Boys dig through the heaps for parts, and the yardman lets them if they show him their finds first.

areas.name: Rush Valley Rust Heaps
areas.text: Mounds of rust taller than a man, picked over by dogs and boys.

areas.name: Rush Valley Scrap Crane
areas.text: A hand crane beside a scale for weighing scrap by the cart.

locations.name: Rush Valley Station
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-6 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The station where the southern line comes into Rush Valley. Touts from a dozen workshops meet every train and look the passengers over for metal arms and legs, so a visitor with automail rarely reaches the street without three offers and a card in each pocket.

areas.name: Rush Valley Booking Hall
areas.text: A tiled hall with a ticket window and a clock that runs fast.

areas.name: Rush Valley Platform
areas.text: A long platform plastered with handbills, crowded at every arrival.

locations.name: Rush Valley Tin Roofs
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-8 · Danger: Low]

A quarter of low workshops whose tin roofs nearly touch from street to street, so a light runner can cross half the town without coming down. The roofs ring underfoot, and the smiths below shout up at anyone rattling them.

areas.name: Rush Valley Chimney Walk
areas.text: A line of chimney stacks that makes a path across the rooftops.

areas.name: Rush Valley Wide Gap
areas.text: A drop two storeys deep between two workshops, the one jump the runners fear.

locations.name: Rush Valley West Alley
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-7 · Danger: Low]

The crooked lane on the west side of Rush Valley where the town's leftovers change hands: worn joints, old watches, goods with the names filed off. The pawn shop stands halfway down, and boys sit on the steps to see who goes in.

areas.name: West Alley Junk Stalls
areas.text: Trestle tables of rusted springs, odd screws and second-hand fingers.

areas.name: West Alley Steps
areas.text: Worn stone steps where the alley's children sit and keep watch.

locations.name: Salt Flats
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

The white salt flats between Ishval and the desert, cracked into plates by the sun. Water here is bitter and the road runs across it in a straight line.

areas.name: Cart Bones
areas.text: The rusted bones of carts left by the road.

areas.name: Salt Plates
areas.text: The cracked white plates of salt under the glare.

locations.name: Salt Pan Works
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-20 · Danger: High]

Shallow pans of brine dry under the sun until rakers can scrape the salt into cones. The work is hard on eyes and hands. The salt goes to Youswell and East City, and the works pays in scrip.

areas.name: Brine Pans
areas.text: The shallow pans in rows, white and blinding.

areas.name: Scrip Store
areas.text: The owner's store where the scrip is spent.

locations.name: Salt Ridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: Severe]

A ridge of salt rock across the desert road, carved into arches and gullies by the wind. A pass through the ridge is the only way for carts without wheels.

areas.name: Pass
areas.text: The narrow pass through the ridge, where the carts go single file.

areas.name: Rock Arches
areas.text: The arches of salt above the road, with the wind whistling through.

locations.name: Sand Rim Caravanserai
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

The last walled stop on the western road, a square of stables and sleeping rooms around a deep well. Caravans heading into the desert fill their skins here, and caravans coming back unload whatever they prefer the city not see.

areas.name: Sand Rim Deep Well
areas.text: The stone well in the middle of the yard, with its long rope and its queue.

areas.name: Sand Rim Sealed Storeroom
areas.text: A locked room behind the keeper's quarters for goods that arrive without papers.

areas.name: Sand Rim Stables
areas.text: Long open stalls where camels kneel and drivers sleep beside them.

locations.name: Sandstone Shrine
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 16-30 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small shrine cut into a sandstone face beside the road, its niches holding lamps that caravans light as they pass. Travellers leave a coin or a prayer and go on.

areas.name: Shrine Face
areas.text: The carved sandstone face with its niches of lamps.

locations.name: Sanvento
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate]

An Aerugonian border town in the hills beyond the pass, the town Amestris reached in its first push and was driven back from. Its people are proud of having held and tired of being shelled.

areas.name: Garrison Barracks
areas.text: An old monastery turned into barracks for the red-coated garrison.

areas.name: Sanvento Piazza
areas.text: A sloping square under a domed church, with a fountain that no longer runs.

locations.name: Scar's Brother's Study
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A scholar's house in the ruins, where the brother of the man now called Scar studied alchemy and the eastern art of Xing from whatever books he could find. Most of the books burned. The diagrams he chalked on the wall did not.

areas.name: Scar's Brother's Book Room
areas.text: Shelves of blackened spines and loose pages.

areas.name: Scar's Brother's Chalk Wall
areas.text: A whitewashed wall covered with circles and notes in a careful hand.

locations.name: Scorpion Flats
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

South of the ruins the ground is paved by nature with flat grey stones, and every one has a scorpion under it. Travellers keep their boots laced, shake them out each morning and never sit. The refugee children know which stones to lift for a dare.

areas.name: Carcass Hollow
areas.text: The hollow where a dead camel lies.

areas.name: Stone Field
areas.text: The field of flat stones.

locations.name: Sea Road Harbour
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

Far down the river, where it opens into the sea, Xing's ocean harbour shelters junks with ribbed sails. On the quays they say a ship can reach the western nations by sea, slowly, by a long road that never touches the desert.

areas.name: Harbour Master's Tower
areas.text: A square tower over the harbour mouth with a signal gong.

areas.name: Sea Road Agents' Row
areas.text: A row of awnings where agents keep their passage books and their discretion.

areas.name: Sea Road Junk Anchorage
areas.text: The sheltered water where the junks ride at anchor, sails furled like fans.

locations.name: Seminary of the Sun
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 11-15 · Danger: Moderate]

Cornello founded a school for young preachers beside the church and filled it with boys from poor families who were promised a life of honour. It is half empty now. The few novices who stayed still rise at dawn to greet the sun, with no prophet to lead them.

areas.name: Sun Seminary Cloister
areas.text: A square walk of yellow stone around a dry fountain.

areas.name: Sun Seminary Novices' Dormitory
areas.text: A long room of narrow beds, most of them stripped.

areas.name: Sun Seminary Sermon Library
areas.text: Shelves of bound sermons and a lectern facing east.

locations.name: Sheep Pastures
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

The grassy pastures that fill the land around Resembool, dotted with flocks and the shepherds' huts. The wool carries the town's name to the markets of the east.

areas.name: Lower Meadow
areas.text: The long meadow by the lane, grazed close and green.

areas.name: North Field
areas.text: The high field where the flock is kept in the summer, with its shelter and its wall.

locations.name: Shepherd's Drift
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

An old drift mine cut straight into the hillside before the town had its shafts, abandoned now and used by herders as a pen in bad weather. The tunnel runs further in than any herder has gone.

areas.name: Drift Inner Gallery
areas.text: A black tunnel that slopes gently down into the hill.

areas.name: Drift Mouth
areas.text: The low entrance, propped with grey timbers and fouled by goats.

locations.name: Shepherd's Rest Tavern
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-7 · Danger: Low]

The drinking house on the south lane, rougher than the inn and fonder of its regulars. Shepherds leave their dogs under the tables and their crooks in a barrel by the door.

areas.name: Tavern Crook Barrel Door
areas.text: The low door with its barrel of crooks and the boot scraper beside it.

areas.name: Tavern Dartboard Corner
areas.text: A smoky corner with a dartboard, a chalk slate and a settle.

locations.name: Shepherds' Bothy Ridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-9 · Danger: Low]

A bare ridge where the shepherds stay out with the flocks through lambing, sleeping in a turf-roofed bothy with a fire that is never let out. The night sounds up here are mostly ewes in labour.

areas.name: Bothy Lambing Fold
areas.text: A ring of hurdles on the lee side of the ridge, strawed for the ewes.

areas.name: Bothy Peat Hearth
areas.text: The one room of the bothy, with a peat fire, bunks and a log book on a nail.

locations.name: Sheska's Book-Buried Flat
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A cheap rented room up three flights where a bespectacled young woman named Sheska lives among more books than floor. She lost her library job for reading instead of shelving, and spends what she earns on her sick mother and on more books. Visitors knock twice and then start digging.

areas.name: Sheska's Book Stacks
areas.text: A room of leaning towers of books with one narrow path to the window.

areas.name: Sheska's Reading Nook
areas.text: A chair under a lamp, hemmed in by the tallest piles.

locations.name: Shrine of the Western Sage
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-20 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A modest shrine on a hill road, raised to the Philosopher of the West, the stranger who came out of the desert centuries ago and taught Xing the art that became alkahestry. Pilgrims leave little circles of folded paper on the altar.

areas.name: Sage's Paper-Circle Altar
areas.text: The low altar heaped with folded paper circles, some years old.

areas.name: Western Sage Hill Road
areas.text: The stepped path up to the shrine, lined with stones pilgrims have carved.

locations.name: Silent Lantern House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High]

A teahouse in a back street of the capital, with a lantern over its door that is never lit. The tea is poor, the booths are curtained and the customers talk very little.

areas.name: Bamboo-Blind Booths
areas.text: Curtained booths along the back wall where nobody sees the next table.

areas.name: Unlit Lantern Doorway
areas.text: The narrow street door under its dark lantern, watched from across the lane.

locations.name: Silica Kilns
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

A glassmaker has built three beehive kilns at the edge of the glass flats and turns the white sand into bottles, lamp chimneys and windowpanes. The heat near the kilns is worse than the desert.

areas.name: Beehive Kilns
areas.text: The three round kilns, glowing day and night.

areas.name: Blowing Bench
areas.text: The bench and pipes of the glassblower.

locations.name: Single Men's Lodging House
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A long house of bunks for the miners with no family in town, mostly young men who came for work from the farms of the east. The bunks are shared in shifts, so the beds are never cold.

areas.name: Lodging House Bunk Room
areas.text: Tiers of bunks and the snores of the off shift.

areas.name: Lodging House Stove Corner
areas.text: A pot-bellied stove ringed with drying boots and socks.

locations.name: Slate Hill Quarry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A slate quarry cut into a hill east of the city, where the slates for every roof in the north are split. The splitters work in an open shed and the cutters on the face in all weathers.

areas.name: Slate Quarry Face
areas.text: The terraced face of grey slate, reached by ladders and ledges.

areas.name: Slate Splitting Shed
areas.text: The open shed where the slates are split and trimmed by hand.

locations.name: Sledwright's Yard
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A yard where sledges, snowshoes and skis are made and mended, for the farms, the post and the army alike. The sledwright steams his runners in a long box by the stove.

areas.name: Sledwright's Runner Rack
areas.text: The rack of finished runners, skis and snowshoes along the wall.

areas.name: Sledwright's Steam Box
areas.text: The long box by the stove where ash is steamed to bend into runners.

locations.name: Smugglers' Saddle
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A saddle between two peaks west of the pass, reached by goat tracks and marked only by cairns. It is the way across the border for anyone who cannot use the road.

areas.name: Cairn Track
areas.text: The goat track marked by heaps of stones.

areas.name: Saddle Crest
areas.text: The windy crest with Aerugo on one side and Amestris on the other.

locations.name: Snow Field Inn
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-22 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A plain inn on the road below the fort, serving soup, bread and hot tea to the carters and the garrison men on leave. Its landlady asks no questions and expects a fair tip.

areas.name: Snow Field Taproom
areas.text: The low room with its stove, its benches and its bread.

areas.name: Upper Room
areas.text: The room under the roof where guests sleep in blankets.

locations.name: Snowbell Chapel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A plain stone chapel in the lower town, where the faithful of the north come for funerals and the winter feast. Its bell is rung by hand in snowstorms so that lost travellers can find the town.

areas.name: Bell Hood
areas.text: The wooden hood on the roof, reached by a ladder, where the bell rope hangs.

areas.name: Chapel Crypt
areas.text: The low crypt under the nave, mostly empty, with a bricked alcove.

areas.name: Snowbell Nave
areas.text: The narrow nave of pews and candles, cold even in summer.

locations.name: Snowmelt Sulphur Baths
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-16 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

Hot springs on the eastern slopes, roofed with a timber bathhouse that an old couple run for soldiers on leave and the odd traveller. The water stinks of sulphur and takes the cold out of the bones.

areas.name: Sulphur Baths Changing Room
areas.text: A plank room of benches, pegs and a stove for warming towels.

areas.name: Sulphur Baths Steam Pool
areas.text: The main pool under a timber roof, its water grey and steaming.

locations.name: Snowmelt Tarn
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-24 · Danger: High]

High in the south-western mountains a small lake fills each spring with snowmelt. Its water is cold enough to stop the heart, and a hermit fisherman lives in a hut on its shore.

areas.name: Fisher's Hut
areas.text: A low hut of stone and turf with nets drying on the roof.

areas.name: Tarn Black Shore
areas.text: The stony shore of the tarn, the water black and still.

locations.name: Snowplough Sheds
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The railway sheds south of the city where the snowplough engines are kept fired up all winter. When the line to the capital closes, every man here is called out to dig it open again.

areas.name: Plough Engine Shed
areas.text: The vaulted brick shed where the plough engines wait with steam up.

areas.name: Plough Turntable Pit
areas.text: The open turntable in front of the shed, ringed by drifts.

locations.name: South City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The main military hub and cultural centre of the south of Amestris, south of Dublith and famous for its sights. Its barracks, supply depots and rail junction feed the bloody border war that the southern headquarters has fought with Aerugo at Fotset since 1911, and its streets are full of soldiers going to the line and wounded coming home.

areas.name: Front Road Gate
areas.text: The gate on the road south toward Fotset and the line.

areas.name: South Station
areas.text:
The rail junction with its trains for the front and its tired crowds.

The rail and coach service serves this yard: coaches run to Dublith (about 12 Cens); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Supply Depot
areas.text: The depots of crates, tins and blankets along the rail siding.

locations.name: South City Barracks
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 9-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Block after block of brick barracks where the southern regiments sleep between tours of the line. Reveille sounds before dawn, and by breakfast the parade ground is full of companies being counted.

areas.name: Barrack Blocks
areas.text: Long brick halls of iron cots, footlockers and rifle racks.

areas.name: Quartermaster's Store
areas.text: A counter and shelves where boots, belts and blankets are signed for.

areas.name: Southern Parade Ground
areas.text: A dusty square of beaten earth where companies drill and are inspected.

locations.name: South City Cathedral
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The great church of the south, older than the barracks around it and the first thing a visitor is told to see. Its bells ring for weddings, for the hour and, three or four times a week now, for the funerals of men brought home from the line.

areas.name: Bell Tower Stair
areas.text: A narrow spiral up to the bells, with a view of the whole city from the top.

areas.name: Cathedral Nave
areas.text: A long cool hall of pale stone, candles and worn pews.

areas.name: Cathedral Steps
areas.text: The wide steps where guides wait for visitors and beggars wait for the guides.

locations.name: South City Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The market of South City, a crowded square of produce, tinned food and cheap clothes. Soldiers spend their pay here and the wounded come to buy what the ration does not give them.

areas.name: Produce Row
areas.text: The stalls of fruit and bread, bright under the sun.

areas.name: Tin Corner
areas.text: The stalls of tins and bottles, stacked to the awning.

locations.name: South City Telephone Exchange
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The exchange that carries every call between the southern command, the front and the capital. Rows of operators sit at the boards in headsets, and an army clerk sits behind them listening to more than he admits.

areas.name: Cable Vault
areas.text: The basement where the trunk lines enter the building in heavy bundles.

areas.name: Switchboard Hall
areas.text: A long hall of plug boards and operators speaking in low voices.

locations.name: South Command Headquarters
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The headquarters of the southern command, a block of map rooms and offices where the front's plans are drawn. Its officers are polite and short of sleep.

areas.name: Map Room
areas.text: The long room of maps pinned to boards, with the pins moved each day.

areas.name: Officers' Wing
areas.text: The offices and quarters of the senior officers.

locations.name: South Hood
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 3-9 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A hill town on the far side of the mountains from Rush Valley, older and slower than its neighbour, living on goats, orchards and the traffic over the pass. Few of its people wear automail, and those who do bought it over the hill.

areas.name: South Hood Market Cross
areas.text: A worn stone cross in a little square where the carts load.

areas.name: South Hood Pass Gate
areas.text: The last house of the town, where the mountain road begins.

areas.name: South Hood Terraces
areas.text: Stepped orchards of almond and olive above the roofs.

locations.name: South Hospital
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The military hospital of South City, the place the wounded from the Aerugo front are brought first. Its wards are full and its nurses work in shifts that run into one another.

areas.name: Back Ward
areas.text: The quiet ward for those who will not get better.

areas.name: Triage Ward
areas.text: The ward where the new arrivals are sorted by their wounds.

locations.name: South Junction Engine Sheds
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-13 · Danger: Moderate]

The engine sheds behind South Station where locomotives are turned, coaled and mended between runs to the front. The work never stops, and the fitters sleep in shifts on benches beside the pits.

areas.name: Coaling Stage
areas.text: A raised stage where coal is shovelled down into the tenders.

areas.name: Inspection Pits
areas.text: Brick pits under the rails where men work beneath the engines.

areas.name: Roundhouse
areas.text: A great round shed around a turntable, ringed with engines.

locations.name: South Watch Post
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A small post at the edge of the South City district, a hut and a fence that watch the road to the south. Its two soldiers are glad of company and bored of their own.

areas.name: Guard Hut
areas.text: The hut with its stove, its kettle and its logbook.

locations.name: Southern Copper Workings
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 11-15 · Danger: Moderate]

Copper mines in the hills east of the supply road, worked harder since the war began because shell bands and telephone wire both need copper. The army guards them and the miners resent it.

areas.name: Copper Headframe
areas.text: The wooden tower and winding gear above the main shaft.

areas.name: Lower Drifts
areas.text: Wet, cramped tunnels deep under the hill.

areas.name: Smelter Shed
areas.text: A roaring shed where the ore is melted and poured.

locations.name: Southern Gazette Office
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-11 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The office of the south's daily paper, which prints the war news the censor allows and the theatre notices nobody censors. Boys run out of its doors at dawn with the first edition under their arms.

areas.name: Editor's Room
areas.text: A cramped room of proofs, ashtrays and a locked desk.

areas.name: Press Hall
areas.text: The hall of the printing press, loud and smelling of ink.

locations.name: Southern Officers' Club
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A quiet club for the officers of the southern command, all leather, brandy and billiards. What is said over its card tables decides more postings than anything written at headquarters.

areas.name: Club Billiard Room
areas.text: A long room of mahogany and clicking balls.

areas.name: Officers' Card Room
areas.text: A smoky room of green-baize tables and lowered voices.

locations.name: Southern Ordnance Works
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-15 · Danger: Moderate]

A factory on the city's northern edge that fills shells and packs cartridges for the line. Most of its workers are women from the city, and the yellow powder stains their hands for weeks.

areas.name: Filling Shed
areas.text: A long shed of benches where powder is weighed into casings.

areas.name: Powder Magazine
areas.text: A half-buried store of powder kegs behind earth banks.

areas.name: Works Gate
areas.text: The gate where every worker is searched going in and coming out.

locations.name: Southern Pass Fort
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 13-17 · Danger: Moderate]

A stone fort astride the road where it climbs the hills toward Aerugo, with towers on both sides and a gate that has not opened for trade in years. It was built after the war of 1835 and has been refitted for this one.

areas.name: Fort Cistern
areas.text: A vaulted cistern under the courtyard.

areas.name: Fort Ramparts
areas.text: The stone walk between the towers, with guns facing south.

areas.name: Pass Gate
areas.text: The great gate across the road, barred and guarded.

locations.name: Southern Recruiting Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A hall near the headquarters where volunteers sign on, are measured and listened to by a tired doctor. Posters on every wall show smiling soldiers marching south.

areas.name: Enlistment Desk
areas.text: Long tables where names are taken and oaths sworn.

areas.name: Medical Corner
areas.text: A curtained corner with a scale, a chart and a cold stethoscope.

locations.name: Southern Road Inn
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-18 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

An inn on the road between South City and the line, for carters, couriers and soldiers on leave. Its beds are full every night and its owner keeps a bottle of the good stuff for the officers.

areas.name: Southern Inn Taproom
areas.text: The noisy room with its long benches and its beer barrels.

areas.name: Stable Yard
areas.text: The yard of wagons, horses and straw.

locations.name: Southern War Cemetery
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A military cemetery on the slope east of the city, its rows of white markers growing longer every month. An old section holds the dead of the war fought on this border in 1835, their stones gone grey.

areas.name: New Rows
areas.text: Raw earth and fresh markers, with mourners nearly every day.

areas.name: Old War Graves
areas.text: Weathered stones of the 1835 war under old cypresses.

locations.name: Southfield Market Gardens
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

South of the last tram stop the streets give out into small walled plots where families grow the capital's greens. Carts leave for Market Row in the dark so the produce is on the stalls by first light, and the gardeners' children weed the rows when school lets out.

areas.name: Southfield Cold Frames
areas.text: Low rows of glass frames over seedlings, propped open on sticks when the sun is out.

areas.name: Southfield Potting Shed
areas.text: A tarred shed of pots, sacks and a cot pushed behind the seed drawers.

locations.name: Southwest Ranges
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High]

South of the border hills the land rises into mountains that neither Amestris nor Creta has ever properly mapped. Goats and the people who herd them are the only regular travellers.

areas.name: Ranges Goat Ledge
areas.text: A thin track along a ledge above a long drop.

areas.name: Snowfield Saddle
areas.text: A saddle between two peaks, white even in summer.

locations.name: Stag Ridge Lodge
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A hunting lodge on a ridge east of the city that the northern command's generals use for shooting parties. It is shut most of the year, and opened with a great deal of fuss when someone from the capital visits.

areas.name: Stag Ridge Gun Room
areas.text: The locked room of sporting rifles, cartridges and maps of the hunting grounds.

areas.name: Stag Ridge Trophy Hall
areas.text: The great room of antlers, mounted heads and a fire big enough to roast a deer.

locations.name: State Certification Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The hall where would-be State Alchemists sit the national examination: a written paper, a psychological evaluation, and a practical test before a board of officers who judge whether the art is any use in the field. Most who come fail. The few who pass leave with a silver watch, a code name and an order to report.

areas.name: State Certification Judges' Gallery
areas.text: A raised gallery with padded chairs for the panel.

areas.name: State Certification Practical Yard
areas.text: An open yard of raw stone and timber where candidates show what they can do.

areas.name: State Certification Written Hall
areas.text: The domed hall of single desks set wide apart, an invigilator at the front.

locations.name: Station Hotel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A grand hotel built across the square from the railway when tourists still came south for the sights. Officers on leave, reporters from the capital and families visiting the wounded now fill its rooms.

areas.name: Hotel Dining Room
areas.text: White tablecloths, a slow ceiling fan and a menu that is shorter than it used to be.

areas.name: Hotel Lobby
areas.text: A lobby of palms, brass and armchairs where everyone watches everyone else.

locations.name: Statue of Leto
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

In the square below the church stands Leto himself, many times the height of a house: bearded, bare-chested, a sceptre in one fist and a crown of rays on his head. The Fullmetal Alchemist raised him out of the paving with one transmutation, in the middle of his fight with Cornello, and the town never had the heart, or the masons, to take him down.

areas.name: Leto Plinth
areas.text: The broad stone base, its sides scrubbed and chalked and scrubbed again.

areas.name: Shadow of the Sceptre
areas.text: The strip of square the sceptre's shadow sweeps across through the day, where old men set their stools to follow the shade.

locations.name: Storm Wall Shelter
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

A curved wall of stone built across the path of the storms. When the sky turns brown, caravans run for it, tie their animals to the iron rings and lie down on the lee side with cloths over their faces.

areas.name: Lee Side
areas.text: The sheltered side of the wall, crowded when the storms come.

areas.name: Windward Drift
areas.text: The heaped sand on the storm side, higher every season.

locations.name: Stucco Lanes
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-24 · Danger: High]

Behind the palace the poorest homes of Xerxes still stand in close lanes: small rooms of mud brick under white stucco, the walls cracked in webs. Numbers are painted over many doors in faded red. Bats live in the back rooms.

areas.name: Bat Rooms
areas.text: The dark back rooms where the bats roost by day.

areas.name: Numbered Doors
areas.text: The lane of low doorways under faded red numbers.

locations.name: Sulphur Springs
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-30 · Danger: Severe]

Hot water wells up through cracked stone here and sits in pools ringed with yellow crust, steaming even in the noon heat. Herders bring their old men to soak stiff joints. Everyone else holds their nose: the smell carries a mile downwind.

areas.name: Crust Field
areas.text: The cracked field of sulphur around the pools.

areas.name: Steaming Pools
areas.text: The pools of hot water among the yellow crust.

locations.name: Sun Street Forge
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 11-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The town blacksmith shoes the carters' mules, mends ploughs and, these days, makes hinges for half the new doors in town. His street was renamed for the sun in the prophet's time, and nobody has bothered to give it back its old name.

areas.name: Sun Street Forge Hearth
areas.text: The hearth, the bellows and the anvil at the heart of the shop.

areas.name: Sun Street Shoeing Bay
areas.text: An open bay at the front where mules are tied and shod.

locations.name: Sunken Lane Crossing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

An ordinary crossing of shop streets in the middle of the city, remembered now for a single wet afternoon. A tall man in dark glasses fought the Fullmetal Alchemist here in front of a crowd, and when his red eyes were seen he broke the road open under himself and dropped into the drains.

areas.name: Sunken Lane Cave-In
areas.text: A jagged pit in the road with the sound of water rushing somewhere below.

areas.name: Sunken Lane Shopfronts
areas.text: Boarded windows and a grocer who swept up the glass and opened again next morning.

locations.name: Sunwheel Inn
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-13 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Two floors around a courtyard and a fig tree, with a gilt sun nailed over the gate from the days when pilgrims came to hear the prophet. The pilgrims have stopped coming; the inn takes in soldiers, salesmen and families whose houses lost their roofs.

areas.name: Sunwheel Attic
areas.text: The low room under the roof that guests are told is for storage.

areas.name: Sunwheel Courtyard
areas.text: The shaded court with its fig tree, its well and its long table.

locations.name: Supply Road South
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The supply road from South City to the front, a line of trucks and wagons that never stops. Fuel and ammunition go up it, and the wounded come back down it.

areas.name: Convoy Lane
areas.text: The lane of trucks and wagons, dusty and loud.

areas.name: Fuel Dump
areas.text: The dump of drums and sandbags beside the road.

locations.name: Surveyors' Cairn
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-13 · Danger: Moderate]

A cairn on the highest hill north of the town, set by the army surveyors who mapped the coal field. The view takes in the whole district, the spur and the edge of the sand.

areas.name: Cairn Benchmark Stone
areas.text: A stone with a brass plate set into its top.

areas.name: Cairn Lookout Slope
areas.text: A slope where one can see the town and the dunes beyond.

locations.name: Tailings Hills
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The grey heaps of waste rock piled behind the mine, grown with scrub and cut by old tracks. Children are forbidden to climb them and do so anyway.

areas.name: North Heap
areas.text: The biggest of the heaps, grey and loose underfoot.

areas.name: Old Tracks
areas.text: The rusted tracks between the heaps where the carts once ran.

locations.name: Tamarisk Caravanserai
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A walled inn built around a courtyard where the caravans pen their animals for the night. Merchants sleep in the upper rooms, drovers in the arcade below. Two old tamarisk trees at the gate give the place its name and its only shade.

areas.name: Caravanserai Courtyard
areas.text: The great square yard of pens and water troughs.

areas.name: Card Cellar
areas.text: The low cellar where the game runs every night.

areas.name: Lattice Rooms
areas.text: The merchants' rooms above, cool behind their screens.

locations.name: Tanners' Lane
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The lane of tanneries on the river, where the hides from the hunters and the farms are cured for the furriers and the bootmakers. Nobody lives on it by choice, and the rents are the cheapest in the city.

areas.name: Tanners' Bark Pits
areas.text: The sunken pits of tanning liquor, steaming in the cold.

areas.name: Tanners' Hide Frames
areas.text: The yard of wooden frames where hides are stretched and scraped.

locations.name: Tea Terraces
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

Terraces of tea on the hills above the river, cut into steps and worked by pickers in straw hats. The tea goes down the river to the capital and out to the coast in sealed chests.

areas.name: Lower Terrace
areas.text: The first terrace, close to the road, with its drying sheds.

areas.name: Water Channel
areas.text: The stone channel that runs along the hillside above the terraces.

locations.name: Temple of the Domes
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

Three domes stand together on the western side of the ruins, their blue tiles mostly fallen. Pigeons nest in the arches, and caravan men who shelter here say the echo answers a moment late.

areas.name: Inner Dome
areas.text: The tallest dome, its walls covered in rows of names in an old script.

areas.name: Tiled Forecourt
areas.text: A square of loose blue tiles where the faithful once washed their feet.

locations.name: Terrace Vineyards
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate]

Vineyards stepped up the hills east of South City, where the wine the south is known for has been made for generations. Picking goes on whatever the front does, and the pickers know every path over the hills.

areas.name: Press House
areas.text: A stone barn of presses, vats and sticky floors.

areas.name: Upper Terraces
areas.text: The highest rows, where the grapes ripen first.

locations.name: The Ceded Strip
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 13-17 · Danger: Moderate]

The strip of borderland Amestris took from Aerugo along with Fotset when the war began. Its farms were Aerugonian, its farmers have fled, and both countries' maps claim it.

areas.name: Abandoned Farmsteads
areas.text: Empty farmhouses with their doors open and their wells fouled.

areas.name: Fallen Boundary Stones
areas.text: A line of toppled stones that once marked the border.

locations.name: The Sandbag Tavern
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate]

Soldiers on leave drink here, sitting on real sandbags that a sergeant hauled in as a joke years ago. The owner lost an arm at the wall and serves with an automail hand that can open a bottle by the neck.

areas.name: Sandbag Bar
areas.text: The bar with its sandbag seats and its beer-ringed counter.

areas.name: Sandbag Dart Corner
areas.text: The corner by the dartboard where bets are laid in cigarettes.

locations.name: Thornback Gully
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High]

A deep gully choked with thornbush runs from the hills down to the border, and its stream crosses into Creta under a bank of rock. It is the smugglers' road, known to everyone and patrolled by no one who wants to come back.

areas.name: Rock Bank Crossing
areas.text: Where the stream goes under the rock into Creta, the water knee-deep.

areas.name: Thornback Path
areas.text: A track tunnelled through the thornbush, wide enough for one mule.

locations.name: Thornscrub Hills
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 11-16 · Danger: Moderate]

Low hills north of the town covered with thornbush and red stones, where the grass gives out and the dunes begin. The herders use it in spring and the foxes use it all year.

areas.name: Thornscrub Hollow
areas.text: A sheltered hollow where travellers camp out of the wind.

areas.name: Thornscrub Ridge
areas.text: A ridge of thornbush with a long view of the dunes.

locations.name: Tombs of the Mercury Emperors
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

In the hills north of the capital, three generations of emperors lie under grassy mounds at the end of a road lined with stone animals. All three died of elixirs laced with mercury, drunk in the hope of living forever, and the guides tell it plainly, as a warning.

areas.name: Second Mercury Mound
areas.text: The middle tomb, a grass mound with a stone door half buried at its foot.

areas.name: Spirit Road of Stone Beasts
areas.text: A long road lined with stone elephants, camels and lions facing one another.

areas.name: Tomb Keepers' Lodge
areas.text: A low house where the keepers live and keep the offerings.

locations.name: Tucker House
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A roomy house on the city's quiet western side, bought with a State Alchemist's grant and run with no woman in it. The Sewing-Life Alchemist works downstairs among his cages and papers, while his small daughter Nina rolls on the grass with Alexander and asks every visitor to stay and play.

areas.name: Tucker House Cellar Laboratory
areas.text: Stone steps down to cages, a chalked circle on the floor and a smell of animals.

areas.name: Tucker House Lawn
areas.text: The overgrown grass at the front, worn bare where a girl and a dog wrestle.

areas.name: Tucker House Library
areas.text: A long room of crammed shelves where a guest may read on biology and chimeras for days.

locations.name: Unfinished Rail Embankment
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

An embankment runs east out of the crossing and simply stops in the sand. Years ago the army began a spur to carry salt and stone to the eastern line; rails still lie stacked beside it, and the workers' huts have fallen in.

areas.name: Rail Stacks
areas.text: The rusting piles of rails and spikes beside the line.

areas.name: Railhead Stop
areas.text: The end of the embankment, where the earthwork ends in a heap.

locations.name: Upriver Iron Foundry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

Up the river in the hills, a waterwheel works the bellows of a furnace that never cools. The iron goes down the river on barges to the port and the capital.

areas.name: Foundry Pig-Iron Yard
areas.text: A riverside yard of iron bars stacked for the barges.

areas.name: Foundry Waterwheel Bellows
areas.text: The great wheel and the leather bellows it pumps.

locations.name: Valdemar Automail Clinic
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A small automail shop that fits and repairs mechanical limbs for veterans in the capital. The fitter learned his trade in Rush Valley and still sends there for the parts he cannot make. His waiting room is full of men who came home from Ishval missing an arm or a leg.

areas.name: Valdemar Fitting Chair
areas.text: The strapped chair where the nerve connections are made, a leather bit on a hook.

areas.name: Valdemar Parts Bench
areas.text: A long bench of limbs in pieces, springs, screws and a lathe.

locations.name: Valley Road Toll House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-7 · Danger: Low]

A stone toll house where the road from Dublith begins its climb toward Rush Valley, with a pole across the way and a keeper who knows every carter by name. People on foot walk round the pole; wheels stop and pay.

areas.name: Valley Road Barrier Pole
areas.text: The striped pole and the lamp that hangs over it.

areas.name: Valley Road Keeper's Room
areas.text: A small room of books, a stove and a shotgun on two nails.

locations.name: Vestry Bridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-30 · Danger: Severe]

A long steel girder bridge that carries the western main line over the river a few miles out of the capital. Fishermen sit on the banks below, and soldiers on the trains lean from the windows to watch the water.

areas.name: Vestry Bridge Girder Span
areas.text: The open girder deck, sleepers over air and the river far below.

areas.name: Vestry Bridge Willow Bank
areas.text: The muddy bank under the willows where the fishermen sit.

locations.name: Veterans' Hall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A hall where the veterans of the Ishval war gather for drink and for the pensions the state pays late. The medals on the wall are many, and the men who wear them do not talk about the years they earned them.

areas.name: Drinking Room
areas.text: The long room of tables and the bar, full of quiet talk.

areas.name: Medal Wall
areas.text: The wall of medals and photographs, each name written under its picture.

locations.name: Voss Licensed Gunsmith
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A licensed gunsmith on the market street who repairs service rifles for the garrison and sells pistols to civilians with the right papers. The papers are checked more carefully when an officer is in the shop.

areas.name: Voss Gun Counter
areas.text: A glass counter of pistols and boxed cartridges with a book chained to one end.

areas.name: Voss Proof Cellar
areas.text: A sandbagged cellar where repaired guns are fired into a box of sand to be tested.

locations.name: Waggoner's Rest Inn
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The last inn on the north road before the city gate, built when the coaches still ran and kept busy now by carters, drovers and farmers who would rather not pay city prices for a bed. The taproom is low and dark and the landlady's stew is famous for two miles in every direction.

areas.name: Waggoner's Stable Yard
areas.text: A cobbled yard of stalls, a water trough and carts parked shaft to shaft.

areas.name: Waggoner's Taproom
areas.text: A low-beamed taproom with a big fire, settles along the walls and the stew pot on the hob.

locations.name: Wallenstein Officers' Club
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A club in a grand old house where officers of rank go to read the papers, play billiards and drink. Junior officers can enter only as guests, and the doorman knows to the button what each man's rank is.

areas.name: Wallenstein Billiard Room
areas.text: A green table under a lamp, with a cue rack and a scoring board.

areas.name: Wallenstein Card Room
areas.text: A small locked room with a round table and heavy curtains.

areas.name: Wallenstein Reading Room
areas.text: A quiet room of leather chairs, newspapers on poles and a ticking clock.

locations.name: Wandering Priest's Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A moving camp of Ishvalan evacuees, led by the old warrior priest who once taught Scar. They left the south when the army grew thick there and have drifted east by stages, never staying long in one place.

areas.name: Wandering Priest's Tarp
areas.text: A tarp stretched from a pole, where the master sits and receives anyone.

areas.name: Wandering Priest's Tether Line
areas.text: A rope between stakes where the camp's goats are tied.

locations.name: War Orphans' Home
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A charity home north of the barracks for children whose fathers died at the front or whose villages were shelled. Its matron runs it on donations and nerve, and the older children work in the market to help.

areas.name: Home Dormitory
areas.text: A long room of narrow beds and a few treasured toys.

areas.name: Vegetable Patch
areas.text: A walled garden of beans and tomatoes the children tend.

locations.name: Weber Street Free Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-16 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A free clinic in the poor end of the capital, run by two doctors who left the army hospital because they wanted to treat people who could not pay. The queue starts before dawn, and the nurse turns nobody away.

areas.name: Weber Clinic Examining Room
areas.text: A small room with a bed, a sink and a cabinet of medicines.

areas.name: Weber Clinic Waiting Room
areas.text: A crowded room of benches where the sick wait to be called.

locations.name: West City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The western city of Amestris and the military command headquarters for the area. Little is known of it outside the west, yet its army is large and every man in it is schooled in the guerrilla fighting of the long border quarrel with Creta: small patrols, hard hills and long silences.

areas.name: River Quay
areas.text: The quay on the western river where the barges load for the border.

areas.name: West Command Yard
areas.text: The yard of the command headquarters, with its flagpole and its sentry boxes.

areas.name: West Station
areas.text:
The rail station on the western line, with its guards and its wide platforms.

The rail and coach service serves this yard: coaches run to Central City (about 16 Cens); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

locations.name: West City Courier Office
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The office of the city's daily paper, with a press in the back that shakes the floor every night. Its notice window is where people come to read the casualty columns, and on bad days a crowd stands silent in front of it.

areas.name: Courier Notice Window
areas.text: The window on the street where the casualty columns are pasted up each morning.

areas.name: Courier Press Hall
areas.text: The rattling press and its stacks of fresh, wet paper.

locations.name: West City Garrison Chapel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-16 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A plain chapel near the cemetery road where the garrison's chaplain says words over the dead of each patrol. Regimental flags, faded and torn, hang from the beams, and families light candles in a tray of sand by the door.

areas.name: Candle Porch
areas.text: The porch with its tray of sand and its stubs of candle.

areas.name: Flag Nave
areas.text: The nave under the hanging flags, its benches worn by boots.

locations.name: West City Gasworks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-17 · Danger: Moderate]

The gasworks makes the gas that lights the city's streets from coal brought down the line. Its round holder rises and sinks as the day goes on, and children dare each other to climb its frame.

areas.name: Gasholder Frame
areas.text: The iron frame around the rising holder, a ladder up one side.

areas.name: Gasworks Retort House
areas.text: The hot house of retorts where coal is cooked into gas and coke.

locations.name: West City Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The market of West City, with dried goods from the border, river fish and cheap blankets. Traders from the hills come down to sell and go back up with tins.

areas.name: Dried Goods Row
areas.text: The stalls of salt fish, dried meat and grain.

areas.name: Hill Traders' Yard
areas.text: The yard where the traders from the hills leave their mules.

locations.name: West City Rail Yard
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Every soldier bound for the border passes through this yard east of the western headquarters, where troop carriages wait on the sidings beside coal wagons and flatcars of field guns. The western command keeps more rolling stock here than any other area, and it can move a regiment faster than the other commands can pack one.

areas.name: Troop Sidings
areas.text: Long lines of carriages where companies sleep the night before they leave.

areas.name: Turntable Pit
areas.text: The round pit where engines are turned, the turntable groaning under each one.

areas.name: Yard Coaling Stage
areas.text: The raised stage where engines take on coal, black dust over everything.

locations.name: West City Soldiers' Orphanage
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-15 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The war has filled this tall grey house with the children of soldiers who did not come back. Two widows run it on the army's small allowance, and the older children work at the brewery to make it stretch.

areas.name: Orphanage Schoolroom
areas.text: A cramped schoolroom with one slate per two children.

areas.name: Orphanage Yard
areas.text: A yard of packed dirt with a single tree and a skipping rope.

locations.name: West City Telephone Exchange
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-17 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A narrow building of tall windows where young women in headsets work the switchboards that connect West City to itself and, by trunk line, to the rest of the country. The army has its own wires, but its officers ring their wives through here like anyone else.

areas.name: Exchange Switchboard Floor
areas.text: Rows of switchboards and the hum of plugs going in and out.

areas.name: Trunk Line Room
areas.text: The locked room where the long-distance cables come up out of the floor.

locations.name: West Command Headquarters
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The headquarters of the western command, a fortified block with steel shutters, map tables and a radio room that never sleeps. Its generals plan the patrols and its clerks keep the count of the dead.

areas.name: Map Tables
areas.text: The long tables of maps and pins, the border drawn in red.

areas.name: Radio Room
areas.text: The room of wireless sets and their operators, hissing all night.

locations.name: West Quay Tannery
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-16 · Danger: Moderate]

Downstream of the port, where the stink can drift away over the river, the tannery turns hill cattle hides into boot leather for the army. The workers come home stained to the elbow.

areas.name: Tannery Hide Racks
areas.text: Racks of stretched hides along the riverbank.

areas.name: Tannery Lime Pits
areas.text: Square pits of lime where hides soak for weeks.

locations.name: Westbank Gasworks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High]

Coal comes in by barge and wagon and leaves as the gas that lights the capital's lamps and kitchens. The two gasholders rise and fall with the day's demand, and the retort house roars around the clock. Families who live nearby wash their curtains every week and still cannot get them white.

areas.name: Westbank Gasholder Yard
areas.text: The yard beneath the two iron gasholders, rising and falling in their frames.

areas.name: Westbank Retort House
areas.text: A furnace hall where stokers feed coal into the glowing retorts.

locations.name: Western Alchemy Registry
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 15-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]
