Alchemy is a licensed science in Amestris, and this office keeps the western register: who practises, what they practise and whether the army has a use for it. Civilian alchemists come here to stamp their papers; state alchemists passing through come to sign the book.

areas.name: Registrar's Counter
areas.text: A counter of dark wood with a brass seal press and a queue of nervous applicants.

areas.name: Testing Floor
areas.text: A slate floor marked with old chalk circles where practical tests are given.

locations.name: Western Barracks
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Four long brick blocks around a parade square house the soldiers of the western garrison between their turns at the border. Men who have been out in the hills sleep through the bugle; recruits fresh off the train stand at attention long before it.

areas.name: Barrack Block Four
areas.text: The last block, smelling of boot grease and wet wool.

areas.name: Mess Hall West
areas.text: A long hall of tables where the soup is thin and the bread is good.

areas.name: Parade Square West
areas.text: A square of beaten earth where drill is called at dawn.

locations.name: Western Cemetery
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The military cemetery on the western edge of the city, rows of white crosses under cypresses. The garrison's dead are buried here with their rank and their unit on the stone, and their families come to see them once a year.

areas.name: Cross Rows
areas.text: The rows of white crosses, each with its rank and its unit.

areas.name: Cypress Walk
areas.text: The path between the cypresses that leads to the back wall.

locations.name: Western Garrison Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

A forward camp of the western garrison, tents in rows behind wire and a flag on a pole. Its men go out on patrol for days and come back thinner each time.

areas.name: Patrol Post
areas.text: The post where the patrols sign out and back in.

areas.name: Western Tent Rows
areas.text: The rows of tents, muddy under the rain.

locations.name: Western Hills
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The hills between West City and the border, rough with scrub and cut with caves. Guerrilla fighters use them for cover and the patrols come in and out of them at their peril.

areas.name: Scrub Ridge
areas.text: The ridge of scrub that gives the patrols a view of the border.

areas.name: Western Cave Mouth
areas.text: The mouths of the caves in the rock, cold and dark.

locations.name: Western Home for Disabled Soldiers
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-16 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

Soldiers too badly hurt to go home live out their days at this long low house on the plain. They keep a vegetable garden, play cards on the veranda and argue about the war with anyone who will sit still.

areas.name: Veterans' Garden
areas.text: The garden of beans and cabbages kept by one-armed gardeners.

areas.name: Veterans' Long Veranda
areas.text: The veranda where the residents sit in rows and play cards.

locations.name: Western Limb Works
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Automail is fitted in the west mostly to soldiers, and this workshop near the hospital does almost nothing else. Its benches are lined with arms built for rifle work and legs built for hill marching, each one tagged with a name and a regiment.

areas.name: Lathe Corner
areas.text: The corner where the lathe turns out joints, curls of steel on the floor.

areas.name: Limb Racks
areas.text: Racks of finished arms and legs, each tagged for its owner.

areas.name: Limb Works Fitting Chair
areas.text: A room with a padded chair, straps and a box of nerve-connection tools.

locations.name: Western Military Hospital
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The military hospital of West City, where the garrison's wounded from the border skirmishes are treated. Its wards fill after every patrol and empty only slowly.

areas.name: Surgeon's Room
areas.text: The small room of instruments and the surgeon's desk.

areas.name: Ward B
areas.text: The ward of iron beds where the patrol wounded are kept.

locations.name: Western Military Stockade
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

North of the city, a timber stockade holds deserters, drunk soldiers and the odd Cretan prisoner until a court martial decides what to do with them. It stands apart from the town so the shouting does not carry.

areas.name: Court Martial Hut
areas.text: A hut with a table, three chairs for the judges and one stool.

areas.name: Stockade Mud Yard
areas.text: The muddy yard inside the stakes where prisoners walk in a circle.

locations.name: Western Mountain Pass
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The pass that climbs out of the capital's valley into the western mountains, a road of switchbacks through pine and mist. Border guards post themselves at the top and keep a close count of who goes west.

areas.name: Pass Post
areas.text: The guard post at the top, with its bell and its shuttered hut.

areas.name: Switchback Road
areas.text: The zigzag road up the mountain with its stone markers.

locations.name: Western Officer Cadet School
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 15-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Young men who want commissions in the western army are taught here, in classrooms hung with maps of the hills and on a range behind the gymnasium. The instructors are border veterans, and they teach guerrilla tactics rather than the parade-ground war of the textbooks.

areas.name: Cadet Dormitory
areas.text: A long room of iron cots, boots lined up exactly.

areas.name: Cadet Range
areas.text: The range behind the gymnasium, targets shot to splinters.

areas.name: Map Classroom
areas.text: A classroom whose walls are papered with contour maps of the border.

locations.name: Western Plain Farms
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate]

East and south of the city the land flattens into barley and beet fields broken by rows of poplars. The farmers here sell to the army, lose their sons to it, and complain about it in equal measure.

areas.name: Beet Clamp
areas.text: A long earth mound where the beet harvest is stored over winter.

areas.name: Blue-Shutter Farmhouse
areas.text: A farmhouse with blue shutters and a kitchen that always has bread.

areas.name: Poplar Windbreak
areas.text: A long line of poplars sheltering the fields from the hill wind.

locations.name: Western Quartermaster Depot
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-20 · Danger: High]

Everything the western army eats, wears or shoots comes through this fenced depot of long sheds, a weighbridge and a clerks' office. A railway spur runs right inside the fence so the crates never touch a public street.

areas.name: Depot Long Sheds
areas.text: Sheds of stacked crates stencilled with unit numbers.

areas.name: Depot Spur Gate
areas.text: The gate where the rail spur passes under the fence.

areas.name: Depot Weighbridge Office
areas.text: The office by the weighbridge where every wagon is weighed and written down.

locations.name: Western River Port
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The river port of West City, where barges carry goods and soldiers up and down the river. The port is busy and its warehouses are guarded.

areas.name: Quay Cranes
areas.text: The cranes and the stacks of crates along the water.

areas.name: Western Warehouse Row
areas.text: The row of guarded warehouses behind the quay.

locations.name: Western Signal Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The signal station on the high ground above West City, a mast and a row of huts from which the garrison sends its messages to the border posts by lamp and by wire.

areas.name: Mast Base
areas.text: The base of the mast with its wire drums and its ladder.

areas.name: Western Lamp Room
areas.text: The room of shutters and lamps that talk to the border.

locations.name: Western Timber Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

Woodcutters fell larch on the northern slopes here and slide the logs down chutes to the road. The army buys the timber for trench props, railway sleepers and coffins, in that order.

areas.name: Larch Log Chute
areas.text: The long wooden chute down the slope, slick with bark.

areas.name: Larch Sawpit
areas.text: The deep pit where two men saw the logs into planks, one above and one below.

locations.name: Wexler Alchemical Supply
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A shop of minerals, chalk, inks and reference books for the alchemists of the east, licensed and unlicensed alike. Its owner is no alchemist himself but can name any compound by its smell and will not sell to anyone under sixteen.

areas.name: Wexler Chalk Room
areas.text: A back room of chalk sticks, rope and drawing compasses for laying out circles.

areas.name: Wexler Reagent Counter
areas.text: A long counter of labelled jars and a brass scale with tiny weights.

locations.name: Whiteout Cirque
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-22 · Danger: High]

A high bowl of ice ringed by peaks to the east of the fort, a place of pure black rock and white snow where a blizzard comes over the rim with no warning at all. Men lost here are found in spring, if they are found.

areas.name: Cirque Cairn Rim
areas.text: The ragged rim of the bowl, where small cairns of stone stand half buried.

areas.name: Cirque Ice Floor
areas.text: The flat floor of the bowl, a frozen tarn under deep snow.

locations.name: Willow Lake Pavilions
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

South-east of the capital a lake ringed with willows holds a scatter of pavilions on islands and piers. Courtiers hire boats to drink and write verse, and the boatmen row slowly on purpose.

areas.name: Willow Lake Pleasure Boats
areas.text: The painted boats tied at the main pier, each with a roofed cabin.

areas.name: Willow Lake Poets' Pavilion
areas.text: An island pavilion where verses are written on the pillars.

locations.name: Wind Gap Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

A camp under the lee of a rock wall, used by hunters, trappers and the garrison's patrols. The tents are patched and the fire is kept small, since the wind takes the smoke away in moments.

areas.name: Lee Wall
areas.text: The rock wall that shelters the camp from the wind.

areas.name: Trappers' Tents
areas.text: The tents and the rack of drying hides beside them.

locations.name: Windpump Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A windpump and tank on the dry plain east of the front, the only water for miles, guarded because both armies want it. Water carts queue at its pipe every morning before the heat.

areas.name: Pump Tower
areas.text: The creaking tower of vanes and the pipe beneath it.

areas.name: Water Cart Queue
areas.text: The rutted ground where carts wait their turn.

locations.name: Wire Fields
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate]

Belts of wire and shell craters east of the front trench, laid by both armies and mended by both at night. Nothing grows here but one burned tree that both sides use for ranging.

areas.name: Burned Tree
areas.text: A blackened trunk standing alone in the craters.

areas.name: Wire Belt
areas.text: Coil upon coil of rusted wire on iron stakes.

locations.name: Wolfpack Hollow
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

A sheltered hollow east of the range's spine where the wolves gather in winter. Deer come down into it for the moss, and the wolves come after the deer.

areas.name: Wolfpack Hollow Floor
areas.text: The sheltered floor of the hollow, trodden into paths by paws.

areas.name: Wolfpack Hollow Rim
areas.text: The ring of rocks and pines above the hollow, where the wolves watch.

locations.name: Wool Sheds
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

The long sheds beside the station where the wool is graded, pressed and baled before it goes on the train. The town's biggest workplace in shearing season.

areas.name: Bale Store
areas.text: The store of pressed bales waiting for the train.

areas.name: Grading Floor
areas.text: The floor where the wool is sorted by its grade.

locations.name: Xerxes
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: Severe]

The ruin of an ancient country, a city of broken columns and stone walls half buried in the dunes. Over a million people lived here four centuries ago, with domed temples, markets and a court of scholars and alchemists; all of them vanished at once, and only the legends of the neighbouring lands and the sand keep what they built.

areas.name: Broken Colonnade
areas.text: The row of fallen columns and the stone roads between them.

areas.name: Buried Stair
areas.text: The stair half buried in sand, leading into the old city's halls.

locations.name: Xerxes Plantations
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

Long ago the suburbs of Xerxes fed a million people. Their field walls still run in straight lines for miles, filled level with sand, and in a strong wind whole furrows rise out of the ground and sink again by evening.

areas.name: Buried Furrows
areas.text: Rows of ridged earth that the wind uncovers and covers again.

areas.name: Petrified Grove
areas.text: A stand of palm trunks turned to stone, still upright.

locations.name: Xerxes Signal Tower
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe]

A round tower of fired brick on the eastern rise, with a stone fire bowl on its roof. From the top a watchman could see the palace dome in one direction and the empty road toward Xing in the other. Its stair has worn into a slope.

areas.name: Fire Bowl Roof
areas.text: The roof and its great stone bowl, open to the wind.

areas.name: Worn Stair
areas.text: The inner stair, its steps rubbed smooth into a ramp.

locations.name: Xerxes Stepwell
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-24 · Danger: High]

Steps go down in a square spiral, landing after landing, to a well at the bottom of the shaft. The upper flights are choked with sand. At the lowest landing there is still water, dark and cold, and the refugees haul it up in relays.

areas.name: Upper Flights
areas.text: The sand-choked top of the shaft, where the carriers dig out the steps each morning.

areas.name: Water Landing
areas.text: The last landing over the black water, cool even at noon.

locations.name: Xing Barracks
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The barracks of the emperor's guard, grey walls and a drill yard where the soldiers train in the morning. The officers wear the house's colours and speak with an accent the capital finds amusing.

areas.name: Drill Yard
areas.text: The square where the guard drills with spears and bows.

areas.name: Officers' Hall
areas.text: The hall of the officers, with its maps and its banners.

locations.name: Xing Capital
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The capital of Xing, an absolute monarchy of fifty hereditary clans under one Emperor, who binds each clan to him by taking its chief's daughter as a concubine and fathering one heir for each. Its tiered roofs and red gates rise above lantern-lit streets; a foreigner is welcomed as an envoy or not at all.

areas.name: Caravan Gate
areas.text:
The gate where the desert caravans enter the city, checked by the emperor's officers.

The rail and coach service serves this yard: coaches run to Desert Crossing (about 30 Cens); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Clan Quarter
areas.text: The walled quarter of the clan houses, each with its own gate and guards.

areas.name: Lantern Street
areas.text: The main street of lanterns, shops and tea-houses, busy until late.

locations.name: Xing Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The great market of the capital, with silk awnings, jade, spices and tea laid out in stalls that run for streets. Haggling is expected and the traders are very good at it.

areas.name: Jade Row
areas.text: The row of jade sellers under lamps.

areas.name: Silk Street
areas.text: The street of silk awnings and bright cloth.

locations.name: Xingese Trading House
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A mud-brick house with a curved roof built over it in the style of the east: the agency of a Xingese trading family. Silk, tea and medicines come in; machine parts, rifles and books go out, when the customs house allows.

areas.name: Lantern Hall
areas.text: The front room under red lanterns, where the agent pours tea.

areas.name: Silk Store
areas.text: The locked back room of bolts and boxes.

locations.name: Xingese Well Tower
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe]

Xing's emperors built this square tower of rammed earth around a well, to mark the edge of their claim and to water their envoys. A few soldiers live in it and rarely see their officers.

areas.name: Rammed Earth Walls
areas.text: The thick walls and their walk, with the banner on a pole.

areas.name: Tower Well
areas.text: The well in the court inside, with a bucket on a long sweep.

locations.name: Yao Clan Estate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The estate of the Yao clan, a compound of gardens and ponds behind a painted gatehouse. The clan is one of the older houses and its servants know the rules of every visitor.

areas.name: Lotus Garden
areas.text: The ponds of lotus and the stone paths between them.

areas.name: Yao Gatehouse
areas.text: The painted gate with its guards and its guest book.

locations.name: Yao Clan Rice Lands
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

South of the capital the Yao clan's farmland runs flat to the sky, paddy after paddy divided by dykes and studded with villages on mounds above the floodline. The Yao are one of the largest of the fifty clans, over half a million strong, and most of them live and work on this land.

areas.name: Yao Headman's Village
areas.text: A village on a mound with a drum tower and a granary on stilts.

areas.name: Yao Paddy Dykes
areas.text: The raised earth paths between the flooded fields, just wide enough for a cart.

areas.name: Yao Threshing Floors
areas.text: Beaten-earth floors where the sheaves are flailed after harvest.

locations.name: Yao Retainers' Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The families sworn to guard the Yao heir train in this hall, young and old on the same floor. They learn the knife, the sword and the grenade, and the sense for a living body that lets a guard feel a man coming before she sees him.

areas.name: Retainers' Sparring Floor
areas.text: A floor of scarred boards where the retainers fight in pairs from dawn.

areas.name: Yao Mask Wall
areas.text: A wall of pegs holding the retainers' masks, two of them empty.

locations.name: Yellow Silt Ferry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate]

Where the river is too wide to bridge, a flat ferry hauls itself across on a rope. One family has worked the crossing for generations and knows everyone who uses it.

areas.name: Ferrymen's Rope House
areas.text: A shed where the great rope is spliced and tarred.

areas.name: Silt Ferry Landing Stage
areas.text: A timber stage on the near bank, slick with river mud.

locations.name: Yock Island
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A small island in the middle of Kauroy Lake, near Dublith, with rocky shores and pine scrub. Izumi Curtis sent two brothers there to survive a month alone without alchemy and to work out what All is One and One is All means.

areas.name: Lake Camp
areas.text: A clearing in the pines above the shore, where the brothers must make do without alchemy.

areas.name: Pine Scrub
areas.text: The scrub of pines behind the shore, where the wind is loud.

areas.name: Rocky Shore
areas.text: The shore of stones, slippery with weed and cold to the touch.

locations.name: Yock Island Ridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-8 · Danger: Low]

The rocky spine of Yock Island, a short climb through wind-bent pines to the one spot where the whole lake can be seen. Foxes den among the roots and birds nest in the crags.

areas.name: Yock Ridge Crags
areas.text: Grey crags streaked white by nesting birds.

areas.name: Yock Ridge Fox Earths
areas.text: Holes among pine roots, the ground scattered with feathers.

locations.name: Yock North Shore
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-8 · Danger: Low]

The north shore of Yock Island, facing Dublith across the water, all stones and driftwood. From here the town's lights look close enough to swim to, and they are not.

areas.name: Yock Driftwood Point
areas.text: A point heaped with white driftwood and an old boat's keel.

areas.name: Yock North Shore Stones
areas.text: Round grey stones that slide underfoot down to the water.

locations.name: Yock Toad Pool
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-7 · Danger: Low]

A hollow in the south of Yock Island where rainwater gathers in a pool among the rocks, the nearest thing the island has to a well. Toads crowd its edges, snakes hunt the toads, and rabbit runs lead down to drink.

areas.name: Yock Rabbit Runs
areas.text: Paths worn through the grass down to the pool.

areas.name: Yock Toad Pool Rocks
areas.text: Flat rocks round the water, warm in the afternoon.

locations.name: Yoki's Company Store
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The general store on the square, the only one the lieutenant permits, where the miners buy flour, lamp oil and boots against next month's wages. Everything is on the slate, and the slate never clears.

areas.name: Company Store Back Shed
areas.text: A shed of barrels and sacks where the better goods are kept for officers.

areas.name: Company Store Counter
areas.text: A long counter with brass scales and the chained debt book.

locations.name: Yoki's Estate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The house of the lieutenant who holds the land, a stone building with guards at its gate and a garden walled off from the town. He is proud of the house and of the taxes that paid for it.

areas.name: Walled Garden
areas.text: The garden of clipped hedges and a sundial.

areas.name: Yoki's Gatehouse
areas.text: The gate with its two guards and its book of callers.

locations.name: Youswell
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A coal-mining town on the eastern frontier of Amestris, the nearest inhabited place to the desert. The town is grey with dust, its inns and shops charge travellers far too much, and its people distrust anyone in uniform: for years the land under it belonged to Lieutenant Yoki, who raised the taxes and cut the wages to fill his own purse.

areas.name: Mine Road Depot
areas.text:
The rail spur's depot where the coal wagons are loaded and the mine carts come up.

The rail and coach service serves this yard: coaches run to East City (about 12 Cens), Desert Crossing (about 9 Cens); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Miners' Row
areas.text: The row of cottages with their dust-grey steps and their washing lines.

areas.name: Youswell Square
areas.text: The square with the lieutenant's notice board and the water pump.

locations.name: Youswell Air Shaft
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A brick chimney standing alone on the scrub above the workings, with a furnace at its foot that draws the foul air up out of the galleries. On cold mornings it breathes like a sleeping animal.

areas.name: Air Shaft Furnace Grate
areas.text: An iron grate at the chimney's foot, its fire banked low.

areas.name: Air Shaft Scrub Rise
areas.text: The rise of scrub around the chimney, warm underfoot.

locations.name: Youswell Bakehouse
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-9 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The bakery that has the shift's bread ready before dawn, so the men go down with something in their pails. The baker's oven is the warmest place in town and children loiter by it in winter.

areas.name: Bakehouse Front Sill
areas.text: A window sill where the morning loaves are sold straight to the shift.

areas.name: Youswell Bakehouse Oven Room
areas.text: A low brick oven glowing behind an iron door.

locations.name: Youswell Brickworks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-13 · Danger: Moderate]

A small brickworks at the edge of town that turns the clay under the coal seams into the bricks of every chimney in Youswell. It burns slack from the mine that nobody else will buy.

areas.name: Brickworks Drying Racks
areas.text: Long racks of green bricks drying in the sun.

areas.name: Brickworks Kiln Floor
areas.text: The arched kiln, its doors bricked up and its fire roaring.

areas.name: Brickworks Mule Mill
areas.text: A ring where a mule plods round turning the clay paddles.

locations.name: Youswell Chapel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 6-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The chapel of the town, whitewashed and plain, with a small bell that is rung for every death in the mine. The graveyard behind it is full of men who died young.

areas.name: Graveyard
areas.text: The rows of stones in the dust behind the chapel.

areas.name: Youswell Chapel Hall
areas.text: The plain room of pews and a small altar.

locations.name: Youswell Clay Pit
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-13 · Danger: Moderate]

The pit where the brickworks digs its clay, a yellow hole in the ground that fills with water after rain. Children slide down its sides in summer.

areas.name: Clay Pit Barrow Ramp
areas.text: A ramp of planks where the barrows are pushed up to the kiln road.

areas.name: Clay Pit Floor
areas.text: The yellow floor of the pit, slick and full of puddles.

locations.name: Youswell Coal Mine
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The main coal mine of Youswell, with its headframe over the shaft and the galleries that run under the hills. Miners work in shifts, and the foremen count every man down and every man up.

areas.name: Headframe
areas.text: The timber tower over the shaft, its wheel creaking.

areas.name: Lower Gallery
areas.text: The galleries under the hills, low and wet, lit by lamps.

locations.name: Youswell Coke Ovens
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A bank of brick ovens where coal is baked into coke for the foundries of the west. The ovens are never allowed to go out, and the men who tend them work in a heat that ages them fast.

areas.name: Coke Oven Bank
areas.text: Brick domes in a line, each with an iron door glowing at the seams.

areas.name: Coke Quenching Yard
areas.text: A yard where the hot coke is raked out and doused in clouds of steam.

locations.name: Youswell Dispensary
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 7-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The town's only medical help, a dispensary run by a retired army surgeon who sets bones, lances boils and listens to lungs full of coal. The coughs here are the kind that do not get better.

areas.name: Dispensary Bottle Shelves
areas.text: Shelves of tinctures and a locked cabinet of morphine.

areas.name: Dispensary Surgery
areas.text: A scrubbed table, a lamp and a tray of instruments.

locations.name: Youswell Dry Wash
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-15 · Danger: Moderate]

A dry riverbed that only runs in a storm, a wide bed of smooth stones that the town uses as a road in summer. When it rains in the hills it fills in minutes.

areas.name: Dry Wash Cottonwood Bank
areas.text: A cut bank under a dead cottonwood where the water once ran deep.

areas.name: Dry Wash Stone Bed
areas.text: The broad bed of smooth stones, hot in the sun.

locations.name: Youswell Guardhouse
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-13 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A guardhouse of a dozen soldiers posted to keep the peace, which in practice means keeping Yoki's peace. The men are bored, underpaid and as disliked as their officer.

areas.name: Guardhouse Lockup
areas.text: Two cells with straw on the floor and a bucket in each.

areas.name: Guardhouse Mess Room
areas.text: A bare room of a table, tin plates and a card game that never ends.

locations.name: Youswell Lamp Room
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 7-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A long room at the pit gate where every miner draws a lamp and hangs a brass token in its place. The lamp keeper counts the hooks at the end of the shift and knows before anyone else when a man has not come up.

areas.name: Lamp Room Token Board
areas.text: A board of hooks where the brass tokens hang, one for every man below.

areas.name: Lamp Room Trimming Bench
areas.text: A bench where wicks are trimmed and the glass is polished.

locations.name: Youswell Pawn and Loan
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 7-11 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A cramped shop where miners pawn their watches before the tax day and redeem them after payday, if they can. The pawnbroker is polite and patient and owns half the wedding rings in Youswell.

areas.name: Pawn Back Room Safe
areas.text: A room behind a curtain with a safe and shelves of tagged belongings.

areas.name: Pawn Counter Grille
areas.text: A counter behind iron bars and a book of tickets.

locations.name: Youswell Pick Forge
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-11 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The smithy where picks are drawn out and sharpened, cage chains repaired and pony shoes fitted. Every miner in town owes the smith a favour and he never collects it.

areas.name: Pick Forge Grindstone Shed
areas.text: A lean-to where a boy turns the wheel and the picks are edged.

areas.name: Pick Forge Hearth
areas.text: The fire, the bellows and the anvil, black with years of use.

locations.name: Youswell Pithead Baths
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A brick bathhouse by the pit, built by the miners themselves when the old owner would not. The shift washes off the coal here before going home, and the gossip of the whole town runs through its steam.

areas.name: Pithead Baths Boiler Cellar
areas.text: A cramped cellar of pipes and a boiler that knocks like a fist.

areas.name: Pithead Baths Steam Hall
areas.text: Rows of tin basins and benches under a pall of hot steam.

locations.name: Youswell Post and Telegraph
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-11 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The town's single wire to the world, a post office whose clerk sends the mine's orders to East City and the miners' letters to their mothers. Every message passes under the lieutenant's eye.

areas.name: Post Office Sorting Shelf
areas.text: Pigeonholes of letters and a sack waiting for the evening train.

areas.name: Telegraph Key Desk
areas.text: A desk with the brass key, the sounder and a pad of yellow forms.

locations.name: Youswell Powder Magazine
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A stone hut set apart from everything, where the blasting powder for the mines is kept under lock and a sentry's eye. Nobody smokes within a hundred paces, not even the soldiers.

areas.name: Magazine Keg Vault
areas.text: A cool stone room of kegs stacked on wooden racks.

areas.name: Magazine Sentry Fence
areas.text: The wire fence and the sentry box at its gate.

locations.name: Youswell Rail Tunnel
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The short tunnel that carries the coal spur under the first of the hills, a mouth of brick and a long dark arch. Trains slow to walk through it and the drivers sound their horns.

areas.name: Dark Arch
areas.text: The black middle of the tunnel, dripping and cold.

areas.name: Tunnel Mouth
areas.text: The brick arch of the entrance with its warning board.

locations.name: Youswell Road Checkpoint
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-13 · Danger: Moderate]

A barrier on the coach road west, where Yoki's soldiers stop every cart and coach leaving or entering Youswell. Nothing leaves without a stamp and nothing is stamped without a fee.

areas.name: Youswell Checkpoint Pole
areas.text: The striped pole across the road and the sentry beside it.

areas.name: Youswell Checkpoint Stamp Hut
areas.text: A tiny hut where the corporal stamps passes and pockets the fees.

locations.name: Youswell Schoolhouse
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-9 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A single room where the children of the mine learn letters until they are old enough to go down. The teacher has asked for more books for years and been sent tax forms instead.

areas.name: Schoolroom Benches
areas.text: Rows of benches, a blackboard and a stove that smokes.

areas.name: Youswell Schoolhouse Yard
areas.text: A beaten yard with a bell post and chalk marks for hopscotch.

locations.name: Youswell Water Tower
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The water tower that feeds the mine's boilers and the town's pumps, an iron tank on legs above the roofs. It is the highest point in Youswell and the guards post a man on its ladder.

areas.name: Pump House
areas.text: The pump house at the tower's foot, loud with the engine.

areas.name: Tank Ladder
areas.text: The iron ladder up the tower, with its guard post at the top.

locations.name: Youswell Weighbridge
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 8-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The scale on the spur where every wagon of coal is weighed before it leaves for the main line, and the figure is written in two books. The weighman sits in a hut with a window onto the scale.

areas.name: Weigh House Window
areas.text: The hut where the weighman reads the beam and writes the figures.

areas.name: Weighbridge Wagon Queue
areas.text: A siding of coal wagons waiting their turn on the scale.

locations.name: Ziegler Brick Pits
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

Half the capital is built of the brick dug and fired out here on the clay flats to the south-west. The working face moves a little further every year, leaving behind steep-sided pits that fill with rain and turn the colour of rust. Mothers in the brickmakers' cottages tell their children the old pits have no bottom.

areas.name: Ziegler Brickmakers' Row
areas.text: A terrace of low cottages, every one built of its own seconds.

areas.name: Ziegler Drowned Pit
areas.text: The oldest pit, its water dropping by the day as the pumps thud on its rim.

areas.name: Ziegler Kiln Yard
areas.text: A yard of stacked green bricks around a domed kiln that is fired once a week.

factions.name: Aerugo army
factions.info: The army of Aerugo, south of Amestris. It has held out against Amestris for a longer war than the western one, though Amestris has the upper hand in men and machines. Its army is tied down on the front at Fotset, the town whose taking started the war. A stranger meets it as a soldier on a long line; a prisoner meets it as a long wait. One who serves in it rises by holding the line another week.

factions.name: Armstrong Family
factions.info: An illustrious noble house that has served in the army for generations and held sway in the money, military and politics of Amestris for 180 years, every member of it proud, strong and given to sparkling. Philip Gargantos Armstrong heads it with Mrs. Armstrong at his side; their children are Olivier, the eldest, a major general at Briggs, the civilian daughters Amue Armstrong and Strongine Armstrong, Alex, the only son and a major, and Cathrine, the youngest. The family seal copies the curled forelock they all share. A stranger meets the family in the drawing room or on the parade ground; a rival meets it as a wall. One who is taken in learns its strength and rises by the family's rules.

factions.name: Atelier Garfiel
factions.info: An automail shop in Rush Valley owned by Garfiel, a big, soft-spoken master of the trade, and the shop where Winry Rockbell takes work as an apprentice. It is known on the street for fine joints and fair dealing, and its window is always crowded with limbs waiting for their owners. A customer meets it as a bench and a tape measure; a mechanic meets it as a standard to beat. One who works here rises by doing the work cleanly and on time.

factions.name: Blue Squad
factions.info: A band of political extremists in the east of Amestris that calls itself the Eastern Liberation Front. It robs, bombs and threatens in the name of freeing the east from the capital, and it has made the rail lines its favourite stage. Its leader sits in an East City cell, and the men still free talk of nothing but getting him out. A traveller meets the squad as a gun in a railway carriage; an officer meets it as a manifesto on his desk. One who joins learns to move in a cell of a dozen men and rises by daring.

factions.name: Briggs garrison
factions.info: The soldiers who hold Fort Briggs on the border with Drachma, in the snows of the Briggs range, under Major General Olivier Mira Armstrong. It is the army's northern wall, a garrison with its own tanks and its own rules. Winters are long and fierce. A stranger meets the garrison as a guard who will not let them pass; a friend meets it as a hard but honest comrade. One who serves here learns to hold a position in bad weather and rises by never giving the snow a gap.

factions.name: Central Command
factions.info: The top of the military government of Amestris: the Führer and a body of generals under his direct control, who hold the final word on every military operation. Its headquarters is a walled compound at the heart of Central City, raised on a pyramid-like mound behind a moat, and it doubles as the Führer's residence. Nobody enters without a summons or a uniform. A stranger meets it as a petitioner turned away; a soldier meets it as an order. One who serves here gains rank by loyalty to the office, not to the men who hold it.

factions.name: Chang clan
factions.info: One of the fifty clans of Xing, small and poor, with little standing at the court. Its daughter May Chang is the Emperor's seventeenth princess, and the clan's hope rides on her bringing home a secret that will win the Emperor's favour. Its people are skilled in alkahestry and the martial arts, and they are proud the way a small house has to be. A stranger meets the clan as a modest hall in the capital; a rival clan meets it as a knife in the dark. One who joins rises by service to the princess.

factions.name: Church of Leto
factions.info: The faith of Leto, the sun god, which the prophet Cornello brought to the poor town of Reole and used to make himself its unquestioned ruler. He works miracles that seem to break the law of exchange and promises his followers wealth, endless life and even the return of their dead. A stranger meets the church as a crowd at the statue; a sceptic meets it as a sales pitch. One who joins it rises by bringing in offerings and by keeping the town's faith.

factions.name: Creta army
factions.info: The army of Creta, the country west of Amestris, which has fought its neighbour over the border for longer than anyone living can recall. Its soldiers know the western hills and passes and fight in small, hard patrols. A stranger meets it as a challenge from a ridge; an Amestrian patrol meets it as a shot from cover. One who joins rises by holding a pass.

factions.name: Curtis Meats
factions.info: A meat shop in Dublith, kept by Izumi and Sig Curtis with one assistant, Mason. The shop is narrow and goes back further than it looks. It sells meat and ties to the neighbourhood, and its back room is where the Curtises keep their own business. A stranger meets the shop as a counter and a cleaver; a friend meets it as a warm welcome. One who works here learns the trade and rises by keeping the Curtises' trust.

factions.name: Devil's Nest
factions.info: A large pub on the bad side of Dublith whose cellar runs into a maze of escape routes and the sewers below. Its crew are outcast mercenaries who keep an ear on all the business of the country's underworld. A stranger finds the bar's door and little else; a city guard finds the cellar too late. One who works here rises by knowing the routes and keeping quiet.

factions.name: Drachman army
factions.info: The army of Drachma, the large belligerent state to the north of Amestris behind the Briggs range, which has fought Amestris on and off for generations. A pact of non-aggression signed early in the century holds, shakily, and the border is never quiet for long. A stranger meets the army as an enemy patrol; a prisoner meets it as a hard interrogation. One who serves in it rises by surviving the northern winters and winning the next fight.

factions.name: Eastern Command
factions.info: The State Military's command for the east, seated in East City and counted the strongest offensive force in the nation. Its men bore most of the Ishval war and came home veterans, and they think of the east as theirs. Lieutenant General Grumman commands it, and the men hold him in high regard. A traveller meets the command as a checkpoint and a long wait; a recruit meets it as hard drill and good officers. One who serves rises by steady work.

factions.name: Elric brothers' circle
factions.info: The people who stand behind Edward and Alphonse Elric: Winry Rockbell, who keeps their automail and their home, and Izumi Curtis, who taught them alchemy. The circle has no office and no seal, only the loyalty of its members. A stranger meets the circle as a pair of brothers on a road; a friend meets it as a family. One who joins the circle rises by standing with the brothers when the road is hard.

factions.name: Glotz Pawn Shop
factions.info: A pawn shop in the west alley of Rush Valley, crowded with old tools, odd jewels and one very valuable vase. The owner buys what he is offered and asks no questions about where it came from. A customer meets it as a bell and a dusty counter; a pickpocket meets it as the place to turn a wallet into money. One who works for it rises by bringing good goods and keeping their mouth shut.

factions.name: Havoc General Store
factions.info: A small-town general store in the east of Amestris, run by the parents of Jean Havoc for eighty years. It sells tinned goods, tools, cloth and gossip, and its counter is where the town hears the news. A customer meets it as a bell over the door and a friendly word; a neighbour meets it as the place that gives credit when the harvest is late. One who works here rises by keeping the books honest and the shelves full.

factions.name: Ishvalan Warrior Priests
factions.info: The warriors of the Ishvalan faith, who defend the people and its rites. The order is known only through the men who were part of it, and it is thin on the public record. A stranger meets a warrior priest as a quiet man on a road; a soldier meets one as a danger. One who joins learns the rites of war and the duty of a warrior to the people.

factions.name: Ishvalans
factions.info: The ethno-religious people of Ishval, the region in the south-east of Amestris razed in the civil war that began in 1901; most of the survivors live scattered in slums and camps across the country. Nearly all have brown skin, white hair and red eyes. They follow Ishvala, the god of creation, whose teaching forbids alchemy, since to remake what the god made is to defy him. A stranger meets them as a neighbour on a market road or a survivor at a grave; a State Military patrol meets them as a suspect. One who joins them learns the faith's words and rises by keeping its rites in a land that has not forgotten the war.

factions.name: LeCoulte Automail
factions.info: An automail shop in the mountains between Rush Valley and South Hood, run by the old master Dominic LeCoulte and his son Ridel, who lives there with his wife Satella LeCoulte. It sits far from town for the materials and because Dominic refuses to live among people. The shop has steady customers, Paninya among them, and ties to the workshops in town. A stranger meets the shop as a long climb to a workbench; a customer meets it as a fair deal. One who works here rises by fitting limbs well and by keeping the LeCoulte name.

factions.name: Madame Christmas's house
factions.info: A hostess bar in Central City kept by Madame Christmas, a gruff woman who raised Roy Mustang as her own. Its hostesses are charming, sharp and much better informed than the officers who drink there. A customer meets it as a warm room and a good bottle; a regular meets it as the best gossip in the capital. One who works here rises by listening more than talking.

factions.name: Mustang Unit
factions.info: Colonel Roy Mustang's unit: five officers and a dog, each with a particular skill, who work as one close family. Its members are Heymans Breda, Jean Havoc, Riza Hawkeye, Kain Fuery and Vato Falman, with Black Hayate as their hound. The unit moved from East City to Central City when Mustang took his post in the capital, and its aim is to put him in the Führer's office. A stranger meets the unit as soldiers on a job; a friend meets it as a family. One who joins it starts as an attached aide and rises by loyalty to the Colonel and by work done in the open.

factions.name: National Central Library
factions.info: The national library in the capital, the largest store of books and records in Amestris, kept in several branches. Most of it is open to anyone; some branches open only to State Alchemists and officers of rank. Its staff are quiet, exact and proud of their catalogue. A reader meets it as a high reading hall; a scholar meets it as a restricted stack and a clerk with a list of names. One who works here rises by knowing where every book is.

factions.name: Radio Capital
factions.info: A broadcaster in Central City, which runs interviews and news in the capital, mostly political programmes that listeners find dull, and its staff will not always follow the government's line. Its studio takes guests off the street and does not always say who put them on the air. A stranger meets the station as a voice in a shop window; a guest meets it as a live microphone. One who works here rises by delivering a good story and keeping the station's line.

factions.name: Rockbell Automail
factions.info: An automail workshop in the Rockbell house at Resembool, run by Pinako Rockbell with her granddaughter Winry Rockbell. The house is also home to the Elric brothers while they are in town. The workshop builds and fits automail limbs and keeps them working. A stranger meets the house as a plain country home with a workshop out the back; a customer meets it as the one place that can fix a metal arm. One who works here learns the craft and rises by fitting limbs that hold.

factions.name: Rush Valley automail trade
factions.info: The automail engineers of Rush Valley, the boomtown of the broken-down, who hold contests in the street and push their wares on anyone with a steel limb. They are rivals in every shop and allies against every outsider. A visitor meets them as hands grabbing at a sleeve to see the arm beneath; a customer meets them as the best limbs in the country. One who joins rises by making a limb the street talks about.

factions.name: Scar's vigil
factions.info: A lone vigilante who hunts State Alchemists, moving through the country with a few companions and no fixed seat. The public knows the name Scar and the cross-shaped scar on his forehead, and the alchemical tattoo on his arm, and it knows the killings. A stranger meets the vigil as a rumour; a State Alchemist meets it as a death. In 1914 a few strays fall in with him, Yoki, a disgraced former officer, the loudest of them. One who joins the vigil learns to kill quietly and to leave no witness.

factions.name: State Alchemists
factions.info: The alchemists the State Military employs in an elite government programme. The licence brings a large yearly research grant to spend as the holder likes, a rank equal to major, the best materials, the state laboratories and the classified files; it costs three rules: obey the military, never make gold, never make a human. Each holder carries a silver pocket watch as identification and faces a research assessment every year, and one who shows no progress is discharged. Ordinary alchemists live by the creed of being for the people, so the public calls the licensed the dogs of the military, and since Ishval the fighters among them are sent to war as human weapons. One earns the licence by passing a written test, a psychological evaluation and a practical before a military board, and the Führer sets the title it carries.

factions.name: State Military
factions.info: The armed forces of Amestris and, in all but name, its government: the Führer is its Generalissimo, it rules from Central City and keeps a command headquarters in each of the four outer areas. Its soldiers wear blue, salute every superior on entry and keep to a strict protocol, and those who break it face detention or court-martial. The army holds the long border wars with Aerugo in the south and Creta in the west, guards the north against Drachma, and keeps order in the cities. A stranger meets it as a checkpoint, a recruiting poster or a patrol; a foreigner meets it as a prisoner. One who joins trains at the military academy, starts as a private and climbs by orders obeyed and wars won, and the highest ranks sit close to the Führer.

factions.name: Xing imperial house
factions.info: The ruling house of Xing, a monarchy across the Eastern Desert from Amestris. The Emperor rules fifty hereditary clans, and the clans compete for the throne through heirs and envoys. The house sends its princes and envoys abroad to find the means to succeed. A stranger meets the court as an envoy or a suppliant; a clan rival meets it as a blade in the dark. One who serves the house rises by serving a clan well.

factions.name: Yao clan
factions.info: The well-to-do Yao clan of Xing, led by Ling Yao, twelfth son of the Emperor and liege of the clan. With the Emperor failing and the heirs at one another's throats, Ling crossed the desert to Amestris after the secret of immortality, and the Philosopher's Stone above all; his bodyguards Lan Fan and her grandfather Fu travel with him. A stranger meets the clan as a prince's party; a rival clan meets it as a threat. One who serves the clan rises by serving Ling's cause and by Lan Fan's test.

factions.name: Youswell miners
factions.info: The coal miners of Youswell, a frontier town near the desert border, black to the elbows and loyal to one another before anyone else. For years the land under them belonged to Lieutenant Yoki, who raised their taxes and cut their wages, and they learned to distrust any uniform. A stranger meets them as a hard stare in the town's inn; a friend meets them as men who will dig all night to get one of their own out. One who joins rises by work and by trust.

creatures.name: Aerugan arms dealer
creatures.info: A merchant in Aerugo who sells rifles and munitions to whichever side pays, and to the Ishvalan guerrillas when no one else will. Smooth, calculating, and armed under a loose coat. Fights little and runs with the cart.

creatures.name: Aerugan soldier
creatures.info: A soldier of the Aerugan army holding the south, with a rifle and a canteen. Stubborn, short of supplies and trained to outlast a longer war. Fights from trench lines and falls back in order.

creatures.name: Aerugo officer
creatures.info: An officer of the Aerugan army holding the south against a larger neighbour, with a squad of conscripts and a store of munitions to guard. Stubborn and short of sleep. Fights from a trench line and gives ground in order.

creatures.name: Amestrian general
creatures.info: A general of the State Military, with a staff of aides and a seat at the planning table. Measures people by what they can carry out. Fights rarely, and then with a sword and the authority of his rank.

creatures.name: Amestrian lieutenant
creatures.info: A lieutenant of the State Military, commanding a platoon in the field or a post in the city. Writes orders in a neat hand and expects them read twice. Fights from behind the line with a pistol and a whistle.

creatures.name: Amestrian officer
creatures.info: An officer of the State Military with a cloak, a sword belt and the regimental badge, who signs the papers and takes the blame for them. Careful about rank and correct in front of superiors. Fights with a sidearm and a cordon of men.

creatures.name: Amestrian private
creatures.info: A private of the State Military, a rifle on the shoulder and the rank marks on the uniform still bare. Drilled to march and to obey a sergeant before he thinks. Fights with the rifle at a distance and a bayonet at a wall.

creatures.name: Amestrian sergeant
creatures.info: A sergeant of the State Military who runs a squad of privates and answers to the lieutenant above. Hard, practical, and quick to note who slept on watch. Fights with a sidearm and a rifle, and keeps the men in the line.

creatures.name: Armstrong-blooded strongman
creatures.info: A man of the Armstrong family, built like a fortress, with a stance no one fails to notice. Earnest, loud, and never in a hurry to sit down. Fights with his fists and a body that shrugs off the blow.

creatures.name: Automail mechanic
creatures.info: A mechanic of Rockbell Automail, with a workshop, a bench full of joints and a lot to say about how a limb should be fitted. Blunt and practical. Fights with a wrench and a clamp.

creatures.name: Bido
creatures.info: A small, bald lizard-man chimera of Greed's gang, long-nailed and able to cling to walls and ceilings. A spy more than a fighter. Fights with a scratch and a quick climb out of reach.

creatures.name: Blue Squad soldier
creatures.info: A member of the Blue Squad, a unit of the State Military, in uniform and field kit, with the squad's own bearing. Fast in a street, neat in a barracks, and loyal to the sergeant who picked them. Fights with rifle and knife at close range.

creatures.name: Briggs captain
creatures.info: A captain of Fort Briggs, a close subordinate of the commander, with combat automail for the right arm and a dry sense of humour. Keeps the garrison moving and the officers in line. Fights with a sidearm and swapped automail.

creatures.name: Briggs commander
creatures.info: The commander of Fort Briggs, a major general of the northern garrison, with a family blade and the nerve of the snow. Hard, precise, and short with those who waste the garrison's time. Fights with a sword and the shot of a pistol.

creatures.name: Briggs winter scout
creatures.info: A scout of the Fort Briggs garrison, trained for the snow and cold of the northern range. Hardy, silent on snow, and able to live a night in the open. Fights with a rifle in the drifts.

creatures.name: Central City citizen
creatures.info: A resident of Central City, a clerk or a shop-keeper or a tram worker, who reads the papers and walks the avenues. Busy, wary of the military, and proud of the city's grandeur. Fights only to get away.

creatures.name: Central Command adjutant
creatures.info: An adjutant at Central Command, who carries the appointment book and the seal and decides who sees the commander. Polite, unhurried, and never without a pen. Fights not at all, and calls the guard when pressed.

creatures.name: Central Command secretary
creatures.info: A secretary of the Führer's office in Central City, keeper of the day's calls and the sealed letters. Quiet, efficient, and far better informed than the staff around them. Fights with a letter opener, and badly.

creatures.name: Central Researcher
creatures.info: A researcher of the State Military's laboratories, in a white coat over a uniform, with a notebook of readings and a bench of equipment. Curious, precise, and too busy to be scared. Fights with the lab bench and a shout for guards.

creatures.name: Chimera hound
creatures.info: A chimera of two living kinds fused into one, here a hound with a second beast's limbs in its flanks. Hungry, sharp, and bred to hunt. Fights with teeth and a sudden charge.

creatures.name: Chimeric dog
creatures.info: A big household dog bred for a laboratory's chimera work, gentle with people and devoted to whoever feeds it. Fights with a bite and a heavy lunge.

creatures.name: Church enforcer
creatures.info: A deacon of the Church of Leto who enforces the prophet's creeds in Reole and half knows of the army he is raising. A true believer, strict and devout, and blind to the fraud. Fights with a club and calls the faithful.

creatures.name: Church of Leto acolyte
creatures.info: A believer in Leto's church in the poor eastern town of Reole, in a ceremonial robe, who sells faith as a service. Earnest or fraudulent by the day. Fights only with a cudgel and a crowd.

creatures.name: Combat automail soldier
creatures.info: A soldier with combat automail in place of a lost arm or leg, the metal limb fitted with claws, a blade or a firearm. Accustomed to being looked at and to the weight. Fights with the limb as a weapon and the rest of the squad at its side.

creatures.name: Creta border highlander
creatures.info: A villager of the mountains on the Creta border, who farms a steep valley between two armies and guides travellers over the passes. Hardy, close-mouthed and used to hearing guns in the next valley. Fights with a staff and a good knife.

creatures.name: Creta officer
creatures.info: An officer of the Cretan army on the Amestrian border, who reads the valley's maps by lamplight and counts the rifles on the far ridge. Formal, weary and sure of the ground. Fights with a sidearm and a squad on the cliff.

creatures.name: Cretan soldier
creatures.info: A soldier of the Cretan army on the border with Amestris, with a short spear for the valley passes. Holds the ridge and does not give it up for a quarrel over a valley. Fights with spear and rifle on the cliffs.

creatures.name: Darius
creatures.info: A human chimera of the State Military, one of Kimblee's four guards in the north, serious and dry and quick to change sides. Shifts into a great bipedal gorilla and fights with brute strength.

creatures.name: Devil's Nest bouncer
creatures.info: A bouncer at the Devil's Nest bar in Dublith, wide and quiet, who knows the escape routes under the floor. Watches the room and moves the drunk ones out. Fights with his hands and a short bar stool.

creatures.name: Dolcetto
creatures.info: A human chimera of Greed's gang, a former soldier fused with a dog: short, fast, keen-nosed and proud of a dog's loyalty. Fights with a katana.

creatures.name: Drachman artillerist
creatures.info: A crewman of the Drachman guns, with a long-range piece and a crate of shells, serving the army's artillery. Proud of the weight of the metal. Fights with the gun at range and a sidearm when overrun.

creatures.name: Drachman soldier
creatures.info: A soldier of the Drachman army, in a heavy coat and a fur-lined cap, with a rifle carried against the cold. Brave in the snow and tired of an enemy he cannot see. Fights with rifle and bayonet in a cold line.

creatures.name: Dragon's Pulse adept
creatures.info: An alkahestrist of Xing who reads the Dragon's Pulse, the flow of life running through the earth, and senses every living thing nearby. Serene on the surface and sharp inside. Heals first, and fights by pinning an array with kunai and striking through the ground at range.

creatures.name: Dublith butcher
creatures.info: A butcher of Curtis Meats in Dublith, who sells cuts to the town and keeps a cleaver on the block. Blunt and kind to the regulars, and short with strangers who ask questions. Fights with a cleaver and the back door.

creatures.name: East City shopkeeper
creatures.info: A shopkeeper in East City who sells groceries and gossip to the military's families. Chatty, observant, and cautious about uniforms in the street. Fights with a broom and a loud voice.

creatures.name: Firearms officer
creatures.info: An officer trained on the army's guns, carrying a service pistol and a spare magazine, and able to strip a rifle in the dark. Disciplined and dry about what a bullet can do. Fights at range with aimed fire and stays under cover.

creatures.name: Former soldier drifter
creatures.info: A former soldier of the State Military who left the army and keeps walking the roads, shouldering a pack. Reluctant company, honest about his past. Fights with a rifle butt and a long walk.

creatures.name: Greed's gang chimera
creatures.info: A human chimera of the crew at the Devil's Nest in Dublith, once a soldier wounded in battle and fused with an animal in an army laboratory. Loyal to the boss who took them in. Fights with claws, a club and a bite.

creatures.name: Heinkel
creatures.info: A human chimera of the State Military, one of four sent to guard and report on Solf J. Kimblee in the north. Quiet and practical, content to follow until he is not. Shifts into a maned lion-man and fights with claws, strength and eyes that see in the dark.

creatures.name: Ishval desert scout
creatures.info: A scout who knows the desert of Ishval by its rock and its wells, moving quietly ahead of a column or a band of fighters. Watchful and frugal. Fights at range and runs for the next ridge.

creatures.name: Ishval garrison brigadier
creatures.info: A brigadier general who held the Kanda region during the Ishval war, with the orders of that campaign on his desk. Cool, exact, and certain the orders were lawful. Fights with a pistol and the garrison at his back.

creatures.name: Ishvalan avenger
creatures.info: A lone vigilante of the Ishvalan faith who hunts State Alchemists in revenge for the slaughter of his people, with no fixed camp. Silent, precise and unstoppable on a road. Fights bare-handed with a warrior monk's speed, and what his tattooed right arm grips it breaks apart; he does not stop at a warning.

creatures.name: Ishvalan civilian
creatures.info: A townsperson of Ishval, a farmer, a trader, or a woman with children behind her, who has lived through a war that was not their choice. Wary of soldiers and of strangers alike. Fights only to protect the family and runs when it can.

creatures.name: Ishvalan fighter
creatures.info: A fighter of the Ishvalan resistance, in plain desert cloth and a sash, trained in melee as a discipline of the faith. Counts for many soldiers on a field and keeps to the rocks. Fights with a blade, a club and the ground beneath.

creatures.name: Ishvalan marksman
creatures.info: A marksman of the Ishvalan guerrillas, with a long rifle taken or traded from the south and a patience learned in the hills. Quiet and unseen until the shot. Fights from cover at long range and disappears.

creatures.name: Ishvalan monk
creatures.info: A monk of the Ishvalan faith, who trains the body in strikes, disarms and holds, and reads the faith's rules on alchemy as a line not to cross. Calm, bare-handed, and sure of his footing. Fights with strikes and joint locks.

creatures.name: Ishvalan scholar
creatures.info: A learned Ishvalan who keeps the scriptures of Ishvala and the people's history, with books and lamps in a study. Thoughtful and grieving, and armed with a pen more than a blade. Fights with a fallback to the knife.

creatures.name: Ishvalan Warrior Priest
creatures.info: A retired priest-warrior of the Ishvalan faith, who trained a young fighter in the old arts and keeps to the rules of the order. Patient, austere, and clear about what the faith asks. Fights with spear and bare hands.

creatures.name: Jerso
creatures.info: A soldier made a chimera in the army's experiments and put under Kimblee's command, grim on duty and a joker off it. Shifts into a squat toad-like beast and fights with a sticky, binding spit.

creatures.name: Madame Christmas hostess
creatures.info: A hostess of Madame Christmas's bar in Central City, part of the madame's quiet information network, who passes on what she hears under cover of a date. Charming, watchful, and unafraid of men with guns. Fights with a quick exit.

creatures.name: Martel
creatures.info: A snake chimera of Greed's gang, a former soldier who can bend and coil her body through any gap, even into an empty suit of armour. Cool, amused, and quick to reach a foe from the rafters. Fights with knives, coil and fang.

creatures.name: Maxim gunner
creatures.info: A gunner on the Maxim M1910, a water-cooled machine gun set on a tripod behind sandbags, feeding the belt and calling the range. Stolid and patient until the line is in front of him. Fights from behind the gun and holds the road.

creatures.name: Mustang Unit officer
creatures.info: An officer of the Mustang Unit, the team that moved from East City to Central Command with its colonel. Dry, sharp, and watchful of the chain of command. Fights with a pistol and an eye for the one sniper on the roof.

creatures.name: Novice alchemist
creatures.info: A novice alchemist with a notebook, a set of chalk and a thin apprentice's coat, working in a town library or a state workshop for a teacher who expects results. Eager and careless with the rules. Fights with a few quick circles, and fails loudly when the matter is wrong.

creatures.name: Panda companion
creatures.info: A tiny panda who travels with a Xingese girl, copies her every pose and loves her like a sister. Cute and vicious: it bites anyone who comes too close to its mistress. Fights with teeth and claws.

creatures.name: Pet cat
creatures.info: A house cat of Dublith, the pet of a little girl, who dies giving birth to her kittens and is buried in a small grave the girl and Izumi Curtis dig together. Gentle and cheerful in life. Fights not at all.

creatures.name: Pet dog
creatures.info: A country family's dog, lively, loyal and quick to chase a cart. It trusts whoever its family trusts, barks at strangers on the road and will not leave a child alone in the dark. Fights with a bite and a bark.

creatures.name: Reole townsperson
creatures.info: A townsperson of Reole, a desert settlement in Eastern Amestris, living under the shadow of the Church of Leto. Devout in public and sharp in private. Fights little and keeps the peace.

creatures.name: Resembool farmer
creatures.info: A farmer of Resembool, working fields and a hand-built house in a quiet country village. Friendly to neighbours and wary of the army's men. Fights with a rake and an opinion.

creatures.name: Roa
creatures.info: A human chimera of Greed's gang, a big former soldier fused with an ox, strong rather than quick and able to stand toe to toe with the Strong-Arm Alchemist. Fights with a sledgehammer and his fists.

creatures.name: Rush Valley engineer
creatures.info: An automail engineer of Rush Valley who walks the streets looking for metal limbs to admire, upgrade or sell to. Cheerful, pushy and the first to know who is in town. Fights with a spanner and a shrug.

creatures.name: Rush Valley mechanic
creatures.info: A mechanic of the automail trade in Rush Valley, working for LeCoulte Automail or a rival shop, with a hammer on the bench and a bench full of work. Quick, competitive, and short on sleep. Fights with a hammer when a rival comes in.

creatures.name: Rush Valley townsperson
creatures.info: A resident of Rush Valley, the automail town, who lives among the workshops without making limbs: a shopkeeper, a mechanic's family, a child underfoot. Fights rarely, and with whatever is on the bench.

creatures.name: Sewn speaking chimera
creatures.info: A child and her dog fused into one shaggy beast by her own father, a State Alchemist, to pass his yearly assessment. It speaks a few broken words and still wants to play. It does not fight.

creatures.name: State Alchemist
creatures.info: A State Alchemist of the State Military, holding a certificate and a silver watch, with a licence to act in the army's name and a rank that puts a Major's authority on the uniform. Trained in the circle and the field. Fights with transmutation at range and a circle drawn in chalk.

creatures.name: The Gate of Truth
creatures.info: The Gate of Truth, the realm an alchemist is pulled into after a human transmutation, where a being called Truth speaks and takes its toll. The same to everyone, and its doors read differently to each. Only the soul gets through.

creatures.name: Tucker-made chimera
creatures.info: A speaking chimera made from a living woman by an East City alchemist chasing his certification, kept out of sight in his house. Confused, pitiful and begging for an end. Fights only in a rush of panic and claw.

creatures.name: Ulchi
creatures.info: A human chimera of Greed's gang, a very tall man fused with a crocodile who minds the bar's ground floor. Fights with crushing jaws and a reptile's strength.

creatures.name: War dog
creatures.info: A trained military dog kept by an officer of the State Military, taught to sit, guard and fetch on command. Keen-nosed, loyal, and quick to find the one who does not belong. Fights with a bite and a bark that stops a crowd.

creatures.name: Western guerrilla fighter
creatures.info: A soldier of the West's big army, schooled in the guerrilla fighting of the long Creta border war: small patrols, night raids and hill ambushes. Lean, patient and suspicious of open ground. Fights from cover with rifle and knife and is gone before the reply.

creatures.name: Xingese court official
creatures.info: An official of the Xing court in silk, with a seal of office and a retinue of clerks who know which house is rising. Polite, cold, and playing for the throne. Fights, if ever, through hired blades.

creatures.name: Xingese explosives expert
creatures.info: A specialist in Xingese explosives, with a satchel of charges and a tally of every bang he has set off. Methodical, a little theatrical, and careful with the fuse. Fights with bombs and kunai from a distance.

creatures.name: Xingese guard
creatures.info: A guard of the Xing imperial house, in lacquered armour with a short sword, dutiful and careful about the gate and the crown. Fights in a close line and checks every charm.

creatures.name: Xingese martial artist
creatures.info: A martial artist of Xing, trained in unarmed and armed styles, an acrobat who senses chi in the body of an opponent. Fights with hands, feet and a kunai, always moving.

creatures.name: Xingese merchant
creatures.info: A merchant of Xing, trading across the Eastern Desert. Courteous, watchful of the scale, and fond of a bargain. Fights with a knife in a crowd and a shout for the guard.

creatures.name: Yao clan retainer
creatures.info: A bodyguard to the crown prince of the Yao house, with an automail arm that ends in a long blade. Fiercely loyal and short on patience for insult. Fights with the blade and a sharp, close guard.

creatures.name: Youswell miner
creatures.info: A coal miner of Youswell, black to the elbows, who works the pits the army leases and drinks at the one inn in town. Fights with a pick handle and the rest of the shift behind him.

creatures.name: Zampano
creatures.info: A soldier made a chimera in the army's experiments and put under Kimblee's command beside Jerso, level-headed and ashamed of what he has become. Shifts into a bristling boar-like beast and fights with tusks and a volley of quills.

items.name: Acolyte's Robe Trim
items.info: A gold trim on a white robe, worn by acolytes.

items.name: Adjustable Spanner
items.info: A sliding-jaw spanner with a knurled wheel, the general wrench of every man who fixes things and does not own a full kit. 18 Cens, sold at Forge Street.

items.name: Aerugo Tag
items.info: A bronze tag stamped with the army's mark.

items.name: Alchemist Handbook
items.info: A pamphlet that sets out the old creed of the craft, be thou for the people, beside the three rules the state lays on its licensed alchemists: obey the military, make no gold, make no human. A young student reads it once and then keeps it. 3 Cens, sold at Market Row.

items.name: Alchemist's Primer
items.info: A thin book with a worn cover that sets out the three steps of alchemy in plain language and gives a dozen simple circles to copy. Most students of the craft start from one. 90 Cens, sold at Stall Lane.

items.name: Alembic Still
items.info: A copper pot and a coiled condenser that separate a liquid into its parts by heat and cooling. Herbalists use it for perfumes, and a student uses it for everything else. 120 Cens, sold at Market Row.

items.name: Alkahestry Kunai Set
items.info: A set of six steel kunai with ringed hilts and a cord tied through each one, the tools of the Xingese arts. Alkahestry uses them to fix a pattern at the points of a pentagram, and the set is sold with a short guide to the placements. 120 Cens, sold at Jade Row.

items.name: Alphonse's Armour Plate
items.info: A plate of armour, kept from the brothers' road.

items.name: Aluminium Ingot
items.info: A light grey bar of aluminium alloy, cast in a mould and sold to makers who want a frame lighter than steel. It bends where steel would hold. 70 Cens, sold at Mine Road Depot.

items.name: Amestrian Beer
items.info: A pint of pale ale in a heavy glass, poured from a cask at the bar. It is the drink of the working man after a shift. 6 Cens, sold at Front Bar.

items.name: Ancient Brass Lamp
items.info: A lamp of old brass with a spout and a handle shaped like a coiled serpent, found among the scrolls of the Xingese archive. Found, never sold: Scroll Room.

items.name: Antique Coin of Xerxes
items.info: A worn bronze coin with a horned figure on one face and a strange script on the other, found in the sand of the old road. Collectors pay well for coins from the ruined kingdom. Found, never sold: Dune Sea.

items.name: Antique Pistol Box
items.info: A walnut case with a brass lock and a velvet lining cut to hold a pair of pistols, sold empty by a pawnbroker who kept the guns. 310 Cens, sold at Glotz Pawn Shop.

items.name: Antiseptic Tincture
items.info: An amber tincture in a dark bottle, painted on a wound to slow the rot. It is the cure for the infections that follow a rifle wound. 14 Cens, sold at Dispensary.

items.name: Apple Preserve Jar
items.info: A jar of apple and cinnamon preserve, sealed with wax and a paper cover. A spoon of it on bread is the best thing a child can get. 6 Cens, sold at Herb Garden.

items.name: Appraiser's Scale
items.info: A small brass scale for weighing gold and stones.

items.name: Apprentice's Chalk Case
items.info: A tin case of worn chalk and a folded sheet of practice circles.

items.name: Apprentice's Goggles
items.info: Scratched goggles for the workshop floor.

items.name: Apprentice's Hex Set
items.info: A set of small hex keys in a canvas fold.

items.name: Armoured Cuff
items.info: A steel cuff that wraps the forearm and the wrist, sold by the Rush Valley forges to men who work with heavy tools and want a blow turned before it lands. 40 Cens, sold at Forge Street.

items.name: Army Carbine
items.info: A shorter rifle with a folding bayonet lug and a stock cut for use inside a vehicle or a trench. Engineers and drivers carry it because it fits where the infantry rifle will not. 210 Cens, sold at Drill Ground.

items.name: Ash Spear
items.info: An ash spear with a steel head and a cord at its middle.

items.name: Assistant's Cleaver
items.info: A worn cleaver with a wooden handle.

items.name: Assistant's Log
items.info: A log of feeding and sleep times, kept for each candidate.

items.name: Assistant's Pass
items.info: A paper pass for the laboratory's outer doors, stamped in red.

items.name: Atelier Order Slip
items.info: A pink order slip from the shop's pad, with a number on it.

items.name: Attached Aide's Armband
items.info: A dark armband with the unit's crest, worn by the newest recruit.

items.name: Attendant's Mark
items.info: A small mark under the collar, shown to the order's doors.

items.name: Automail
items.info: A replacement limb, set into the body at the joints and driven by nerve signals rather than an outside power source. It is a common sight in the cities, and a bad fitting leaves the owner clumsy for months. Found, never sold: Rockbell Automail.

items.name: Automail Finger Set
items.info: A set of five replacement fingers with their own small motors, bolted onto a worn hand plate. A fitter can swap them in an afternoon if the arm is already in the workshop. 110 Cens, sold at Rockbell Automail.

items.name: Automail Gear Set
items.info: A wrapped bundle of brass gears and small axles, cut to standard sizes for the common joints. A fitter buys a set and files it to fit. 30 Cens, sold at Forge Street.

items.name: Automail Joint Oil
items.info: A tin of thin oil with a fine spout, used to keep the joints of an automail limb moving without a squeal. A drop too many leaves a sticky mess on the fingers. 8 Cens, sold at Forge Room.

items.name: Automail Repair Kit
items.info: A canvas roll of spanners, wire, a soldering iron and a small hammer, enough to get a limb walking again on the road without a workshop. 85 Cens, sold at Automail Row.

items.name: Automail Spare Actuator
items.info: A sealed pneumatic cylinder that drives the elbow or the knee of an automail limb. It wears out first, and a limb with a dead actuator is good for nothing but a shelf. 120 Cens, sold at Forge Room.

items.name: Avenger's Mark
items.info: A scar cut on the palm, the sign of a sworn avenger.

items.name: Back Room Key
