categories.name: Origin and People
categories.info: Where you come from: the place, the people and the country you know best. Each origin gives a habit of its own ground.

categories.name: Calling and Art
categories.info: The trade or art you live by: alchemy, the state's certificate, the military, the Xingese arts or the automail trade. Each opens a ladder.

categories.name: Weapon Art
categories.info: The weapon or the fight you trained in. It comes with a weapon and an opening move, and opens its own ladder.

categories.name: Discipline
categories.info: Your focus within your calling or your weapon: the part of it you have given your life to. Each opens its own ladder of techniques.

categories.name: Flaw
categories.info: The weakness you carry. The narrator holds you to it, and it pays you back a little. A lost limb brings its automail.

categories.name: Birth
categories.info: A gift, a training or a mark from before your story starts. The Gate's toll is not offered at creation: it is paid in play.

categories.name: Background
categories.info: What you did before your story starts. It gives a habit of that trade.

categories.name: Perk
categories.info: A small advantage you were born with or earned.

categories.name: Era
categories.info: When your story starts: the year of the war or the road it opens in. Each start opens in one era; Write Your Own lets you choose.

categories.name: Run
categories.info: How the story bends: the cycle as the series has it, or a cycle broken at a great event.

skills.name: agility
skills.info:
Running, climbing, leaping, rolling and keeping balance on a moving train. A basic success gets there; a great success gets there first, or where nobody thought a person could.

Covers: running, climbing, leaping, rolling and balance on a moving train or a roof. Not: enduring, which is stamina, and strength, which is might. Easy: climb a village wall. Medium: leap roof to roof in a poor district. Hard: swim a moat under fire. Very hard: climb a fortress's outer wall by hand. Extremely hard: cross a moving train's roof in a gale.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: alchemy
skills.info:
The art of changing matter by exchange: a material understood, broken down and reformed, its cost paid in matter of the same kind. A basic success changes what you have studied; a great success reshapes it whole, with no rebound.

Covers: comprehension, deconstruction and reconstruction of a material; the transmutation circle as the focus; Equivalent Exchange and the Rebound when an exchange is overreached; the art's rungs open the full reshaping and the rest. Not: a circle drawn in chalk, which is circle-craft, and a bullet's making, which is firearms. Easy: turn a loose iron filing into a bolt the size of a thumb. Medium: mend a cracked table leg from its own wood. Hard: reshape a broken chair into a stool with a clean seat. Very hard: turn a wall of a shop into a door for a fleeing witness. Extremely hard: rebuild a bridge rail that a Rebound has torn in half.

Primary Attribute: Craft

skills.name: alkahestry
skills.info:
The Xingese art of the Dragon's Pulse: healing and purification drawn from the life that runs through the land, activated by kunai set at the points of a pentagram. A basic success heals or purifies; a great success opens a larger array than any Amestrian circle could hold.

Covers: the Dragon's Pulse drawn from the land: medical transmutation, purification, the pentagram in the open and the array that uses several points. Not: a plain circle, which is circle-craft, and the sense of a living thing, which is chi-sense. Easy: heal a grazed hand with kunai set at the pentagram. Medium: clean a poisoned well with a purification circle. Hard: stop a fever with a five-point array. Very hard: open a pentagram in the open air on a hillside. Extremely hard: draw a multi-point array across a village square.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: automail-engineering
skills.info:
Building, fitting and tuning automail: the steel and carbon frames, the nerve joints, the calibration that makes a limb answer its wearer. A basic success fits a limb that works; a great success builds one a soldier would trust in a fight.

Covers: building, fitting and tuning automail: steel and carbon frames, nerve joints, the calibration to the wearer's body. Not: a machine's repair, which is engineering, and a forge's work on blades, which is smithing. Easy: adjust a loose elbow joint. Medium: fit a new leg to a child who grew. Hard: tune a limb so a hand closes right. Very hard: build a combat arm with a hidden blade. Extremely hard: rebuild a lost arm from a soldier's wrecked joint in one night.

Primary Attribute: Craft

skills.name: awareness
skills.info:
Noticing: the sniper on the roof, the tail in the crowd, the loose stone, the thing out of place. A basic success spots what is obvious; a great success spots what was hidden on purpose.

Covers: noticing: the ambush in a pass, the tail in a crowd, the loose stone, the thing out of place. Not: a trail on the ground, which is tracking, and a clue in a corpse, which is forensics. Easy: spot a pickpocket in a market. Medium: see the ambush before the rocks fall. Hard: notice a man following you through three streets. Very hard: spot the sniper's glint on a rooftop. Extremely hard: see the feint before the blow.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: chi-sense
skills.info:
Feeling the Dragon's Pulse: the life in people and animals, the flow of the land, a Stone's presence nearby. A basic success senses living things close by; a great success reads what they intend.

Covers: feeling the Dragon's Pulse: living things in a place, the flow of the land, a Stone's presence nearby. Not: crossing into a trance, which is meditation, and knowing a story, which is lore. Easy: feel that a forest has people in it. Medium: know the flow of a river's life at night. Hard: feel a living animal behind a wall. Very hard: sense a Stone's presence in a room. Extremely hard: read the intent of an armed man before he moves.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: circle-craft
skills.info:
Drawing transmutation circles and arrays: the rune, the rim, the scale of the work. A basic success draws a circle that holds; a great success draws one that takes a whole room and keeps its shape under load.

Covers: drawing circles and arrays: the rune, the rim, the scale of the work, the circle that holds under load. Not: the chemistry of a material, which is alchemy, and an alchemical tattoo worn on the skin, which is a trait. Easy: draw a circle with chalk on a stone floor. Medium: draw a rim that holds a heavy cart. Hard: etch a circle into a steel plate. Very hard: draw an array across a barrack's yard. Extremely hard: draw a circle in dirt with a stick and keep its runes straight in the rain.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: command
skills.info:
Leading people in the open: soldiers, a crew, a militia, a band of workers. A basic success is obeyed; a great success holds a line that was breaking.

Covers: leading people in the open: soldiers, a crew, a militia, a band of workers. Not: courtly manoeuvring, which is intrigue, and a lie, which is deception. Easy: get a ferry crew rowing together. Medium: rally a village against raiders. Hard: hold a militia line through a charge. Very hard: lead a work gang through a collapse. Extremely hard: hold a line of men under a barrage.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: deception
skills.info:
Lies, false names, forged papers, a uniform worn with confidence. A basic success is believed; a great success is believed by someone who was warned.

Covers: lies, false names, forged papers, a uniform worn with confidence through an inspection. Not: moving unseen, which is stealth, and an honest plea, which is negotiation. Easy: lie to an innkeeper about your name. Medium: pass as a refugee at a border ferry. Hard: hold a forged pass's story for a week. Very hard: fool a military inspector face to face. Extremely hard: talk your way past a guard in a uniform that is not yours.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: demolition
skills.info:
Explosives, fuses, grenades and the charge placed where a wall will fall. A basic success brings the target down; a great success brings down the wall and nothing else.

Covers: explosives, fuses, grenades and the charge set where a wall will fall; the trench-clearing of the front. Not: a gun, which is firearms, and the drill of a siege engine, which is engineering. Easy: set a fuse and walk away. Medium: bring down a shed without hurting the house beside it. Hard: throw a grenade into a trench. Very hard: clear a trench line with three charges. Extremely hard: bring down a fortress wall at the right moment.

Primary Attribute: Craft

skills.name: engineering
skills.info:
Trains, tanks, the drills of a siege and the machines that change a war. A basic success keeps a machine running; a great success builds or breaks one.

Covers: machines that change a war: trains, tanks, drills, the siege engines of the front; the rails and the fittings. Not: a small lock, which is tinkering, and automail's fitting, which is automail-engineering. Easy: keep a train's brakes working. Medium: repair a broken axle on a supply wagon. Hard: stop a tank with what is in a village. Very hard: bring a stalled supply train over a snow pass. Extremely hard: find the one weakness of a siege drill.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: firearms
skills.info:
Handguns, rifles and the field gun on its bipod: loading, aim, the steady breath, the clean recoil. A basic success hits what was aimed at; a great success hits from cover at a range the rifle was never meant for.

Covers: handguns, rifles and the field gun: loading, aim, the steady breath, the clean recoil; the Amestrian army's standard weapons. Not: a machine gun on its tripod, which is heavy-weapons, and a thrown knife, which is thrown weapons. Easy: hit a bottle at twenty paces. Medium: hit a man running across a yard. Hard: keep a rifle steady on a windy ridge. Very hard: hit a sniper's window from a moving train. Extremely hard: shoot the lock off a Briggs armoury door from the far side of the yard.

Primary Attribute: Craft

skills.name: flame-alchemy
skills.info:
The combat specialism of the State Alchemists' Flame: air made dense around a target until it burns, water split into fuel and oxidiser through gloves. A basic success sets a target alight; a great success burns a street and keeps the fire where it was aimed.

Covers: the combat specialism of Flame: oxygen made dense around a target until it burns, water split into fuel and oxidiser through gloves. Not: a torch or a match, which anyone can light, and alkahestry's healing, which is alkahestry. Easy: set a straw dummy alight with a snap of gloves. Medium: burn a wooden door from its hinges. Hard: split a pail of water into fuel and oxidiser. Very hard: hold a ring of fire against three soldiers. Extremely hard: burn a barracks' gate and keep the fire from the stable next door.

Primary Attribute: Craft

skills.name: forensics
skills.info:
Reading a scene: the wound, the burn, the blood pattern, the shell casing, the thing someone left behind. A basic success finds the cause of a death; a great success finds who arranged the scene.

Covers: reading a scene: wounds, burns, blood pattern, shell casings, and the thing someone left behind. Not: a trail on the ground, which is tracking, and a lie told in a room, which is deception. Easy: tell how a body was moved. Medium: find the calibre of the round in a wall. Hard: tell a poisoning from a fall. Very hard: tell which officer had been in a room and when. Extremely hard: tell that a scene was staged by someone who knew the trade.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: heavy-weapons
skills.info:
Machine guns, the crew-served gun, the saw-armed automail arm and the grenade launcher. A basic success keeps the gun firing; a great success holds a position alone under a barrage.

Covers: machine guns, the crew-served gun, the saw-armed automail arm, the grenade launcher; a position held under fire. Not: a single rifle, which is firearms, and a charge laid in the ground, which is demolition. Easy: set up a machine gun in a trench. Medium: keep a gun firing with a jammed belt. Hard: hold a crossroads with a gun crew. Very hard: swing a saw-armed arm through a barricade. Extremely hard: hold a pass alone under a barrage.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: intrigue
skills.info:
Ministries, courts and the army's chain of favours: who owes whom, what may not be said, which door a bribe opens. A basic success reads the room; a great success turns an official or outwits an officer.

Covers: ministries, courts and the army's chain of favours: who owes whom, what may not be said, which door a bribe opens. Not: a lie told to a stranger, which is deception, and the street's rules, which is streetwise. Easy: learn which official takes gifts. Medium: get a meeting with a colonel's aide. Hard: read a dinner party for who holds the power. Very hard: turn a clerk who keeps the records. Extremely hard: outplay a bureaucrat in his own office.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: lore
skills.info:
Amestris's history, the old kingdoms, the Ishvalan faith, the customs and records of each nation. A basic success recalls what a scholar would; a great success recalls what the archive was meant to lose.

Covers: the nation's history, the old kingdoms, the Ishvalan faith, the customs and records of each people. Not: a town's gossip, which is streetwise, and a court's debts, which is intrigue. Easy: name the nations and their arts. Medium: tell the story of the Ishval war. Hard: recall the Ishvalan faith's rules on alchemy. Very hard: read a record in a national library. Extremely hard: know what the archive was meant to lose.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: medicine
skills.info:
Field care, bandages, bone-setting, fever and infection, the doctor's craft in a war. A basic success stabilises; a great success brings someone back from the edge.

Covers: field care, bandages, bone-setting, fever and infection, the doctor's craft in a war. Not: healing by alchemy, which is alchemy or alkahestry, and a sick mind, which is resolve. Easy: bind a cut. Medium: set a broken arm. Hard: bring a fever down with the right herbs. Very hard: keep a burned soldier alive through the night. Extremely hard: close a gunshot wound on a field table.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: might
skills.info:
Raw strength: lifting, breaking, holding, dragging a cart off a trapped child. A basic success moves what one person should; a great success moves what three should.

Covers: raw strength: lifting, breaking, holding, dragging. Not: a fist fight, which is unarmed, and keeping going, which is stamina. Easy: carry a wounded friend a mile. Medium: force a barred door. Hard: hold a gate against a ram. Very hard: lift a cart off a trapped child. Extremely hard: hold a locked gate shut against a crowd.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: military-doctrine
skills.info:
The State Military's ranks, orders, courts-martial and the oaths an officer swears to. A basic success knows the rule that applies; a great success finds the gap in the rule that its authors did not see.

Covers: the State Military's ranks, orders, courts-martial and the oaths an officer swears; the rules that bind a soldier and a State Alchemist. Not: a court's favours, which is intrigue, and a soldier's drill, which is command. Easy: name the ranks from private to general. Medium: read a standing order and know its limit. Hard: know which court hears a charge. Very hard: find the rule that frees a soldier from a bad order. Extremely hard: find where a rule's author left a gap.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: monk-melee
skills.info:
The melee discipline of the Ishvalan monks: disciplined strikes, throws and holds, trained for a field where the numbers were never on their side. A basic success strikes true; a great success puts a soldier down before the rifle comes up.

Covers: the Ishvalan monk discipline: strikes, throws and holds trained for a field where the odds were against them. Not: a sword, which is swordsmanship, and an open fist brawl, which is unarmed. Easy: strike a guard's wrist and take his baton. Medium: throw an attacker off a wall. Hard: hold a man's arm in a joint lock until he stops. Very hard: hold a gate for a retreat with bare hands. Extremely hard: put a rifle-armed soldier down before the rifle comes up.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: negotiation
skills.info:
Honest talk: a plea, a bargain, a reason given across a table. A basic success gets a hearing; a great success changes a mind that was made up.

Covers: honest talk: a plea, a bargain, a reason given across a table. Not: a lie, which is deception, and an order, which is command. Easy: talk a shopkeeper into a loan. Medium: talk a frightened village into opening its gate. Hard: talk a deserter out of a bad plan. Very hard: talk a sergeant into letting a prisoner go. Extremely hard: talk an angry crowd down from a riot.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: resolve
skills.info:
Holding steady: fear, pain, a sergeant's shouting, a royal's stare, a confession. A basic success holds; a great success holds and acts anyway.

Covers: holding steady against fear, pain, a sergeant's shouting and a royal's stare; a voice in a dark room. Not: a steady breath, which is wildcraft, and enduring the road, which is stamina. Easy: keep your nerve under a sergeant's shouting. Medium: face a charging horse without running. Hard: sit through a night in a cell and keep your name. Very hard: meet an officer's eyes and hold. Extremely hard: keep a steady hand when a friend bleeds in your arms.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: sewing-life
skills.info:
Bio-alchemy: the study of living tissue, the stitching of flesh and the making of chimeras, which the law forbids on people. A basic success closes a wound the body accepts; a great success joins two living things into one that lives.

Covers: the study of living tissue: stitching flesh, the bio-alchemy of the army's laboratories, the chimera made from living parts. Not: a bandage, which is medicine, and a sick mind, which is resolve. Easy: close a deep cut with alchemical stitching. Medium: join a dog's torn leg to a healthy limb. Hard: study a dead animal's organs for a lab report. Very hard: bind two living creatures into one body. Extremely hard: make a chimera from a soldier's wounded arm.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: smithing
skills.info:
Forge, anvil and whetstone: making, sharpening and mending steel and armour. A basic success repairs or sharpens; a great success forges a blade a master would sign.

Covers: forge, anvil and whetstone: making, sharpening and mending steel and armour. Not: a machine, which is engineering, and the sword's use, which is swordsmanship. Easy: sharpen a dull blade. Medium: mend a dented helm. Hard: forge a serviceable knife in a village forge. Very hard: forge a breastplate that a rifle round will not pierce. Extremely hard: forge a sword of a kind a master would sign.

Primary Attribute: Craft

skills.name: stamina
skills.info:
Enduring: the desert, a long march, hunger, a cold night in the field, a long fight. A basic success keeps going; a great success keeps going when everyone else has stopped.

Covers: enduring the desert, a long march, hunger, a cold night in the field, a long fight. Not: strength, which is might, and living off the land, which is wildcraft. Easy: walk a day on a refugee road. Medium: stand a night watch in the cold. Hard: cross a salt flat on foot. Very hard: march with a column for a week. Extremely hard: keep going through a long fight with a wound in the side.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: stealth
skills.info:
Moving unseen and unheard: rooftops at night, crowds, shadows, the empty corridor of a military office. A basic success passes the careless; a great success walks past a patrol that is looking for you.

Covers: moving unseen and unheard: rooftops, crowds, masks and shadows, the empty corridor of an office after dark. Not: a false name, which is deception, and the reading of a patrol's route, which is awareness. Easy: slip out of an inn at night. Medium: cross a lit courtyard unseen. Hard: pass a checkpoint in the dark. Very hard: walk the halls of a military office at night. Extremely hard: move through a fortress wall's gallery past a patrol.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: streetwise
skills.info:
Markets, docks, the back streets of a city and the rules a stranger must not break. A basic success finds the right stall; a great success finds the thing nobody sells.

Covers: markets, docks, back streets and the rules a stranger must not break: where to buy, who to ask, what to avoid. Not: a court's favours, which is intrigue, and a fair price, which is trade. Easy: find the black market in a port town. Medium: find a bed in a poor district without papers. Hard: find a smuggler who will carry you north. Very hard: buy a safe pass from a gang on the docks. Extremely hard: move a fugitive through a city without the constables hearing.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: swordsmanship
skills.info:
The sword as the army and the old masters teach it: stance, cut, the parry that is also a stroke. A basic success lands or turns a cut; a great success wins the exchange with one blow.

Covers: swords: stance, cut, parry, the single stroke that ends an exchange, a master's lessons kept. Not: a staff or a spear, which is polearms, and a thrown knife, which is thrown weapons. Easy: cut a rope in one stroke. Medium: hold a doorway against two soldiers. Hard: beat a Creta officer blade to blade. Very hard: turn a bayonet with a short sword. Extremely hard: cross swords with a trained state swordsman and live.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: thrown-weapons
skills.info:
Kunai, knives and throwing blades, the Xingese way of the hidden hand. A basic success hits or pins; a great success pins a sleeve to a wall from across a courtyard.

Covers: kunai, knives and throwing blades: a hit from a hidden hand, a pin, a throw that lands where it was meant. Not: a bow, which is not in the list, and a knife in a hand, which is unarmed. Easy: pin a sleeve to a door. Medium: cut a rope across a room with one kunai. Hard: drop a runner at forty paces. Very hard: pin a fleeing thief's coat to a post. Extremely hard: throw a kunai through a window into a lamp.

Primary Attribute: Craft

skills.name: tinkering
skills.info:
Locks, traps, small mechanisms and the clever small device. A basic success opens or sets the simple kind; a great success opens a strongbox nobody else could.

Covers: locks, traps, small mechanisms, chutes and counterweights, the clever small device. Not: a war machine, which is engineering, and forging a part, which is smithing. Easy: open a merchant's strongbox. Medium: set a snare that holds a man. Hard: pick the lock of a military cell door. Very hard: rig a door to fall on the next person through. Extremely hard: open a royal vault with three tries.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: tracking
skills.info:
Following a trail by sign, scent and broken ground: the hunter's craft in a desert or a mountain pass. A basic success finds the trail; a great success finds the quarry.

Covers: following a trail by sign, scent and broken ground: the hunter's craft in desert, forest and mountain. Not: noticing an ambush, which is awareness, and the land's food, which is wildcraft. Easy: follow boot prints to a camp. Medium: follow a cart's track after rain. Hard: track a fugitive through a town. Very hard: track a wounded animal across a ridge. Extremely hard: track a man across a salt flat by a single broken stone.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: trade
skills.info:
Bargaining, prices, cargo, and what a thing is worth in cens and in foreign coin. A basic success gets a fair price; a great success gets the merchant's own price.

Covers: bargaining, prices, cargo, and what a thing is worth in cens and in foreign coin. Not: the black market, which is streetwise, and a bribe, which is intrigue. Easy: buy a loaf at a fair price. Medium: sell a pelt in a strange town. Hard: buy a train ticket without being cheated. Very hard: outbargain a supply quartermaster. Extremely hard: sell a shopkeeper his own goods back at a better price.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: unarmed
skills.info:
Fists, throws, wrestling and the holds of the street and the barracks. A basic success lands or escapes; a great success pins or throws a man through a door.

Covers: fists, throws, wrestling, the holds and slams of the ring and the street. Not: a blade, which is swordsmanship, and a Xingese kunai throw, which is xing-martial. Easy: win a tavern scuffle. Medium: pin a thief. Hard: throw a soldier through a door. Very hard: hold a drunken man until the constable comes. Extremely hard: take a rifle from a soldier's hands with a turn of the wrist.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: wildcraft
skills.info:
Living off the land: desert, mountain, river and forest; shelter, fire and water without a road. A basic success keeps a party fed and dry; a great success crosses the worst ground alive.

Covers: living off the land: desert, mountain, river and forest; shelter, fire and water without a road. Not: a trail, which is tracking, and the weather at sea, which is sailing. Easy: find water on a hillside. Medium: build a dry shelter in a forest. Hard: find the way through a mountain pass without a guide. Very hard: keep a party alive a week in a salt desert. Extremely hard: cross a frozen river without a boat.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: xing-martial
skills.info:
The Xingese martial arts of the kunai and the explosive: footwork, the strike, the weapon that appears from a sleeve. A basic success lands the blow; a great success ends the fight with the first throw.

Covers: the Xingese martial arts: kunai, explosives, footwork and the weapon drawn from a sleeve; the Xingese way of the body. Not: a sword, which is swordsmanship, and a barrack's brawl, which is unarmed. Easy: draw a kunai from a sleeve and strike. Medium: throw a kunai and a dart in one motion. Hard: take a guard's sword with a Xingese throw. Very hard: fight a duel on a rooftop with two blades. Extremely hard: fight through a crowded market with kunai and the flat of the hand.

Primary Attribute: Body

lowText.body: A frail frame. A long march leaves you spent, a fall breaks more than it should, and the weight of a field gun or a front-line pack is beyond you; a hard fight ends early for you.
lowText.craft: Clumsy hands. Your chalk smudges, your circle breaks at the rim, a firearm jams in your grip, and automail answers you a moment late.
lowText.wit: A slow understanding. A material you have not studied stays a stranger, a lie gets past you, and a trap is sprung before you see it; the first gate of alchemy stays shut.
lowText.spirit: A soft resolve. Fear and pain take hold of you, a sergeant's shouting breaks your nerve, and a royal's stare settles on you like a weight you cannot put down.

lore.name: Aerugo
lore.info: Aerugo, south of Amestris, is a principality: much smaller, and rich in farmland. It would rather trade than fight, and spends what it can on its fields and its commerce. Its soldiers wear red coats with yellow cords and white sashes, and they have held a much larger enemy at bay at Fotset for years. Amestrians call Aerugo a nation of shopkeepers. Southern veterans who have faced its army do not.

lore.name: Aerugo army
lore.info: The army of Aerugo, south of Amestris. It has held out against Amestris for a longer war than the western one, though Amestris has the upper hand in men and machines. Its army is tied down on the front at Fotset, the town whose taking started the war. A stranger meets it as a soldier on a long line; a prisoner meets it as a long wait. One who serves in it rises by holding the line another week.

lore.name: Aerugo war
lore.info: The war with Aerugo in the south is the oldest of Amestris's open wars, begun in 1835 and broken now and then by ceasefires and talks that never last. The present fighting turns on Fotset, a border town Amestris took along with a strip of Aerugo's land; the Aerugo royal family took it as an insult and poured troops in, and the slaughter that followed went Amestris's way at first. Then Aerugo threw more than half its army at the line and drove the southern forces back into Fotset, where the front has stuck. Central sends tanks and fresh troops south; the East spares a few. The southern army has paid in men, money and influence, and South City's taverns are full of the wounded.

lore.name: Aerugo's guns in Ishval
lore.info: Ishval held for seven years because someone kept it armed. The rebels fought with rifles and machine guns whose model numbers had been effaced, and everyone in the army knew whose they were: Aerugo's, smuggled north to bleed Amestris's southern border by proxy. When the end came and Ishvalan refugees begged Aerugo for sanctuary, its government shut the door and denied ever having sent a single crate, for fear of reprisal from the Amestrian army. Ishvalans remember that betrayal almost as bitterly as the order itself.

lore.name: Alchemists keep their notes in code
lore.info: Alchemists have a duty to the public and a deep distrust of it at the same time. They believe their art should serve the people, yet they know what a careless or cruel person could do with a master's research. So nearly every serious alchemist writes their notes in code: cookbooks that are not about cooking, travel diaries that are not about travel, ciphers keyed to a word only they know. Another alchemist of equal skill might break one with enough time. Everyone else just sees recipes. Stealing an alchemist's notebook is a crime the thief rarely profits from.

lore.name: Alchemy
lore.info: Alchemy is the science of changing matter by transmutation: taking what is in front of you, understanding it, breaking it down and building it back up as something else. A trained alchemist can mend a broken radio, raise a wall out of a road or turn a fence into a spear, given the right materials and the right circle. It is a science, not magic. It demands chemistry, physics and centuries of theory, and on top of all that an inborn knack for feeling how matter and energy move, which is why not everyone who studies it can do it. Amestris prides itself on its alchemists, and most towns of any size have at least one.

lore.name: Alex Louis Armstrong
lore.info: Major Alex Louis Armstrong, the Strong-Arm Alchemist, is a giant of a man who fights with his fists in gauntlets etched with circles and turns stone into spikes, cannons and statues of himself. He weeps freely, poses often and tears off his shirt at the slightest emotion. He served in Ishval and was sent home after refusing to keep killing civilians. Officers in Central who know him call him the kindest man in the army, and nobody disputes the strongest.

lore.name: Alexander
lore.info: Shou Tucker's daughter keeps a huge white dog called Alexander, who jumps on every visitor and knocks most of them over. He is gentle, noisy and the girl's best friend, since her father is busy with his research and her mother has gone. East City neighbours know the pair well: a little girl in a dress and a dog nearly the size of a pony, playing in a big quiet garden.

lore.name: Alkahestry
lore.info: Alkahestry is Xing's own form of alchemy. It does much the same work, but its purpose is different: where Amestrian alchemy grew toward engineering and war, alkahestry grew out of medicine and the search for the elixir of life. Its practitioners heal better than any Amestrian, mending wounds and easing sickness by guiding the body's own energy. They can also do what Amestrian alchemists cannot, sending a transmutation through the ground to act far away. It is almost never seen outside Xing; an alkahestrist in Amestris is a curiosity, and a much-sought one.

lore.name: All is One, One is All
lore.info: One teacher in the south gives her students a riddle and a month alone on an island to answer it: all is one, one is all. The answer, as she tells it, is that the world is the all and you are the one, a small part whose life and death keep the whole moving. You die, you rot, grass grows from you, beasts eat the grass and are eaten in turn, and the cycle goes on. Alchemy is only that flow put to use. Her students say they did not understand until they were very hungry.

lore.name: Alphonse Elric
lore.info: Alphonse Elric is Edward's younger brother, fourteen years old, and is never seen outside an enormous suit of old armour taller than most doors. Strangers often take him for the older brother, or for the famous alchemist. He is gentle and polite, loves cats, studies alchemy as well as his brother does, and fights better than most soldiers. Few in the army know why he wears the armour, and Edward bristles if anyone asks.

lore.name: Amestris
lore.info: Amestris is a landlocked country of about fifty million people, walled in by Drachma to the north, Creta to the west, Aerugo to the south and the Eastern Desert to the east. On paper it is a parliamentary republic; in practice the Führer is head of state, head of government and commander of the army at once, and the generals of Central Command decide what parliament later approves. The country is cut into five administrative areas, Central, East, North, South and West, each with its own city and its own military headquarters. It was stitched together from older lands and peoples over centuries, so a train ride across it passes from the mild, dry warmth near the southern border to snow that never melts in the Briggs range. The bulk of the people are farmers, miners and townsfolk who see the army every day and their parliament never.

lore.name: Amestris's borders
lore.info: Amestris is landlocked. Drachma lies to the north behind the Briggs range, Creta to the west across the plains, Aerugo to the south over a warm border of farmland, and the Eastern Desert to the east, with Xing somewhere beyond it. No river or sea gives the country a port; everything moves by rail and road. People say Amestris has a war on every border but one, and the desert only escaped because nobody could find anything there to take.

lore.name: Animals of the Briggs range
lore.info: The Briggs mountains look lifeless from the fort's walls, but they are not. Eagles nest on the high crags, rabbits and mountain deer feed among the conifers lower down, and wolves follow the deer. Above them all ranges the Briggs grizzly, and the garrison's winter exercises are planned with it in mind.

lore.name: Annexation of Ishval
lore.info: Ishval was once its own land, a religious people on the rocky edge of the eastern desert, and like many others it was absorbed by Amestris. By law the Ishvalans became full citizens: free to worship Ishvala, free to enlist in the army, protected by the same civil rights as anyone in Central. The law did not settle the quarrel. The Ishvalans rejected alchemy as arrogance against their god, the rest of Amestris counted it a national pride, and old clashes with the central government left resentment on both sides. What held between them until 1901 was called peace, and few on either side believed it.

lore.name: Armstrong Family
lore.info: An illustrious noble house that has served in the army for generations and held sway in the money, military and politics of Amestris for 180 years, every member of it proud, strong and given to sparkling. Philip Gargantos Armstrong heads it with Mrs. Armstrong at his side; their children are Olivier, the eldest, a major general at Briggs, the civilian daughters Amue Armstrong and Strongine Armstrong, Alex, the only son and a major, and Cathrine, the youngest. The family seal copies the curled forelock they all share. A stranger meets the family in the drawing room or on the parade ground; a rival meets it as a wall. One who is taken in learns its strength and rises by the family's rules.

lore.name: Asbec
lore.info: Asbec is a northern town near the Briggs mountains, cold, poor and out of the way. On its edge sprawls a slum that has become one of the larger refuges for Ishvalans since the war, a settlement of patched huts and shared fires where families who fled the east wait out the winters. Local soldiers mostly leave it alone. Anyone looking for an Ishvalan who does not want to be found eventually hears the name Asbec.

lore.name: Atelier Garfiel
lore.info: An automail shop in Rush Valley owned by Garfiel, a big, soft-spoken master of the trade, and the shop where Winry Rockbell takes work as an apprentice. It is known on the street for fine joints and fair dealing, and its window is always crowded with limbs waiting for their owners. A customer meets it as a bench and a tape measure; a mechanic meets it as a standard to beat. One who works here rises by doing the work cleanly and on time.

lore.name: Atelier Garfiel workshop
lore.info: Atelier Garfiel is one of the best-regarded automail workshops in Rush Valley, run by Garfiel, a big, flamboyant engineer who is generous with apprentices and very good at his work. The shop does fittings, repairs and custom jobs, and its workbench is never empty. Engineers in town send him the hard cases.

lore.name: Automail
lore.info: Automail is the Amestrian name for armoured mechanical prostheses that work like living limbs. Wired straight into the wearer's nerves, an automail arm or leg needs no outside power; the nerve signals drive its motors and actuators, so the owner moves it by will. Most are a steel frame under steel plating, though modern makers use carbon fibre, chrome, copper-nickel and aluminium alloys for lighter or tougher models. Nothing else in Amestrian engineering comes close to it, and foreign visitors who see one for the first time often refuse to believe it.

lore.name: Automail in daily life
lore.info: Twenty years of war have left Amestris full of amputees, and automail is a common sight: steel arms on veterans in the cafés, a girl with steel legs running across a square, a dog with a metal paw. The surgery is expensive and agonising and the recovery takes years, so it is a serious decision, but a good automail limb works almost like the real thing. Automail engineers are respected tradespeople in every town, and in Rush Valley they are celebrities.

lore.name: Automail surgery
lore.info: Getting automail is not like buying a wooden leg. The fitting needs an engineer who is also a surgeon. What is left of the limb may have to be cut back further, then a permanent port is set into the body and every nerve is connected to it, one at a time, while the patient is awake to feel it. Then the limb itself is attached, and every nerve fires at once. Recovery and learning to use the limb usually take about three years. A few stubborn people have done it in one.

lore.name: Bad side of Dublith
lore.info: Every town has its rough quarter, and Dublith's is notorious in the south. Its bars stay open all night, its alleys run down to the sewers, and its people work in what they call business. A large pub called the Devil's Nest is the heart of it. Strangers who wander in by accident are told kindly to wander out again; those who come on purpose had better know someone.

lore.name: Baschool
lore.info: Baschool is an abandoned mining town east of Fort Briggs. Its people are gone, leaving empty houses under the snow and a winding maze of mine caverns beneath. Northerners say the workings are easy to get lost in and hard to get out of, and nobody goes there without a reason.

lore.name: Basque Grand
lore.info: Brigadier General Basque Grand, the Iron Blood Alchemist, is a legend of the Ishval war, a burly officer who fights with gauntlets that transmute cannons and steel out of the ground and is a master of hand-to-hand combat besides. He took command in Kanda after its first commander was killed by a stray bullet, and has a reputation for ruthlessness. Recruits are told his war stories and lose sleep.

lore.name: Be Thou For The People
lore.info: The unofficial creed of every alchemist outside the army is Be Thou For The People: use the art for the good of ordinary folk, not for profit and not for a party. Village alchemists live by it, mending tools and bridges for free or for supper, and they are honoured for it in their towns. The creed is the main reason alchemists are loved in Amestris. It is also the reason free alchemists despise State Alchemists, who in their eyes traded the creed for a grant and a rank.

lore.name: Berthold Hawkeye
lore.info: Berthold Hawkeye was a reclusive alchemist who worked out the theory of flame alchemy and refused to join the State Military. He lived in poverty with his daughter Riza, took one apprentice, a young Roy Mustang, and died of illness in 1905 without, people say, ever writing his research down. Alchemists who knew of him call him a genius who wasted his life. His apprentice does not.

lore.name: Bio-alchemy
lore.info: Bio-alchemy is the study of transmuting living things, and it is the slowest and least rewarding branch of the craft. Its great project is the chimera, the joining of two creatures into one, and its history is a long list of dead ends and false starts. Living matter does not want to be rearranged, and a mistake breathes. Most bio-alchemists work for the army or the national laboratories, where the funding is. The field's single famous success of recent years is Shou Tucker's talking chimera, and even that died within days.

lore.name: Black Hayate
lore.info: Lieutenant Riza Hawkeye of Eastern Command keeps a black-and-white puppy she named Black Hayate, a stray found in the rain by one of her colleagues. She housebroke him by firing at the floor near his paws, and he is now the best-trained dog in the eastern army, unofficially attached to Colonel Mustang's staff. Soldiers joke that he outranks the privates.

lore.name: Blue Squad
lore.info: A band of political extremists in the east of Amestris that calls itself the Eastern Liberation Front. It robs, bombs and threatens in the name of freeing the east from the capital, and it has made the rail lines its favourite stage. Its leader sits in an East City cell, and the men still free talk of nothing but getting him out. A traveller meets the squad as a gun in a railway carriage; an officer meets it as a manifesto on his desk. One who joins learns to move in a cell of a dozen men and rises by daring.

lore.name: Body, mind and soul
lore.info: Alchemists describe a person in three parts. The body is matter, bones and blood and organs, governed by the same laws as everything else. The soul is the self: the part that thinks and feels and is said to leave at death. The mind is what joins them, and as long as it holds, body and soul pull toward each other however far apart they are forced. Medical alchemy works on the first part. The other two belong to philosophers and priests, and the law makes sure alchemists leave them there.

lore.name: Briggs garrison
lore.info: The soldiers who hold Fort Briggs on the border with Drachma, in the snows of the Briggs range, under Major General Olivier Mira Armstrong. It is the army's northern wall, a garrison with its own tanks and its own rules. Winters are long and fierce. A stranger meets the garrison as a guard who will not let them pass; a friend meets it as a hard but honest comrade. One who serves here learns to hold a position in bad weather and rises by never giving the snow a gap.

lore.name: Briggs grizzly
lore.info: The Briggs grizzly is the most famous animal in the north and one of the most feared in Amestris. Standing on its hind legs it reaches about three metres, and it is said to be able to break a soldier's back with one swipe. Briggs troops are taught to give one a very wide berth. Bringing back a dead one is a feat northerners talk about for years, and there is a woman in the south who did it at eighteen with a machete.

lore.name: Briggs mountains
lore.info: The Briggs range at the northern tip of Amestris is one of the most infamous mountain ranges anywhere. Its peaks are huge, its passes narrow, and snow lies on it all year; in winter the cold drops far below freezing and blizzards arrive without warning, leaving a world of black rock and white snow. Nobody lives there for long except soldiers. Conifers cling to the lower slopes, and eagles, rabbits, mountain deer, wolves and the great Briggs grizzlies live higher up. The range is the border with Drachma, and it is a better wall than anything men have built.

lore.name: Buccaneer
lore.info: Captain Buccaneer of Fort Briggs is a huge officer with a combat automail right arm he swaps out for different models depending on the job, the Crocodile chainsaw being his favourite. He is loud, devoted to his general and a terror on the training field. New arrivals at Briggs meet him first, which is the point.

lore.name: Cens
lore.info: The money of Amestris is the cens, issued as paper notes and metal coins. The ten-cens coin is brown copper; the hundred is silver, with the number on one face and the national dragon on the other; there is a larger silver coin as well. The ten-thousand note carries a picture of Central Command on the back. A cup of coffee costs about a hundred cens, a long-distance call from a pay phone a little over five hundred, and on the frontier an innkeeper may charge whatever the traffic will bear.

lore.name: Central City
lore.info: Central City is the capital of Amestris and its largest city, a bustling metropolis of stone avenues, tram lines, department stores, theatres and cafés. Here stand Central Command, the National Central Library, the parliament house and the five national laboratories. Being so close to the government gives the city a calm that the provinces envy and resent: crime is low, the streets are swept and soldiers are everywhere. Every ambitious officer wants a posting here, and every country cousin gets lost on the first day.

lore.name: Central Command
lore.info: The top of the military government of Amestris: the Führer and a body of generals under his direct control, who hold the final word on every military operation. Its headquarters is a walled compound at the heart of Central City, raised on a pyramid-like mound behind a moat, and it doubles as the Führer's residence. Nobody enters without a summons or a uniform. A stranger meets it as a petitioner turned away; a soldier meets it as an order. One who serves here gains rank by loyalty to the office, not to the men who hold it.

lore.name: Central Command Headquarters
lore.info: At the heart of the capital, behind a moat and atop a stepped, pyramid-like base, stands the headquarters of the State Military's high command. Central Command is the Führer and the generals directly beneath him, and the building is both their headquarters and the Führer's residence. It dictates law to the whole country and commands every military operation. Visitors cross the moat on guarded bridges and wait in marble halls; very few see the upper floors, and nobody sees the cellars.

lore.name: Central Prison
lore.info: Central Prison, in Central City, is the country's chief penal institution, and it holds hundreds of inmates: ordinary felons, court-martialled soldiers and a few people whose crimes the newspapers were never told. It answers to the State Military, and Central Command leans on it when it wishes. Condemned men wait there for their sentences to be carried out, and the papers report the executions.

lore.name: Chang clan
lore.info: One of the fifty clans of Xing, small and poor, with little standing at the court. Its daughter May Chang is the Emperor's seventeenth princess, and the clan's hope rides on her bringing home a secret that will win the Emperor's favour. Its people are skilled in alkahestry and the martial arts, and they are proud the way a small house has to be. A stranger meets the clan as a modest hall in the capital; a rival clan meets it as a knife in the dark. One who joins rises by service to the princess.

lore.name: Chi sense
lore.info: The warriors of Xing's royal clans are taught to read the Dragon's Pulse in living things, and the best of them can feel where a person is and how they move without looking, track a man through a crowd, or count the guards in a house from the street. The sense takes years of training and is almost unknown outside Xing.

lore.name: Chiko
lore.info: In Dublith, a little girl once brought her dead cat, Chiko, to the butcher's wife, who was known to be an alchemist, and asked her to fix it. The woman knelt, explained gently that a life once lost cannot be given back, and helped her dig a grave in the garden. The story went round the neighbourhood, and Dublith mothers still tell it to children who ask why the alchemists cannot bring grandfather home.

lore.name: Chimera
lore.info: A chimera is a living creature made by alchemically fusing two or more different organisms into one, so that it carries traits of each. Making one is a recognised branch of bio-alchemy, and a hard one; most attempts die on the table or soon after. Those that live tend to be strong, strange-looking and short-tempered, and the few that serve anyone are used as guard beasts. People in the countryside tell stories about chimeras escaped from laboratories, and few of the stories are true.

lore.name: Church of Leto
lore.info: The faith of Leto, the sun god, which the prophet Cornello brought to the poor town of Reole and used to make himself its unquestioned ruler. He works miracles that seem to break the law of exchange and promises his followers wealth, endless life and even the return of their dead. A stranger meets the church as a crowd at the statue; a sceptic meets it as a sales pitch. One who joins it rises by bringing in offerings and by keeping the town's faith.

lore.name: Cold-climate automail
lore.info: Ordinary steel automail is dangerous in the north. Its oils freeze, the metal draws heat from the body, and frostbite eats the flesh around the port. Northern engineers build cold-climate limbs instead, from carbon fibre and light alloys with special oils, lighter and weaker than steel but safe at Briggs temperatures. Anyone heading north with automail is told to have it changed before they go. Those who ignore the advice usually learn on the first mountain pass.

lore.name: Combat alchemy
lore.info: Combat alchemy is the other great speciality: fast, practical transmutations made for the battlefield. A combat alchemist learns to throw up cover, break an enemy's ground, arm themselves from the scenery and do it all in a breath. The best carry their circles ready-drawn on gloves, gauntlets or skin. Before Ishval it was a soldier's trade like any other; since the war it has a darker name, and a combat-certified State Alchemist can expect to be called up whenever the army wants a front ended quickly.

lore.name: Combat automail
lore.info: Two decades of war have turned automail into a weapon. Combat models hide blades in the shin, cannons in the leg, rifles in the forearm or diamond-tipped claws on the fingers, sometimes at the cost of the limb's ordinary use. A few enthusiasts have gone so far as to have healthy limbs removed so they can wear weaponised replacements, which most engineers find appalling and some find profitable. The Blue Squad and the Briggs garrison both field combat automail, for very different reasons.

lore.name: Comprehension, deconstruction, reconstruction
lore.info: Every transmutation runs through three steps. Comprehension: understanding the structure of the material, down to how its parts are joined and how energy flows through it. Deconstruction: pouring energy in to break that structure into something malleable. Reconstruction: keeping the energy flowing so the material settles into its new shape. Most failures happen at the first step. An alchemist cannot change what they do not understand, so a new alloy or an unfamiliar compound is simply beyond them until someone tells them its make-up. This is why alchemists hoard books and guard their notes; knowledge is the wall every one of them runs into.

lore.name: Counting the years
lore.info: Amestris counts its years plainly, by number, with no reign names or great epochs; this is 1914. Amestrians date their own lives by the wars instead: before Ishval and after, before the order and after, the year Bradley came in, the year the station blew up. Ask an eastern grandmother when she married and she will say two winters before the fighting, then work out the number.

lore.name: Creta
lore.info: Creta lies west of Amestris, a federation of tribes and states with a long, bloody history of border disputes with its neighbour. Its tribes are diverse in custom and quarrel among themselves. More western nations lie beyond it, and Amestrians know even less of those. Western merchants and scholars cross the border in quiet times; in bad years nobody crosses at all.

lore.name: Creta army
lore.info: The army of Creta, the country west of Amestris, which has fought its neighbour over the border for longer than anyone living can recall. Its soldiers know the western hills and passes and fight in small, hard patrols. A stranger meets it as a challenge from a ridge; an Amestrian patrol meets it as a shot from cover. One who joins rises by holding a pass.

lore.name: Creta border war
lore.info: To the west, Amestris and Creta are not formally at war, yet the border has been bleeding for years. Rather than commit the whole army, Central lets the large and well-drilled western command wear Creta down; Creta must throw a much greater share of its own strength at the line just to hold it. The town of Pendleton, the first Amestris won in this quarrel, is held up to the troops as proof the war can be won, and it has seen more than its share of careless orders and heavy losses. Western soldiers are trained hard in guerrilla fighting, and they need it. A posting to West City is a posting to the front.

lore.name: Creta's federation
lore.info: Creta is a federal union of many former tribes, each keeping its own local leaders under a central government that watches them closely. The tribes are diverse and dislike one another, so the central government keeps controlled borders between their territories to stop them coming to blows. That decentralisation is Creta's weakness: Amestris has taken several of its towns over the years, and most of those towns have never accepted the new flag. A Cretan officer is a federal soldier first and a tribesman always.

lore.name: Curtis butcher shop
lore.info: Curtis Meats in Dublith is a narrow shop with a sign that says simply MEAT and a chalkboard of specials out front. It sells beef, pork, chicken, cheese, garlic and spices to half the town, and it is run by Sig Curtis, a huge, silent man, and his wife Izumi, a housewife who coughs blood and is not to be crossed. Their assistant, Mason, does the talking. Locals say the Curtises are the nicest couple in town, and that nobody has ever robbed them twice.

lore.name: Curtis Meats
lore.info: A meat shop in Dublith, kept by Izumi and Sig Curtis with one assistant, Mason. The shop is narrow and goes back further than it looks. It sells meat and ties to the neighbourhood, and its back room is where the Curtises keep their own business. A stranger meets the shop as a counter and a cleaver; a friend meets it as a warm welcome. One who works here learns the trade and rises by keeping the Curtises' trust.

lore.name: Den
lore.info: Den is the Rockbell family's dog in Resembool, who lost her left foreleg in a traffic accident while protecting Edward Elric and his friends, and now walks on an automail leg built by her owners. She greets the Elric boys when they come home and barks at whatever else turns up on the road.

lore.name: Devil's Nest
lore.info: A large pub on the bad side of Dublith whose cellar runs into a maze of escape routes and the sewers below. Its crew are outcast mercenaries who keep an ear on all the business of the country's underworld. A stranger finds the bar's door and little else; a city guard finds the cellar too late. One who works here rises by knowing the routes and keeping quiet.

lore.name: District: Briggs and Fort Briggs
lore.info: Briggs and Fort Briggs is a district of Amestris and its neighbours. The snow range on the Drachma border and the fort that holds it: Fort Briggs and its garrison, the refugee town of Asbec, the abandoned mine of Baschool, and the lands to the north where Drachma's army waits behind its own border. Winter here is measured in lives. Its hub is Fort Briggs; its other places: Briggs, Briggs Pass, Frostline Outpost, Asbec, Baschool, Drachma, Wind Gap Camp, Snow Field Inn, Ice Road Crossing, Briggs Lookout Hut, Old Lumber Camp, Briggs Main Tunnel, Briggs Boiler Deck, Briggs Engineering Bay, Briggs Wall Infirmary, Briggs Stockade, Briggs Gun Gallery, Briggs Stores Tunnels, Briggs North Rampart, Briggs Tank Proving Ground, Briggs Barrack Tiers, Briggs Customs Hall, Briggs Telegraph Room, Briggs Remount Stables, Briggs Wallfoot Snowfield, Drachman Siege Camp, Drachman Border Blockhouse, Grizzly Gully, Hermit's Bivouac, Whiteout Cirque, Eaglehead Crag, Wolfpack Hollow, Briggs Pinewood, Briggs Supply Railhead, Briggs Rail Snowshed, Briggs Ski Patrol Hut, Briggs Garrison Graveyard, Briggs Pass Telegraph Relay, Glasswater Tarn, Briggs Sled Kennels, Range Pelt Post, Briggs Charcoal Clearing, Snowmelt Sulphur Baths, Highcrag Goat Steading, Greywall Quarry, Asbec Halt, Asbec Soup Kitchen, Asbec Tinsmiths' Row, Asbec Back-Street Hideout, Baschool Mine Galleries, Baschool Company Store, Baschool Pithead. lore.name: District: Central City
lore.info: Central City is a district of Amestris and its neighbours. The capital of Amestris and the seat of its government: the legislature, the military's top command, the national library and laboratories, and the great rail terminal. Soldiers in state blue walk the avenues and every stranger's papers are read twice. The roads are the station's platforms and the plaza avenues, and the trains run out in every direction. lore.name: District: Dublith and Yock Island
lore.info: Dublith and Yock Island is a district of Amestris and its neighbours. The southern lake town of Dublith on Kauroy Lake, its island of the survival test, and the automail boomtown of Rush Valley north of it. Fishermen, butchers and automail smiths live side by side, and the bars close early. Its hub is Dublith; its other places: Devil's Nest, Curtis Meats, Curtis House, Yock Island, Kauroy Lake, Rush Valley, LeCoulte Automail, Glotz Pawn Shop, Dublith Chapel, Lakeside Halt, Dublith Rail Yard, Kauroy Ferry Pier, Old Lake Fort, Island Cove, Atelier Garfiel, Rush Valley West Alley, Rush Valley Station, Rush Valley Contest Square, Rush Valley Parts Market, Rush Valley Tin Roofs, Rush Valley Nerve Clinic, Rush Valley Patients' Lodging, Rush Valley Foundry, Rush Valley Scrap Yard, Rush Valley Engineers' Hall, Valley Road Toll House, LeCoulte Cliff Road, Rush Valley Iron Diggings, South Hood, Rush Valley Chapel, Dublith Sewers, Kauroy Fish Hall, Dublith Abattoir, Dublith Tannery, Kauroy Lake Hotel, Dublith Schoolhouse, Dublith Town Clinic, Dublith Military Police Post, Dublith Low Wharf, Dublith Post and Telegraph Office, Kauroy Boatyard, Kauroy Ice Works, Kauroy Net Lofts, Dublith Cattle Pens, Kauroy Beacon, Heron Islet, Kauroy Reed Marsh, Kauroy South Shore Hamlet, Yock North Shore, Yock Island Ridge, Yock Toad Pool, Dublith Fig Orchards, Kauroy Dairy Farm, Dublith Brick Kilns, Kauroy Outflow Mill, Kauroy Bathing Beach. By land it joins Central City, South City and the Aerugo border.

lore.name: District: East City
lore.info: East City is a district of Amestris and its neighbours. The strongest offensive force in Amestris: a garrison of veterans from the Ishval years, barracks, trams and canals. Many call the city a backwater and its officers do not argue. The roads lead north to the Ishval country, south to Youswell and back west to the capital. lore.name: District: Eastern Desert
lore.info: Eastern Desert is a district of Amestris and its neighbours. The desert between Amestris and Xing: caravan yards, dune seas, glass flats, the ruins of a country older than any kingdom in the books of Amestris, and the wells that decide who crosses. Few go into it without a guide and fewer come back without one. lore.name: District: Ishval and Reole
lore.info: Ishval and Reole is a district of Amestris and its neighbours. The region of the Ishvalans, who follow Ishvala: razed in the civil war that began in 1901 and left empty under army guard, its survivors scattered across the country and its ruins still standing. Reole lies to the north-west, the town of the sun god Leto that the prophet Cornello ruled. Its people carry the war with them, and the soldiers who guard the road are not always welcome. lore.name: District: North City
lore.info: North City is a district of Amestris and its neighbours. The State Military's northern command, a city south of the Briggs range with its headquarters, its market and the road up to the fort. Its people are hardy and its officers are careful, and the rail line ties it to the capital. Its hub is North City; its other places: North Command Headquarters, North City Market, Briggs Road, Northern Rail Halt, Northern Inn, North Watchtower, Cemetery of the North, Northern Farms, Frozen Lake, Grain Mill Quarter, Central Road Crossing, Ice House, Back Lane Clinic, North Area Barracks, North City Officers' Billet, Requisition Hall, Fort Escort Yard, North City Telephone Exchange, North City Hall, North Herald Press, Northern Savings Bank, Kettle and Stove Café, Bear's Head Tavern, Lantern Music Hall, Oven Street, North City Bathhouse, Gate Ward Guardhouse, North City Stockade, North Area Military Hospital, Pinewood Orphanage, Lower Town School, Snowbell Chapel, Frostworks Automail, Lindqvist Alchemy Supply, Northern Quartermaster's Depot, Snowplough Sheds, North City Coal Yard, North City Gas Works, Northern Foundry, Tanners' Lane, Northbank Sawmill, Sledwright's Yard, North City Horse Fair, Fir Hill Brewery, North Line Trestle, Range Weather Station, Northern Drill Field, Stag Ridge Lodge, Kessel Ford, Blackpine Wood, Grey Wolf Hills, Slate Hill Quarry, Charburners' Clearing, Hollin Peat Moor. lore.name: District: Resembool and the Rain River
lore.info: Resembool and the Rain River is a district of Amestris and its neighbours. The sheep country of the south-east, a quiet farming town on the Rain River and the village between it and East City. Its wool goes east by train and its families know one another's business. The station was struck in 1907 and rebuilt, and the town keeps its own counsel about what it remembers. Its hub is Resembool; its other places: Rockbell Automail, Elric House, Rain River, Rain River Bridge, Resembool Church, Sheep Pastures, Nameless Village, Rain River Mill, Eastern Farm Road, Hilltop Lookout, Wool Sheds, Resembool Hill Cemetery, Resembool Sheep Festival Meadow, Rebuilt Station Row, Resembool Post Office, Resembool Schoolhouse, Resembool Woolpack Inn, Resembool Dry Goods Store, Resembool Farrier's Forge, Resembool Military Police Post, Resembool Country Surgery, Resembool Bakehouse, Resembool Carding House, Resembool Sheep Auction Ring, Quartermaster's Wool Office, Resembool Station Goods Yard, Resembool Line Water Tank, Resembool Line Signal Box, Rain River Rail Viaduct, Rain River Fellmonger's Yard, Resembool Ewe-Milk Dairy, Resembool Wheelwright's Shop, Shepherd's Rest Tavern, Resembool Lime Kiln, Resembool Stone Quarry, Resembool Downs, Shepherds' Bothy Ridge, Resembool Hill Oak, Rain River Fox Covert, Rain River Sheep Wash, Rain River Reed Marsh, Rain River Alder Wood, Rain River Ferry, Rain River Eel Weir, Rain River Oxbow, Riverside Sparring Meadow, Resembool Drovers' Road, East Road Coaching Inn, Coach Road Roadmender's Cottage, Mauro's Surgery, Nameless Village Halt, Nameless Village Smallholdings, Blank-Sign Crossroads. lore.name: District: South City and the Aerugo border
lore.info: South City and the Aerugo border is a district of Amestris and its neighbours. The southern military hub at South City, the supply road to the front, the ruined town of Fotset and the long line that faces Aerugo across the hills. The war in the south has run for years and most of it is fought in ruins. Its hub is South City; its other places: South Command Headquarters, South City Market, South Hospital, Fotset, Aerugo Front Line, Aerugo, Border Watchtower, Southern Road Inn, Dry Riverbed, Supply Road South, South Watch Post, Old Frontier Mill, Hill Shepherd Camp, South City Cathedral, Fountain Promenade, South City Barracks, Station Hotel, Limb Works of the South, South City Telephone Exchange, Southern Gazette Office, Southern Recruiting Hall, Southern Officers' Club, Southern War Cemetery, Old Border War Memorial, South Junction Engine Sheds, Hillside Convalescent Home, Aerugonian Prisoner Compound, Southern Ordnance Works, Cavalry Remount Depot, War Orphans' Home, Old Customs House, Pawnbroker of Front Street, Terrace Vineyards, Old Olive Grove, Limestone Quarry, Southern Copper Workings, Maren Hamlet, Holm Oak Wood, Windpump Station, Red Gullies, Railhead Camp, Forward Dressing Station, Gun Line Ridge, Reserve Trenches, Wire Fields, Fotset Chapel Ruin, Fotset Rail Bridge, Fotset Refugee Tents, Southern Pass Fort, The Ceded Strip, Sanvento, Aerugonian Farmlands, Red Coat Encampment, Aerugonian Customs Post, Smugglers' Saddle. By land it joins Dublith and Yock Island.

lore.name: District: West City and the Creta border
lore.info: West City and the Creta border is a district of Amestris and its neighbours. The western command at West City and the border with Creta: river port and hospital, the wall through the hills, the mountain passes and the small patrols that fight the border war. Little of the west is known in the capital, and the soldiers who serve there rarely come home to talk of it. Its hub is West City; its other places: West Command Headquarters, West City Market, Western Military Hospital, Western River Port, Creta, Creta Border Post, Border Wall, Western Hills, Mountain Pass West, Abandoned Mine West, Western Garrison Camp, Border Road Inn, Western Cemetery, Western Signal Station, Pendleton, Pendleton Front, Cretan Tribal Line, West City Rail Yard, Western Barracks, West City Telephone Exchange, Western Limb Works, Western Alchemy Registry, West City Garrison Chapel, Western Officer Cadet School, West City Courier Office, Railway Hotel West, The Sandbag Tavern, Western Quartermaster Depot, West City Gasworks, West Quay Tannery, Dockside Free Clinic, Hill Barley Brewery, West City Soldiers' Orphanage, Western Military Stockade, Iron Bridge West, Western Plain Farms, Western Home for Disabled Soldiers, Halden Junction, Larch Hollow, Greyface Quarry, Ridge Sheep Station, Larch Ridge Halt, Border Refugee Camp, Pendleton War Cemetery, Pendleton Field Hospital, Cold Seam Colliery, Hill Powder Magazine, Western Timber Camp, Eagle Crag Lookout, Thornback Gully, No Man's Strip, Cretan Hill Fort, Frontier Customs House, Northroad Coaching Inn, Snowmelt Tarn, Southwest Ranges. lore.name: District: Xing
lore.info: Xing is a district of Amestris and its neighbours. The Emperor's country beyond the desert: a capital of tiered roofs and red gates, fifty clans with their own halls, a river port that carries the tea and iron of the mountains, and an archive that keeps the empire's histories. Its court is careful about who is let in. Its hub is Xing Capital; its other places: Imperial Palace, Clan Halls, Yao Clan Estate, Xing Market, Eastern Harbour Road, River Port, Western Mountain Pass, Jade Temple, Imperial Archive, Mountain Shrine, Xing Barracks, Eastern Border Post, Tea Terraces, Chang Clan Compound, Court of Fifty Concubines, Heirs' Pavilions, Imperial Physicians' Pavilion, Silent Lantern House, Yao Retainers' Hall, Han Smugglers' House, Sand Rim Caravanserai, Clan Flashpowder Works, Sea Road Harbour, Yao Clan Rice Lands, Hall of Purification Arts, Shrine of the Western Sage, Tombs of the Mercury Emperors, Dragon's Pulse Peaks, Pulse Spring Valley, Kunai Forge Lane, Elixir Apothecaries' Street, Little Panda Bamboo Grove, Hall of Nine Cups Teahouse, Lantern Opera House, Inkstone Lane, Magistrate's Court of the Capital, House of Foreign Guests, Bridge of Clan Truces, Ever-Full Granaries, Imperial Horse Relay, Grain Canal Locks, Yellow Silt Ferry, Cormorant Fishers' Village, Willow Lake Pavilions, Mulberry Silk Sheds, Celadon Kiln Hill, Bamboo-Pipe Brine Wells, Upriver Iron Foundry, Northern Jade Diggings, Pine Smoke Ridge, Ginseng Slopes, Imperial Hunting Park, Cloud Step Hermitage, Red Banner Ravines, Northern Steppe Horse Runs. lore.name: District: Youswell and the coal frontier
lore.info: Youswell and the coal frontier is a district of Amestris and its neighbours. A coal-mining town on the desert's edge and the land around it: the mines, the coal flats and the spur that carries the coal west. For years a lieutenant owned the land and taxed it hard, and the people of the town work the shafts for what they can get. Its hub is Youswell; its other places: Youswell Coal Mine, Yoki's Estate, Desert Edge Well, Rail Spur Halt, Tailings Hills, Miners' Hall, Youswell Chapel, Coal Flats, Youswell Rail Tunnel, Youswell Water Tower, Halling's Tavern, Mine Number Eight, Desert Approach Road, Pickaxe Inn, Yoki's Company Store, Lieutenant's Tax Office, Youswell Guardhouse, Youswell Pick Forge, Youswell Lamp Room, Youswell Pithead Baths, Youswell Bakehouse, Youswell Post and Telegraph, Single Men's Lodging House, Dust Lane Market, Youswell Pawn and Loan, Youswell Schoolhouse, Youswell Dispensary, Miners' Widows' Laundry, Youswell Weighbridge, Youswell Brickworks, Youswell Coke Ovens, Coal Screens of Youswell, Pit Prop Timber Yard, Youswell Powder Magazine, Pit Pony Stables, Flooded Number Three Pit, Shepherd's Drift, Youswell Air Shaft, Black Seam Outcrop, Coal Spur Junction, Platelayers' Hut, Youswell Road Checkpoint, Goatherds' Steading, Thornscrub Hills, Youswell Dry Wash, Frontier Pinewood, Charcoal Burners' Clearing, Kessel Hamlet, Surveyors' Cairn, Brenner Farm, Youswell Clay Pit, Miners' Allotments. lore.name: Dogs of the military
lore.info: To the public, State Alchemists are dogs of the military: alchemists who turned their backs on the creed for money and rank and sold their art to the government. The phrase was common before Ishval and is everywhere since. A village alchemist will not share a drink with one; a teacher of the old school may throw one out of the house. Some State Alchemists wear the name as armour and even joke about it. Some never get used to it.

lore.name: Dominic LeCoulte
lore.info: Dominic LeCoulte is a grumpy old automail engineer who lives in the mountains outside Rush Valley with his son Ridel and daughter-in-law Satella LeCoulte. He is one of the finest engineers in the country, builds hidden weapons into limbs without spoiling their shape, and refuses every apprentice who comes knocking. He once built new legs for an orphan girl who lost both of hers in a train crash, though he will claim he did it because she annoyed him.

lore.name: Dr. Knox
lore.info: Dr. Knox served as an army physician in Ishval and came back a bitter man. He works as a forensic pathologist in Central City now, examining bodies for the army, and keeps his own counsel about what he saw in the east. He respected the Rockbells more than anyone he met in the war.

lore.name: Drachma
lore.info: Drachma lies north of the Briggs range, a vast, cold, belligerent country whose armies have fought Amestris more times than either side bothers to count. Little of it is known in the south beyond its soldiers and its weather, and a pact of non-aggression signed early in the century is the only thing between them. Briggs soldiers watch the Drachman side of the valley the way sailors watch the sky: not with fear, exactly, but never with their backs turned.

lore.name: Drachman army
lore.info: The army of Drachma, the large belligerent state to the north of Amestris behind the Briggs range, which has fought Amestris on and off for generations. A pact of non-aggression signed early in the century holds, shakily, and the border is never quiet for long. A stranger meets the army as an enemy patrol; a prisoner meets it as a hard interrogation. One who serves in it rises by surviving the northern winters and winning the next fight.

lore.name: Dragon's Pulse
lore.info: Xingese philosophy holds that a current of life runs through the earth, flowing from the mountain peaks down across the land the way blood runs through veins and feeding everything it passes. They call it the Dragon's Pulse. Alkahestry draws on it, and so do Xing's martial arts: a trained warrior learns to sense the flow in the ground and in living bodies, and so to feel people moving behind a wall. Amestrian alchemists say their own power comes from the movement of the earth's crust. Xingese visitors smile politely when they hear it.

lore.name: Dublith
lore.info: Dublith lies in the centre of the southern area, a warm town like most of the south. Its chief sight, by its own account, is Kauroy Lake and the island in the middle of it. The town has a respectable side, where Izumi Curtis and her husband run their butcher's shop, and a bad side, where the bars stay open late, the alleys connect to the sewers and nobody asks questions. Southern people say Dublith is a good place to be born and a bad place to owe money.

lore.name: East City
lore.info: East City is the main city of the eastern area and the seat of its military command. People in Central call it a backwater with no future; the eastern army laughs at that, because it is the country's strongest offensive force, full of veterans who did seven years in Ishval. The Marl River runs through the town and feeds a network of drainage tunnels. Lieutenant General Grumman commands here, Colonel Roy Mustang does the work, and the Fullmetal Alchemist turns up from time to time to hand in a late report.

lore.name: Eastern Command
lore.info: The State Military's command for the east, seated in East City and counted the strongest offensive force in the nation. Its men bore most of the Ishval war and came home veterans, and they think of the east as theirs. Lieutenant General Grumman commands it, and the men hold him in high regard. A traveller meets the command as a checkpoint and a long wait; a recruit meets it as hard drill and good officers. One who serves rises by steady work.

lore.name: Eastern Command veterans
lore.info: The eastern headquarters in East City bore the heaviest burden of the Ishval war, and its soldiers have not forgotten it. Its men are hard, loyal to their own officers, and suspicious of orders from Central. Lieutenant General Grumman, an old man fond of chess and pretty women, sits at the top and is held in great regard; Colonel Roy Mustang, the Flame Alchemist, runs the day-to-day business and is widely expected to go further. The building is old, draughty and always slightly short of everything.

lore.name: Eastern Desert
lore.info: The great desert east of Amestris is a vast, barren waste of sand and stone with almost no water, and it separates the western countries from Xing. No army has ever tried to cross it, and few caravans do: the heat, the storms and the distance kill the unprepared. The shortest road from Amestris to Xing runs across it anyway. Smugglers who know the wells make a living there, and the ruins of Xerxes are the only shelter halfway.

lore.name: Edward Elric
lore.info: Edward Elric, the Fullmetal Alchemist, is a fifteen-year-old State Alchemist from Resembool, the youngest ever certified. He has a steel right arm and left leg, wears a red coat with a black mark on the back, transmutes by clapping his hands and loses his temper at any remark about his height. He travels constantly with his brother, chasing rumours of the Philosopher's Stone, and leaves wreckage, rescued townsfolk and furious officers behind. People are surprised to find him clever, rude and kind in roughly equal measure.

lore.name: Elric brothers' circle
lore.info: The people who stand behind Edward and Alphonse Elric: Winry Rockbell, who keeps their automail and their home, and Izumi Curtis, who taught them alchemy. The circle has no office and no seal, only the loyalty of its members. A stranger meets the circle as a pair of brothers on a road; a friend meets it as a family. One who joins the circle rises by standing with the brothers when the road is hard.

lore.name: Emperor of Xing
lore.info: Xing is ruled by an Emperor, and the Emperor holds the fifty clans together by blood. From each clan he takes the chief's daughter as a concubine, and each bears him one heir, so that every clan has a prince or princess with a claim to the throne. It binds the clans to the crown and sets them at each other's throats, because when the Emperor dies only one heir will rule. In 1914 there are forty-three heirs, twenty-four princes and nineteen princesses, and the Emperor is said to be failing. Assassination between the siblings is common enough to be expected.

lore.name: Equivalent Exchange
lore.info: The first law of alchemy is Equivalent Exchange: to gain something, something of equal value must be lost. Teachers split it in two. Conservation of mass says nothing can be made from nothing; a kilogram of iron needs at least a kilogram of iron to become. Natural providence says a thing can only become another thing of the same basic nature; water becomes something watery, stone becomes something stony. Every child apprentice learns it before anything else, and most alchemists come to treat it as more than physics, as a rule for living. Plenty of people outside the craft find that a cold way to see the world.

lore.name: Executive Order Number 3066
lore.info: The order that ended the Ishval war was signed by King Bradley in 1908. It did two things. First, it struck every Ishvalan serving in the State Military from the ranks and imprisoned them as traitors, whatever their record. Second, it sent State Alchemists with combat-ready arts to the front, not as officers but as weapons, with orders to finish the rebellion and the people behind it. Some copies call it a presidential decree; soldiers just say three-oh-six-six. Within months it did what seven years of rifles had not. It is the reason a State Alchemist's silver watch still draws a spit on the pavement in some eastern towns.

lore.name: Faith in Amestris
lore.info: Amestris has no state church and little organised religion outside its annexed peoples. The Ishvalans worshipped Ishvala, and the survivors still do; Reole has recently taken to Leto. The bulk of the people put their faith in the army, the railway and alchemy, and alchemists in particular are apt to treat religion as something science will one day explain. Preachers and miracle-workers turn up anyway, especially in the poor eastern towns, and do well there.

lore.name: Father Cornello
lore.info: Father Cornello is the prophet of Leto in Reole, a stout, bald preacher in a priest's robe with a red stone set in a ring on his finger. Before the faithful he works wonders, and he promises those who serve Leto more miracles, even the return of their dead. Reole loves him.
