Alchemists who hear the stories notice that every miracle is something an alchemist could do with a circle, and wonder where his circle is.

lore.name: Feeling about the army
lore.info: The ordinary Amestrian respects the army, depends on it and, in many places, dislikes it. The military runs the government, takes the sons, fills the jails and fights the wars, and people say so in private. The East resents it most, since the East paid for Ishval; the capital is friendliest. State Alchemists catch the worst of it. Alchemists in general are loved and State Alchemists are not, and a traveller with a silver watch learns to keep it in his pocket.

lore.name: Firearms
lore.info: Guns are everywhere in Amestris. Soldiers carry rifles and pistols, police carry revolvers, farmers keep shotguns and hunters keep long rifles, and the army fields machine guns and submachine guns at the front. The standard military handgun holds about twelve rounds. Officers carry their own pistols, often foreign. An alchemist who thinks a circle beats a rifle should remember the rifle does not need to understand the target first.

lore.name: Flag of Amestris
lore.info: The flag of Amestris is a silver dragon rampant on a green field. It flies over every headquarters and station, and a version with a border is worn as a badge on army uniforms. The same dragon appears inside the hexagram of the State Alchemist emblem and on the face of the hundred-cens coin. In the annexed towns the flag is more often saluted than loved.

lore.name: Flame alchemy
lore.info: The Flame Alchemist, Roy Mustang, fights with an art few others could copy. He does not make fire from nothing. His gloves are woven from a cloth that throws sparks when he snaps his fingers, and his alchemy adjusts the air around the target, feeding oxygen to the spark until it becomes a jet of flame aimed where he wants it. The theory behind it was worked out by his old teacher and is not written down anywhere public. Damp gloves stop the spark, which is why his own staff say he is useless in the rain.

lore.name: Fort Briggs
lore.info: Fort Briggs stretches across the one narrow valley through which the Briggs mountains can be crossed, a single enormous wall packed with gun positions, barracks, a prison, research workshops, supply tunnels and a great central passage that runs its full length. Anyone travelling between Amestris and Drachma must pass through it. To Amestrians the name means endurance and strength, and some soldiers tremble at the thought of a posting there. Its garrison, under Major General Olivier Mira Armstrong, is the hardest in the army and proud of it.

lore.name: Fotset
lore.info: Fotset is a town on the southern border, taken from Aerugo by Amestris and fought over ever since. It is now the centre of the Aerugo front: trenches, shelled streets, field hospitals and an endless rotation of troops from South City. Soldiers sent there are told it is a matter of national honour. The ones coming back say it is a matter of mud.

lore.name: Founding of Creta
lore.info: Creta was founded around the year 900, when the chief of the strongest tribe in the western hills, a man the Cretans call Cretua, brought his neighbours under one government and made the rule hereditary in his own family. The union held, but the tribes never loved one another. Creta still governs itself as a federation: each former tribe keeps its local leaders, and the central government keeps guarded borders between them to stop them fighting. Amestrian officers say a Cretan general has to watch his own country as closely as the front.

lore.name: Führer of Amestris
lore.info: The Führer is the head of state, the head of government and the commander-in-chief of the State Military all at once, the generalissimo of the army and the president of the country in one office. The holder comes from the top of the army. King Bradley was appointed around 1894 and has held it since, and orders that bear his signature end arguments; a word from him in a corridor can renew a State Alchemist's certificate or end an officer's career. The office answers to no election, and after twenty years few young soldiers can picture anyone else in it.

lore.name: Giolio Comanche
lore.info: Major Giolio Comanche, the Silver Alchemist, is a tiny, elderly veteran with a grandfather's face and a hunger for battle. He was one of the State Alchemists sent to Ishval and was the only one seen smiling when the order came; he was carried off the field cursing with his left leg shattered, and walks on a peg now. He fights with swords, throwing blades and chained blades he transmutes on the spot.

lore.name: Glotz Pawn Shop
lore.info: A pawn shop in the west alley of Rush Valley, crowded with old tools, odd jewels and one very valuable vase. The owner buys what he is offered and asks no questions about where it came from. A customer meets it as a bell and a dusty counter; a pickpocket meets it as the place to turn a wallet into money. One who works for it rises by bringing good goods and keeping their mouth shut.

lore.name: Glotz Pawn Shop shelves
lore.info: In the west alley of Rush Valley, the Glotz Pawn Shop buys and sells anything. Its shelves are crowded with valuables of every kind, some of them very fine, and the owner does not ask where they came from. Local thieves sell their takings there; their victims sometimes buy them back. Everyone knows how it works, and nobody seems to mind.

lore.name: God's Model Automail
lore.info: The God's Model Automail line is the most expensive automail in Amestris, and it looks it: an ornate, engraved upper arm and a shine standard models cannot match. Wealthy amputees order it to be seen in it, and engineers admit the workmanship is superb. Those who have worn both say the cheaper models do the same work. Those who own one say they do not.

lore.name: Grumman
lore.info: Lieutenant General Grumman, commander of the eastern headquarters, is one of the most influential officers in the army and an old man of about seventy. He plays chess for hours, beats most of his officers at it and looks like everyone's harmless grandfather, which he is not. For reasons nobody quite explains he has been left in the East for years instead of rising to Central Command. His troops would follow him anywhere.

lore.name: Guard chimeras
lore.info: The chimeras that survive their making are usually put to guarding something. A beast with a lion's chest, a bird's legs and a serpent for a tail does not need training to frighten a burglar. Reole's prophet is said to keep one at his church. They are dangerous to their owners as well as intruders, and few live long in captivity.

lore.name: Halling
lore.info: Halling is a Youswell miner, the town's unofficial chief and the voice of the miners in their hopeless negotiations with Lieutenant Yoki. He runs a tavern-inn with his wife and son and charges travellers a fortune for a bed, purely because Yoki leaves him no choice. Friends say he would take a loss to help anyone in trouble, and often does.

lore.name: Havoc General Store
lore.info: A small-town general store in the east of Amestris, run by the parents of Jean Havoc for eighty years. It sells tinned goods, tools, cloth and gossip, and its counter is where the town hears the news. A customer meets it as a bell over the door and a friendly word; a neighbour meets it as the place that gives credit when the harvest is late. One who works here rises by keeping the books honest and the shelves full.

lore.name: Havoc General Store counter
lore.info: In a small eastern town, the Havoc family has run a general store for eighty years, as the sign proudly says: flour, nails, lamp oil, seed, boots and whatever else a village needs. The family's son went into the army and did well enough to serve under the Flame Alchemist. His parents are prouder of the store.

lore.name: Heavy Combat M1913-A
lore.info: The Heavy Combat M1913-A, better known as the Crocodile, is a cold-climate combat arm with no hand at all. In place of fingers it carries a large gas-driven chainsaw fitted with a clamping jaw. Like other northern automail it is built of carbon fibre to keep frostbite away, and the exhaust from its engine warms the wearer's shoulder, so a soldier can fight longer in the cold than with any other model. It is loud, terrifying and entirely Briggs.

lore.name: Homunculus
lore.info: A homunculus, in the old texts, is an artificial human, a person made by alchemy rather than born. The idea is older than Amestris and turns up in every library's oldest shelves. Modern alchemists treat it as a fantasy: no one in recorded history has come anywhere close, and the law forbids anyone to try. Students sometimes argue about whether it is possible in principle; professors usually end the argument by asking where they intend to find the soul. Outside the lecture hall the word turns up mostly in old stories.

lore.name: Horses and mules
lore.info: For all its trains and motorcars, Amestris still moves on hooves. Farm carts and buggies are horse-drawn in most of the country, even as motorcars and steam engines take over the towns. Out in the countryside, a farmer's horse can matter more to him than his house.

lore.name: Human chimeras
lore.info: Joining animals is legal, if rarely successful. Joining a human being to an animal counts as human transmutation and is banned outright under the military's authority. Alchemists are taught that the few who have flouted the ban made nothing that could live as a person, and that is all most of them want to know.

lore.name: Human Transmutation
lore.info: Every alchemist in Amestris is forbidden by national law to transmute a human being: to bring back the dead, to make an artificial person, or to remake a living body or soul. Most people believe the ban exists because the act is monstrous and because it always ends in catastrophe. Every recorded attempt to bring someone back has failed, and the alchemists who tried were maimed or killed by the rebound. Teachers tell their apprentices bluntly that the dead stay dead. Those who have tried anyway rarely speak about it, and they tend to recognise one another.

lore.name: Human weapons in Ishval
lore.info: When Executive Order 3066 sent the State Alchemists east, the war changed in weeks. Flame, explosion, iron and stone were turned on fortified quarters, then on whole districts. The Flame Alchemist became a hero of Ishval there; the Crimson Alchemist became something else. Officers who had led men through seven years of attrition watched a single alchemist do a battalion's work in an afternoon. The newspapers called them heroes. The men who stood beside them called them human weapons, and so did the alchemists themselves, once the drinking started. The phrase stuck, and it is still what most Amestrians picture when they hear the words State Alchemist.

lore.name: Infamy in Amestris and Its Neighbours
lore.info: Every state has its own law, and every state agrees on this: a killing that served nothing is remembered. Word travels faster than any traveller, by telephone, telegraph and newspaper along the rail lines. The State Military posts wanted notices, the police keep files, and the village simply remembers faces. A name that becomes notorious closes the respectable doors first, then the trains and the coaches, and at the last brings soldiers who do not ask questions and hunters who are paid not to. Human transmutation, the making or remaking of a person, is banned to every alchemist in Amestris. The only way back that anyone remembers is the old one: penance in a quiet chapel, slowly, before the altar.

lore.name: Investigations office
lore.info: The army's investigations office in Central City handles intelligence, criminal cases inside the military and anything that needs looking into quietly. Its officers dig through records, interview witnesses and keep files on everyone important. Lieutenant Colonel Maes Hughes runs a section of it, and he is famous in the corridors less for his work than for the photographs of his wife and daughter he shows everyone, whether they ask or not.

lore.name: Isaac McDougal
lore.info: Isaac McDougal, the Freezing Alchemist, resigned his certificate after Ishval and vanished. He was a master of water and ice, able to freeze a street in a moment or boil the water in a man's body. Rumours put him among anti-government movements and say he talks of exposing something rotten in Central. The army wants him back, very badly.

lore.name: Ishval
lore.info: Ishval is a region in the south-east of Amestris, on the edge of the Eastern Desert: rocks and sand, very little farmland and no resources worth fighting over, which is perhaps why its people built their life around discipline and prayer. It was once a crossing for traders and smugglers coming from Xing. Since the war it has been a desolation of ruined districts, Gunja, Kanda, Daliha and others, occupied by Amestrian troops and soaked, its survivors say, in blood and bad dreams. Almost no Ishvalan lives there now.

lore.name: Ishval Civil War
lore.info: The war that began in 1901 lasted seven years before it was ended by force. The Amestrian army far outnumbered the Ishvalans, yet the rebels held, fighting a guerrilla war among the rocks with weapons smuggled in from Aerugo. The fighting spread until the whole East Area was a war zone; towns as far off as Resembool were struck. In 1908 the Führer issued Executive Order 3066 and sent State Alchemists to the front, and within a year Ishval was emptied: its towns razed, its people killed or scattered as refugees. Amestrians call it the Ishval Civil War. Survivors call it the war of extermination, and few Amestrian veterans argue with them in private.

lore.name: Ishvala
lore.info: Ishvala is the god of all creation in the Ishvalan faith, and the Ishvalans call him the only true god. Little of his teaching is written down for outsiders. What every Amestrian knows is that his faithful read it as forbidding alchemy: to break down and remake what Ishvala made is to say a human hand can improve on his work, which is perversion and arrogance. Since the war his worship has been close to extinct, kept alive in refugee slums and in the memories of a few old priests.

lore.name: Ishvalan faith and custom
lore.info: Ishvalan life is built around prayer and discipline. The faithful pray together, live simply, and keep strict codes of conduct that outsiders say were shaped by a harsh, barren land. The dead are said to go to their god. Teaching passes down through prophets, and the greatest of them in living memory, the Grand Cleric Logue Lowe, was last heard of in the war.

lore.name: Ishvalan features
lore.info: Nearly every Ishvalan has the same three marks: dark brown skin, white hair and red eyes. The traits breed true, so a soldier with a single Ishvalan grandparent can still carry the red eyes and spend his life hiding them behind tinted goggles. In the East those features are enough to get a man refused at an inn or stopped by a patrol. Some Amestrians are fascinated; most look away.

lore.name: Ishvalan refugees
lore.info: Since the war, Ishvalans have lived scattered and hunted. They are citizens by law, yet most Amestrians treat them with fear, pity or open contempt, and they have fallen below second-class standing in practice. Refugee slums cling to the edges of towns from the East to the far North; Asbec near the Briggs range holds a large one, and some families crossed the sands to live among the ruins of Xerxes. Dark skin, white hair and red eyes mark an Ishvalan in any crowd, so many keep hoods up, goggles on and names to themselves. A soldier who sees red eyes in a market may ask for papers; a decent one looks away.

lore.name: Ishvalan warrior monks
lore.info: The monks of Ishval train in unarmed fighting as part of their spiritual discipline, the body made obedient to the soul. Amestrian officers who fought them reckoned one trained monk was worth about ten ordinary soldiers in close quarters. The order that taught them was broken in the war and its masters killed or scattered. A few survived, old men in hiding who still rise before dawn to practise. Soldiers in the East are warned to keep their distance from any Ishvalan man with a steady stance and empty hands.

lore.name: Ishvalan Warrior Priests
lore.info: The warriors of the Ishvalan faith, who defend the people and its rites. The order is known only through the men who were part of it, and it is thin on the public record. A stranger meets a warrior priest as a quiet man on a road; a soldier meets one as a danger. One who joins learns the rites of war and the duty of a warrior to the people.

lore.name: Ishvalans
lore.info: The ethno-religious people of Ishval, the region in the south-east of Amestris razed in the civil war that began in 1901; most of the survivors live scattered in slums and camps across the country. Nearly all have brown skin, white hair and red eyes. They follow Ishvala, the god of creation, whose teaching forbids alchemy, since to remake what the god made is to defy him. A stranger meets them as a neighbour on a market road or a survivor at a grave; a State Military patrol meets them as a suspect. One who joins them learns the faith's words and rises by keeping its rites in a land that has not forgotten the war.

lore.name: Izumi Curtis
lore.info: Izumi Curtis keeps a butcher's shop in Dublith with her husband Sig, and calls herself a housewife. She is also one of the finest alchemists and martial artists in the south, trained in the northern mountains, who once taught the Elric brothers. She despises State Alchemists, is often ill, coughs blood when she overexerts herself and does it anyway. People in Dublith know to be polite to her.

lore.name: Jude
lore.info: A rumour goes round among alchemists about Jude, the blind alchemist in the service of the wealthy Hamburgang family. When their young daughter Rosalie Hamburgang died, the story says, Jude brought her back, and she is alive in the house today; his scarred, sightless eyes are the price he paid. The family keeps to itself and lets no one ask him how. Alchemists who hear it either go looking or refuse to believe a word.

lore.name: Kanda
lore.info: Kanda was one of the districts of Ishval and among the hardest fought in the war. Its first commander, Brigadier General Fessler, spent his own men so recklessly that his troops hated him, and when he fell to what everyone agreed was a stray bullet, Basque Grand took the district. Two Resembool doctors treated both sides there, and Kanda's surviving refugees still say their names. Kanda now is broken walls and a guard post.

lore.name: Kauroy Lake
lore.info: Kauroy Lake, by Dublith, is the town's pride and its main attraction for visitors, a broad lake full of fish. In the middle sits Yock Island, small and wild, with nobody living on it. Locals point it out to visitors and then tell them about the teacher who sends her students there.

lore.name: Kimblee's crime
lore.info: Among the State Alchemists sent to Ishval, the Crimson Alchemist, Solf J. Kimblee, was the one even other veterans would not drink with. Near the war's end he turned his explosive alchemy on his own superior officers, killing several, and was arrested and sent to prison in Central City, where he has sat since. Soldiers who served near him tell stories of a polite, well-dressed man who hummed while things burned. Most of them are glad he is behind bars, and quietly afraid of the day someone decides he is useful again.

lore.name: King Bradley
lore.info: Führer King Bradley, born in 1854, is the most powerful man in Amestris and one of its most admired. A hero of the wars before his election, he wears a patch over his left eye and is said to be the finest swordsman alive; soldiers swear they have seen him cut bullets out of the air. In public he is a warm, witty old gentleman who visits the wounded and remembers names. In policy he is the man who signed Executive Order 3066, and nobody in the East forgets it.

lore.name: King Bradley's rise
lore.info: Around 1894 the army chose a decorated general, a war hero and a famously deadly swordsman, as Führer. King Bradley has ruled ever since, for twenty years now, and under him the military became the country's first and last concern. There have been fighting and massacres on most of the borders since he took office, and harsh civil wars inside them, always under the command of Central's army. He is also, by every account, a charming man in person: a grandfather in spirit who visits troops, jokes with clerks and dotes on his wife and young son. Newspapers print the charm; the border towns remember the campaigns.

lore.name: King of Xerxes
lore.info: History remembers the last King of Xerxes as a beloved ruler who reigned well into old age over a happy, prosperous people, and as the last of anything: his kingdom vanished in his reign and left no chronicle of its end. His castle still stands at the heart of the ruins. What he did or failed to do is anyone's guess, and desert storytellers guess freely.

lore.name: LeCoulte Automail
lore.info: An automail shop in the mountains between Rush Valley and South Hood, run by the old master Dominic LeCoulte and his son Ridel, who lives there with his wife Satella LeCoulte. It sits far from town for the materials and because Dominic refuses to live among people. The shop has steady customers, Paninya among them, and ties to the workshops in town. A stranger meets the shop as a long climb to a workbench; a customer meets it as a fair deal. One who works here rises by fitting limbs well and by keeping the LeCoulte name.

lore.name: LeCoulte workshop
lore.info: Dominic LeCoulte's workshop sits in the mountains between Rush Valley and South Hood, because Dominic likes the ore close and people far. He is the best engineer in the region and a famously bad-tempered one, and he refuses every apprentice who asks. His work is lightweight, precise and full of hidden tricks: blades and guns tucked inside legs without spoiling the line of the limb. Rush Valley's engineers speak his name with respect and keep their distance.

lore.name: Leto
lore.info: Leto is the sun god of Reole, a small, poor desert town in the east. His worship is young and his church new; a preacher named Cornello brought it, calling himself Leto's prophet, and began to work miracles before the faithful, promising that Leto would reward their service with more miracles, even the return of their dead. Nearly everyone in Reole believes. The rest of the country has not heard of Leto at all, and the few alchemists who have heard of Cornello are curious how he does it.

lore.name: Living with automail
lore.info: Automail never stops needing care. It must be oiled, adjusted and overhauled, and an overhaul means disconnecting it from the nerves and connecting it again, which hurts just as much the hundredth time. Steel conducts heat and cold into the flesh around the port, so desert sun and northern frost are both miserable; weather changes make the scar ache. Engineers warn that heavy automail strains a growing body and can stunt it. Wearers learn to carry a spanner and to find a mechanic in every town.

lore.name: Logue Lowe
lore.info: Logue Lowe was the Grand Cleric of Ishval, the faith's spiritual leader, honoured by his people as a prophet of Ishvala. During the war he went to the Amestrian lines under escort and asked for a meeting with the Führer, offering his own life if it would spare his people. Nobody outside the army knows what answer he received. The Ishvalan refugees speak of him with a reverence they give no one else, and none of them will tell an Amestrian anything more.

lore.name: Madame Christmas's bar
lore.info: In a quiet street of the capital, a hostess bar run by a big, shrewd woman everyone calls Madame Christmas serves drinks, music and the company of her girls to officers and businessmen. It is a respectable establishment by the standards of such places, and very well informed: men talk, and the girls listen. The Madame is said to have raised a nephew who went into the army and did well. She does not discuss him with strangers.

lore.name: Madame Christmas's house
lore.info: A hostess bar in Central City kept by Madame Christmas, a gruff woman who raised Roy Mustang as her own. Its hostesses are charming, sharp and much better informed than the officers who drink there. A customer meets it as a warm room and a good bottle; a regular meets it as the best gossip in the capital. One who works here rises by listening more than talking.

lore.name: Maes Hughes
lore.info: Lieutenant Colonel Maes Hughes of the investigations office in Central is Roy Mustang's oldest friend and a veteran of Ishval. He is cheerful, sharp and very well informed, and he cannot get through a conversation without producing a photograph of his wife Gracia or his little daughter Elicia, who turns three this year. Colleagues dodge him in corridors. Every one of them would trust him with their life.

lore.name: Mauser C96
lore.info: The Mauser C96 is a distinctive foreign-pattern pistol that a few Amestrian officers carry in place of the service handgun, a favourite of men who like to be noticed. At Fort Briggs, Captain Buccaneer wears one, and new arrivals who give the garrison any reason for suspicion tend to meet it before they meet him.

lore.name: Maxim M1910
lore.info: The Maxim M1910 is a heavy machine gun served by a crew, and soldiers who fought in Ishval remember it bitterly: the Ishvalan rebels had them, along with crates of other foreign arms, and every Amestrian veteran knows they came from Aerugo. A Maxim nest in the rocks could hold a street against a company.

lore.name: Medical alchemy
lore.info: Because knowledge is the hard limit of the craft, most alchemists specialise, and medicine is one of the oldest specialities. A medical alchemist studies the body as thoroughly as a surgeon does, then learns to mend tissue, close wounds and set bone by transmutation. It is slow, precise work. Amestrian medical alchemy is good but limited, and physicians who have met Xingese alkahestrists admit the east does it better. The State Alchemist Tim Marcoh was the country's most famous medical researcher before he vanished.

lore.name: Miles
lore.info: Major Miles is Major General Armstrong's adjutant at Fort Briggs, a quiet, intelligent officer who wears tinted snow goggles indoors and out. He is efficient, loyal and fair to his soldiers. Briggs men say he hides his eyes because one of his grandparents was Ishvalan. At Briggs nobody cares, which is one reason he serves there.

lore.name: Military academy
lore.info: Anyone who wants to serve as a soldier of the State Military must pass through the military academy, where cadets are tested in mind and body and drilled in law, tactics and obedience. The academy does not turn anyone away for sex or ancestry; women and men of every background graduate side by side, and some of the army's best officers came from humble towns. Friendships formed there last careers. So do rivalries. Every officer can tell you who topped their year.

lore.name: Military chimeras
lore.info: Soldiers swap stories about special troops who answer only to Central Command: men who move too fast, heal too quickly or smell things no one else can, and serve as bodyguards to a few chosen officers. Officially the army fields no such thing. Most soldiers treat the stories the way they treat ghost stories about haunted barracks, and keep their bayonets close anyway.

lore.name: Military law
lore.info: The State Military runs on its own law. A soldier who breaks protocol faces detention; a serious breach goes to a court-martial, whose verdicts are quick and rarely appealed. Officers are expected to salute every superior on entry, and soldiers are forbidden to carry on romantic relationships with one another, a rule observed in the breach in every barracks. A court-martialled soldier goes to Central Prison with the ordinary felons, and the newspapers print the sentences. Civilians who cross the army can find themselves in front of the same courts.

lore.name: Military police
lore.info: In most Amestrian towns the police are soldiers. The State Military keeps a police force for law and order inside towns and cities, and its guards wear a black version of the blue uniform to mark them out. They handle thieves and drunks the way any police would, and dissidents the way any army would. In the East, where the army is not loved, people cross the street when the black coats come. Central's police are better dressed and much harder to bribe.

lore.name: Military ranks
lore.info: The State Military's ranks run from private up through lance corporal, corporal, sergeant, master sergeant and warrant officer to second and first lieutenant, captain, major, lieutenant colonel, colonel, brigadier general, major general, lieutenant general and general, with the Führer above them all. The insignia sit on the shoulder marks of the uniform. State Alchemists hold the rank of major from the moment they are certified and stand to one side of the ordinary ladder, with their own titles and their own supervision. A fifteen-year-old major is still a major, and sergeants three times his age salute him.

lore.name: Model 24 Stielhandgranate
lore.info: The stick grenade is a charge in a metal head on a wooden throwing handle. The handle lets a soldier throw it farther than a round grenade, and the charge is heavy enough to wreck a vehicle. It is a soldier's weapon, and an officer seen with one is expecting a very bad day.

lore.name: Modified M1910
lore.info: The Modified M1910, which soldiers call the Mad Bear G, is a cold-climate combat arm: a carbon-fibre alloy frame, light and very tough, with fingertips hardened and sharpened with diamonds. Northern engineers rate it among the best cold-climate models ever built. Captain Buccaneer of Briggs keeps one to swap onto his shoulder socket when the Crocodile is too much.

lore.name: Motorcars and the industrial age
lore.info: Just past the first decade of the century, Amestris is in the middle of an industrial revolution. Steam locomotives and motorcars are overtaking horse carriages, though the cart and buggy are still everywhere. Electricity lights the cities while gas lamps burn in rural towns, and coal fires the furnaces, the trains and the stoves. Chemistry and metallurgy have leapt ahead, helped by the country's alchemists. The one thing that seems a century early is automail, and nobody can quite explain why the country that makes it still runs on coal.

lore.name: Mr. Han
lore.info: Among the Han clan of Xing are men who make a living carrying travellers across the Eastern Desert in secret, by routes and wells only they know. Amestrians who need to reach Xing quietly, or Xingese who need to reach Amestris, sooner or later find their way to a smuggler called Mr. Han. He charges what the journey is worth and never asks why.

lore.name: Mrs. Bradley
lore.info: The Führer's wife is a kind, round-faced woman who lives with him and their son at the presidential residence in Central Command. She appears beside her husband at ceremonies, hospitals and charity events and is genuinely liked, even by people who dislike him. Her first name is hardly ever printed; to the country she is simply Mrs. Bradley.

lore.name: Mustang Unit
lore.info: Colonel Roy Mustang's unit: five officers and a dog, each with a particular skill, who work as one close family. Its members are Heymans Breda, Jean Havoc, Riza Hawkeye, Kain Fuery and Vato Falman, with Black Hayate as their hound. The unit moved from East City to Central City when Mustang took his post in the capital, and its aim is to put him in the Führer's office. A stranger meets the unit as soldiers on a job; a friend meets it as a family. One who joins it starts as an attached aide and rises by loyalty to the Colonel and by work done in the open.

lore.name: Mustang's staff
lore.info: Colonel Mustang keeps a small, loyal staff at East City: Second Lieutenant Jean Havoc, a chain-smoking country boy who leads in the field; Second Lieutenant Heymans Breda, a heavyset genius at strategy who is terrified of dogs; Vato Falman, a warrant officer and walking encyclopaedia; and Master Sergeant Kain Fuery, a gentle radio enthusiast. With Riza Hawkeye they work like a family. Other officers find them odd, and envy them.

lore.name: Nameless Village
lore.info: Somewhere between East City and Resembool is a village whose station signs are blank. Ask its name and people shrug, and they seem content to leave it that way. It is a poor, out-of-the-way place where a passenger only gets off by mistake. In recent years the villagers have boasted of a doctor who arrived from nowhere and treats the sick for almost nothing, with results that look like miracles. They guard him jealously.

lore.name: Names of the Stone
lore.info: The Stone goes by many names, and alchemists who chase it tend to collect them: the sage's stone, the heavenly or celestial stone, the great elixir, the red tincture, the fifth element, the red stone. Each comes from a different school and a different century, and arguing over which is the proper one is a pastime of students in the national library. Whatever the name, the books agree it is red.

lore.name: National Central Library
lore.info: The national library in the capital, the largest store of books and records in Amestris, kept in several branches. Most of it is open to anyone; some branches open only to State Alchemists and officers of rank. Its staff are quiet, exact and proud of their catalogue. A reader meets it as a high reading hall; a scholar meets it as a restricted stack and a clerk with a list of names. One who works here rises by knowing where every book is.

lore.name: National Central Library branches
lore.info: The National Central Library is the largest store of books and records in Amestris, collected from across the country and its whole history. It is divided into numbered branches, each housing a different kind of material, and most are open to the public. Some are reserved for State Alchemists and officers of rank, the First Branch above all, which holds government records and research. The librarians are proud and severe, and scholars from all five areas queue at the doors. A clerk who remembers everything she reads is worth more than the catalogue.

lore.name: National laboratories
lore.info: Five national laboratories operate within the capital's limits, run by the State Military for alchemical and scientific research. State Alchemists may use them, and many of the army's projects are developed in them, from metallurgy to medicine. Laboratory 5, beside Central Prison, was closed some time ago, though it still has a sentry at the gate and razor wire on the wall. Locals say nobody guards an empty building that carefully.

lore.name: New Optain
lore.info: New Optain is a bustling city in the eastern area, with a line to East City. A major general, Halcrow, commands there and makes no secret of his dislike for the young colonel at East City who has risen so fast under Lieutenant General Grumman. Halcrow outranks him and cannot touch him, and it shows.

lore.name: Newspapers
lore.info: Every city prints its own papers and Central prints several, full of war news, society columns, army promotions, court-martial verdicts and crime. The papers love a State Alchemist story: a heroic one when the army wants good press, a frightening one when it does not. Reporters chase the Fullmetal Alchemist for quotes; he gives them, and then the army has to apologise for them. Readers in the East take what Central's papers say with a fistful of salt.

lore.name: North City
lore.info: North City lies south of the Briggs range, a picturesque town under snow most of the year, with steep roofs, warm taverns and the northern military headquarters. It is the supply depot and medical centre for Fort Briggs; the road to the fort is hard to travel, and anyone on army business must check in at North City first and either walk the mountain road or wait for an escort from the fort. Northerners say the town is lovely and the politics in its headquarters are not.

lore.name: Olivier Mira Armstrong
lore.info: Major General Olivier Mira Armstrong commands Fort Briggs and is the heir of the Armstrong family, a woman of about thirty-seven whom her soldiers call the northern wall and her rivals, behind her back, the Ice Queen. She is a brilliant commander and swordswoman, utterly fearless and contemptuous of weakness, cowardice and her younger brother. The Briggs garrison is devoted to her. Central's generals find her very useful and very uncomfortable.

lore.name: Paninya
lore.info: Paninya is a quick, cheerful teenage girl of Rush Valley with two automail legs, the right hiding a blade in the shin and the left a small cannon. Her parents died in a train accident that took her legs. The townspeople know her as a pickpocket who works the visitors and sells to the pawn shop, and they let it go, because she is charming and nobody can catch her.

lore.name: Parliament of Amestris
lore.info: Amestris has a parliament, elected and seated in Central City, and the constitution gives it the power to make law. In practice it is a facade. The army's high command allocates the regional governments as it likes, the important posts are filled by appointment, and the votes in parliament come after the decisions, not before. People vote for their members anyway, out of habit or hope, and the members give fine speeches. Ask a Central cab driver who runs the country and he will point at the moat around Central Command, not at the parliament house.

lore.name: Pendleton
lore.info: Pendleton is a western town, the first Amestris won in its long quarrel with Creta, and the army holds it up to the troops as a symbol of victory. It is also where the western war is bloodiest. Reckless orders from above have cost enormous numbers of men there, and the cemeteries outside the town are growing faster than the town itself.

lore.name: People of Amestris
lore.info: Amestris is a melting pot of the peoples it conquered. The majority are fair-skinned with dark hair and eyes; in the east many have tanned skin with brown hair and eyes; a fair-haired, blue-eyed folk turns up everywhere, and is found in no neighbouring land. The Ishvalans of the east are the most distinct, with their dark skin, white hair and red eyes. The country is crowded in the centre, east and south, thin in the west and lonely in the north. Most people live in the countryside, though the cities are growing every year.

lore.name: Perfect attack, perfect defence
lore.info: Officers say the army has two finest divisions and that they are opposites. The eastern army, hardened by seven years in Ishval, is the country's best offensive force, its soldiers veterans to a man; they call it the perfect attack. The Briggs garrison in the north holds the Drachma border and is the perfect defence. The two have never fought side by side. Staff officers like to imagine what they could do together, and generals in Central are glad the question has never come up.

lore.name: Philosopher from the East
lore.info: Every Amestrian alchemist hears the story in their first lessons. More than three hundred and fifty years ago a wise man came out of the east, from the direction of the desert, and taught the people here the principles of transmutation, and with it turned a minor country into a power. The tale says nothing of his face or his fate, and scholars still argue over whether he was one man or several. In Xing a matching story is told the other way round, of a Philosopher of the West who crossed the sands and taught the Xingese.

lore.name: Philosopher of the West
lore.info: Xingese records say that four hundred years ago the art they call alkahestry did not exist. Their healers swallowed minerals and potions they believed would lengthen life, and three generations of the imperial family died of mercury taken as medicine. Then a stranger came across the desert from the west, from Xerxes they say, and taught real transmutation. Xingese physicians wove his teaching into their older healing arts, and alkahestry was born. Xing honours him as the Philosopher of the West and knows nothing more of him; whether he and Amestris's own wise stranger were one man is a favourite argument wherever alchemists of both countries meet.

lore.name: Philosopher's Stone
lore.info: The Philosopher's Stone is the dream at the end of alchemy: an amplifier so perfect that, the legends say, an alchemist holding it can set aside the law of Equivalent Exchange and do anything. It is said to be blood red and unbreakable, a perfect material. Generations of alchemists have searched for it, written books about it and died poor. In practical modern times most masters say it exists only in the fancies of romantics. The State Military pays for research into everything; whether it pays for this, it does not say.

lore.name: Pinako Rockbell
lore.info: Pinako Rockbell is Resembool's automail engineer, a tiny, pipe-smoking old woman who was a surgeon in her youth and still drinks most men under the table. She raised her granddaughter after her son and daughter-in-law died in Ishval and looked after the Elric boys when their mother died. Engineers who knew her in her prime still go pale at her name.

lore.name: Plague of 1904
lore.info: In 1904 an outbreak of illness reached Resembool, a town too small for much of a hospital, and among those it took was Trisha Elric, a young mother of two boys who had raised them alone since her husband walked out. Her grave stands on the hill above the town. Local people still mention her kindly when the Elric boys come home, and pass quickly to something else.

lore.name: Princes and princesses of Xing
lore.info: Among the Emperor of Xing's forty-three heirs, a few names reach Amestris through merchants. Ling Yao, the twelfth prince and heir of the great Yao clan, is said to be clever, cheerful and dangerous, guarded by a grandfather and granddaughter of the clan's retainers, Fu and Lan Fan. May Chang, the seventeenth princess, of the small and powerless Chang clan, is a child prodigy in alkahestry. Both clans are said to be desperate for the Emperor's favour.

lore.name: Purification circle and kunai
lore.info: Where an Amestrian alchemist draws a new circle for every job, an alkahestrist uses one design for everything: a five-pointed star inside a ring. To work it at a distance, the practitioner throws kunai, the short Xingese throwing blades, to mark its points, five at the star and five more where the effect is meant to land, and sends the energy through the earth between them. It is quick and astonishing to watch. It also means an alkahestrist with no blades left is in serious trouble.

lore.name: Radio
lore.info: Radio Capital, a station in Central City syndicated across the country, broadcasts news, speeches and official announcements, and is generally agreed to be boring. In towns with a set, families gather to hear the Führer's addresses and the war bulletins; in the countryside a radio is a luxury. The station's staff take pride in the reach of their signal and complain about the material. People say that if anything truly important ever happened, Radio Capital would be the last to say so.

lore.name: Radio Capital
lore.info: A broadcaster in Central City, which runs interviews and news in the capital, mostly political programmes that listeners find dull, and its staff will not always follow the government's line. Its studio takes guests off the street and does not always say who put them on the air. A stranger meets the station as a voice in a shop window; a guest meets it as a live microphone. One who works here rises by delivering a good story and keeping the station's line.

lore.name: Rain River
lore.info: The Rain River runs through the south-eastern sheep country, and Resembool sits on its banks. It is not grand, and nobody outside the region could find it on a map, but the town's flocks graze along it and its people give directions by it: this side of the river or that.

lore.name: Rasayana
lore.info: Rasayana is an ancient Ishvalan word for a miraculous medicine that lengthens life. Since the war scattered the people who used it, hardly anyone outside a few Ishvalan families has heard the word, and no Amestrian library explains it.

lore.name: Rebound
lore.info: Alchemy draws on forces that belong to the world, not to the alchemist, and the world does not forgive a cheat. Attempt too much from too little and the transmutation does not simply fail; the energy thrown out of balance swings wildly to settle itself, and that is a rebound. A rebound can twist the result into something monstrous, maim the alchemist, or kill them. Every teacher has a story about a student who tried to skip the arithmetic. The worst rebounds of all, the ones teachers lower their voices about, come from trying to transmute a human being.

lore.name: Reole
lore.info: Reole, which some spell Liore, is a small, poor desert town in the east whose people are deeply religious. It has taken to the worship of Leto, the sun god, and to his prophet, Father Cornello, who rules the town now in all but name from his church. A great statue of the sun god stands inside. Visitors say the faithful are warm, the water is scarce, and the prophet's miracles draw crowds from the whole district.

lore.name: Reole's church
lore.info: Leto's church in Reole is the biggest building in the town, a domed temple on the square with a great statue of the sun god inside and a pulpit where Father Cornello performs his miracles. The faithful gather every evening to pray, and the rest of the town hears his sermons on the radio. Its acolytes are earnest, its guards are armed, and its back rooms are closed to all but the prophet's favourites.

lore.name: Resembool
lore.info: Resembool is a small farming town on the banks of the Rain River in the south-east, known across the region for its sheep. Its wool goes into army uniforms, which made it prosperous and, in 1907, made it a target; the station was bombed during the Ishval war and the town never grew again. It is green, quiet and slow. Every spring it holds a big sheep festival. The Elric brothers were born here, and the Rockbells keep their automail workshop on the hill.

lore.name: Resembool sheep
lore.info: The sheep of Resembool are the town's wealth. They graze along the Rain River, and their wool goes to the army for uniforms, which is what made the town grow and what made it a target in 1907. Every year a big sheep festival marks the start of spring. Visitors complain the whole town smells of sheep. Locals do not notice.

lore.name: Resignations after Ishval
lore.info: The war broke several of the alchemists who fought it. Some handed back their silver watches and walked away from the grant, the rank and the pension. Tim Marcoh, the Crystal Alchemist and a medical researcher, deserted after the war and vanished with his notes; the army still lists him as a fugitive. The Strong-Arm Alchemist, Alex Louis Armstrong, broke down at the front and was sent home for refusing to keep killing civilians. People whisper that the Freezing Alchemist resigned and went underground. For every hero of Ishval, a dozen alchemists would rather nobody asked.

lore.name: Restricted shelves
lore.info: Part of what draws alchemists into the State Alchemist programme is the library. The National Central Library opens most of its branches to anyone, but certain branches hold texts only State Alchemists and officers of sufficient rank may read. The best-known is the First Branch, a vast store of government records and research. Even so, readers who go looking for certain subjects come away puzzled at how thin the shelves are. Some think the library's founders simply never collected them. Some think something else.

lore.name: Riza Hawkeye
lore.info: Riza Hawkeye, a first lieutenant, is Colonel Mustang's adjutant and one of the best marksmen in the State Military. Calm, disciplined and severe, she keeps the colonel's schedule, his paperwork and, people say, his life in order, and she is the only member of his staff who served with him in Ishval. She owns a dog trained to perfection. Soldiers who have seen her shoot do not make jokes about her within earshot.

lore.name: Rockbell Automail
lore.info: An automail workshop in the Rockbell house at Resembool, run by Pinako Rockbell with her granddaughter Winry Rockbell. The house is also home to the Elric brothers while they are in town. The workshop builds and fits automail limbs and keeps them working. A stranger meets the house as a plain country home with a workshop out the back; a customer meets it as the one place that can fix a metal arm. One who works here learns the craft and rises by fitting limbs that hold.

lore.name: Rockbell automail workshop
lore.info: The Rockbell family's automail workshop in Resembool has fitted limbs across the east for decades. Pinako Rockbell, a surgeon and engineer in her day and still sharp-tongued in old age, founded it and trained her granddaughter Winry in the trade. Their limbs are sturdy, reliable and built to fit. The workshop's most famous customer is the Fullmetal Alchemist, who breaks his arm more often than any other client they have had.

lore.name: Rockbell house
lore.info: On a hill above Resembool stands the Rockbell house, a wooden farmhouse with a workshop where Pinako Rockbell and her granddaughter Winry build automail. Customers come from all over the east. A dog with an automail foreleg keeps watch on the porch. The house is also, by long habit, the place the Elric brothers stay when they come home, since their own house burned down the night they left.

lore.name: Rose Thomas
lore.info: Rose Thomas is a young woman of Reole, one of Father Cornello's most devoted followers. The man she loved died not long ago, and the prophet has promised her that Leto will bring him back if she prays faithfully. She prays every day at the church and tells every stranger about the miracle she is waiting for.

lore.name: Roy Mustang
lore.info: Colonel Roy Mustang, the Flame Alchemist, is the hero of Ishval and runs the day-to-day business of the eastern headquarters under Grumman, about twenty-nine and rising fast. He is charming, vain, said to have a different date every night, and useless in the rain. Everyone in the army knows he wants to be Führer one day; his rivals call it arrogance, his staff call it the plan. He is the Fullmetal Alchemist's commanding officer, which both of them complain about.

lore.name: Ruins of Xerxes
lore.info: In the middle of the Eastern Desert lie the ruins of Xerxes: the broken walls of a royal city, the domes of temples, and at the centre the shell of a great castle. The ancient wells still hold water, so the ruins serve as an oasis for anyone crossing between Amestris and Xing. Since the war, Ishvalan refugees have made a quiet home among the stones. Scholars who visit find carvings in a script few can read and an air that makes the hair on the neck rise.

lore.name: Runes and triangles
lore.info: Inside a transmutation circle sit the runes, and the most basic of them are triangles. Pointed up or down, with or without a bar across, a triangle stands for water, earth, fire or air. The hexagram is a favourite base because its overlapping triangles represent all four elements at once. Beyond those come older and stranger signs: astrological marks, symbolic images, lines of text in old scripts. Some schools work through the four classical elements, others through the three principles of salt, sulphur and mercury. Students spend years learning which rune does what, and a master's notebook is mostly runes.

lore.name: Rush Valley
lore.info: Rush Valley, just north of Dublith, is the automail capital of Amestris. Engineers crowd its streets, show off their work in public contests and push their wares on anyone who walks past with a prosthetic, so a visitor with an automail limb can barely get from the station to the inn without three sales pitches and an inspection. Shops like Atelier Garfiel work late into the night. Pickpockets do well here too. The town is loud, oily, cheerful and proud of every bolt.

lore.name: Rush Valley automail trade
lore.info: The automail engineers of Rush Valley, the boomtown of the broken-down, who hold contests in the street and push their wares on anyone with a steel limb. They are rivals in every shop and allies against every outsider. A visitor meets them as hands grabbing at a sleeve to see the arm beneath; a customer meets them as the best limbs in the country. One who joins rises by making a limb the street talks about.

lore.name: Rush Valley's boom
lore.info: Twenty years of constant war produced a great many amputees, and the town that served them grew rich. Rush Valley, just north of Dublith, has grown fast in recent years as the centre of automail making; now it is a town of workshops, competitions and loud men who chase passers-by down the street to sell them a better knee. The rest of the country calls it the boomtown of the broken-down, and the town wears the name half with pride and half without.

lore.name: Scale of a circle
lore.info: Size matters to a circle. A small circle on a desk moves small things; a circle chalked across a courtyard can raise a wall the height of a house. The old texts speak of circles drawn as large as cities or even whole countries and of effects to match, though no one in living memory has attempted such a thing, and lecturers treat those passages as theory. The practical lesson for a working alchemist is simpler: if a job is too big for your circle, draw a bigger one, and make sure your understanding is big enough too.

lore.name: Scar's vigil
lore.info: A lone vigilante who hunts State Alchemists, moving through the country with a few companions and no fixed seat. The public knows the name Scar and the cross-shaped scar on his forehead, and the alchemical tattoo on his arm, and it knows the killings. A stranger meets the vigil as a rumour; a State Alchemist meets it as a death. In 1914 a few strays fall in with him, Yoki, a disgraced former officer, the loudest of them. One who joins the vigil learns to kill quietly and to leave no witness.

lore.name: Selim Bradley
lore.info: Selim is the Führer's young son, adopted, a polite and cheerful schoolboy who is plainly adored by both parents. He wants to grow up to be like his father and says so to every officer he meets. Society columns print his school prizes and his birthday parties. Officers who must deal with the Führer at home learn to be very nice to Selim.

lore.name: Shou Tucker
lore.info: Shou Tucker, the Sewing-Life Alchemist, is a mild, bespectacled bio-alchemist in East City who won his certificate two years ago with a talking chimera. He lives quietly with his five-year-old daughter Nina Tucker and her dog; his wife left, people say. His assessment is due and he has shown nothing new since, and colleagues have noticed how tired he looks.

lore.name: Shou Tucker's house
lore.info: The Sewing-Life Alchemist lives on the outskirts of East City in a big, quiet house with a library, a laboratory and cages for his animals. His wife left some years ago, the neighbours say. His little daughter and her huge white dog play in the yard, and the girl waves at anyone passing. The colonel at Eastern Command sends visiting alchemists there to use the library. The house is always a little too quiet.

lore.name: Sig Curtis
lore.info: Sig Curtis is Izumi's husband, a huge, bearded, silent butcher with a fearsome face who is gentle with children, devoted to his wife and bad at small talk. He is not an alchemist. He does not need to be. Dublith's toughs cross the street when they see him coming.

lore.name: South City
lore.info: South City is the military and cultural centre of the southern area, south of Dublith, famous for its sights and its tourists. The southern headquarters here runs the long war with Aerugo, and the city's hospitals and taverns are full of men back from Fotset. In the shopping streets it is hard to tell there is a war at all. State Alchemists working in the south hand in their yearly reports at the headquarters, usually at the last minute.

lore.name: South Hood
lore.info: South Hood is a town beyond the mountains that rise between it and Rush Valley. Travellers on the mountain road pass a lonely automail workshop, run by a gruff old engineer who would rather live among the rocks and the ore than in any town. The road is steep and few take it without business at one end.

lore.name: State Alchemist certificate
lore.info: A State Alchemist's certificate is printed on heavy paper and signed in the Führer's name. It names the holder and the title the Führer has chosen for them, states that they must follow all orders and policies of the military, promises ample research funds, access to classified documents and government facilities and the rank of major, and warns that a holder who shows no progress at the yearly assessment will be discharged. Most holders frame it. A few burn it.

lore.name: State Alchemist programme
lore.info: The State Alchemists are alchemists employed by the State Military under an elite government programme. Each one holds a rank equal to major from the day of certification, draws a large research grant every year to spend as they please, may enter the national laboratories and read classified documents, and climbs the ranks faster than an ordinary officer. In exchange they belong to the army. In peace they research; in war they are sent wherever the Führer wants them.

lore.name: State Alchemist titles
lore.info: Each certificate bears a title the Führer chooses, drawn from both the alchemist's art and their character: the Flame Alchemist, the Strong-Arm Alchemist, the Iron Blood Alchemist, the Crystal Alchemist, the Silver Alchemist, the Sewing-Life Alchemist, the Fullmetal Alchemist. The title becomes a public name; newspapers use it, enemies use it, and some holders come to prefer it to their own. A few are compliments. Others seem to have been chosen with a cruel sense of humour, and alchemists compare them with all the pettiness of schoolchildren comparing nicknames.

lore.name: State Alchemists
lore.info: The alchemists the State Military employs in an elite government programme. The licence brings a large yearly research grant to spend as the holder likes, a rank equal to major, the best materials, the state laboratories and the classified files; it costs three rules: obey the military, never make gold, never make a human. Each holder carries a silver pocket watch as identification and faces a research assessment every year, and one who shows no progress is discharged. Ordinary alchemists live by the creed of being for the people, so the public calls the licensed the dogs of the military, and since Ishval the fighters among them are sent to war as human weapons. One earns the licence by passing a written test, a psychological evaluation and a practical before a military board, and the Führer sets the title it carries.

lore.name: State Military
lore.info: The armed forces of Amestris and, in all but name, its government: the Führer is its Generalissimo, it rules from Central City and keeps a command headquarters in each of the four outer areas. Its soldiers wear blue, salute every superior on entry and keep to a strict protocol, and those who break it face detention or court-martial. The army holds the long border wars with Aerugo in the south and Creta in the west, guards the north against Drachma, and keeps order in the cities. A stranger meets it as a checkpoint, a recruiting poster or a patrol; a foreigner meets it as a prisoner. One who joins trains at the military academy, starts as a private and climbs by orders obeyed and wars won, and the highest ranks sit close to the Führer.

lore.name: Survival of the fittest
lore.info: Fort Briggs lives by a single law, and its commander, Major General Olivier Mira Armstrong, states it plainly: the strong survive and the weak die. In the mountains this is not cruelty but weather. A soldier who cannot carry his share in a blizzard kills the men beside him, so Briggs trains hard, promotes by merit and takes no excuses, and every man and woman there is expected to fight. Nobody at Briggs cares where you were born, what colour your eyes are or who your father is. They care whether you can still stand at the end of a winter exercise.

lore.name: Tavern talk
lore.info: In any Amestrian tavern the talk runs the same way: the price of bread, the war in the south, who has been conscripted, what the State Alchemists are up to, and whether the Führer looked tired in the latest photograph. In the East men lower their voices about Ishval and the Blue Squad. In Central they talk promotions. In the North they talk weather, and then Drachma, and then weather again.

lore.name: The Armstrong lineage
lore.info: For one hundred and eighty years the Armstrong family has served Amestris in its army, its banks and its parliament. Generals, financiers and politicians all bear the same curled forelock and, it is said, the same embarrassing habit of glowing with pride when they speak of the family. The former patriarch, Philip Gargantos Armstrong, retired a general. His eldest daughter commands Fort Briggs; his only son is the Strong-Arm Alchemist; three more daughters round out the house. The family's art of alchemy is passed down from generation to generation, and they mention it often.

lore.name: The Blue Squad
lore.info: The Eastern Liberation Front, which everyone calls the Blue Squad, is a band of political extremists based in the East Area. What exactly they want beyond hurting Central's government and its eastern command nobody has managed to pin down. Their record of crimes against the government and its eastern command is long. Early in 1914 the eastern army caught and jailed their leader, and every officer in East City expects his men to try something to get him back.

lore.name: The country in spring 1914
lore.info: As the spring of 1914 opens, Amestris looks stable from Central and restless everywhere else. The Führer is in health and popular. The Aerugo war grinds on at Fotset, the western command bleeds slowly around Pendleton, and the Drachma pact holds by habit. In the east, Ishval lies occupied and empty, Reole has given itself to a preacher who works miracles, and the Blue Squad's leader sits in a cell. A new rumour is going around the eastern barracks: that someone has started killing State Alchemists, and that the killer has a cross-shaped scar on his forehead.

lore.name: The doctors of Kanda
lore.info: Two Resembool surgeons, Yuriy Rockbell and Sarah Rockbell, left their daughter with her grandmother when the war reached its height and went to the front to treat the wounded. They worked in the Kanda district of Ishval and treated anyone carried in, Amestrian or Ishvalan, which made them loved by the people of Kanda and a nuisance to some officers. Both died there in 1908. Doctors who served in Ishval still speak of them as the best the war had, and more than a few Ishvalans alive today owe them their lives.

lore.name: The Drachma pact
lore.info: North of the Briggs mountains lies Drachma, a belligerent state that has fought Amestris on and off for as long as either has had an army. Early in the 1900s the two signed a pact of non-aggression, and it has held, barely, ever since, with threats on both sides every few seasons. What keeps the peace is less the paper than the mountains: an army crossing the Briggs range in winter dies of the cold before it reaches a wall, and the one valley where a road runs through is blocked by Fort Briggs. Northern soldiers trust the fort, not the treaty.

lore.name: The emperors and mercury
lore.info: Before alkahestry, the court of Xing chased long life through the mouth. Physicians ground minerals and brewed tonics, and the imperial family drank them, mercury above all, because it was believed to lengthen life. Three whole generations of the family died of it, the chronicles say, before the new art taught anyone better. Xingese alkahestrists tell the story to every apprentice as the reason their art tests a medicine before it prescribes one.

lore.name: The end of the war
lore.info: By 1909 the fighting in Ishval was over. The region was occupied by the army, its districts in ruins, and the Ishvalan people were close to gone: the survivors scattered into slums across the country, from the East to the far North, and as far as the ruins of Xerxes in the desert. The automail trade boomed on the wounded. Several State Alchemists resigned their certificates in disgust at what they had done. Others went home and never spoke of it again. The army gave out medals, and the eastern army came home the most experienced fighting force in the country.

lore.name: The expansion wars
lore.info: Amestris grew by war. Since its founding the state has pushed against every border, annexing towns, then provinces, then whole peoples, and folding their land into its own areas. The Ishvalans of the east and the border towns taken from Creta in the west all came under Amestrian rule this way, and the war with Aerugo has run since 1835. The habit shaped the country: a stable economy and a strong government came to depend on the next campaign, and the army rose to the top of every ladder of prestige. Old soldiers say Amestris has never known a decade without a front somewhere. Young recruits are told the wars keep the nation safe; their grandmothers, in the annexed towns, remember it differently.

lore.name: The festival duel
lore.info: During one of the army's festivals in Central, the Fullmetal Alchemist and the Flame Alchemist were put up against each other in a public exhibition match before a crowd. Soldiers who were there still argue about who really came off better. The match did more for both men's fame than any report.

lore.name: The fifty clans of Xing
lore.info: Xing's people belong to fifty hereditary clans, which differ hugely in size and standing. The Yao clan is among the great ones, with more than half a million people; the Chang clan is small, poor and has little influence; the Han clan has members who make a living smuggling travellers across the desert. Each clan backs its heir to the throne with money, warriors and spies, and a clan's fortunes rise or fall with its prince's.

lore.name: The Flamel
lore.info: The Flamel is an old alchemical sign: a cross with a serpent wound around it, a pair of detached wings above and a crown on top. In alchemy it stands for fixing the volatile, a step in the making of medicines. A teacher in Dublith wears it tattooed over her heart, and her two famous students carry it, one on the back of a red coat and the other on the shoulder of his armour. Many people assume it is a family crest. It is closer to a school badge.

lore.name: The founding of Amestris
lore.info: Amestrian schoolbooks put the country's official founding around 1550, though people lived on the land long before any government pulled them together. What changed everything, the old histories say, was alchemy. A stranger remembered only as the Philosopher from the East brought the art to a small, quarrelling country, and with it the country learned to build, mine and fight better than its neighbours. Within a generation the new state was taking land from the peoples around it, and it has not stopped since. Nobody can say who he was or where he went; the legend gives him no name and no grave.

lore.name: The Gate
lore.info: Alchemists who have tried to transmute a person and survived sometimes describe the same thing: a great stone door standing alone in an endless white, carved with a design that is different for every person who sees it. When it opens there is darkness behind it, an eye, and many small black hands that pull you through. What happens inside they cannot or will not describe, except that they came back knowing more than before and missing something they had brought. Most scholars treat the accounts as the fever dreams of the badly injured. A few do not.

lore.name: The gold law
lore.info: No alchemist in Amestris may make gold. The rule is not about morality; it is about money. If anyone with chalk and lead could make gold, the national economy would collapse within a season, so the transmutation is banned for every practitioner in the country and punished hard. State Alchemists, who work under the government's eye, are watched most closely and face military charges if caught. Rumours about this or that wealthy alchemist's secret fortune are common in the taverns and almost always wrong.

lore.name: The Gold Steiner story
lore.info: Mountaineers in the north tell a tale about a young woman who came seeking an apprenticeship from the famous alchemist Silver Steiner and found only his elder brother, Gold Steiner, an eighty-eight-year-old martial artist who was hard of hearing. Gold misunderstood her and handed her a machete with orders to live alone in the Briggs mountains for a month. She came back carrying a dead bear. Silver Steiner had already died; Gold Steiner took her on himself, and she beat him senseless in her first sparring bout. The northerners insist every word is true, and alchemists in the south say they know who she grew up to be.

lore.name: The Ishval war as the army teaches it
lore.info: At the military academy, the Ishval war is taught as a lesson in pacification: a long insurgency, foreign arms, a rebel population that would not negotiate, and a decisive commitment of new force that ended it in a year. Cadets learn the name of the order and not much about what followed. The veterans who teach the course often teach it flatly, eyes on the page. Ask one about it after hours and he will either change the subject or tell you more than the syllabus ever would.

lore.name: The Ouroboros
lore.info: The ouroboros is one of alchemy's oldest symbols: a winged serpent swallowing its own tail, coiled into a ring, often with a hexagram inside. It stands for the endless cycle of birth and death, for wholeness and for infinity, and some read it as an eclipse. It turns up in old manuscripts, on jewellery and as a tattoo among people who like to look mysterious. Scholars note that the shape is very like a transmutation circle and argue about which came first.

lore.name: The race for immortality
lore.info: The Emperor of Xing is old and sick, and his heirs know the surest way to his favour is to give him what he most wants: a way to live forever. Clan agents have been sent in every direction to look for it, and some of them have heard the western legend of a stone that defies the laws of alchemy. A Xingese prince or princess turning up in Amestris asking questions about immortality would surprise nobody who knows Xing, and would worry a good many people who know Amestris.

lore.name: The regional headquarters
lore.info: Outside the capital, government means the army. Each of the four outer areas has a military headquarters in its main city, East City, North City, South City and West City, and the commanding general there is governor in all but name, answerable only to Central. The headquarters compete fiercely: for budget, for promotions, for the Führer's attention. Officers posted to one carry its loyalties for life, and a transfer between them can feel like moving to a different army. Regional commanders have little real freedom from Central, and a great deal of politics among themselves.

lore.name: The Resembool station bombing
lore.info: In 1907, at the height of the Ishval war, Ishvalan fighters struck Resembool with explosives. The quiet sheep town was a target because of its wool, which went into the army's uniforms, and the blast flattened several blocks around the railway station. The station was rebuilt and the town recovered, but its growth stopped there; Resembool has stayed a small place ever since. Locals do not talk about it much. Ask an old farmer about the war and he will point at the newer brick near the platform and leave it at that.

lore.name: The road between Amestris and Xing
lore.info: There are two ways to go from Amestris to Xing. The long way runs south through Aerugo to the sea and around by ship, weeks of sailing and ports. The short way runs across the Eastern Desert, by camel or on foot, from well to well, past the ruins of Xerxes, with a guide who knows the dunes. Most who make the short crossing are smugglers, refugees, or people who would rather not answer questions at a port. Many who set out without a guide are never heard of again.

lore.name: The shot of 1901
lore.info: In 1901, in a tense and occupied Ishval, an Amestrian soldier shot and killed an Ishvalan child. The army called it an accident. The region did not believe it. Riots and protests followed within days, then attacks on garrisons, then open war. Every Ishvalan family can tell you where it was when the news came, and every veteran of the eastern army knows the date the fighting began. Who the soldier was, and what became of him, nobody in the street can say; the records released to the public say only that he was a member of the State Military.

lore.name: The silver watch
lore.info: Every State Alchemist carries a silver pocket watch engraved with the programme's emblem, the Amestrian dragon inside a hexagram. It is their identification: shown at a checkpoint, it opens doors and makes any soldier below major stand straighter. It also tells everyone in the room exactly what its owner is, which in the East is not always a good thing. The watch has no other power that anyone knows of. Holders tend to keep theirs on a chain, out of sight, and to take it out only when they must.

lore.name: The speaking chimera
lore.info: The only chimera known to have spoken human words was made by Shou Tucker in 1912. It said a few sentences in a strained voice, among them that it wanted to die, then refused to eat and starved within days. The board granted Tucker his certificate on the strength of it. People who heard it never forget the voice, and some of them have wondered ever since how an animal learned to sound so sad.

lore.name: The State Alchemist examination
lore.info: Candidates face three trials. A written examination tests theory, and it is famously hard. A psychological evaluation tries to decide whether the candidate is stable enough to be trusted with what the army will ask of them. Last comes the practical: a demonstration before a board of officers, which in some years has included the Führer himself, to show that the candidate's art works in the real world. Most fail. Those who pass receive their certificate weeks later, from Central, with a title chosen for them.

lore.name: The State Alchemist killer
lore.info: In the East, people have begun to whisper about a killer who hunts State Alchemists: a big, dark-skinned man with a cross-shaped scar across his forehead and a tattooed right arm that destroys whatever it touches. Survivors say he speaks of god before he kills. The army has no name for him, so the soldiers call him Scar. Every State Alchemist in the eastern area has been told to keep their watch out of sight and to travel in company.

lore.name: The Stone in legend
lore.info: Old tales put the Stone at the heart of disasters and miracles alike, among them a vague one about the vanished desert kingdom of Xerxes that most scholars refuse to credit. A preacher who works miracles is always suspected of having one. Serious alchemists treat these stories the way physicians treat folk cures: some grain of truth, buried under a great deal of hope. The Elric brothers are known to be hunting for it, and people who like the boys hope they find something better.

lore.name: The talking chimera
lore.info: In 1912 an East City alchemist, Shou Tucker, presented the State Alchemist board with a chimera that could speak human words. It said only a few sentences, refused food and died soon after, yet it was enough to win him a certificate and the title of the Sewing-Life Alchemist. Bio-alchemy had never produced anything like it. Two years later the achievement is still cited in lectures, and Tucker is under pressure to repeat it before his next assessment, because the board has not seen anything new from him since.

lore.name: The telephone
lore.info: Telephones are common in Amestrian cities and offices. Every headquarters has its switchboard, officers ring each other across the country, and public telephones stand in stations and on street corners, where a long-distance call costs a fistful of coins. Operators connect the calls, and everyone in the army assumes someone else is listening, so careful officers speak in codes, pet names and talk about girlfriends that do not exist. Smaller towns may have a single line at the post office, and the countryside has none.

lore.name: The three rules
lore.info: Every State Alchemist swears to three rules. Obey the military: follow every order of your superiors and serve the nation, not yourself and not the crowd. Do not create gold: all alchemists are forbidden to make it, to keep the economy from collapsing, but State Alchemists are watched more closely and face military charges if caught. Do not create humans: human transmutation is banned for everyone, and doubly for the State Alchemists, whose resources make a serious attempt more likely. Breaking any of the three ends a career at best.

lore.name: The Truth
lore.info: The few who come back from the door speak of someone waiting at it: a white, featureless figure with the shape of the one who stands there, who calls itself by many names, the world, the universe, god, the truth, and you. It talks politely, laughs at you, and takes its toll. Those who meet it say it is neither cruel nor kind, only exact; it takes what you can least bear to lose and calls that fair. Those who tell of it are few, and they do not tell it twice.

lore.name: The Xerxes legend
lore.info: Four hundred years ago a great kingdom stood in the desert east of Amestris. Xerxes had a million people, domed temples, busy markets, deep wells and a royal city of brick and stone, and its scholars studied alchemy long before Amestris did. Then its people vanished, all of them, and nobody survived to explain why. Some say plague, some say a curse, and alchemists whisper that a Philosopher's Stone had something to do with it. Most educated people call that last part a fairy tale. The ruins are real enough, and caravans still water at the old city.

lore.name: The yearly assessment
lore.info: Once a year every State Alchemist must hand in an assessment report showing what their research has achieved with the grant. A holder who shows no progress is put on probation; a second failure costs them the certificate. Holders sweat over it every season, and late reports are a running joke at the regional headquarters. Gossip says the Führer has been known to sign a renewal personally, on the spot, if he happens to bump into the alchemist in a corridor.

lore.name: Tim Marcoh
lore.info: Doctor Tim Marcoh was the Crystal Alchemist, a State Alchemist and medical researcher who served in Ishval and then deserted, taking his research with him. The army lists him as a fugitive. He was a soft-spoken, nervous man with a reputation for brilliance in medical alchemy, and some say he is still practising medicine somewhere in the countryside under another name.

lore.name: Trains of Amestris
lore.info: Steam railways tie Amestris together.
